bottlenecks.name: Orbit determination and uncertainty realism
bottlenecks.description: Maintaining catalogs and operator orbits with covariances that are actually realistic: atmospheric drag (the largest LEO prediction error), space-weather storms, sensor biases, unannounced maneuvers, data association and the shift from Gaussian to curved, non-Gaussian uncertainty over days. The May 2024 Gannon storm degraded collision prediction for days; ESA estimates ~54,000 objects >10 cm exist versus ~40,000 catalogued, and ~1.2 million 1-10 cm fragments are untracked.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium. Certified non-Gaussian propagation, bounded-error Pc and better drag-uncertainty models are expert-scarce applied math that on-demand capability makes routine (P1). But the binding constraint is data: no theorem detects an untracked fragment or forecasts a coronal mass ejection's arrival.

bottlenecks.name: Conjunction assessment and collision-avoidance operations
bottlenecks.description: Screening tens of thousands of objects against each other, computing Pc, deciding and coordinating maneuvers. Starlink performed 148,696 avoidance maneuvers Jun-Nov 2025 and 207,152 Dec 2025-May 2026 (over 40 per satellite per year) at a Pc threshold of 3e-7, 100x stricter than the 1e-4 industry norm. Cross-operator coordination is manual or bilateral; a Dec 2025 Chinese launch put a payload within ~200 m of a Starlink with no ephemeris sharing.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium-High for the mathematical parts: provably sound screening filters, verified coordination protocols, defensible thresholds (P2, P1). Low for the binding parts: data sharing, standards, US-China politics and conservative operator policy.

bottlenecks.name: Trajectory design and optimization
bottlenecks.description: Low-thrust, multi-body, cislunar and interplanetary trajectory design: initial-guess generation, local optimization, global search, invariant-manifold and low-energy transfers, contingency sets. Solved in principle, expensive in expert time; designs are locally optimal with unknown gaps.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High. This is the clearest 'solved in principle, expert-scarce' area. Pre-release agents already derive Pontryagin conditions and write shooting codes (HELIOS, Jul 2026); GTOC 12 agents doubled strategic scores in two years but failed on implementation details that stronger models plus verification fix. Moment-SOS methods are starting to give global-optimality certificates (Jul 2026).

bottlenecks.name: Onboard guidance and control, and GNC software verification
bottlenecks.description: Real-time convex and successive-convexification guidance (powered descent, rendezvous), attitude control, hybrid mode logic for docking and capture, learned controllers under runtime assurance, and the verification and validation that typically dominates flight-software cost. Proofs exist for idealized 3-DoF landing; 6-DoF guarantees, solver numerics and hybrid/contact logic are mostly validated by Monte Carlo and test.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High for proofs (convergence, feasibility, floating-point bounds, barrier certificates) via P1 and P2. The gates are specifications, tool qualification and certification acceptance, which compress far less than the cognitive work.

bottlenecks.name: Autonomous navigation
bottlenecks.description: Earth-independent navigation for cislunar and deep-space craft: optical and terrain-relative navigation, X-ray pulsar navigation, weak-signal GNSS at lunar distance (LuGRE fix on the Moon, Mar 2025), lunar PNT constellations (Moonlight, LunaNet) and their integrity guarantees.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low-Medium. Integrity-certified filters and fault detection become cheap; accuracy remains set by sensors, clocks and signal geometry.

bottlenecks.name: Long-term dynamics and environment evolution
bottlenecks.description: Stability of cislunar and lunar orbits (frozen orbits, DROs, NRHOs, resonances), disposal-orbit safety, chaos and transport in three- and four-body models, and decade-scale debris-environment (Kessler cascade) modeling for capacity and licensing questions.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium for theory (computer-assisted transport bounds, proven thresholds in source-sink models), Low for operational change: chaos sets prediction horizons no proof removes, and debris models are dominated by uncertain inputs (fragmentation data, launch rates, compliance).

astro.scenario_contrast: S1 (Plateau): research-grade math reaches outside teams around 2027-28 but stays mostly in proofs; the domain's one robust effect by 2031 is trajectory design on demand (High), with first missions flying AI-designed trajectories around 2029. Verified solvers, proof-carrying GNC toolchains and certified screening appear around 2030 as research artifacts (Medium); nothing at tier 6-7 beyond flown trajectories is more than Low. S2 (Exponential, base case): the cognitive clock collapses tiers 1-4 into 2027-2028 - SCP guarantees, certificates, certified Pc, verified solvers, coordination protocols, hybrid docking proofs and the GNC toolchain are all High by 2031. Then the physical clock takes over: flight demos land in 2029-2030 (Medium) because of software freezes, test campaigns and manifests; operational proof-backed uncrewed GNC (2029) and cross-operator autonomous collision avoidance (2030) are Medium, the latter capped by standards and regulators; crewed certification credit and 'LEO safe at 100k satellites' stay Low because tool qualification, untracked debris and geopolitics bind. S3 (Recursive) pulls every cognitive node to 2027 and buys about one year at tiers 5-6 (e.g. landing-guidance demo 2028, proof-backed ops 2028), but launch cadence, design-freeze cycles, sensor deployment, standards bodies and US-China coordination move barely at all: several tier 5-6 nodes (AI-designed trajectories flown, autonomous navigation demo) have the same year in S2 and S3. The gap between the cognitive frontier and flown capability widens with each scenario: in S2 it is roughly 2-3 years; in S3 3-4 years.
key_insights: Start from the field: astrodynamics' math effort sits in orbit-determination uncertainty, conjunction operations, trajectory design and GNC verification - bespoke applied math, not famous conjectures. The catalog families nearest the domain (146, 347, 343, 143) concern model maps and planar fields; their astro effect is confidence-only and near nil. The lever is the capability (P1) and formal verification (P2).

The fastest real effect is trajectory design on demand: it was visible before the release (HELIOS, Jul 2026; GTOC 12 agents doubling strategic scores in two years) and needs no regulator. High by 2031 in every scenario; flown AI-designed trajectories by 2028 in S2.

Verified GNC is the highest-value chain: SCP convergence proofs -> verified onboard solvers -> proof-carrying GNC toolchain -> flight demo -> operational uncrewed use. In S2 the math is done by 2028, flight demos 2029, operational uncrewed use 2029; crewed certification credit stays Low through 2031 because tool qualification and human-rating clocks bind.

Space traffic is data- and politics-bound, not math-bound: ~1.2 million untracked 1-10 cm fragments, drag forecasts limited by space weather, and no US-China ephemeris sharing (Dec 2025 near-miss at ~200 m). Certified Pc and verified screening can cut false alarms (Starlink maneuvers at 3e-7, 100x stricter than the norm, ~355k maneuvers a year) only if covariances are realistic.

The cognitive clock compresses tiers 1-4 by 2-3 years from S1 to S2; tiers 5-7 move 1-2 years at most, and S3 adds about one more year. Launch manifests, design freezes, test campaigns, standards bodies and sensor deployment are the binding gates for every tier 5-7 node.

Chaos sets hard horizons that no proof removes: unstable cislunar orbits like NRHOs have prediction horizons of days to weeks. AI math can certify where orbits are regular and bound station-keeping given a controller model, but Monte Carlo and active control remain.

Cislunar math will arrive before cislunar traffic: Gateway's cancellation (Mar 24, 2026) removes the main NRHO traffic node; cislunar object counts stay in the tens; the gate for a traffic service is funded sensors, not algorithms.

The new failure mode is specification error: a June 2026 audit showed kernel-accepted agent formalizations with weakened hypotheses and parameter restrictions. For flight software, a proof of the wrong property gives false assurance at scale, so specification review and independent checking become the scarce resource.
nil_effects: No catalog result changes an orbit, maneuver or trajectory: 146, 347, 343 and 143 concern the standard map, Hamiltonian fixed points, symplectic packing and planar polynomial fields; the release has no n-body, KAM-for-three-body or Arnold-diffusion-rate results.

Chaotic prediction horizons (Lyapunov times of days to weeks for NRHO-type orbits) are a property of the dynamics; proofs cannot extend ballistic predictability, so station-keeping and Monte Carlo remain.
Untracked debris: about 1.2 million 1-10 cm fragments cannot be screened against; detecting them needs sensors, not mathematics.

Delta-v physics: the rocket equation and multi-body energetics are fixed; global-optimality certificates typically expose gaps of a few percent, and low-energy transfers trade flight time for propellant rather than giving it free.
Space-weather forecast lead time (coronal-mass-ejection arrival and orientation) limits storm-time drag prediction regardless of model sophistication.
Launch cadence, design-freeze cycles and lander schedules (Artemis III as a 2027 LEO docking test, crewed landings targeted 2028) are set by hardware and programs, not by AI math.
Coordination with non-cooperating operators (including US-China data sharing) is a political gate; a provably safe protocol does nothing if one fleet does not run it.
Galactic speedups in the release (matrix multiplication exponent, sub-n-log-n FFT) give no practical speedup to orbit propagation, screening or onboard estimation codes.
Hardness results such as Unique Games (102) bound worst-case fleet-scale tasking, but individual collision-avoidance maneuver planning is small and solved per event, so the ceilings do not bind.
Navigation accuracy at the Moon and in deep space is set by sensors, clocks and signal geometry; certified filters change assurance, not accuracy.

signposts.event: Public availability (API or product) of a research-grade math model from any lab, with pricing usable by aerospace teams.
signposts.what_it_changes: Starts every P1 chain (SCP guarantees, transport proofs, global certificates, trajectory design on demand); its date is the main S1-versus-S2 discriminator. If later than mid-2028, shift S2 tier 2-4 years right by about one year.

signposts.event: An AI agent places top-3 in a Global Trajectory Optimization Competition (GTOC) with minimal human input (2027-28).
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms trajectory design on demand and flown AI-designed trajectories (High). Failure due to the same implementation errors found in the GTOC 12 study would push those nodes a year later.

signposts.event: First independent Comparator check of openai/math Lean families, including 347, 143, 104, 139 and 140.
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves those families from T3 to T4; mainly tests the verification pipeline that astro verification chains rely on, since their direct astro effect is small.

signposts.event: Release of a public formal astrodynamics library or a verified embedded SOCP/QP solver with floating-point bounds (e.g. at NASA Formal Methods 2027).
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the verified-GNC chain is on the S2 track (toolchain 2028, flight demo 2029). Absence by end-2028 moves those nodes toward S1 timing.

signposts.event: Starlink's next two semiannual FCC reports (maneuvers per satellite; currently over 40 per year and rising).
signposts.what_it_changes: If per-satellite maneuvers flatten while the fleet grows, better covariances and Pc methods are biting (raise astro-leo-safety-at-scale). Continued tripling means data and coordination bind (keep Low).

signposts.event: FCC action on SpaceX's up-to-1-million-satellite orbital data center application, and the FY2027 appropriation for the Office of Space Commerce (request $11M vs $52.5M).
signposts.what_it_changes: An aggregate risk or capacity metric in an FCC order raises astro-capacity-licensing; a gutted TraCSS lowers astro-catalog-scale-screening adoption and cislunar traffic management.

signposts.event: First automated cross-operator maneuver-coordination agreement (e.g. Starlink with Amazon Leo) or a CCSDS/ISO maneuver-intent standard draft.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the regulatory gate is moving for astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale; inclusion of a Chinese operator would be a major upside surprise.

signposts.event: NASA or FAA guidance on AI-generated formal evidence for flight software, or the first DO-178C/DO-333 credit for AI-produced proofs in aviation.
signposts.what_it_changes: The leading indicator for infra-tool-qualification and astro-human-rated-proof-credit; without it, crewed credit stays Low or Speculative in every scenario.

signposts.event: The next G4-G5 geomagnetic storm.
signposts.what_it_changes: Shows whether storm-time screening still degrades for days as in May 2024; a materially better outcome would raise astro-thermosphere-drag-uq.

auton.domain: Autonomy, robotics, ISRU, life support and human spaceflight systems

bottlenecks.name: Verifying autonomous behavior (planners, fault responses, learned perception, multi-robot teams)
bottlenecks.description: Showing that a rover, excavator, assembly robot or habitat fault manager does the right thing across the situations it will meet, when ground control is 1.3 s (Moon) to 4-24 min (Mars) away or blacked out behind a crater rim. Today the main method is human plan review plus simulation: Perseverance's first AI-planned drives (Dec 8 and 10, 2025; 210 m and 246 m, planned with Anthropic's Claude) were checked by running the commands through JPL's digital twin across more than 500,000 telemetry variables before uplink. CADRE (three cooperating rovers, launching on IM-3, planned late 2026) will be NASA's first multi-robot autonomous team beyond Earth, without formal proofs of its leader election or task re-allocation.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~25% of the domain's mathematical and modeling effort (judgment, general); the largest recurring cost in operating surface robots
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mostly 'solved in principle but expensive and expert-scarce': reactive synthesis from temporal-logic specs, probabilistic model checking, reachability and barrier certificates, runtime-assurance (Simplex) proofs all exist but each application needs a specialist to build abstractions and specs. On-demand research math collapses that cost (P1->P2). Genuinely open: verifying learned perception and large neural controllers at scale (closed-loop neural verification still does not scale to autonomy-size networks, arXiv 2609.16298, Sep 2026). Catalog touch: family 104 (mean-payoff/stochastic/parity games, T3) and the hardness family for planning ceilings; both small.

bottlenecks.name: Regolith and contact physics (granular flow, terramechanics, frictional contact, sintering)
bottlenecks.description: Every excavator, conveyor, wheel, drill, grasp, connector mate and sintered landing pad depends on models of granular media and frictional contact that are not predictive. Polar icy regolith is the worst case: lab tests (Sep 2026) show excavation energy for ice-cemented simulant rising from 2.74 to 143 J/g as ice goes from 1 to 12 wt% (52x), while pressure-sintered ice gets easier to dig with more ice; nobody knows which form exists at the poles. Granular continuum models (e.g. mu(I) rheology) are ill-posed in parts of their range (general), so codes regularize ad hoc; DEM is accurate but expensive. Contact simulators (MuJoCo, Drake, PhysX) use different contact regularizations and disagree in stick-slip and jamming (general).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Two genuinely open math problems with leverage: well-posedness/selection for frictional multi-contact dynamics and convergence of the time-stepping schemes used in simulators; and well-posed continuum theories of dense granular flow. AI can attack both (P1->P5->P6). But the dominant uncertainty is data (regolith ice form, dusty-vacuum friction and adhesion), which only landed missions and low-gravity experiments provide. No catalog family addresses these directly.

bottlenecks.name: ISRU process development and scale-up (oxygen from regolith, water ice, Mars CO2 to propellant)
bottlenecks.description: High-temperature multiphysics (molten-oxide electrochemistry at ~1,600 C, carbothermal reduction, solid-oxide CO2 electrolysis, Sabatier), electrode and crucible life, regolith handling and thermal management, scaled from lab rates to plant rates. Demonstrated: MOXIE peaked at 12 g O2/h on Mars (122 g total, 2021-23); KSC/Lunar Resources LR-1 molten regolith electrolysis produced 0.07 kg O2/h for 9 h from 25 kg of simulant in vacuum (late 2024); NASA/Sierra Space CaRD integrated solar-carbothermal prototype confirmed CO production (Feb 2026); Blue Origin's Air Pioneer MRE reactor extracted oxygen (Jun 2026); OxEon MOMS targets 1-3 kg O2/h plus methane. Targets: ~10 t O2/yr (~1.1 kg/h) at under 30 kW for a lunar plant; ~25 t O2 for a NASA-style Mars ascent vehicle; roughly 1,000 t of methalox per Starship return (general).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mostly expert-scarce, not open: reduced-order multiphysics models with error bounds, model-predictive control, Bayesian optimal experimental design to cut test count. The binding gates are physical: anode and crucible life (endurance tests run 10^3-10^4 hours), test-facility throughput (thermal-vacuum chambers that tolerate molten regolith), surface power, and landing opportunities. AI compresses design iterations, perhaps by 1-2 years in S2, but not endurance or launch.

bottlenecks.name: Life-support reliability and loop closure (physico-chemical and bioregenerative)
bottlenecks.description: Sizing spares and crew maintenance for regenerative ECLSS, raising oxygen and water recovery, and stabilizing bioregenerative loops (microbes, algae, plants, crew). ISS reached 98% water recovery (Brine Processor, Jun 2023), but the last public ECLSS reliability dataset dates from 2004 (ICES 2025). A 2025 Bayesian analysis from ISS data estimates 907 crew-hours of ECLSS maintenance (~45 min/day) and availability 0.9687 for a 1,200-day Mars mission, with the 5th-percentile spares mass equivalent to a 10x MTBF improvement, so uncertainty spans an order of magnitude. MELiSSA's pilot plant has integrated up to four compartments (2025). Artemis II (Apr 1-11, 2026) still had a urine vent line freeze.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Reliability and sparing math is solved in principle (semi-Markov, Bayesian) but hard to scale to system-of-systems, so expert time is the unlock (P1). Bioregenerative stability theory is partly open; family 149 (permanence for weakly reversible mass-action networks, T1) is an idealized building block. Binding: operating hours (a zero-failure demonstration at 95% confidence needs about 3x the target MTBF in unit-hours, general) and long closed-loop tests.

bottlenecks.name: Crew health and radiation risk
bottlenecks.description: Estimating cancer, cardiovascular and CNS risk from galactic cosmic rays and solar particle events, and providing Earth-independent medical care. NASA's career limit is 600 mSv effective dose; a 2026 Space Weather study finds Mars missions on minimum-energy trajectories stay below 1,000 mSv in active solar cycles but stay below 600 mSv only near solar maximum or on faster transfers. Dose transport is well validated (blind Artemis I comparisons, 2025); biological risk per unit dose is not (high-LET radiobiology, dose-rate effects, transfer from terrestrial epidemiology).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Small. Transport and dosimetry math is mature. Risk-model uncertainty is data-bound: no human high-LET cohort exists and animal cancer studies take years per cohort. AI helps assemble mechanistic models and medical decision support (P1), not the biology.

bottlenecks.name: Operations planning and logistics under delay (scheduling, task allocation, comm windows, power)
bottlenecks.description: Scheduling dozens of robots and crew tasks around two-week lunar nights, crater-rim comm blackouts, battery limits and launch cadence; NASA's Moon Base plan (Mar 2026) targets up to 30 robotic landings from 2027 and crewed landings every six months, which multiplies the number of assets per operator.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Largely expert-scarce custom planning and optimization (P1). The catalog's hardness results (102 UGC, 125 k-median 1+2/e, T3; 124 three-machine scheduling, 110 k-server, 111 prophet inequalities, T1) set ceilings (P3) but rarely bind on small, structured real instances.

auton.scenario_contrast: S1 (Plateau): research-grade math reaches outside teams around 2027-28 and diffuses slowly. The domain's expert-scarce work (reliability models, reactor ROMs, synthesized planners) becomes routine around 2029-2030; open problems (frictional contact, granular well-posedness) stay open; proof-carrying autonomy first flies around 2031. 13 of 30 nodes have an earliest year of 2031 or sooner, mostly operations planning, analysis tools and the first lunar oxygen demo. S2 (Exponential, base case): the cognitive clock collapses. Every tier 1-2 node and most tier 3-4 nodes in this domain arrive in 2027-2029, including credible attacks on contact mechanics and granular rheology. The tree then hits a physical wall: polar ground-truth data (2028), CLPS landing success, the 2030 lunar fission reactor, Mars windows (late 2028, early 2031), endurance tests for anodes, and reliability hours for life support. Results: routine AI-planned operations (2027), proof-carrying lunar autonomy (2028 tool, 2029 flight), a 10x operator-productivity gain (2029), first lunar oxygen (2029), crew-optional lunar operations (2031); tonne-scale lunar oxygen, Mars-class life support, narrower radiation risk and Mars propellant plants stay beyond 2031. 25 of 30 nodes have an earliest year of 2031 or sooner (earliest year, not likelihood: several carry Low or Medium bands). S3 (Recursive): cognitive nodes move about a year earlier, and autonomous labs compress experiment-gated nodes (anode materials, bioregenerative tests, many parallel reliability units) by about a year. Launch windows, landing reliability, surface power, biology (cancer latency, crop cycles) and endurance hours do not compress, so S3 adds only 3 nodes over S2 (narrower radiation risk, tonne-per-year lunar oxygen and Mars-class life support, all at the 2031 edge with Low-to-Medium bands; 28 of 30) and leaves the Mars propellant plant and the Mars logistics outcome beyond 2031.
key_insights: This domain's math is overwhelmingly bespoke and 'solved in principle but expert-scarce' (autonomy verification, reliability and sparing, reactor models, mission planning). On-demand research math matters far more here than any catalog theorem; only 104, 149 and the hardness family (102, 124, 125, 110, 111) touch the domain, all through ceilings (P3) or model confidence (P5).

The capability channel has already reached flight operations: Perseverance's AI-planned drives (Dec 2025) show the first-order effect is cognitive and near-term. What AI math adds is the second step, machine-checked plans and proof-carrying autonomy, which makes AI planning acceptable without line-by-line human review (S2: tool 2028, first lunar flight 2029).

Two genuinely open problems with real engineering leverage are not in the catalog: well-posedness and convergence for frictional multi-contact dynamics (the sim-to-real gap for grasping, docking and assembly) and well-posed continuum models for dense granular flow (excavation and construction). Negative answers would be as useful as positive ones, because they mark where simulation results are artifacts.

ISRU is a hardware, power and test problem with a vast scale gap: 0.07 kg O2/h (MRE, 2024) and 12 g/h (MOXIE) versus ~1.1 kg/h for a 10 t/yr lunar plant and ~65 kg O2/h for a Starship return. AI compresses design iterations by perhaps a year; it cannot compress anode endurance tests (10^4 h), test-facility throughput, surface power (fission arrives 2030) or Mars windows.

The data gate binds the regolith chain: excavation energy varies 52x across plausible polar ice forms. No model, however well-posed, can be validated before a polar lander digs (about 2028 in every scenario, with VIPER exposed to the New Glenn pad loss).

Life-support reliability is demonstrated in operating hours: a zero-failure 95%-confidence demonstration needs about 3x the target MTBF in unit-hours. Better math narrows the order-of-magnitude MTBF uncertainty in today's sparing estimates, but ISS (the only long-duration testbed, retiring around 2030-2032) sets the clock.
Radiation and biology are near-nil effects: dose transport is already accurate, the 600 mSv limit is policy, and risk-per-dose uncertainty needs in-vivo data on multi-year cycles.

The strategic five-year outcome is operational, not physical: roughly tenfold more robot work per operator and, under S2, crew-optional lunar base operations by about 2031. NASA's pivot from Gateway to a surface Moon Base (Mar 2026; 30 CLPS landings from 2027) is the demand signal that makes this the place AI math shows up first.
nil_effects: Mars launch windows (late 2028/early 2029, early 2031) and transit times: orbital mechanics, not mathematics, limit Mars ISRU and outpost chains to at most two attempts in the horizon.
Starship-scale Mars propellant production before 2032: needs landed megawatt-class power, ice mining and a sub-scale demo first; Speculative in every scenario.
Deep-space radiation dose rate and the mass needed to shield against it: physics fixes these; the 600 mSv career limit is policy and unlikely to move by 2031.
Biological clocks: crop growth cycles (60-120 days), animal-model cancer latency (years) and crew physiology studies cannot be accelerated by AI mathematics.
Lunar night (~14 Earth days), polar thermal extremes and abrasive, electrostatically clinging dust: environmental constraints on surface robots that set duty cycles regardless of autonomy quality.
Endurance and reliability evidence: anode life tests (10^3-10^4 h) and ECLSS MTBF demonstrations (about 3x MTBF in unit-hours at 95% confidence) run on calendar time.
Lander success rates and lift capacity (e.g. the May 2026 New Glenn pad loss delaying Blue Moon Mk1 and VIPER): physical and industrial gates on every surface demo.

Galactic speedups (107 matrix multiplication omega <= 9/4, 130 FFT below n log n) give no onboard-compute or autonomy speedup; 139 (log-concave sampling with d^epsilon queries, T3) and 140 (memory-sample lower bounds, T3) are theoretical ceilings for onboard estimation and learning with no practical change, since real posteriors are rarely well-conditioned log-concave and flight processors are not at those asymptotic limits.

signposts.event: Any lab makes research-grade math capability publicly purchasable (API or product) by mid-2027.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the S2 timing for cap-research-math-public, pulling the synthesis, reliability-UQ and contact-mechanics nodes into 2027-2028; if access slips past 2028, shift those nodes toward S1.

signposts.event: Independent Comparator runs on openai/math families 104 (RandomizedMeanPayoff.lean), 149 (MassAction.lean) and 124 (ThreeMachine.lean).
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves those premises to T4 and removes the 'conditional' label from the planning-ceilings and bioregenerative nodes; also resolves whether 149 and 124 are T1 (per the overview) or T3 (per lean/docs).

signposts.event: CADRE operates on the Moon after IM-3 (late 2026 or 2027) and reports leader election and task re-allocation results.
signposts.what_it_changes: Establishes the multi-robot autonomy baseline that proof-carrying autonomy improves on; a failure for software reasons would raise the value of verified autonomy.

signposts.event: JPL reports routine or kilometer-scale AI-planned drives, or a Moon Base robot operator adopts AI planning with formal plan checking.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms auton-ai-planned-ops-routine (2027) and the surface-productivity outcome; absence by end-2027 pushes both a year later.

signposts.event: A CLPS, LTV or NASA FFR provider publishes formally synthesized or proof-carrying autonomy artifacts.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the P2 bridge for uncrewed surface robots on the S2 schedule (tool 2028, flight 2029).

signposts.event: Blue Moon Mk1/VIPER launch date after the LC-36 rebuild, and Chang'e-7 or other polar landers returning geotechnical data.
signposts.what_it_changes: Sets the date of the icy-regolith ground-truth node, which gates the whole excavation chain in every scenario.

signposts.event: An ISRU oxygen payload is manifested on a named 2027-2029 CLPS flight; an MRE or carbothermal run passes 1,000 h.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms or delays first oxygen on the Moon (S2 2029) and the anode-life node; no manifest by end-2027 pushes the demo past 2030.

signposts.event: NASA releases updated ISS ECLSS failure data, or Exploration ECLSS units report multi-year ISS run time.
signposts.what_it_changes: Unlocks the data gate for the reliability-UQ node and starts the operating-hours clock for Mars-class life support.

signposts.event: AI-produced results on frictional contact well-posedness or granular rheology appear in mechanics or applied-math venues.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms that the capability reaches applied PDE and nonsmooth mechanics (S2); absence through 2028 suggests the plateau scenario for applied math.

signposts.event: Starship ship-to-ship propellant transfer (expected early 2027) and any SpaceX 2028 Mars cargo manifest that includes ISRU hardware.
signposts.what_it_changes: Determines whether the Mars ISRU demo node is reachable in the 2028-29 window at all; without a manifest by 2028 it moves beyond 2031 in every scenario.

capability.domain: The capability curve itself: trajectory, access and gates

bottlenecks.name: Physical clock: test, fabrication, qualification, launch
bottlenecks.description: Once a math or design result exists, flown change waits on hardware build, integration and test, qualification campaigns (thermal-vacuum, vibration, life tests), supplier lead times (rad-hard parts often 12-24+ months) and launch slots. These sit on the critical path of every space program and compress little under any AI scenario (general).
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~40% of the lag between 'AI can do the math' and 'a space system behaves differently' (judgment, general)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Limited. Optimal experiment design, better first-pass designs and fewer design escapes can cut test iterations and rework (estimated 10-30%, general), but cannot shorten a 10,000-hour thruster life test, a creep test or a fab cycle.

bottlenecks.name: Access and release governance
bottlenecks.description: The strongest math models are internal or restricted. GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld for deception on Sep 29, 2026; Anthropic's Mythos tier is restricted; US pre-release review adds roughly 12-30 days (GPT-5.6 cleared a 12-day White House gate, Jul 2026); the DC Circuit upheld the DoD 'supply chain risk' designation of Anthropic on Sep 25, 2026; ITAR/CUI and classified data need accredited environments.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: None directly; this is policy, safety and accreditation. Competition among at least four labs and open-weight followers erodes it over time.

bottlenecks.name: Trust and verification bandwidth
bottlenecks.description: Machine checking is cheap but not free (a local Comparator run hit 7 GiB memory caps on two of three openai/math targets); statement audits and human understanding do not scale (722 manuscripts at once; nothing above T3). Engineers will not use a result in a review they cannot trust.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High: autoformalization plus independent AI auditors can cut audit cost from expert-weeks to hours, leaving the human judgment of 'is this the right property'.

bottlenecks.name: Formal infrastructure for applied math
bottlenecks.description: Lean/Mathlib is strong in discrete math and weak in PDE (3 of 16 families formalized), dynamics (2 of 12), numerical analysis and floating point. Applied results therefore stay at T1 and cannot feed formal verification (P2).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High: agents can write library code at scale (FLT: 13.4M lines). The gate is abstraction design and community review bandwidth, not proof labor.

bottlenecks.name: Certification and regulatory acceptance
bottlenecks.description: DO-178C/DO-333/DO-330, NASA software assurance and ECSS give credit to formal methods but not to AI-produced proofs or AI tools; standards change on 5-10 year cycles (general).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Moderate: AI drafts specifications and certification evidence and can be treated as an untrusted generator behind a qualified checker; acceptance remains institutional.

bottlenecks.name: Data for learned and theory models
bottlenecks.description: Space physics is data-poor: one Sun with ~15 years of SDO imagery, few hypersonic flights, sparse thermosphere density data. The weather playbook (ERA5's 40+ years of reanalysis) does not transfer where data cannot be simulated.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low-moderate: physics priors, provable identifiability limits and optimal sensor placement; AI cannot create flight data.

bottlenecks.name: Compute and price
bottlenecks.description: Not binding for math: a research-grade result costs ~$200 in tokens (Astra's ten August results ~$2,000 at API rates). Binding for the recursive scenario and for training large emulators (compute stock grows 3.4x/yr; GW-scale sites take ~2.1 years).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Not applicable; this is capital, fabs and power.

capability.scenario_contrast: S1 Plateau (task-horizon doubling every 12-18 months): the Oct-2026 internal level reaches outside teams in 2028, research-grade applied math in 2029, multiphysics design optimization in 2030, applied Lean libraries in 2030; validated physics theory and regulator credit for AI proofs slip past 2031. By 2031 the autonomous horizon is ~4 work-months (~16x today). Space effects are P1 consulting-style analysis, P3 ceilings and AlphaEvolve-type heuristics; new programs run 10-20% shorter. S2 Exponential, base case (doubling every 6-9 months, matching METR's ~7-month long-run trend): public access in 2027, applied math in 2027, applied Lean libraries and verified numerics in 2028, design optimization and autonomous labs at scale in 2028, physics theory in 2029, first certification credit in 2030; horizon ~1 work-month by end-2027 and several work-years by 2031. The cognitive clock runs 10-50x faster by 2029, but fabrication, test, qualification and launch compress only 1.1-1.3x, so new programs are ~30-40% shorter and flown evidence appears only in 2030-31. S3 Recursive (S2 until 2028, then ~3-month doubling once AI speeds its own R&D 3x or more): cognitive work is near-free from ~2029 and closed-loop labs compress materials and chemistry iteration, but launch, flight test, qualification and fabs still bind; programs are at most ~50% shorter, and the recursion itself is bounded by compute supply (stock ~3.4x/yr, ~2.1 years per GW-scale site). Across all three, the biggest difference is how many design iterations and how much verification each program buys - not launch cadence, propellant chemistry or the physics of space.
key_insights: Two clocks: under S2 the cognitive clock doubles every 6-9 months while the physical clock (test, fab, qualification, launch) barely moves, so Amdahl's law caps schedule compression for new space programs at ~30-40% (S2) and ~50% (S3), not 10x.

Price is not the gate: a research-grade result costs ~$200 in tokens (Astra's ten August results ~$2,000), so 1,000 hard problems a year cost less than one engineer. The gates are access, trust and integration.

Public models already do research math at the easy end (GPT-6 Astra: 106 ErdosBench open problems, first ever FrontierMath Erdos solves), so the P1 channel opens in late 2026 for ordinary engineering math; catalog-level capability is 6-12 months away under S2.

Access is governed, not just priced: Astra went from reveal to public in ~5 weeks, but GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld, Anthropic's top tier is restricted, US pre-release review adds 12-30 days, and the DoD bars contractors from using Claude on defense work - removing the lab with the only Comparator-checked mega-formalization from defense-space workflows.

For space, ITAR/CUI and classified accreditation is the binding access gate for real engineering data; open-weight models at research level (2028 in S2) would bypass it for both US firms and adversaries.

Formal infrastructure for continuous math is the gating infrastructure for the formal-verification bridge: PDE 3 of 16 and dynamics 2 of 12 families formalized versus logic 5 of 6; applied Lean libraries arrive ~2028 in S2 and verified numerics alongside.

Verification has moved from proving to auditing: a laptop-class Comparator run of three openai/math targets passed one and ran out of memory on two, and the statement gaps found so far are scope gaps - cheap AI-assisted statement audits are the unlock that lets engineers use AI results in reviews.
The weather playbook transfers first where training data can be simulated (CFD, structures, thermal) and last where nature is the only source (space weather from one Sun, rare hypersonic flights).

Practical algorithm discovery (AlphaEvolve: 0.7% of Google's fleet compute recovered, generally available since Jul 2026) and hardness ceilings act within the window; the catalog's galactic speedups (107, 130) never will.

The shortest path from AI math to flown hardware runs through firms that own both a frontier lab and the launch manifest (SpaceX/SpaceXAI), then new entrants without legacy processes; agencies and crewed programs come last because of qualification.
nil_effects: Launch physics: the rocket equation, propellant energy density and structural mass fractions do not change; AI design optimization yields single-digit percent gains in launch performance.
Durations set by physics or time: thermal-vacuum and vibration campaigns, 10,000+ hour electric-thruster life tests, creep and oxidation tests, battery cycling, radiation beam tests.
Fabrication and supply-chain lead times (rad-hard parts often 12-24+ months, wafer runs, large forgings) and launch-manifest slots, even under S3.
Galactic speedups (107 matrix-multiplication exponent, 130 FFT below n log n) give no practical gain to onboard or ground compute.
Positive well-posedness results (e.g. 362 Vlasov-Maxwell, T3) change confidence in plasma codes, not the codes or thruster performance.
Deployed cryptography: nothing in the release (279 is theory only) weakens space-link crypto; the capability is a watch item, not an effect.
Data scarcity in space physics: one Sun with ~15 years of SDO data, few extreme storms, few instrumented hypersonic flights; AI cannot create flight data.
Standards cycles: DO-178C-class standards turn over on 5-10+ year cycles, so certification credit for AI proofs stays capped at Medium likelihood by 2031 in every scenario.
Compute for the recursive scenario: fabs, HBM, packaging and power (GW-scale sites ~2.1 years) bound S3's own acceleration.
Price of math: already near zero relative to engineering labor, so further price falls change little.

signposts.event: Independent Comparator run plus statement audit published for a headline family (102 Unique Games or 362 Vlasov-Maxwell) by Hexagon, Buzzard's group or similar, Q4 2026 to Q1 2027.
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves those results to T4 and validates the pipeline; a failed audit would downgrade every T3 premise in the tree and lengthen trust timelines.

comms.domain: Communications, networking, cryptography and constellation operations

bottlenecks.name: Spectrum sharing and interference compliance
bottlenecks.description: More than 10,000 commercial communications satellites operate in LEO with 50,000+ more planned (Roberts, arXiv 2609.36122). Each new system has to show that it does not degrade GSO networks, earlier NGSO systems, terrestrial users or radio astronomy beyond set limits. In 2026 the FCC moved from fixed EPFD power masks to performance-based criteria: no more than 3% time-weighted throughput degradation and 0.4% (NGSO-NGSO) or 0.1% (proposed NGSO-GSO) added unavailability, judged over an orbital simulation (FCC 24-117; FCC vote of Apr 30 2026 per 33FG). ITU Article 22 EPFD limits still apply internationally. Direct-to-device adds out-of-band and harmonic problems: the 2620 MHz D2D downlink's second harmonic already causes at least 59% geodetic-VLBI data loss (arXiv 2608.11659).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mostly expert-scarce rather than open. Needed: certified (interval or proof-backed) bounds on aggregate interference and time-percentage statistics instead of Monte Carlo tails; beam-cell assignment under interference budgets (NP-hard in general, provably near-optimal in special cases, e.g. SkyShare arXiv 2609.00821); game-theoretic coexistence with convergence and uniqueness proofs (arXiv 2609.38935). Genuinely open: tight guarantees for coexistence among three or more equal-priority operators. No catalog family applies; the unlock is capability (P1) plus certified numerics (P2).

bottlenecks.name: Mesh routing, topology and radio resource management at 10,000+ satellites
bottlenecks.description: Laser inter-satellite meshes with 3-4 terminals per satellite, topology that changes continuously, and user-beam handovers about every 15 s (Roberts). The joint problem of pairing laser terminals, routing traffic and allocating rates is NP-hard per topology snapshot (arXiv 2601.21914). Academic designs report 35-145% throughput gains over non-joint baselines and up to 2.3x capacity over +Grid on real Starlink data (arXiv 2602.07756), but operator practice is proprietary and the baselines are naive.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Expert-scarce. Because exact optimality is NP-hard, the useful product is a certificate: a dual bound that says how far the running solution is from optimal, plus decompositions with proven convergence. Agents can also write machine-checked proofs that routing and handover logic is loop-free and converges under churn (P2). Catalog ties are ceilings (102 UGC, T3; 117 sparsest-cut hardness, T1) and a matching speedup (120, T1) that does not matter at this scale.

bottlenecks.name: Tasking, scheduling and ground segment
bottlenecks.description: Earth-observation tasking, downlink and ground-station-as-a-service scheduling, ground-station siting, and optical-ground-station weather diversity. Benchmarks now reach 1,000 satellites and 10,000 requests (EOS-Bench, arXiv 2604.25782); exact integer programming for ground-station selection stops scaling before a ~100-satellite fleet (arXiv 2510.03438). For optical ground networks the bottleneck has moved from peak rate to repeatable service under weather, acquisition and scheduling constraints (Turyshev, arXiv 2606.23711).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Expert-scarce, with ceilings newly proven. Teams need bespoke formulations of each mission's constraints, exact solvers on structured instances and certified-gap heuristics. The catalog adds hardness ceilings (102 T3; 117 and 125 headlines T1), an exact three-machine precedence scheduler (124, T1) and online guarantees (110, 111, T1). These act through P3 within months; most value is P1.

bottlenecks.name: Physical layer: optical links, channel coding and direct-to-device link budgets
bottlenecks.description: Optical links are now proven at 200 Gbps from LEO (TBIRD), 1.8 Gbps operational GEO relay (EDRS) and 267 Mbps from about 19 million miles (DSOC, ended Sep 2 2025). Deep-space optical links are photon-starved and use PPM with superconducting single-photon detectors. Direct-to-device links close with handset antennas and depend on spectrum, aperture and power (Starlink's +10 dB waiver, Mar 2025). Coding is near capacity for long blocks; short packets (D2D signaling, IoT, telecommand) still lose fractions of a dB to finite-blocklength limits.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mixed. Long-block coding is solved; short-block code and decoder design is expert-scarce, and LLM-guided search already finds record codes (arXiv 2609.37056). Receivers that beat photon counting (joint detection approaching the Holevo limit) are genuinely open physics-engineering theory. Catalog: 273 (entropy photon-number inequality, T1) proves multi-user optical capacity limits, a confidence result that changes no hardware.

bottlenecks.name: Security: post-quantum migration, crypto-agility and cryptanalysis risk
bottlenecks.description: Satellites live 15 years in GEO; NIST IR 8547 (draft, Nov 2024) deprecates 112-bit RSA/ECC by 2030 and disallows all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms by 2035. Post-quantum authentication is expensive on constrained, high-latency links (arXiv 2607.23007). Resource estimates for breaking RSA-2048 fell to under a million noisy qubits (Gidney, May 2025). AI cryptanalysis is real but so far hits only non-standard constructions (arXiv 2608.21986).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Implementation and protocol verification is expert-scarce: machine-checked correctness, constant-time and masking proofs for PQC on space processors, and proofs of key-management and in-orbit update protocols (P2). Lattice hardness itself is a genuinely open question; nothing in the release touches it (tl-position-5), and 279 and 138 are not attacks. The capability pointed at cryptanalysis is the watch item.

bottlenecks.name: Quantum communications from space
bottlenecks.description: Satellite QKD is moving from Micius-class demos to small payloads and portable ground stations: Jinan-1's 23 kg payload delivered up to 1.07 Mbit of secure key per pass and a China-South Africa key over 12,900 km (Nature, Mar 2025). Eagle-1 launches late 2026/early 2027 for three years of validation (ESA). Short passes make finite-key effects and device imperfections the limiting theory problem; loss, background light and weather the limiting physics.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Finite-key security proofs that include real device flaws and non-IID signals are partly open and highly specialized (arXiv 2606.29943, 2605.12984), so on-demand help plus formalization (Lean-QIT, arXiv 2607.09632) is the unlock. Catalog: 276 (T3), 266 and 272 (T1) settle ceilings and change no flown protocol.

comms.scenario_contrast: S1 (plateau, analyst default): the research-grade model stays internal until about 2027-28. Communications gets the fast items first: proven ceilings for partitioning, siting and scheduling (102 at T3, others conditional) take effect in 2027 once someone runs Comparator, and AI cryptanalysis audits of non-standard protocols are already happening. Verified post-quantum code for space processors arrives around 2028, certified network optimization around 2028, certified interference showings and verified control-plane software around 2029-30. Nothing physical moves early. S2 (exponential, base case): with task horizons doubling every 6-9 months and public access within 6-12 months, every cognitive node in this tree moves 1-2 years earlier. Certified mesh optimization, verified PQC and code design arrive in 2027; certified interference bounds, verified routing and finite-key QKD proofs in 2028; design optimizers and receiver theory in 2029. Operators can adopt software nodes almost immediately, so tier-6 software outcomes (certified mesh operations in 2028, coexistence scheduling in 2029) follow closely. Physical and institutional gates do not compress: launch and integration lead times, telescope and ground-station capital, spectrum rights and the ITU conference calendar (no international sharing change before about 2031), security certification and procurement cycles (crypto-agile fleets about 2029-30 in both S1 and S2), and the QKD satellites already being built (multi-node demos 2028 in every scenario). S3 (recursive): cognition is near-free from 2028, so design tools and receiver theory land a year earlier still, but tier-5 to tier-7 nodes move by at most a year. The one place S3 changes the risk picture is cryptography, in both directions: cheaper cryptanalysis raises the small chance of a lattice weakness being found (Low rather than Speculative), and AI-accelerated quantum hardware design raises the chance of a code-breaking quantum computer before 2031 from Speculative to Low. Across scenarios the gap between cognitive and physical clocks widens: by 2029 under S2, the math for denser, provably compliant, provably secure constellations will be ahead of the satellites, spectrum rules and certifiers that would use it.
key_insights: The math communications actually spends effort on is bespoke and expert-scarce, not famous: interference statistics, routing and resource-allocation optimization, scheduling, short-block coding, and protocol and crypto verification. The catalog touches it mainly through ceilings (UGC, sparsest cut, k-median) and through quantum and optical capacity theorems that confirm what engineers already assumed (tl-position-4, fc-position-2).

Regulators just turned spectrum compliance into a math problem. The FCC's 2026 move from fixed EPFD masks to performance-based criteria (3% throughput degradation, 0.1-0.4% added unavailability, judged by simulation) makes certified interference bounds the highest-leverage communications application of AI mathematics. Their adoption is limited by operators and regulators accepting them, not by the math.

Because joint laser-terminal pairing, routing and rate allocation is NP-hard per snapshot, the deliverable is a certificate (a proven optimality gap), not an optimum. Certificates convert 'should we buy more lasers or write better software?' into a measured number. Realistic gains over operators' current practice are probably 5-20% capacity (judgment), small next to the 10x V3 hardware step and the regulatory lift.

Nothing in the release weakens deployed or post-quantum cryptography: 279 does not reduce qubit budgets, and 138 does not touch lattices. The risk is the capability. AI agents already broke eight non-standard published constructions in Aug 2026. For satellites launched from 2027 that will operate into the 2040s, the right response is crypto-agility with machine-checked update paths, which is itself something AI makes cheap.

Statement gaps matter even in the 'solid' families. For 117 the Lean main result is the SDP integrality gap, not the NP-hardness headline. For 125 Lean covers a companion recovery result, not the 1+2/e algorithm. For 104 Lean covers a randomized version. Planners should treat those headlines as T1 until audited.

Optical and quantum link performance through 2031 is set by apertures, detectors, weather, pass geometry and launches. Capacity theorems (273 conditional, 276) change confidence, not data rates. The genuinely open, AI-relevant optical problem is receivers that beat photon counting, and its first payoff is a ground demo around 2030 under S2.

Under S2 the cognitive nodes move 1-2 years earlier and software-only outcomes follow within a year, but every node gated by launch, capital, spectrum rights, the ITU calendar or certification moves by a year at most. The exponential shows up as a growing gap between what can be proven and what can be flown, licensed or certified.

Fastest effects (2027 in all scenarios): proven ceilings for tasking and partitioning (P3), and AI audits of bespoke satellite security protocols (P1->P3). Slowest: an international spectrum regime change and certified operational QKD service, neither plausible before about 2030-31 in any scenario.
nil_effects: Deployed cryptography (AES, RSA, ECC, ML-KEM, ML-DSA) is unaffected by the catalog. 279 makes Shor's algorithm exact in theory but does not cut qubit or error-correction budgets, and 138 (Subset Sum in 2^0.49n worst case) is irrelevant to lattice parameters (tl-position-5).

The release's galactic speedups (FFT below n log n, matrix-multiplication exponent ≤ 9/4) give no onboard signal-processing or beamforming speedup (tl-position-1); 120's almost-linear matching is irrelevant at constellation scale, where classical matching already runs in milliseconds.

Link budgets and data rates do not change through 2031 because of any theorem. Optical rates are set by aperture, detector efficiency, pointing and weather; D2D rates by spectrum holdings, satellite aperture and power; deep-space optical by terminals already built (DSOC ended Sep 2025).
Spectrum allocations and the ITU conference calendar: no amount of cognition moves WRC decisions, and international EPFD limits stay in force at least until the conference after WRC-27 (general).
Satellite QKD key rates and coverage are set by loss, background light, clouds and pass duration. 266, 272 and 276 change no protocol on Eagle-1, SpeQtre, QEYSSat or Jinan-class payloads.
Number of laser terminals per satellite, acquisition times and launch cadence, which set mesh capacity more than routing software does.
Quantum optimization for satellite scheduling: 281 (QAOA reaches the SK optimum when size goes to infinity before depth) does not imply any near-term quantum advantage for tasking or routing.
The 2030 and 2035 post-quantum migration deadlines are set by NIST and NSA, not by AI mathematics. AI changes the cost of doing the migration verifiably, not its date.

signposts.what_it_changes: Moves the ceilings and the 276 capacity result from T3 to T4; confirms the P3 nodes for 2027 and lets planners cite the theorems without caveat. A failed audit would downgrade comms-hardness-ceilings-settled and everything that relies on it.

signposts.event: A research-grade math model becomes available to outside engineering teams at a usable price (any lab).
signposts.what_it_changes: Starts the P1 clock for comms-certified-network-optimization, comms-code-design-on-demand and comms-hardness-aware-tasking. Before mid-2027 it confirms S2 timing; slipping past 2028 confirms S1.

signposts.event: An FCC filing, ITU-R WP4A contribution or bilateral coordination agreement that cites machine-checked or interval-certified interference bounds.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms comms-certified-interference-bounds and pulls the D2D coexistence and constellation-design nodes forward a year. Absence through 2028 under public model access would point to regulatory culture, not math, as the gate.

signposts.event: An AI-produced cryptanalysis result against a NIST-standardized scheme or its parameters (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, HQC), or expert confirmation or refutation of the Luo ML-KEM quantum-attack claim (arXiv 2605.17412).
signposts.what_it_changes: A confirmed result moves comms-lattice-weakness from watch item to active and makes crypto-agility an urgent retrofit for satellites in build. A refutation leaves the bands as stated.

signposts.event: Eagle-1 launch and first key-exchange campaign, plus any published security analysis with machine-checked components.
signposts.what_it_changes: Anchors the physical QKD timeline (comms-space-qkd-network-demo, 2028) and tests whether formal finite-key proofs become part of space QKD evaluation (comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs).

signposts.event: A verified PQC library for a radiation-hardened processor or space FPGA, or a CCSDS space-link-security profile with hybrid or post-quantum options.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms comms-pq-verified-implementations and starts the clock on crypto-agile architectures and the verified-command-link flight demo.

signposts.event: A mega-constellation operator or SDA disclosing optimality-gap metrics or formal verification of routing or handover software.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms comms-certified-mesh-operations and gives the first observable data on how much capacity software leaves on the table versus hardware.

signposts.event: Quantum-hardware milestones: logical qubits at scale below threshold, or a published RSA-2048 resource estimate under 100,000 noisy qubits.
signposts.what_it_changes: Raises comms-crqc-before-2031 and the urgency of PQ migration for legacy fleets, independently of AI mathematics.

frontier.domain: The remaining unsolved mathematics that matters downstream, and the order AI cracks it

bottlenecks.name: Turbulence, transition and reacting-flow fidelity
bottlenecks.description: Wall heat flux, combustion stability, plume heating, reentry wakes and separation all rest on turbulence and transition closures that are calibrated, not derived. CFD Vision 2030 named turbulence, transition and separated flow as the leading gap (general). The pure-math frontier here (Navier-Stokes regularity, Onsager/anomalous dissipation, Kolmogorov scaling) is famous but far from the engineering error, which is model-form error in wall-bounded, compressible, reacting flows.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~25% of the mathematical/modeling effort behind space vehicles (judgment, general)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low for the famous problems (frontier-ns-unforced, frontier-turbulence-rigorous are P5 with nil engineering effect); medium for the less famous ones that actually block design: nonuniqueness maps that tell V&V where the equation is at fault (frontier-nonuniqueness-map) and derivatives of chaotic averages that would make gradient design of unsteady flows possible (frontier-chaos-linear-response). Genuinely open research; data binds once theory is cheap.

bottlenecks.name: Verification, validation and uncertainty quantification
bottlenecks.description: Solution verification (grid studies), credibility assessment under NASA-STD-7009B (Mar 2024), margins, rare-event probabilities (conjunction Pc, structural failure at 1e-6) and model-form error. Practice uses estimated, not guaranteed, numerical error, and Gaussian or asymptotic statistics at scale (Starlink alone performed 144,000+ collision-avoidance maneuvers in six months per 33FG, Oct 2025).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High. Mostly solved in principle but expert-scarce: guaranteed a posteriori bounds, certified rare-event estimators, verified stiff integrators (frontier-certified-pde-error, frontier-rare-event-certified, frontier-stiff-certified). On-demand AI is the unlock; the residual limit is data, since no estimator beats the information content of tests.

bottlenecks.name: Optimization, control and scheduling with guarantees
bottlenecks.description: Trajectory optimization, guidance laws, reachability for collision avoidance, constellation tasking and ground-station siting, and verification of learned components. Engineers want certificates (stability, optimality gap, safety envelope) for bespoke problems, plus to know what is impossible.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High. Ceilings act now (frontier-approx-ceilings, frontier-nn-verification-complexity, P3); HJB guarantees and global-optimality certificates are mostly expert-scarce rather than open (frontier-hjb-guarantees, frontier-scalable-global-certificates).

bottlenecks.name: Kinetic and plasma models (rarefied flow, electric propulsion, space weather)
bottlenecks.description: Boltzmann/DSMC for rarefied reentry and plumes, Vlasov/Landau kinetics for thrusters and the magnetosphere, MHD for space weather. Well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Boltzmann/Landau equations, general Landau damping and 3D MHD regularity are open; closures (anomalous transport) are the engineering bottleneck.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium. The open well-posedness problems sit at the difficulty level that fell in Sep-Oct 2026 (362 Vlasov-Maxwell, T3), so they likely fall first (frontier-kinetic-global-regularity, frontier-landau-damping-general, frontier-mhd-wellposedness) but act through P5 (confidence). Quantitative rates and constants are the useful by-product.

bottlenecks.name: Long-term dynamics (n-body, cislunar, debris)
bottlenecks.description: Mission design runs on numerical propagation; rigorous stability and transport bounds exist only for model problems or tiny masses. Arnold diffusion was proven in the planetary 4-body problem only in 2024 (Clarke-Fejoz-Guardia).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low-to-medium. Realistic-constant theorems are open and hard (frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion); finite-horizon certified transport for cislunar orbits is expert-scarce and belongs to the astrodynamics domain.

bottlenecks.name: Materials and chemistry from first principles
bottlenecks.description: DFT accuracy is limited by the unknown exchange-correlation functional; computing it exactly is QMA-hard, and learned functionals (Skala, 2.8 kcal/mol on GMTKN55, Jun 2025) are empirical. Reaction networks for combustion/ablation are stiff and uncertain.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium. Hardness results (275, 278, T1) set limits fast (P3); certified class-restricted functionals (frontier-xc-certified) are data- and compute-gated.

bottlenecks.name: Posing and formal trust of applied problems (the meta-bottleneck)
bottlenecks.description: To use AI mathematics, an engineering question must be stated precisely (assumptions, norms, regimes) and the answer trusted. The Oct 6 problem set was pure-math-skewed (16 PDE + 12 dynamics families of 372, 7.5%); Mathlib lacked Sobolev-space infrastructure as late as Sep 2026 (three groups built their own); formal applied benchmarks score ~35% (StochBench, Sep 2026).
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: <5% of today's effort, but the binding constraint for pathway P2 and for trusting P1 output (judgment)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium-High and fast: agents now build missing library infrastructure cheaply (130k lines of topology in two weeks for ~$100, Urban 2026; Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium formalized in 10 days for $200, Ilin 2026). What stays human: reviewing definitions and statements (frontier-applied-posing).

frontier.scenario_contrast: The frontier compresses along a difficulty ladder, measured from what fell on Oct 6, 2026 (UGC, quasi-RH, forced NS blowup = level D0). Expert-scarce applied problems (HJB guarantees, certified error bars in smooth regimes, rare-event estimators, stiff and transport error theory, inverse-problem stability) sit below D0: capability is not the constraint. Access, posing and formal trust are. Kinetic regularity, general Landau damping, Euler blowup on R^3 and the nonuniqueness map sit at about D0. Unforced Navier-Stokes, realistic-constant n-body stability and linear response for chaotic systems sit 1-3 doublings beyond. Turbulence laws sit 2-4 doublings beyond, plus posing. Certified turbulent CFD needs several open nodes at once, and P vs NP is beyond scaling (barriers). S1 (Plateau): the D0 problems fall 2028-29, applied nodes wait for public access and land 2029-30 (Medium), and everything past D0 except the MHD map slips past 2031; 10 of 26 nodes are >2031. S2 (Exponential, base case): with difficulty doubling every 6-9 months and public access in 2027, D0 problems fall in 2027, applied nodes in 2027-28 (mostly High), unforced NS and the chaos/n-body nodes in 2029, turbulence laws in 2030, and certified turbulent CFD in 2031 (Low). Only P vs NP stays beyond 2031. The median node arrives about 2 years earlier than in S1. S3 (Recursive) moves the hard cognitive nodes another ~1 year (unforced NS 2028, turbulence 2029) and lifts the experiment-gated tool node (gradient design of chaotic systems) to Medium through autonomous validation. P vs NP and a structural break of standardized lattice crypto stay Speculative or Low. Across all three, what binds is not proving but: (1) independent verification bandwidth (Chen-Hou's 2022-23 Euler proof was still drawing clarification notes in Jul-Aug 2026); (2) posing (the Oct release was 7.5% PDE/dynamics by family because that is what was asked); (3) applied formal infrastructure (three groups built their own Sobolev theory in Lean in 2026; StochBench best agent 34.9%); and (4) for anything touching physical closure, data. Shared upstream years assumed (matching the propulsion domain): cap-research-math-internal and cap-autoformalization 2026; cap-research-math-public S1 2028 / S2 2027 / S3 2027; cap-applied-math 2029 / 2027 / 2027; cap-physics-theory >2031 / 2028 / 2028; cap-design-optimization 2030 / 2028 / 2028; infra-verified-numerics 2030 / 2028 / 2028; infra-mathlib-applied 2030 / 2028 / 2027 (this domain's assumption); verif-independent-check 2027 in all three.
key_insights: The key question answered: for the applied problems space engineering actually needs, AI capability is not the binding constraint, since the Oct 2026 model already exceeds what most bespoke engineering math requires. The constraints bind in this order: (1) access (the model is unreleased); (2) posing (stating the engineering question precisely; the Oct release was 7.5% PDE/dynamics by family because that is what was posed); (3) formal trust (applied Mathlib coverage and verified numerics lag informal capability by roughly 2-3 years); (4) data, wherever physics closure is involved. Capability still binds only for the genuinely open frontier: unforced Navier-Stokes, turbulence laws, realistic-constant n-body stability, linear response of chaos, P vs NP.

Strongest evidence on posing vs capability: an agentic workflow formalized a Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium result in 10 days for ~$200 with zero human-written code, and its failures were 'hypothesis creep' and 'definition-alignment bugs' (Ilin, Mar 2026). Proving was cheap; stating correctly was the work.

The Mathlib gap for PDE is real but closing fast. As late as Apr-Sep 2026, three separate groups built their own Sobolev-space infrastructure to formalize elliptic theory, De Giorgi-Nash-Moser and 2D Navier-Stokes Galerkin, and Bedrossian formalized Mouhot-Villani Landau damping (Sep 2026). Agents now build library infrastructure for ~$100 per textbook (Urban 2026), so under S2 the formal layer catches up around 2027-28. The human bottleneck that remains is reviewing statements.

Order of fall under S2: 2027, kinetic regularity (inhomogeneous Boltzmann/Landau), general Landau damping, Euler blowup on R^3, the nonuniqueness map, NN-verification complexity, verified approximation ceilings, plus on-demand HJB guarantees and rare-event estimators; 2028, MHD well-posedness, certified error bars for smooth regimes, certified stiff and transport solvers, inverse-problem stability, scalable global certificates; 2029, unforced Navier-Stokes, realistic n-body constants, linear response of chaos, certified density functionals; 2030, turbulence laws and gradient design of chaotic flows; 2031, certified turbulent CFD (Low); after 2031, P vs NP.

The famous frontier problems have near-zero engineering effect. Navier-Stokes either way, Euler/MHD blowup and billion-year solar-system stability act only through P5 (confidence). What changes engineering are negative results (nonuniqueness tells V&V where the equation, not the code, is at fault) and quantitative by-products (rates, constants, error bounds).

The most consequential unsolved math for space design is not Navier-Stokes but linear response of chaotic averages. It would make gradient-based design of unsteady combustors, nozzles and thrusters possible over thousands of parameters. Under S2 it lands around 2029 (Medium), with tools around 2030 (Low).

Certified error bars split cleanly. Smooth regimes (thermal, structures, laminar) are expert-scarce and land around 2028 under S2 (High). Turbulent and shocked flows may be impossible in pointwise form; nonuniqueness results say what can be certified is statistics plus an explicit selection principle, and model-form error stays data-bound (2031, Low).

Cheap math does not beat data. Demonstrating 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes 230 tests unless a validated physics model carries the extrapolation. Certified rare-event estimators and UQ become routine (High under S2) but move margins only where the models are validated.

Cryptography watch: AI agents broke eight published academic constructions in Aug 2026, while standardized PQC (FIPS 203/204/205) is intact. A structural break by 2031 is Low under S2/S3, but satellites carry hardware crypto for 5-15 years, so crypto agility is the hedge whatever the probability.

The exponential premise has an honest ceiling inside mathematics itself: verification bandwidth. Chen-Hou's computer-assisted Euler proof (2022-23) was still being clarified in Jul-Aug 2026, and no outside Comparator run on openai/math had been reported by Oct 7, 2026. Under S2, proofs arrive faster than the community can certify them unless verification is itself automated (verif-independent-check).
nil_effects: Unforced Navier-Stokes resolved either way: no CFD code, turbulence closure, engine or vehicle changes. Codes already regularize, and any singularity would sit below molecular scales.
Euler and ideal-MHD blowup proofs: no change to space-weather forecast skill, which is limited by solar boundary data (magnetograms) and coronal physics.
Billion-year solar-system stability theorems: no change to mission design, which uses numerical propagation over years with station-keeping margins.
Galactic speedups in the release (matrix-multiplication exponent, sub-n-log-n Fourier transform): no change to onboard compute, signal processing or orbital data centers.
P vs NP: nil either way in practice. P != NP is already assumed by all cryptography and planning software.
Radiation dose accuracy: already validated blind on Artemis I. The remaining error is nuclear cross sections and radiobiology, not transport mathematics.

Reliability demonstration: test counts for zero-failure demonstrations (230 tests for 0.99 at 90% confidence) do not shrink because of mathematics alone. Only validated physics models can stand in for tests.
Density functionals: hardness results (275, 278, conditional) mean no universal efficient functional, so materials programs still need experiments and expensive reference calculations.
Deployed cryptography: nothing in the release weakens RSA, elliptic-curve or standardized post-quantum schemes.
Physical clocks: launch cadence, test-stand time, qualification campaigns and certification timelines are untouched by any frontier theorem in any scenario.

signposts.event: First independent Comparator run plus statement audit on openai/math families (especially 102, 362) or on the Sep 8 forced Navier-Stokes proof, by Hexagon, Buzzard's group or another outside party
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves premises from T3 to T4 and raises the bands of frontier-approx-ceilings and frontier-optical-quantum-capacity. A failure would push every frontier node about a year later and reprice the 245 unformalized families.

signposts.event: A Lean- or interval-verified proof of smooth Euler blowup on R^3 (2027 under S2)
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the S2 pace on the PDE frontier and unlocks frontier-ns-unforced and the MHD blowup question. If nothing appears by end-2028, shift toward S1.

signposts.event: A lab claims unforced Navier-Stokes blowup or regularity (S2: about 2029; S3: about 2028)
signposts.what_it_changes: The clearest test of the exponential premise in this domain. Its engineering effect stays nil, and the paper should say so in advance.

signposts.event: A lab or public model produces 20+ applied-math families (PDE estimates, numerics with certified bounds, UQ, control) in one release
signposts.what_it_changes: Tests the posing hypothesis. If applied families appear as soon as they are posed, capability was never the constraint for applied math, and frontier-applied-posing plus the tier-2 nodes move up a year.

signposts.event: Mathlib merges Sobolev spaces, distributions and basic elliptic/parabolic theory, and applied formal benchmarks (CAM-Bench, StochBench) exceed 80% agent solve rates
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms infra-mathlib-applied on the S2 track (2028), opening P2 verification for numerics and control proofs.

signposts.event: Research-grade math model publicly available to outside teams (OpenAI or a rival) with pricing
signposts.what_it_changes: Turns on P1 for all tier-2 frontier nodes; the S1-to-S2 difference for applied nodes is mostly this date.

signposts.event: A proof of global regularity for the inhomogeneous Landau or Boltzmann equation
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms that the D0-level kinetic problems fall on schedule (2027 under S2) and firms up DSMC and kinetic-solver foundations.

signposts.event: Any AI-produced improvement to lattice-sieving or reduction asymptotics, or an attack on a standardized PQC scheme
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves frontier-lattice-crypto-watch from Low to urgent. Space programs with fixed hardware crypto would need agility retrofits.

signposts.event: NASA, ESA, DARPA or AIAA publishes a formally stated applied open-problem bank
signposts.what_it_changes: Directly relieves the posing constraint and pulls frontier-applied-posing to High under S1.
