auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.title: Correct-by-construction mission planners
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.description: Planners, schedulers and fault responses generated automatically from temporal-logic specifications (reactive synthesis, energy/mean-payoff games, probabilistic model checking) at the scale of real surface operations, each shipped with a proof that the plan meets the spec under the modeled environment.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.status_oct2026: Theory mature, flight use rare: synthesis works for small specs, but abstractions (terrain, energy, comm windows) and specs are built by scarce experts (general). Family 104 claims quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games. Only the randomized quasipolynomial mean-payoff algorithm and a counterexample to Truffet's procedure are formalized (T3, unchecked); the stochastic-game part is T1, conditional. Mean-payoff ('energy') objectives match battery-constrained rovers.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 104 is T3 for the randomized mean-payoff part only and T1 (conditional) for the stochastic-game part
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.why: The cost of synthesis is building a sound abstraction and a correct spec, which is exactly bespoke expert math. An agent that proposes the abstraction, proves it sound, writes the spec, synthesizes the controller and emits Lean or model-checker certificates turns months of formal-methods work into days. 'Achieved' = a synthesized planner for a realistic multi-day surface scenario (energy, thermal, comm windows, faults) with machine-checked certificate, produced with under 10% specialist effort. Family 104 changes the theoretical ceiling for stochastic and mean-payoff games, but practical solvers (Zielonka, strategy iteration) already handle realistic sizes, so its own contribution is P3, small.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.strongest_case_small: Mission operations culture values human-readable, human-reviewed plans; even the AI-planned Perseverance drives were validated by simulation, not proof. Specs, not proofs, are the hard part, and a proof of the wrong property adds little (tl-position-6; tr-position-2).
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.signpost: A CLPS, LTV or NASA surface payload announces spec-to-plan synthesized autonomy in flight software, or ESA/NASA solicitations require correct-by-construction planners.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Auditor (grounding): replaced the nonexistent '(analyst position h)' with tl-position-6 and tr-position-2. The status and premise_tier now scope 104's T3 to its formalized randomized mean-payoff part (statement-gap modifier). Years and bands unchanged.

auton-ops-planning-ceilings.title: Known limits for robot fleet scheduling
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.description: Hardness and optimality results tell surface-ops planners which multi-robot task-allocation, scheduling, partitioning and depot-siting problems can be solved near-optimally and which cannot, so effort moves to problem structure, exact solvers on small instances and heuristics.
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.status_oct2026: 102 Unique Games Conjecture (T3) fixes optimal approximation ratios for many labeling and partitioning problems; 125 metric k-median threshold 1+2/e (T3) bounds depot, charging-pad and relay siting; 124 polynomial-time unit-job scheduling on three identical machines with precedence (T1 per release overview; repo lean/docs/124.md lists a Comparator statement, so possibly T3); 110 optimal randomized k-server (T1) and 111 one-sample matroid prophet inequalities (T1; competitive ratio 2^-310, no polynomial-time implementation asserted) for online dispatch. lean/docs/110.md and 111.md also carry Comparator statements (KServer.lean, MatroidProphet.lean) that are absent from formalization.yaml, so they stay T1. For 125 the yaml main result is the KMedianRecovery (below-2) statement; the 1+2/e threshold appears only in lean/docs/125.md (KMedianThreshold.lean).
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.pathway: P3 (102 hardness; 125 lower bound) + P4 (124, 110, 111 and the 125 algorithm; constants unstated or galactic, not counted as practical)
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.premise_tier: T3 (102, 125); T1 (124, 110, 111): conditional for those parts
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.why: A lunar base with dozens of robots and crew visits every six months is an online scheduling and allocation problem with precedence constraints. Ceilings act in months: they stop teams chasing general-purpose 'optimal' fleet planners and let them judge vendor claims. 124 is a cute fit for a three-robot team with precedence-constrained unit tasks. The parts resting on 124, 110 and 111 are conditional (T1).
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.strongest_case_small: Real instances are small and structured and are solved well by MILP/CP solvers; worst-case hardness and galactic constants (111's 2^-310) say little about them. Most of these results were already believed; the change is from belief to theorem.
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.signpost: Planning papers or vendor documentation for lunar and Mars operations cite these ceilings when scoping fleet planners; otherwise no measurable change expected.
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Auditor (grounding): 124 (exact scheduling) and 110 (k-server) are algorithms (P4), not ceilings, so the pathway is now P3+P4, matching ref-space-math-map. The status gives the repo's tier scope for 110, 111 and 125. Skeptic and advocate (both lenses): the edge into auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops is now soft. A hardness ceiling tells planners what not to attempt and does not gate running a base. Bands unchanged.

auton-certified-contact-sim.title: Contact simulators with error bars
auton-certified-contact-sim.description: Physics engines for grasping, latching, digging and assembly that carry proven convergence and computable error bounds for stated friction and compliance parameters, so a simulation run can count as verification evidence instead of a physical test.
auton-certified-contact-sim.status_oct2026: Not available (general): mainstream engines (MuJoCo, Drake, PhysX/Isaac) use different contact regularizations with no certified error bounds. Not addressed by the catalog.
auton-certified-contact-sim.why: Space robotics qualification leans on physical testing in low-fidelity analogs (air-bearing tables, parabolic flights, dirty thermal-vacuum chambers). A certified simulator, validated against a modest set of vacuum and dust experiments, could replace a large share of those tests with analysis. The math is cognitive-clock work under S2; the binding gate is the validation experiments for dusty, cold, vacuum contact.
auton-certified-contact-sim.strongest_case_small: Error bounds will be conditional on parameters measured in the lab; for lunar dust (electrostatic adhesion, cold welding, abrasion) parameter uncertainty dominates and certified numerics only shrink the smaller error term.
auton-certified-contact-sim.signpost: A contact solver released with a formal convergence proof (e.g. inside Drake or MuJoCo), and a NASA ISAM or Moon Base program accepting its results as verification evidence.
auton-certified-contact-sim.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Advocate: added soft inputs from physclock-optimal-test-campaigns and physclock-ai-run-test-stands, the graph's mechanisms for compressing experiment gates (20-40% fewer tests, adaptive stopping), so the tree shows that path. Years and bands unchanged. Skeptic: S3 is consistent with auton-contact-wellposedness now being S3 2028.

auton-ecls-reliability-uq.title: Honest reliability numbers for life support
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.description: System-of-systems reliability, sparing and crew-maintenance models for regenerative life support with Bayesian uncertainty from ISS failure history: the analysis that decides how many tonnes of spares a Mars crew carries and how much crew time maintenance eats.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.status_oct2026: Methods exist (Langley's EMAT, semi-Markov sparing, Bayesian estimation) but scale poorly to system-of-systems; last public ECLSS reliability data release was 2004 (ICES 2025). A 2025 Bayesian study estimates 907 crew-hours of ECLSS maintenance (~45 min/day) and availability 0.9687 for a 1,200-day mission. 'Solved in principle, expert-scarce and data-limited'.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.why: In the 2025 study the 5th-percentile spares mass corresponds to a 10x MTBF improvement, so the uncertainty band spans an order of magnitude in MTBF. A model that uses every ISS failure record, component physics and shelf-life data, with uncertainty propagated end to end, can narrow that band only if new failure data arrive. Conditional on new failure data: halving MTBF uncertainty (lognormal sigma 0.70 -> 0.35) cuts the 95th-percentile failure-rate multiplier from ~3.2x to ~1.8x, so spares mass at fixed risk falls ~20-40% only if the median holds. Better data can also move the median toward worse reliability, and remodeling the existing 2004-era public data alone narrows the band little (general derivation). The binding gate is data: the last public ECLSS failure release was 2004, and releasing more is an institutional decision that compresses 1.0x. Under S2 the modeling is routine AI applied statistics from 2027, but a credible result waits for released data or NASA in-house work (2028, Medium). Under S3, near-free cognition makes it likely that NASA's own analysts do it in-house with the full record, hence High (judgment).
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.strongest_case_small: Thin data cannot be cured by better math; failure data accrue only with operating hours, and ISS, the only large source, retires around 2030-2032 (extension to 2032 proposed). Better UQ may simply confirm the wide band.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.signpost: NASA publishes an updated ISS ECLSS failure and replacement dataset; Mars architecture studies cite AI-built sparing models.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (band and timing): S2/S3 2027 -> 2028 and S2 High -> Medium. The node's own gate is data, and the last public ECLSS failure release was 2004 (ICES 2025, verified by the auditor). A data release is an institutional decision (1.0x), so the cognitive date (2027) is not the outcome date. The 20-40% spares claim is reworded as conditional on new data, with the skeptic's lognormal arithmetic, which I checked (exp(1.645 x 0.70) = 3.2; exp(1.645 x 0.35) = 1.8). Partly accepted: S3 stays High, because with near-free cognition NASA can do the work in-house without a public release. Skeptic (edge): the outgoing edge to auton-earth-independent-fdir is now soft.

auton-isru-rom-control.title: Fast, trustworthy models of oxygen reactors
auton-isru-rom-control.description: Reduced-order multiphysics models (electrochemistry, melt flow and heat transfer, gas evolution, composition drift) of molten-regolith electrolysis, carbothermal and solid-oxide reactors, with error bounds, used for model-predictive control, optimal test design and scale-up decisions.
auton-isru-rom-control.status_oct2026: Bespoke per team. LR-1 MRE: 0.07 kg O2/h for 9 h on 25 kg simulant in vacuum (ICES 2026); CaRD solar-carbothermal integrated test completed Feb 2026 (no public rate); MOXIE peak 12 g/h; OxEon MOMS designing for 1-3 kg/h O2 with >65% CO2-to-CH4 conversion and 5,000+ h stack tests. Melt composition, liquidus and viscosity drift during electrolysis (Acta Astronautica 2025).
auton-isru-rom-control.why: Going from 0.07 kg/h to a 10 t/yr plant (~1.1 kg/h continuous at under 30 kW, 2025 systems study) is a ~16x step for MRE; MOXIE to MOMS is ~80-250x. Each build-test cycle costs months; good ROMs plus Bayesian experiment design cut the number of cycles, and MPC handles regolith composition drift. Under S2 this is routine AI applied math by 2028.
auton-isru-rom-control.strongest_case_small: The uncertainty sits in property data at 1,600 C (melt viscosity and conductivity vs composition, anode corrosion), not in model reduction; teams already run COMSOL-class models. Plant performance is capped by hardware life and power, which models do not change.
auton-isru-rom-control.signpost: An ISRU payload flies with model-predictive control built on a published reduced-order model; ICES or Acta Astronautica papers report AI-generated reactor ROMs validated against test data.
auton-isru-rom-control.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and advocate (both lenses): infra-verified-numerics moved from hard prerequisite to soft accelerator. Reactor ROMs and MPC get their error bounds from a-posteriori estimators and validation against test data, and melt-property data at 1,600 C dominate the error budget. Skeptic: S3 2027 -> 2028, because the node is data-gated and S3 equals S2 in capability through 2028. This also matches the trunk resolver's infra-verified-numerics S3 2028. Advocate's S1 2030 -> 2029 rejected: neither S1 prerequisite (cap-applied-math, verified numerics) is earlier than 2029, and the data gate does not move. Auditor: pathway relabeled P1 (P6 only for scale-up tools); P6's default band is Low, so High is consistent only with P1. Skeptic and advocate: the outgoing edges to auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo and auton-mars-isru-demo are now soft.

auton-granular-regolith-model.title: Validated models of digging icy regolith
auton-granular-regolith-model.description: Calibrated continuum-plus-DEM models (well-posed where theory allows, empirically regularized otherwise) of excavation, conveying and trafficability for polar regolith, including ice-cemented and vapor-deposited ice forms, predictive enough to size excavators and water-extraction feeders.
auton-granular-regolith-model.status_oct2026: Lab-only. Ice-cemented simulant: excavation energy 2.74 to 143 J/g as ice rises from 1 to 12 wt% (52x, reported as 52 times less efficient). Pressure-sintered simulant: 0.35 to 0.11 J/g, 3.2 times more efficient with more ice. A vapor-deposited sample was much stronger than pressure-sintered and Apollo 16 samples (Space and Planetary Resources, Sep 2026). The authors conclude that icy regolith 'may be easier to excavate and traverse than previously thought' and question ice-cemented simulants as universal proxies. DEM calibration with realistic particle shapes and agglutinates is ongoing (2024-2026). The ice form at the poles is unknown.
auton-granular-regolith-model.why: Without knowing the ice form, excavator power and wear sizing is uncertain by more than 10x. A model calibrated on lab simulants with empirical regularization (today's practice) and then tested blind against the first in-situ polar data (2028 at the earliest) becomes a design basis. A well-posedness theorem raises confidence but is not a precondition (tl-position-2). S3 cannot beat S2 here because the gate is the ground-truth mission, not cognition. S1 lags a year because AI applied math arrives in 2029 in S1, although human teams can do the calibration.
auton-granular-regolith-model.strongest_case_small: One or two landing sites may not represent the variability across permanently shadowed regions; designers will overbuild regardless, and early ice mining may target easier deposits.
auton-granular-regolith-model.signpost: VIPER or another polar lander returns geotechnical data, and a published model predicts it blind within a factor of two.
auton-granular-regolith-model.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Advocate (edges): auton-granular-wellposedness and cap-physics-theory moved from hard prerequisites to soft accelerators, and cap-applied-math added as a hard prerequisite. Calibrated DEM/MPM with empirical regularization is how excavators are sized today, a well-posedness proof changes confidence and not the model (tl-position-2), and the skeptic makes the same point on the wellposedness node. The polar ground-truth data stay the hard gate. Advocate: S1 >2031 -> 2030 (band Low kept), because the binding gate is the 2028 data and not the theorem. Auditor's knock-on (S2/S3 2029 -> 2030) not applied, because ground truth stays 2028 (see that node). Auditor (fact): the status now reports both ice forms and the authors' conclusion (verified against the Crossref abstract).

auton-mre-anode-materials.title: Anodes that survive molten regolith
auton-mre-anode-materials.description: Discovery and life prediction of inert anode and crucible materials for oxygen-evolving electrolysis of molten regolith at ~1,600 C, the component that limits molten-regolith-electrolysis plant life.
auton-mre-anode-materials.status_oct2026: Active research: iridium anodes (costly), zirconia-based hollow anodes (Acta Astronautica, Jun 2025). Longest reported integrated large-scale run: hours (LR-1, 9 h). Plants need thousands of hours.
auton-mre-anode-materials.why: A 10 t/yr plant (~1.1 kg/h, about 8,800 operating hours a year) with anodes lasting 1,000 h needs ~9 anode swaps a year, each a robotic maintenance operation in a 1,600 C cell; at 10,000 h it needs fewer than one. AI-guided and autonomous-lab materials search (S2/S3) can shortlist compositions quickly. But autonomous labs cannot yet process refractory ceramics and superalloys (materials-closed-loop-discovery), and each candidate still needs fabrication and a multi-thousand-hour endurance test at 1,600 C: a 1,000 h screen takes ~6 weeks and a 10,000 h confirmation ~14 months. AI-run test stands can run candidates in parallel, which cuts the number of serial cycles but not the length of any one test. Chain (S2): discovery capability 2029 -> candidate fabricated and screened at 1,000 h, 2030 -> published with endurance data 2030-31 (Medium). S3 lands in the same year, because the discovery prerequisite is no earlier (2029) and endurance hours do not compress.
auton-mre-anode-materials.strongest_case_small: Endurance testing is inherently slow (10,000 h is about 14 months per test) and AI cannot compress it; and the carbothermal route avoids the inert-anode problem entirely, so the whole node may be bypassed.
auton-mre-anode-materials.signpost: A continuous MRE run longer than 1,000 h reported; an AI-discovered anode composition published with endurance data.
auton-mre-anode-materials.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (timing): S3 2029 -> 2030. S3 2029 equalled the hard prerequisite materials-closed-loop-discovery (S3 2029), which leaves no time to fabricate a refractory candidate and run even a 1,000 h screen. Skeptic's S2 2030 -> 2031 and Medium -> Low rejected: a 1,000 h screen is six weeks, so the 2029 -> 2030 lag is enough for a first endurance-backed candidate. Advocate's S3 Medium -> High rejected: parallel stands shorten serial cycles but not single tests, and refractory processing is a stated limit of autonomous labs. Both lenses: new soft edge to auton-lunar-oxygen-ops (anode life limits plant life). Advocate: soft input from physclock-ai-run-test-stands. Auditor (arithmetic): ~8 -> ~9 swaps a year (10,000 kg / 1.14 kg/h = ~8,770 h).

auton-blss-stability-theory.title: Bioregenerative loops with stability guarantees
auton-blss-stability-theory.description: Multi-compartment models of bioregenerative life support (bacteria, algae, higher plants, crew) with certified stability and recovery margins, and controllers designed against those margins.
auton-blss-stability-theory.status_oct2026: MELiSSA pilot plant has integrated liquid streams of three compartments and prepared gas closure across four (ICES 2025). China's Lunar Palace 365 ran 370 days at 98.2% closure (bioRxiv 2021). A 2025 npj Microgravity review flags critical US capability gaps in bioregenerative systems. Family 149 (T1; the formal part is possibly T3 per repo docs) claims a proof of boundedness and persistence for closed weakly reversible mass-action networks, an idealized building block.
auton-blss-stability-theory.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 149 enters only as a soft, conditional (T1) accelerator
auton-blss-stability-theory.why: Instability (microbial washout, crop failure, CO2/O2 imbalance) is the main operational risk of bioregenerative systems and the reason they carry large physico-chemical backups. Certified stability margins define safe operating envelopes and shrink buffer stocks. The value is AI building validated reduced models and Lyapunov or permanence-type certificates for the controlled loop, which do not need family 149. Real loops have Monod and light-limited kinetics, harvesting, control inputs and contamination, so they are not closed weakly reversible mass-action networks. 149 (T1, conditional) contributes only the idealized guarantee that a closed mass-action core cannot lose a species, and it accelerates the work without gating it. Validation uses existing closed-run data (MELiSSA, Lunar Palace), so the gate is data access, not a new test.
auton-blss-stability-theory.strongest_case_small: Biology is not mass-action and real failures come from contamination, disease and equipment; validation needs months-to-years closed tests, so the model may only re-describe what operators already manage empirically.
auton-blss-stability-theory.signpost: Stability certificates and model-based controllers validated against existing MELiSSA or Lunar Palace closed-run data, published by those teams or a NASA or commercial analog group.
auton-blss-stability-theory.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (edge): auton-mass-action-permanence (149, T1) moved from hard prerequisite to soft accelerator. Real BLSS loops are not closed weakly reversible mass-action systems, the node's own why already said 149 contributes only the idealized guarantee, and Lunar Palace 365 ran 370 days at 98.2% closure with no such theorem. Skeptic (gate): experiment -> data, and the signpost now validates against existing closed-run data, which removes the circularity with its own child node auton-blss-closed-test. Auditor (grounding): 'proves permanence' -> 'claims a proof of boundedness and persistence' (T1 wording, formal scope). S3 2028 -> 2029 (resolver): this aligns with the trunk resolver's cap-physics-theory S3 2029 (a hard prerequisite) and with S3 equalling S2 through 2028. Bands unchanged.

auton-radiation-risk-uq.title: Narrower uncertainty on crew radiation risk
auton-radiation-risk-uq.description: Mechanistic radiobiology models (high-LET track structure, non-targeted effects, dose-rate) that shrink the uncertainty on cancer and cardiovascular risk per unit dose for Moon and Mars crews.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.status_oct2026: NASA limit: 600 mSv career effective dose, independent of age and sex. Space Weather (Mar 2026): staying under 600 mSv on a Mars mission requires flying near solar maximum or faster transfers. Tomography review (Jul 2026): recent NASA Space Cancer Risk model revisions and non-targeted-effect scenarios suggest risks may be higher than earlier estimates; uncertainty remains substantial for high-LET radiobiology. Transport models predict dose well (blind Artemis I validation, 2025).
auton-radiation-risk-uq.why: Risk-per-dose uncertainty drives shielding mass and allowed mission duration. Halving it could relax design margins, but that requires new biological data: animal cohorts (years to cancer endpoints), organoid and beam studies at NSRL (limited beam time). S3's autonomous labs could scale in-vitro work, but in-vivo latency is a fixed physical clock.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.strongest_case_small: The 600 mSv limit is a policy choice, not a model output, and is unlikely to move within five years whatever models say; dose physics (not math) sets the mass needed to shield.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.signpost: NASA revises its Space Cancer Risk model with mechanistic components, or changes the 600 mSv standard.

auton-verified-surface-autonomy.title: Proof-carrying autonomy for lunar robots
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.description: Flight software for uncrewed rovers, excavators and other robotic surface assets whose planner, fault responses and safety monitors ship with machine-checked proofs: a synthesized planner plus a runtime-assurance wrapper around learned perception, produced by AI agents at a cost a commercial lunar company can afford. LTV software is out of scope, because it is human-rated even when the vehicle drives without crew (see verif-hls-autonomy-certification).
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.status_oct2026: Not flown. CADRE (late 2026, IM-3) demonstrates multi-robot autonomy (leader election, task re-allocation, cooperative mapping) without proofs; Perseverance's AI-planned drives (Dec 2025) used digital-twin checking. LTV awards (May 2026: Astrolab $219M, Lunar Outpost $220M; Pegasus offers manual, autonomous and remote modes).
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 104 is T3 for the randomized mean-payoff part only
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.why: Moon Base Phase 1 (up to 30 CLPS landings from 2027) puts many robots on the surface with small operations teams, and the verification cost of each autonomous behavior becomes the binding cost of autonomy. Agents that synthesize and prove planners and wrap learned components in proven monitors collapse that cost. The scope is uncrewed operation. CLPS is a commercial service buy with low NASA oversight, and uncrewed commercial robots need only an Article VI mission authorization (EO 14335 directs a streamlined process), so no certification step applies and the gate is supplier adoption. P2's default of Medium assumes a certification step; with none here, S2/S3 High rests on cheap proof tooling (2028) and many Moon Base Phase 1 suppliers. Crew-carrying LTV autonomy would trigger the Medium cap and is excluded.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.strongest_case_small: Most lunar robot losses so far are hardware and environment (landers tipping, thermal, dust, comms), not logic errors; proofs cover the model, not the Moon.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.signpost: A CLPS, LTV or NASA payload provider advertises formally verified autonomy with published proof artifacts; NASA's Fly Foundational Robotics mission or CADRE follow-ons adopt them.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (gate vs band) against the advocate (gate). Both cappers offered the same alternative: drop the crew-carrying LTV from scope, set the gate to adoption, and keep S2 High. The advocate argued for adoption. All three are reconciled by narrowing the scope to uncrewed robots (LTVs excluded, because their software is human-rated) and setting binding_gate qualification -> adoption. Bands Medium/High/High kept. The why no longer both invokes NASA acceptance and denies the cap. Auditor: 104's scope note added to premise_tier. The outgoing edges to auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops and auton-surface-productivity are now soft (all three lenses).

auton-earth-independent-fdir.title: Crew-side fault diagnosis without Mission Control
auton-earth-independent-fdir.description: Onboard diagnosis and repair guidance for habitats, life support and crew medicine that a crew 3-22 light-minutes (one way) from Earth can trust: model-based reasoning and AI assistants whose conclusions are cross-checked against verified system models.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.status_oct2026: Research prototypes: the DARIA/STAMPS anomaly-response architecture (AIAA SciTech, Jan 2026; naming unverified); NASA's progressively Earth-independent medical operations (EIMO) framework, which names clinical AI as a high-value target (2025); AI-assisted medical diagnostics tests on ISS reported in Mar 2026 (press headline only, unverified). ISS relies on ground engineering teams.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.why: Mars crews face light-time delays and blackouts, and ECLSS maintenance alone is estimated at ~45 min/day. Faster, trustworthy diagnosis cuts downtime, spares and risk. Flying it on ISS or an Artemis mission (the signpost) puts a crew-facing safety function, including clinical decision support, under NASA flight-software and medical-operations acceptance, so the band is capped at Medium in every scenario. Sparing and MTBF models (auton-ecls-reliability-uq) inform priors but do not perform diagnosis, so they accelerate this node rather than gate it. Gateway's pause (Mar 2026) moves the uncrewed-habitat testbed role to ISS and the Moon base.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.strongest_case_small: Advisory AI is already available; trust, training and procedures, not mathematics, limit adoption, and for the Moon (1.3 s delay) NASA will keep the ground in the loop.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.signpost: NASA flies an onboard diagnostic assistant with a formal cross-check component on ISS or an Artemis landing mission.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (both lenses, certification cap): S2 High -> Medium. The node covers crew medicine and ECLSS repair guidance, and its signpost is a flight on ISS or Artemis, which needs NASA acceptance. S3 High -> Medium as well (auditor): the scorecard cap applies in every scenario, and the skeptic gave no S3-specific reason to keep High. Skeptic (edge): auton-ecls-reliability-uq moved from hard to soft, because sparing models do not diagnose. Its outgoing edges to auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops (skeptic) and auton-closed-loop-habitat (skeptic) are now soft. Auditor (fact): Earth-Mars one-way light time is ~3-22 min; the two unverifiable status items are marked. Gate adoption -> qualification, so the label matches the acceptance gate the why now names.

auton-excavation-design.title: Design excavators from models, not guesses
auton-excavation-design.description: Model-based sizing and design optimization of excavators, conveyors and ice-processing feeders for polar regolith, replacing much of today's build-and-dig-in-simulant iteration.
auton-excavation-design.status_oct2026: NASA's IPEx is designed to excavate on the order of 20 t of regolith per mission; designs are iterated in simulant test bins. 2026 work on bucket design uses vision-based fill analysis (arXiv 2609.25724).
auton-excavation-design.why: With a validated regolith model, AI multiphysics design optimization can trade bucket geometry, power and wear against the in-situ ice form, avoiding a 10x over- or under-sized machine. The gate is the ground-truth data and model validation, not the optimizer.
auton-excavation-design.strongest_case_small: Excavator mass is a small share of a lunar base; conservative over-design costs little compared with landing slots, so precision design may not change what flies.
auton-excavation-design.signpost: An ISRU excavator or ice-mining payload selected for a 2029-2031 flight with a model-based design report validated against in-situ data.

auton-sinter-process-control.title: Reliable recipes for sintering regolith
auton-sinter-process-control.description: Process windows and closed-loop control for microwave, solar or laser sintering and melting of regolith into landing pads, roads and blast berms, avoiding thermal-stress cracking in lunar thermal extremes.
auton-sinter-process-control.status_oct2026: Multiphysics modeling (Coatings, Feb 2026) finds microwave-sintered bodies crack when cooled faster than ~16 C/min (safe below 15 C/min). Startups pursuing lunar construction: Lunar Forge (Jul 2026), Astroport with Vermeer on autonomous construction machinery (Apr 2026). Plume-surface interaction models that set pad requirements are immature (see prop-psi-models).
auton-sinter-process-control.why: Coupled electromagnetic-thermal-stress models are expert-scarce but well-posed; AI can map process windows across regolith compositions and design controllers that hold cooling rates, cutting the test matrix. Pads matter because landing plumes eject regolith at high speed, a hazard that grows with Starship-class landers.
auton-sinter-process-control.strongest_case_small: Regolith composition and grain size vary by site; vacuum-thermal test facilities are scarce; and on the Moon the binding constraint is kW-to-100s-of-kW power for sintering, not recipes.
auton-sinter-process-control.signpost: A relevant-environment test produces sintered pads that survive a rocket-plume test; a CLPS manifest includes a construction demo.
auton-sinter-process-control.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (both lenses): S2 High -> Medium and S1 Medium -> Low (S3 High kept). The node ends in P6 (default Low) and is gated by scarce relevant-environment vacuum-thermal tests (1.1-1.3x in S2) plus a plume-test signpost. A model-derived process window already exists without AI (Coatings 2026), and S1 Medium did not fit a 2031 earliest year. New soft input from prop-psi-models (skeptic: PSI sets pad requirements). New hard output to auton-robotic-landing-pad (advocate), which gives this formerly dangling node a downstream use.

auton-certified-assembly-skills.title: Robot assembly skills with proven safety envelopes
auton-certified-assembly-skills.description: Learned or optimized manipulation skills (connector mating, truss and solar-array assembly, cable routing, refueling interfaces) wrapped in certified contact simulation and runtime assurance, so qualification can lean on analysis rather than exhaustive physical testing.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.status_oct2026: Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle launched Jul 22, 2026 with two NRL robotic arms and three Mission Extension Pods; NASA's Fly Foundational Robotics mission (Motiv arm, PickNik MoveIt Pro on Space ROS, Feb 2026) targets autonomous and ground-supervised manipulation. Payload's State of ISAM 2026 calls assembly 'perhaps the furthest away from reality' of ISAM capabilities (Apr 2026).
auton-certified-assembly-skills.why: Contact-rich assembly is where learned policies outperform hand-coded ones, but they are hard to qualify. Certified contact simulation provides envelope evidence; runtime assurance keeps the learned policy inside it. The binding gate is validating the envelope in vacuum and microgravity analogs. Verified neural perception would help but is not required, because runtime assurance bounds an unverified policy.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.strongest_case_small: Customers buy servicing (inspection, life extension, refueling) with scripted, teleoperated arms; large-scale assembly lacks a paying customer before Starship-era structures, so the technique may wait for demand rather than math.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.signpost: MRV or FFR on-orbit results reporting autonomous contact tasks under a runtime-assurance monitor; a program accepting simulation evidence for a contact task.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.calibration_note: A4: Hard edge from verif-nn-verification-scale made soft. Assembly skills are qualified through certified contact simulation plus runtime assurance, the documented workaround for networks that cannot be verified, so flight-scale NN verification accelerates this node but does not gate it. Bands Low/Medium/Medium kept; the hard prerequisites are certified contact sim and runtime assurance.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Auditor (fact): the Payload wording is quoted exactly instead of paraphrased in quotation marks. Other facts verified (MRV launch Jul 22, 2026 with two NRL arms and three MEPs; FFR Feb 2026). Years and bands unchanged.

auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.title: First measurements of how hard polar ice is to dig
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.description: In-situ geotechnical and volatile data from lunar south-pole regolith (VIPER, CLPS drills, Chang'e-7, LUPEX, Moon Base Phase 1 rovers): the physical data gate for every excavation and water-extraction model.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.status_oct2026: PRIME-1 drill on IM-2 (Mar 2025) returned limited data after the lander tipped over (general). VIPER: CS-7 task order to Blue Origin (Sep 19, 2025, up to $190M); the lunar-delivery option is exercised only after Blue Moon Mk1's first flight, and the target was late 2027. The May 28, 2026 New Glenn static-fire explosion destroyed the LC-36 transporter-erector and damaged the gantry (best-case pad restoration ~15 months per reporting), and NASA is evaluating Falcon Heavy. Chang'e-7 missed its Aug 2026 window and now targets 2027; its hopper and rover carry water and volatile analyzers, spectrometers and radar but no geotechnical drill. ESA's PROSPECT (ProSEED drill to ~1 m) flies on an Intuitive Machines Nova-C in 2027 to ~84.5 S, a site chosen for sunlight where ice-bearing layers may be out of reach. LUPEX (drill) is planned around 2028-29. Moon Base Phase 1 targets up to 30 CLPS landings from 2027.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.why: This node exists to show a gate AI cannot move: the excavation models above cannot be validated until a polar lander digs into ice-bearing regolith and returns strength or excavation data, not just detection. Chain: CS-7 base task -> Mk1 pathfinder (slipped by the LC-36 loss; New Glenn return to flight or Falcon Heavy) -> delivery option exercised -> VIPER on a second Mk1 (NET 2028, realistically 2029) -> landing -> TRIDENT drilling in ice-bearing regolith. Alternates: PROSPECT's drill (2027, sunlit site, ice possibly out of reach), LUPEX's drill (~2028-29) and Chang'e-8 (~2028-29). Chang'e-7 (2027) gives water data only. Landing success in the CLPS era has been near half (IM-1 and IM-2 tipped, Peregrine failed, ispace M1 and M2 crashed, Blue Ghost 1 succeeded; general), and ice-bearing layers may lie beyond drill reach. At least one usable dataset by 2031 is therefore Medium (judgment, roughly 50-65%), the same in every scenario because the gate is physical. The earliest year stays 2028, given several independent 2027-28 attempts.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.strongest_case_small: Data from one or two sites may not generalize across permanently shadowed regions, leaving models under-constrained even after first contact.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.signpost: Blue Moon Mk1 pathfinder flies and the VIPER delivery option is exercised; PROSPECT drilling results at ~84.5 S (2027); LUPEX or Chang'e-8 drill data from ice-bearing regolith.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (both lenses): bands High -> Medium in all scenarios. Measuring how hard the ice is to dig needs strength or excavation data from ice-bearing regolith. VIPER now sits behind two sequential physical gates (the Mk1 pathfinder, then the option), Chang'e-7 slipped and carries no drill, and CLPS-era landing success is near half. Advocate's High rejected; its new PROSPECT fact is added (verified on ESA's page: Nova-C, 2027, ~84.5 S, ~1 m drill), but the site is sunlit and ice may be out of reach. Auditor's 2028 -> 2029 rejected: the skeptic and advocate both keep 2028, and PROSPECT and LUPEX are 2027-28 attempts. Auditor (contradicted fact): the VIPER task order was Sep 19, 2025 (CS-7, $190M, option contingent), not Dec 2025 (verified, 33FG). The LC-36 damage wording is corrected, and the tier-5 chain is written out. Advocate's MoonFall drone claim is omitted (not verified).

auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.title: First oxygen made on the Moon
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.description: A flight demonstration that extracts at least 1 g of oxygen from lunar regolith on the surface (grams to kilograms), by carbothermal reduction, molten-regolith electrolysis, hydrogen reduction or another route. Sub-gram analytical runs, such as ProSPA's hydrogen-reduction oven test, are precursors and do not count.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.status_oct2026: Ground prototypes only: CaRD integrated solar-carbothermal test (Feb 2026, no flight date), LR-1 MRE (0.07 kg/h, late 2024), Blue Origin Air Pioneer MRE (Jun 2026). NASA's lunar ISRU strategy is a leader/follower sequence of flight demos leading to a pilot plant (NTRS 2025). NASA's LIFT-1 O2-extraction demo was planned in 2023 for a 2027 launch at $200-250M including landing (2026 status unconfirmed). ESA's ProSPA flies a sub-gram hydrogen-reduction test on an Intuitive Machines Nova-C in 2027. Helios (MRE) has reported plans to fly with ispace (date unconfirmed), and ASI's ORACLE carbothermal demo was proposed for a CLPS slot NET 2028 (IAC-23 paper). No payload making 1 g or more of oxygen is confirmed manifested as of Oct 2026; NASA's Mar 24, 2026 RFI seeks payloads for 2027-28 CLPS flights.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.why: The date is set by CLPS manifests, payload funding and lander success, not by AI math, and the demo would happen on roughly this schedule without it. AI reactor models are therefore an accelerator: they can shorten the cognitive third or so of a payload schedule, worth at most about a year between S1 and S2 (Amdahl ~18% vs ~38%). Chain (S1): a LIFT-1-class or commercial MRE or carbothermal payload manifested 2027-28 -> 12-18 months of integration plus typical slips (announced schedules run 1.5-3x long) -> landing 2030. Chain (S2): the same payloads with AI-assisted test design and anomaly closure from 2027 -> landing 2029. Chain (S3): ROM-tuned flight unit and faster integration -> landing 2028. With several independent candidates (LIFT-1, Helios, ORACLE, and Moon Base Phase 1's up to 30 landings) at CLPS-era landing odds of roughly 50-65% (general), at least one success by 2031 is Medium in S1 and S2, where no qualifying payload is yet manifested. It is High in S3, where launch cadence runs 0.5-1 year earlier and more attempts fit before 2031. Bands are judgments, not computed probabilities.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: The demo would happen on roughly this schedule without AI math; oxygen chemistry from regolith was shown on the ground decades ago, and the bottleneck is a landing slot, power and dust-tolerant hardware.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.signpost: An ISRU oxygen payload manifested on a named 2027-2029 CLPS mission.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder. S1 2030 equalled its prerequisite auton-isru-rom-control (S1 2030); a lunar surface payload needs at least 12-18 months from design-complete plus a CLPS slot. Chain (S1): reactor models 2030 -> flight-unit update and integration -> landing 2031 at the earliest. S1 2030 -> 2031 and S1 Medium -> Low; S2/S3 unchanged.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.revision_note: B-moon-mars: All three lenses (edge): auton-isru-rom-control moved from hard prerequisite to soft accelerator. The node's own strongest case says the demo happens on roughly this schedule without AI math. The A3 lag-ladder push (S1 2030 -> 2031, Medium -> Low) was an artifact of that edge and is undone: S1 2031 -> 2030 (the skeptic's year) and S1 Low -> Medium (the advocate's band; a non-AI schedule should not be rated below S2). Advocate's S2 2028 and S2 High rejected: no qualifying payload is manifested as of Oct 2026 (auditor), and payloads need 12-18 months after manifesting. S3 Medium -> High accepted from the advocate: multiple independent attempts plus launch cadence 0.5-1 year earlier in S3 (I verified LIFT-1 cost and target, ProSPA's 2027 Nova-C flight and Moon Base Phase 1's up to 30 landings). Advocate: description now requires at least 1 g, so ProSPA's sub-gram run does not trivially satisfy it. Auditor: S1/S2/S3 chains written out.

auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.title: A lunar robot flies proof-carrying autonomy
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.description: An uncrewed rover, excavator or other robotic surface asset operates on the Moon using autonomy software whose planner and safety monitors carry machine-checked proofs.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.status_oct2026: None. CADRE (late 2026) will be the first autonomous multi-robot team on the Moon, without proofs.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.why: Once proof-carrying autonomy is cheap (S2 2028), adoption needs only one willing payload provider and one successful landing. No certifier is involved: CLPS is a commercial service buy, and uncrewed commercial robots need only an Article VI mission authorization (EO 14335). Chain (S2): proof-carrying autonomy tool 2028 -> integration and a software freeze 12-18 months before landing -> landing 2029. Software uplinks to long-lived robots already on the surface avoid the freeze lag. Chain (S3): the same tool date (S3 equals S2 through 2028) -> landing 2029. Each attempt carries CLPS-era landing odds of roughly 50-65% (general) and depends on a provider choosing proofs without customer pull. The band is therefore Medium in S2 and S3 (judgment), because S3's cheaper cognition raises neither landing reliability nor demand.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.strongest_case_small: Providers may see no customer pull for proofs on uncrewed robots, and landing failures may consume the opportunities.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.signpost: A lunar mission press kit or NASA payload description lists formally verified autonomy as a feature.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder. S3 2028 equalled its prerequisite auton-verified-surface-autonomy (S3 2028); flight software freezes 12-18 months before a CLPS landing. Chain (S3): proof-carrying autonomy 2028 -> integration and software freeze -> lunar landing 2029. S3 2028 -> 2029.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (both lenses): S3 High -> Medium. Over 70% would need a 2028 tool, a 12-18 month freeze, a provider that chooses proofs and a successful landing inside about two years, and S3 does not raise landing reliability. Advocate's S2 Medium -> High rejected for the same reasons, although its no-certifier and uplink points are added to the why. The auditor's S2 chain is written out. The description is narrowed to uncrewed assets to match auton-verified-surface-autonomy's new scope.

auton-blss-closed-test.title: Long closed life-support test run by certified control
auton-blss-closed-test.description: A ground test of 180+ days in which a bioregenerative or hybrid life-support loop runs under model-based control with stability certificates, at 95% or more material closure (food, O2, water). Lunar Palace 365 reached 98.2% over 370 days without such control.
auton-blss-closed-test.status_oct2026: Precedent: China's Lunar Palace 1 ran a 370-day crewed closed test in 2017-18 (general); MELiSSA pilot plant progressing toward full loop closure with rat crew mock-up (2025).
auton-blss-closed-test.why: Crop cycles (60-120 days, general) and the need to observe disturbances and recoveries make the test inherently months long. Chain (S2): stability theory and controllers 2029 -> a funded facility (MELiSSA, a Lunar Palace successor or a US analog) adopts them -> a 180+ day run in 2030-31. That is Low, because it needs a funded facility and campaign inside two years. Chain (S3): theory 2029 with near-free controller design and AI-run parallel small loops -> crew-scale run 2030 (Medium). The US gap is funding, not modeling (npj Microgravity 2025).
auton-blss-closed-test.strongest_case_small: Funding, not modeling, has limited US bioregenerative work (npj Microgravity 2025); a better controller does not create a test facility.
auton-blss-closed-test.signpost: Announcement of a new long-duration closed-loop campaign (MELiSSA full loop, Lunar Palace successor, or a NASA/commercial analog) citing model-based stability control.
auton-blss-closed-test.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: inherits a minor, conditional 149 link through auton-blss-stability-theory.
auton-blss-closed-test.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (gate and band): experiment -> capital and S2 Medium -> Low (S3 Medium kept). The node's own strongest case says funding, not modeling, limits US work, and a crew-scale run after a 2029 theory needs a funded facility plus 6+ months inside 2030-31. Description: 'higher closure than prior tests' was a near-impossible bar (Lunar Palace 365 reached 98.2%) and is now 95% or more. Skeptic: catalog_families [149] -> [] and premise_tier -> n/a, since 149 is now only a soft input upstream. S3 2029 -> 2030 (resolver): the upstream theory moved to S3 2029, and a 180-day run cannot finish in the same year.

auton-assembly-flight-demo.title: Robotic assembly in space with certified skills
auton-assembly-flight-demo.description: An on-orbit or lunar-surface demonstration of multi-step robotic assembly (structure, array or connector mating) using learned or optimized skills qualified mainly by certified simulation plus runtime assurance.
auton-assembly-flight-demo.status_oct2026: MRV (launched Jul 2026) begins servicing operations; FFR in development; OSAM-1 was cancelled in 2024 (general).
auton-assembly-flight-demo.why: Needs the certified-skills toolchain (S2 2030, S3 2029) and a flight slot. Chain (S3): certified contact sim 2028 -> certified skills 2029 -> software upload to a servicer such as MRV, or a NASA FFR follow-on -> demo 2030. The chain multiplies three uncertain steps: two Medium nodes and a host willing either to risk paying missions or to fund a government demo. 'Qualified mainly by certified simulation' is also itself a qualification-acceptance claim, so even S3 is Low (judgment).
auton-assembly-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: No paying assembly customer before Starship-era structures; demonstrations remain government-funded one-offs.
auton-assembly-flight-demo.signpost: MRV or a successor performing an autonomous multi-step contact task beyond grapple-and-dock.
auton-assembly-flight-demo.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (band): S3 Medium -> Low. Three uncertain steps are chained (two Medium nodes plus a flight host), MRV's client operators are unlikely to risk paying missions on a demo, and qualification by simulation is an acceptance claim. No lens argued for keeping Medium. The S3 chain is written out.

auton-mars-isru-demo.title: Kilogram-per-hour propellant production on Mars
auton-mars-isru-demo.description: A MOMS-class solid-oxide unit (1-3 kg O2/h plus methane) operating on Mars, 80-250x MOXIE's peak rate.
auton-mars-isru-demo.status_oct2026: OxEon MOMS hardware in design (ICES 2026). SpaceX reached orbit with Starship on Flight 14 (Sep 28, 2026), and ship-to-ship propellant transfer is expected in early 2027. In Feb 2026 SpaceX made a 'self-growing city' on the Moon (in under 10 years) its priority, with Mars work to begin within 5-7 years, and it told investors it targets an uncrewed lunar landing in Mar 2027 (WSJ via NBC News). Remaining Mars departure windows in the horizon: late 2026 (SpaceX not using it), Dec 2028-Jan 2029, and Feb-Mar 2031 (arrival late 2031).
auton-mars-isru-demo.why: hyper-mars-heavy-landing puts the first 20 t-class Mars landing in the early-2031 window at the earliest (arrival late 2031), after propellant transfer and the Moon. Full chain (every scenario): a launch in the Feb-Mar 2031 window arrives about Sep-Nov 2031, leaving 1-3 months in the horizon. A 1-3 kg/h unit also needs roughly 25-50 kW of landed and deployed power (MOXIE-class scaling, general), a funded MOMS payload on a SpaceX ship (no such contract exists) and an H2 or water source for the methane leg. None of these compress in S3, and SpaceX's Moon-first pivot removes the main sponsor for an early-2031 ISRU payload, so every scenario is Speculative. AI math cannot add windows, shorten transits or raise landing reliability much, and AI reactor models are only an accelerator.
auton-mars-isru-demo.strongest_case_small: Everything here is launch, landing and power; the math contribution is a slightly better-tuned reactor.
auton-mars-isru-demo.signpost: SpaceX or NASA puts ISRU hardware on a Mars cargo manifest for the early-2031 window; a successful heavy landing from the 2028-29 window would pull this node forward to 2030.
auton-mars-isru-demo.calibration_note: A3: Cross-domain consistency and launch windows. Operating a MOMS-class unit on Mars needs a heavy Mars landing, which hyper-mars-heavy-landing puts at 2031 at the earliest in every scenario (Moon priority, propellant transfer first). The late-2028 window is therefore not available in S2/S3; the early-2031 window arrives late 2031. Chain (S2): isru-rom-control 2028 -> unit built for the 2031 window -> landing late 2031 -> operation at the very end of the horizon. S2 2029 -> 2031 (Low -> Speculative), S3 2029 -> 2031 (Low kept); S1 unchanged. A1: new hard edge from hyper-mars-heavy-landing (a kg/h ISRU unit needs a Starship-class Mars landing, as the node's own rationale says); hyper rates the first 20 t+ landing 2031 in every scenario (two windows; transfer and Moon priority first), so S2/S3 2029 moved to 2031 and S1 to >2031. A4: The why and signpost were rewritten for the 2031 landing; they had assumed a 2028-29 landing. A1's note had overwritten A3's, so both are kept here. S2 Speculative (A3, also A1's review flag) and S3 Low are kept. S3 Low sits below hyper-mars-heavy-landing's S3 Medium because the unit must also start up within weeks of a late-2031 arrival.
auton-mars-isru-demo.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (band): S3 Low -> Speculative. The full S3 chain leaves 1-3 months after a late-2031 arrival and needs landed power, a contract and a hydrogen source, none of which S3 compresses. The advocate kept Low but conceded that SpaceX's Feb 2026 Moon-first pivot removes the main route to an early ISRU payload (verified, NBC News Feb 9, 2026). Skeptic: auton-isru-rom-control moved from hard to soft. Auditor (fact): the window list now includes the unused late-2026 window. Advocate: the Moon-first status is added. The why is rewritten, because its 'S3 Low' sentence no longer applies.

auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.title: AI plans rover operations, machines check the plans
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.description: Routine use of AI agents to plan multi-sol rover traverses and multi-robot surface activities, with automated simulation and formal checks replacing most human plan review.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.status_oct2026: Demonstrated once at Mars: Perseverance's first AI-planned drives on Dec 8 and 10, 2025 (210 m and 246 m; Claude vision-language models used orbital imagery and slope data to lay waypoints), checked via JPL's digital twin across more than 500,000 telemetry variables (JPL, Jan 30, 2026). JPL describes a goal of kilometer-scale drives with minimal operator workload.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.why: This is the capability channel in its purest form: no catalog theorem is involved. Ground operations dominate extended-mission cost, and the Moon Base plan multiplies the number of robots per operator. Formal plan checking (model checking of command sequences against flight rules) makes AI plans acceptable without line-by-line human review. 'Routine' means a change in operations culture and flight-rule practice on flagship rovers and Moon Base operators, so it lags the checking tools (verif-fdir-model-checking, S2 2027) by about a year. In 2027 the lunar surface holds only a handful of single-lunar-day landers. Chain (S2): checking tools 2027 -> flight-rule and digital-twin integration at JPL and Phase 1 operators -> majority of drives AI-planned 2028.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.strongest_case_small: Already happening without any new mathematics; rover productivity is capped by power, comm passes, hazards and science-team decision time, not planning.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.signpost: JPL reports a majority of a rover's drives in a quarter as AI-planned, or a kilometer-scale AI-planned drive; Moon Base robot operators adopt the same workflow.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (timing): 2028/2027/2027 -> 2029/2028/2028. A tier-6 'routine' change in flight-rule practice cannot land in the same year that its tier-4 checking tool first exists; this applies the A3 lag-ladder logic. The advocate's chain also starts from 2027 tools, so its 'routine 2027' is the tool date, not the adoption date. Bands unchanged.

auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.title: Lunar base runs itself between crew visits
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.description: Robots, LTVs and base systems operate, maintain and resupply lunar base elements autonomously for months between crewed landings, with Earth supervising rather than commanding.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.status_oct2026: NASA's Moon Base plan (Mar 24, 2026): phased build-up, crewed landings initially every six months, Gateway paused in its current form; budget reported at ~$30B with bulk launch buys near (Bloomberg via 33FG, Oct 6, 2026). Artemis III is a 2027 Earth-orbit test; first landing 2028. Lunar Reactor-1 fission system to land in 2030.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 102 (T3) and 124 (T1, conditional) enter only through auton-ops-planning-ceilings, a soft input
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.why: Between six-month crew visits a base has months of idle infrastructure that must be maintained (dust, thermal cycling, power management). The cognitive enablers (AI-planned operations, runtime-assured autonomy, fault diagnosis) are ready by 2028 in S2. With a 1.3 s light-time, Earth-supervised AI planning and teleoperation can run a base, so proof-carrying autonomy, planning ceilings and crew-side diagnosis accelerate this node rather than gate it. The binding gate is that there must be enough base to operate. Moon Base Phase 2 (2029-2032) brings semi-permanent infrastructure, and sustained presence comes only in Phase 3 (from 2032). Politics and appropriations compress 1.0x, and flagship programs slip 2-7 years (the first crewed landing already slipped ~4 years). Chain (S2): AI operations routine 2028 -> HLS refuel campaign and first heavy cargo landing 2029 -> Phase 2 power, LTVs, a logistics cache and a semi-habitable element operating 2031 -> months of Earth-supervised operation between visits only at the very end of the horizon (Low). Chain (S3): refuel and heavy cargo 2028 -> Phase 2 elements 2030 -> months of uncrewed operation 2031 (Medium). Gateway's pause removes the planned uncrewed-habitat autonomy testbed, so the surface base inherits that role.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.strongest_case_small: With a 1.3 s light-time, the Moon can be run by teleoperation and ground scheduling; autonomy is a cost saver, not an enabler, and little base infrastructure will exist by 2031.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.signpost: Moon Base Phase 2 semi-habitable elements maintained without crew for 3+ months; NASA Phase 2 contracts that specify autonomous operations between crewed missions.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Edges: auton-ops-planning-ceilings and auton-verified-surface-autonomy moved from hard to soft (skeptic and advocate both). auton-earth-independent-fdir also moved to soft (skeptic; the advocate wanted it hard): crew-side diagnosis is for crew present, and this node is about crew absent, with Earth 1.3 s away. New hard prerequisite auton-moon-base-infrastructure (skeptic's missing gate). New soft inputs: prop-psi-models and auton-robotic-landing-pad (advocate). Timing and band, skeptic vs advocate: S3 2030 -> 2031 and S2 Medium -> Low (skeptic). The advocate's S2 2030, S3 2029 and gate -> launch were rejected. NASA's own phasing (Phase 2 2029-2032, Phase 3 from 2032; NBC, verified) and 1.0x appropriations bind, and the band cannot exceed the new hard prerequisite's S2 Low. Gate stays capital (launch now sits on auton-lunar-heavy-cargo-landing). Auditor and skeptic: catalog_families [102,124] -> [] and premise_tier relabeled (124 was cited without 'conditional'); S2 and S3 chains written out. Skeptic: the signpost no longer uses LTV uncrewed operation, which is baseline LTV design.

auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.title: Tonne-per-year lunar oxygen plant
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.description: An operational lunar oxygen plant producing at least ~1 t/yr toward a 10 t/yr pilot scale, feeding life support and lander propellant.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.status_oct2026: No flight unit. A 2025 systems study sketches 10 t/yr by molten regolith electrolysis at under 30 kW with vertical solar arrays and an excavator.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.why: Needs the flight demo, then a funded pilot plant (NASA's leader/follower sequence, LIFT-2-class), regolith handling and maintenance robots. Power is smaller than often assumed. 1 t/yr is ~0.11 kg/h, about 1.6x LR-1's demonstrated rate, and needs ~3-6 kW continuous: linear scaling of the 2025 study's <30 kW for 10 t/yr gives ~3 kW, and small cells lose proportionally more heat (general). A ridge-site solar array can supply that, so fission is not required at this scale. The real gates are run duration (8,760 h a year against LR-1's 9 h), anode life (~9 swaps a year at 1,000 h, or the carbothermal route), keeping a ~1,600 C melt through ridge-site dark periods (storage, or freeze-thaw cycles that stress cells and anodes; general), pilot-plant funding (1.0x) and landing success. Chain (S2): first demo 2029 -> pilot unit funded and designed with AI ROMs and MPC 2029-30 -> build and qualification 18-24 months -> landing 2031 at the earliest -> sustained 1 t/yr rate after 2031 (Low by 2031). Chain (S3): demo 2028 -> near-free design and AI-run test stands 2028-29 -> landing 2030 -> 1 t/yr annualized rate in 2031 (Low, because funding, endurance and landing odds do not compress).
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.strongest_case_small: Every gate is physical (power, landed mass, funding, hardware life); AI math shaves design time on a path dominated by launch cadence.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.signpost: NASA funds an ISRU pilot plant as part of Moon Base Phase 2 with a named delivery date.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Advocate (claim): 'tens of kW of continuous power' corrected. 1 t/yr needs ~3-6 kW (the advocate's linear scaling, which I checked: 30 kW x 8,766 h / 10 t = ~26 kWh/kg). The resolver adds the night-continuity constraint for a molten bath. Skeptic vs advocate on bands: the skeptic wanted S2 Low -> Speculative, and the advocate wanted S2 >2031 -> 2031 and S3 Low -> Medium. Both were rejected and years and bands kept (Speculative/Low/Low). The S2 chain needs a funded pilot plant built and landed within two years of a 2029 demo, and S3 does not compress funding, endurance or landing odds. Both lenses: soft input from auton-mre-anode-materials. Advocate: soft input from auton-lunar-heavy-cargo-landing. Skeptic: soft input from auton-moon-base-infrastructure (a pilot plant is a Phase 2 element). Chains written out.

auton-closed-loop-habitat.title: Mars-class closed-loop life support, demonstrated
auton-closed-loop-habitat.description: Regenerative ECLSS with at least 98% water recovery, 75%+ oxygen recovery and demonstrated reliability good enough for a ~1,000-day Mars mission, flown on ISS, a commercial station or a lunar habitat.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.status_oct2026: ISS: 98% water recovery (2023); Exploration ECLSS testbed integration on ISS in progress (ICES Jul 2026); ISS extension to 2032 proposed. Oxygen recovery from CO2 on ISS is roughly half (general).
auton-closed-loop-habitat.why: Reliability is demonstrated with operating hours: a zero-failure demonstration of MTBF M at 95% confidence needs about 3M unit-hours (general). For an assembly with a 20,000 h MTBF target that is ~60,000 flight unit-hours, about 7 unit-years. The only path that compresses this is acceptance of model-based priors (physclock: 0.3-0.6x, i.e. ~18-36k unit-hours). That needs the credibility standard (S2 2029, Medium) and still needs the 75%+ oxygen-recovery hardware to fly. Parallel ground units can de-risk but do not meet the in-flight criterion, and flight unit-hours before ISS retirement (2030-32) are limited by upmass, crew time and the regenerative units' failure history. Hence Low in S2 and S3, and Speculative in S1, where no credibility standard arrives before 2031. Crew-side diagnosis (auton-earth-independent-fdir) helps operations but is not needed for an ISS demonstration, which the ground supports.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.strongest_case_small: The gap is hardware maturity and test time, which math does not touch; ISS retirement may end the only long-duration flight testbed before demonstration completes.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.signpost: Exploration ECLSS units accumulate multi-year ISS run time with published failure data; a commercial station adopts closed-loop O2 recovery.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (both lenses): S3 Medium -> Low. The definition requires flight, so S3's parallel ground units do not count. Skeptic: S1 Low -> Speculative (no credibility standard in S1 before 2031, so the no-prior binomial applies). Skeptic's S2 Low -> Speculative and the advocate's S2 >2031 -> 2031 cancel out, so S2 stays >2031 Low. The advocate's model-based-prior mechanism is real (physclock 0.3-0.6x) but needs both regulator acceptance and the oxygen-recovery hardware in flight. It is added as soft inputs from physclock-credibility-evidence-standard and physclock-ai-run-test-stands. Skeptic (edge): auton-earth-independent-fdir moved from hard to soft.

auton-mars-propellant-plant.title: Starship-scale propellant plant on Mars
auton-mars-propellant-plant.description: Mars ISRU producing on the order of 1,000 t of methane and oxygen per return flight: about 65 kg O2/h over ~500 days, roughly 5,000x MOXIE's peak rate, plus water-ice mining and order-1-MW continuous power (general estimates).
auton-mars-propellant-plant.status_oct2026: No hardware at this scale; MOXIE demonstrated 12 g/h; MOMS targets 1-3 kg/h.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.why: Requires landed megawatt-class power, ice mining and a sub-scale demo first, across 26-month windows. Even a perfect design in 2027 could not be landed, assembled and run at scale before 2031.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.strongest_case_small: This is the case: the effect of AI mathematics on this node inside the horizon is nil.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.signpost: SpaceX discloses a Mars power and ISRU architecture with flight hardware in test.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (edge): auton-excavation-design moved from hard prerequisite to soft accelerator. That node models lunar polar icy regolith (0.165 g, vacuum, unknown ice form), and Mars mining targets mid-latitude ground ice under an atmosphere at 0.38 g, so the models do not carry over. No date effect (>2031 everywhere); this fixes a misleading skill-tree link. Years and bands unchanged.

auton-surface-productivity.title: Severalfold more robot work per operator
auton-surface-productivity.description: Useful surface work (km driven, kg excavated, tasks completed) per ground-operator hour rises severalfold (3-10x, judgment) versus 2025 practice on lunar or Mars surface robots. It comes mainly from AI planning with automated plan checks and from multi-robot coordination, and verified autonomy accelerates it.
auton-surface-productivity.status_oct2026: Baseline: large ground teams plan rover activities daily (general); first AI-planned Mars drives Dec 2025; CADRE multi-robot demo late 2026.
auton-surface-productivity.why: Moon Base Phase 1 cannot be staffed like MER/MSL-era teams per robot, and planning automation plus automated checking removes the operator bottleneck. The metric is a ratio, so it can be shown without a large fleet: on Mars rovers already flying AI-planned drives checked by a digital twin, and on Phase 1 and CADRE-class lunar robots. Chain (S2): AI-planned operations routine 2028 -> adopted by JPL and Moon Base Phase 1 robot operators -> operator-hours per km or per task reported falling severalfold across successive missions or quarters, 2029. Chain (S3): the same timing, with formal plan checks near-free from 2029 (High). Chain (S1): routine AI planning 2029 -> reported 2031. This is the domain's largest five-year outcome and rests on the capability, not the catalog. The earlier 'tenfold' figure had no source; 'severalfold' matches the signpost.
auton-surface-productivity.strongest_case_small: Productivity is bounded by power (two-week nights), comm windows, dust and hardware failures; operator hours may not be the binding constraint for most robots.
auton-surface-productivity.signpost: NASA or a CLPS provider reports operator-hours per km or per tonne excavated falling severalfold across successive missions.
auton-surface-productivity.calibration_note: A3: Tier-7 rule (strategic outcomes rarely High): a tenfold rise in surface work per operator also needs a lunar robot fleet on the surface (Moon Base Phase 1 landing cadence and success), which AI does not control. S2 High -> Medium; S3 High kept.
auton-surface-productivity.revision_note: B-moon-mars: All three lenses (edge): auton-verified-surface-autonomy moved from hard prerequisite to soft accelerator. The operator saving comes from AI planning plus digital-twin or formal plan checks (Perseverance precedent). Skeptic (claim): 'about tenfold' -> 'severalfold (3-10x, judgment)', matching the node's own signpost; the title changed accordingly. Timing, skeptic vs advocate: S3 2028 -> 2029, because auton-ai-planned-ops-routine is now S3 2028 and the metric is measured across successive missions. The skeptic's S2 2029 -> 2030 and the advocate's S2 2029 -> 2028 were both rejected: S2 stays 2029, one year after routine adoption. Bands: the advocate's S2 High rejected (public reporting of the ratio is uncertain); the skeptic's S3 High -> Medium and S1 Medium -> Low rejected, because its ordering argument fell away once the edge became soft and the bar is now severalfold. Bands stay Medium/Medium/High. Auditor: the tier-7 chains are written out.

auton-mars-architecture-close.title: Mars outpost logistics cut by local resources and recycling
auton-mars-architecture-close.description: Validated ISRU, closed-loop life support and robot-first precursors reduce Earth-supplied mass for a first Mars outpost materially. In the 33FG model, life support is ~20% and power ~25% of a 152 t ten-person manifest. ISRU mainly saves return propellant, which is outside that manifest (general), and ISRU and closure savings are not yet quantified (judgment).
auton-mars-architecture-close.status_oct2026: Industry model (33FG, May 2025): a 10-person Mars outpost needs ~152 t of cargo; ISRU is ~40% of cargo cost, life support ~20% of mass, power ~25% of mass; a robot-only precursor cuts ~29% of cost and ~36% of mass but cannot delete ISRU, power and construction. The -29% cost and -36% mass figures come from removing the crew in a robot-only precursor, not from ISRU or closure.
auton-mars-architecture-close.why: Needs Mars ISRU validated on Mars, Mars-class ECLSS validated in flight and crew-optional operations proven on the Moon, each gated by physical clocks extending to or past 2031.
auton-mars-architecture-close.strongest_case_small: Even under S3, the validation chain runs through Mars windows and reliability hours; design studies can claim the savings earlier, but validated savings arrive after 2031.
auton-mars-architecture-close.signpost: A Mars architecture study from NASA or SpaceX that books ISRU and closure savings against flight-validated data.
auton-mars-architecture-close.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (claim): the '30-40%' figure was borrowed from the source's robot-only precursor result (removing the crew), which the source says cannot delete ISRU, power and construction. It was then credited to ISRU and closure, so the title and description are rewritten. Skeptic: S3 Low -> Speculative, which is also forced by the hard prerequisite auton-mars-isru-demo now being Speculative in S3.

cap-research-math-internal.title: Research-grade math inside the labs
cap-research-math-internal.description: Frontier labs' internal models resolve research-level open problems on request, across all of mathematics, at about three hours of compute per result, with agent-written Lean for a large minority of results.
cap-research-math-internal.status_oct2026: Exists. openai/math (Oct 6, 2026): 722 manuscripts, 372 families from ~4,000 posed problems in under four weeks; 127 families carry unchecked agent-written Lean (T3), e.g. 102 Unique Games and 362 relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell. The model was trained from Aug 28, 2026 for about a month. Anthropic (67.2% of zeta zeros on the critical line; full FLT in Lean, Comparator-checked by Buzzard Sep 4) and Google DeepMind (AlphaProof Nexus, 9 Erdos problems, May 2026) are at or near the same level; the gap between labs is months.
cap-research-math-internal.why: About 9% of posed problems survived into result families; cost is roughly three hours of Pro-tier thinking compute per result, and OpenAI put its ten August results at ~$2,000 of tokens at GPT Sol API rates (~$200 per published success on lab-chosen problems; failed attempts are not counted, so at ~9% survival the cost per accepted result could be ~10x higher). The difficulty ladder moved from IMO gold (Jul 2025) to Erdos-type open problems (spring 2026) to famous conjectures (UGC, forced Navier-Stokes blowup, Sep-Oct 2026) in about 15 months. Every downstream node in the space tree starts here.
cap-research-math-internal.strongest_case_small: Nothing in the release is above T3; the only audit of an earlier OpenAI release covered ten results. The 4,000 problems were chosen by the lab and skew discrete and finitary; PDE (3 of 16 families formalized), dynamics (2 of 12) and topology (1 of 18) are thin, which is where space physics lives. Calegari scored the release at roughly 5 of 100 points on his own list of hard number-theory problems.
cap-research-math-internal.signpost: An independent Comparator run plus statement audit on a headline family (102 or 362) moving it to T4; a published error rate from a random sample of 30 or more families.
cap-research-math-internal.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor + skeptic: $200-per-result figure qualified (selected successes, failed attempts excluded). Year and band unchanged.

cap-research-math-public.title: Research-grade math for outside teams
cap-research-math-public.description: An outside engineering team can buy, on demand, mathematics at roughly the October-2026 internal level (journal-grade open problems, proofs with Lean output) through a public or trusted-access product, for under ~$1,000 per result.
cap-research-math-public.status_oct2026: Partly. Public GPT-6 Astra (paid users from Sep 4, 2026) solved 106 ErdosBench open problems (43 completely) and became the first model to solve any FrontierMath Erdos problem (2 of 68; Epoch, Sep 3, 2026) - research math at the easy end. AlphaEvolve has been generally available to Google Cloud customers since Jul 9, 2026. The model behind openai/math is unreleased; GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld on Sep 29, 2026; Anthropic's Mythos tier is restricted. OpenAI's ChatGPT for Academic Researchers gives 10,000 researchers free access now and 100,000 by 2027 (Jul 29, 2026). OpenAI's chief scientist says the lab does not prioritize math in public models (Sep 10, 2026).
cap-research-math-public.why: The reveal-to-release lag for Astra was about five weeks (Aug 1 reveal, Sep 4 public), but the most capable versions get held back for safety (GPT-6.1 Astra) or restricted (Mythos), and US pre-release review adds 12-30 days. Under S2 a public model matches the Oct-2026 internal level 6-12 months out (mid-to-late 2027); under S1, 12-18 months (2028). At least four labs compete (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, SpaceXAI with 35-58-day Grok cadence) and open-weight followers trail by about a year, which forces release. The binding gate is release governance (lab safety holds plus government review), coded here as regulatory. Regulator cap not applied: government pre-release review (12-30 days) delays release but does not accept or certify results, and the public-release dependency is the scenario definition itself (S1 2028, S2/S3 2027); GPT-6 Astra (public Sep 4 2026, FrontierMath Erdos 2/68) is a partial public equivalent.
cap-research-math-public.strongest_case_small: Labs may keep their best math models internal: OpenAI says its urgency is recursive self-improvement and alignment, the Advisory Group asks labs not to test open problems on proprietary models, and dual-use cyber capability (not math) drives the holds. Public models are jagged - strong on discrete Erdos-style problems, weaker on PDE analysis - so an engineering team may get less than the catalog suggests.
cap-research-math-public.signpost: Any public model scoring 20% or more on FrontierMath Erdos (GPT-6 Astra: 3% in Sep 2026) by end-2027 (S2 on track) versus under 10% (S1); a lab launching a research-math API tier with Lean output.
cap-research-math-public.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor: explains why the regulatory-gate and public-model caps are not applied to this root node. Year and band unchanged.

cap-autoformalization.title: AI turns math into machine-checked proofs at scale
cap-autoformalization.description: Agents turn informal proofs into Lean and complete them, at the scale of hundreds of papers or a multi-million-line project in weeks.
cap-autoformalization.status_oct2026: Exists for discrete and algebraic math. openai/math formalized the main results of 162 papers by agent (unchecked, T3). Anthropic's FLT formalization (about 13M lines of Lean, 29,500 theorems in the final proof, 11 days) passed Buzzard's Comparator run (Sep 4, 2026). Meta's ATLAS reportedly autoformalized 26 textbooks into ~630,000 lines of Lean using 183B+ tokens (May 2026, secondary report via 36Kr). Weak where Mathlib is thin: PDE 3 of 16 families, dynamics 2 of 12, topology 1 of 18.
cap-autoformalization.premise_tier: T3 for the openai/math evidence (agent-written Lean for 127 families, unchecked by outsiders; 362); T4 only for evidence outside openai/math (FLT in Lean, Comparator-checked, Sep 2026)
cap-autoformalization.why: Lean is hard to fool once the statement is right, and proof labor is no longer scarce: the same pipeline that formalized 162 papers can prove properties of flight algorithms and code (P2). 362 shows agents can build missing PDE infrastructure for a single result. What remains scarce is formal semantics for real code and correct statements.
cap-autoformalization.strongest_case_small: Coverage is uneven exactly where space needs it (PDE, numerics, stochastic processes). Agent-written Lean can be enormous and slow to check: two of three openai/math targets exceeded a 7 GiB memory cap in an outside run. A proof of the wrong statement is worthless.
cap-autoformalization.signpost: An agent formalizes a PDE or numerical-analysis paper end to end, including missing library infrastructure, with an outside Comparator pass.
cap-autoformalization.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: nothing in openai/math is above T3 as of 2026-10-07; the T4 label applies only to non-openai/math evidence. Year and band unchanged (capability.json anchor). B-trunk: band set by the capability.json scenario parametrization (S2 is the client premise), not by the fw-horizon-scorecard pathway default (P2 Medium); this node is a capability milestone, not an implication of a catalog result.
