cap-applied-math.title: AI does research-grade applied math
cap-applied-math.description: Engineers routinely get, from AI, well-posedness and stability analyses of their own models, numerical schemes with certified error bounds, uncertainty quantification with guarantees, and optimal-control results with proofs, for low-dimensional and reduced models; certified bounds for realistic 3D multiphysics remain too loose to use.
cap-applied-math.status_oct2026: Not yet a routine service. The catalog shows applied-adjacent depth: 362 Vlasov-Maxwell [L, T3]; 363 and 364 Boltzmann (T1); 372 elasticity inverse problem (T1); 365 boundary problems [L: scalar-conductivity nonuniqueness T3; metric-connection recovery headline T1]; plus the separate forced Navier-Stokes blowup claim (Sep 8). These were lab-posed problems, PDE formalization is thin, and nothing in the release touches UQ, stiff numerics or radiation transport.
cap-applied-math.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 362 is [L] T3 and 365's formalized conductivity-nonuniqueness part is T3 (its recovery headline T1); 363, 364 and 372 are T1 (conditional), supporting evidence only
cap-applied-math.why: Most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems (tl-position-4); what it adds is messy context: empirical coefficients, real boundary conditions, and a need for explicit constants and rates. A stability proof for a specific control law or a convergence bound for a specific solver is a week-to-month task for a specialist (general), which fits inside the S2 task horizon by 2027-28. Under S1, diffusion waits on public access (2028) plus domain workflows. This is mostly 'solved in principle but expert-scarce' work, so on-demand expertise is the unlock.
cap-applied-math.strongest_case_small: Engineers already get adequate answers from simulation and test without proofs; certified bounds for realistic 3D multiphysics are often too loose to use; the gain is confidence, not performance (tl-position-2). Several catalog premises are T1, so implications resting on 363, 364 and 372 are conditional.
cap-applied-math.signpost: A NASA, ESA or major-prime technical report, or an AIAA paper, in which an AI-produced stability proof, convergence proof or certified error bound decides a design question.
cap-applied-math.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: premise label split so the T1 rule does not misfire; scope limited to reduced models (node's own strongest case). Skeptic: Lean is needed for trust, not to produce applied math, so cap-autoformalization hard -> soft. Year and band unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): 365 tier wording aligned with the other branches (formal part T3, recovery headline T1). lettered citation 'position a' replaced with the KB position id tl-position-4. lettered citation 'position d' replaced with the KB position id tl-position-2.

cap-physics-theory.title: AI builds validated physics theory
cap-physics-theory.description: AI derives closures, reduced-order models with proofs, and plasma, materials or combustion theory that beat the human state of the art on held-out experimental data.
cap-physics-theory.status_oct2026: Not yet. The catalog touches foundations (364 Boltzmann from Newtonian gases, T1; 278 Kohn-Sham ensemble representability fails, T1; 263 ionization bounds [L, T3]), but no AI-built closure has displaced an engineering model. The data-driven precedent is weather: ECMWF's AI forecast system went operational on Feb 25, 2025, beating physics models on many measures (up to 20% on cyclone tracks) at ~1,000x less energy per forecast - an emulator, not new theory.
cap-physics-theory.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 364 and 278 are T1 (conditional) and 263 is T3, supporting evidence only
cap-physics-theory.why: Theory-building needs month-to-year research horizons (S2: 2028-29) and validation data. Where databases exist (turbulence DNS, DFT databases, plasma experiments) validation is a cognitive task and S2 delivers by 2029; where it needs new experiments, the physical clock binds. Under S3 closed-loop labs supply validation data from ~2028. These are genuinely open problems, unlike most nodes in this tree.
cap-physics-theory.strongest_case_small: Turbulence and anomalous-transport closures have resisted 60+ years because the missing information is not in the equations; learned closures have historically failed out of distribution. The catalog premises here are T1, so the chain is conditional.
cap-physics-theory.signpost: An AI-derived closure or reduced model adopted in a production code (NASA FUN3D, US3D, or a major plasma code) after blind validation on data it never saw.
cap-physics-theory.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: band is set by the shared capability parametrization (Low/Medium/High), not by families 364, 278 and 263; relabelled so the T1 rule does not misfire. Year and band unchanged (capability.json anchor). B-trunk: S3 High -> Medium and S3 2028 -> 2029: the P6 default is Low, validation data run on the physical clock (experiments 1.3-1.5x in S3), and blind validation in a production code takes 1-2-year V&V cycles that cannot fit in 2028 when S3 only begins to diverge. S2/S3 Medium stays one band above the P6 default because the band is set by the capability parametrization.
cap-physics-theory.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (+ auditor P6-override flag): S3 2028 -> 2029, S3 High -> Medium. Cascade with autofix to five S3 dependents.

cap-design-optimization.title: AI multiphysics design with guarantees
cap-design-optimization.description: AI runs end-to-end multiphysics design optimization (aero-thermal-structural-propulsion) with constraint satisfaction and model-relative error bounds inside validated envelopes (physical margins still come from test), producing designs that pass existing engineering review gates.
cap-design-optimization.status_oct2026: Early. Generative structural design and AI-generated engine geometry exist (general); AlphaEvolve is generally available for problems with checkable objectives (Jul 9, 2026). Chip design is the leading indicator: Cadence reported a fully autonomous design agent (Jun 2026), Synopsys and AMD launched agents (Oct 2, 2026), and OpenAI-Synopsys announced an EDA-operating model (Oct 6, 2026) - all secondary press reports.
cap-design-optimization.why: EDA shows the pattern: when the simulator is trusted and the objective is checkable, agents already do weeks of design work. Space multiphysics simulators are less trusted (turbulence, ablation, combustion), so guarantees hold only inside validated envelopes. Under S2, applied math (2027) and engineering-grade agents give design loops by 2028; learned emulators speed the loops but are not required (EDA agents and adjoint CFD optimization run on the real solvers); under S1, 2030.
cap-design-optimization.strongest_case_small: Design quality is bounded by model fidelity, and optimizers exploit model error. Launch-vehicle performance is set mostly by the rocket equation and propellant chemistry, leaving single-digit percent gains; the hardware still has to be built and tested.
cap-design-optimization.signpost: A prime or NewSpace firm publicly attributes a flown or hot-fired hardware design (engine, structure, heat shield) to an AI design loop whose model-based margins its review board accepted.
cap-design-optimization.calibration_note: B-trunk: band set by the capability.json scenario parametrization (S2 is the client premise), not by the fw-horizon-scorecard pathway default (P1->P6; P6 default Low); this node is a capability milestone, not an implication of a catalog result.
cap-design-optimization.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: guarantees are model-relative (optimizers exploit model error), and emulators are not required, so learned-emulators hard -> soft. Auditor: pathway-override note. Years and bands unchanged (S2 2028 is the client premise). | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): soft edge from frontier-scalable-global-certificates (B-math-frontier request 3).

cap-autonomous-labs.title: AI-run closed-loop labs at scale
cap-autonomous-labs.description: AI plans, runs and interprets experiments on robotic lab hardware, closing design-build-test loops for materials, chemistry and components at 10x or more the throughput of human-run labs.
cap-autonomous-labs.status_oct2026: Early. Periodic Labs launched with a $300M seed (Sep 30, 2025); Radical AI and others run self-driving materials labs; DOE's Genesis Mission, which includes autonomous laboratories at national labs (general), selected its first 278 projects on Jul 22, 2026 (largest a three-year $60M nuclear-energy award); the widely reported ~$5B figure is a multi-agency commitment headline, not DOE lab money (unverified). No space-qualified material has come out of a closed loop yet.
cap-autonomous-labs.why: Cognition is not the lab bottleneck; robots, synthesis throughput and characterization are. Under S2 and S3 the planning agent is effectively free, so capital (roughly $10-100M per lab, general) and the physics of synthesis bind. Solution chemistry and thin films speed up most; bulk aerospace materials least.
cap-autonomous-labs.strongest_case_small: Superalloys, UHTCs and ablators need furnaces, bulk processing and days per sample; creep, oxidation and radiation tests run in real time (years of creep data cannot be compressed). Qualification, not discovery, sets the insertion timeline for space materials.
cap-autonomous-labs.signpost: An autonomous lab reports a new material entering a space-qualification program; Genesis Mission autonomous-lab throughput milestones.
cap-autonomous-labs.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: research-math-public hard -> soft (labs such as Periodic Labs and Radical AI run without it; the node itself says cognition is not the lab bottleneck). Auditor: Genesis Mission figure corrected. Year and band unchanged.

infra-mathlib-applied.title: Lean libraries for the math engineers use
infra-mathlib-applied.description: Mathlib or companion libraries cover Sobolev spaces, weak solutions, standard PDE energy estimates, ODE and numerical-analysis theory, and stochastic processes well enough that applied results formalize routinely.
infra-mathlib-applied.status_oct2026: Thin. Mathlib has ~138,000 definitions, ~290,000 theorems and 772 contributors (stats page, accessed Oct 7, 2026). openai/math formalized 3 of 16 PDE families and 2 of 12 dynamics families versus 5 of 6 logic families. 362 [L, T3] shows agents can build what one result needs.
infra-mathlib-applied.why: Agents now write library code at FLT scale, so proof labor is not the gate; good abstractions and community review are. Under S2, agent-built applied libraries mature in 2027 and are integrated into Mathlib by 2028; under S1, review bandwidth stretches this to 2030. Every P2 chain that touches continuous physics (GNC stability, plasma, CFD error bounds) waits on this node. Companion libraries may reach partial coverage in 2027 (three groups each built Sobolev theory in Lean in 2026; Urban built 130k lines of formal topology in two weeks for ~$100, per frontier research), but routine formalization of applied results needs reviewed, maintained coverage, which the S2 premise dates to 2028; S3 equals S2 until 2028, and review does not compress before the recursion starts.
infra-mathlib-applied.strongest_case_small: Mathlib's maintainers and review process are the bottleneck and may resist agent-written code; parallel libraries could fragment the ecosystem; formal PDE theory still won't cover the empirical closures engineers actually use.
infra-mathlib-applied.signpost: Mathlib or a Lean FRO-backed library merges Sobolev embeddings, Lax-Milgram and standard energy estimates; an applied PDE family from the catalog (363, 364 or 372) receives a Comparator-checked formalization.
infra-mathlib-applied.calibration_note: B-trunk: band set by the capability.json scenario parametrization (S2 is the client premise), not by the fw-horizon-scorecard pathway default (P2 Medium); this node is a capability milestone, not an implication of a catalog result.
infra-mathlib-applied.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 2027 -> 2028. Advocate's S2 2027 (companion libraries) rejected: S2 2028 for applied Lean libraries is the client premise; the evidence is kept in why as a 2027 signpost. P2-override note added.

infra-verified-numerics.title: Verified floating-point and numerics toolchain
infra-verified-numerics.description: A toolchain that proves floating-point programs and numerical methods (ODE integrators, linear solvers, convex optimizers, filters) meet stated error bounds, from the mathematics down to compiled code.
infra-verified-numerics.status_oct2026: Pieces exist outside Lean - Coq's Flocq and CompCert, Gappa, FPTaylor, Frama-C (general) - but there is no integrated stack and Lean lacks a mature IEEE-754 plus numerical-analysis library. The catalog contains no numerics results, and the release does not touch numerical analysis of stiff systems.
infra-verified-numerics.why: Verified numerics is solved in principle but expert-scarce: a round-off and truncation analysis of a GNC loop takes a specialist weeks to months (general). Agents that already write millions of lines of Lean remove the labor; integration with existing Coq tools or a Lean port is a 1-2 year engineering job under S2.
infra-verified-numerics.strongest_case_small: Proofs on real flight code stall on compiler semantics, nonstandard FPUs on rad-hard processors and environment models, not on the numerics; many GNC teams already use fixed-point or conservative margins that make the proof unnecessary.
infra-verified-numerics.signpost: An agent-generated, machine-checked round-off bound for a flight Kalman filter or guidance law reported by NASA, ESA, AdaCore, Galois or a prime.
infra-verified-numerics.calibration_note: B-trunk: band set by the capability.json scenario parametrization (S2 is the client premise), not by the fw-horizon-scorecard pathway default (P2 Medium); this node is a capability milestone, not an implication of a catalog result.
infra-verified-numerics.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 2027 -> 2028 (a 1-2 year integration job cannot finish in the year its prerequisite cap-applied-math appears; S3 equals S2 until 2028). P2-override note added.

infra-tool-qualification.title: Regulators accept AI-produced proofs
infra-tool-qualification.description: A certification authority or its delegate (an FAA ACO or DER under DO-178C with DO-333 and DO-330, a NASA center technical authority under NPR 7150.2, ESA product assurance under ECSS, or Space Force) accepts a software plan (PSAC or software development plan; an SOI-1-equivalent agreement) that takes verification credit for proofs whose contracts, invariants and proof scripts were written by AI agents and discharged by a qualified checker. The likeliest first route is an already-qualified or qualifiable checker (SPARK GNATprove, Frama-C WP, Astree); qualifying a new small kernel (Lean or Comparator) is a later, separate step that the dependents in this branch do not need. The agent is an untrusted generator that needs no tool qualification; human obligations shrink to reviewing specifications and justifying assumptions.
infra-tool-qualification.status_oct2026: No credit yet for AI-generated proofs. DO-333 already credits formal methods; FAA and EASA AI guidance addresses AI inside aircraft, not AI as a development or verification tool (general). The plausible route is 'checker, not generator': qualify the Lean kernel or Comparator and treat the agent as untrusted. Evidence for the route in 2026, not credit: AI coding agents wrote a bare-metal Ada/SPARK security stack whose 49,280 proof obligations GNATprove discharged at a claimed 20-40x lower supervision cost, and the agents tried to bypass weak checks, which is why the checker, not the agent, must be the trust boundary (Philipp, arXiv 2607.14340, Jul 2026 preprint). AdaCore released GNAT Foundry Intersection, an open-source agent workflow gated by SPARK proof, requirements-based tests and MC/DC, which AdaCore calls a demonstration rather than a certification process (Sep 14, 2026).
infra-tool-qualification.why: Aviation software standards turn over on 5-10+ year cycles (DO-178B 1992, DO-178C 2011), but the checker route needs no new standard: under DO-330 a tool needs qualification only when its output is not otherwise verified, and here a qualified checker verifies the AI's output. 'Achieved' means plan acceptance, which is the client's base-case premise for first certification credit (S2 2030, S3 2029). A completed certification that banks the credit follows one DO-178C-scale project later, about 2-4 years (S2 about 2032 or later), so dependents that need a specific program to accept the evidence lag this node. Upside: the verification domain dated DO-333 credit through existing checkers to 2028 in S2; a DO-178C or NPR 7150.2 plan accepted in 2028-29 would pull this node forward a year. Verified floating point and AI-drafted specs accelerate but do not gate it: credit for proofs of FDIR logic, parsers or mode machines needs no verified numerics, and human-written, human-reviewed specs qualify. Capped at Medium because it needs regulator acceptance.
infra-tool-qualification.strongest_case_small: Regulators move slowly and specifications become the bottleneck. Uncrewed commercial space needs no software certification at all, so this gate matters mainly for crewed vehicles, aviation-adjacent systems and NASA human-rating.
infra-tool-qualification.signpost: A PSAC, software development plan or ESA product-assurance plan accepted with verification credit for AI-written proofs checked by GNATprove, Frama-C WP or Astree (in 2028-29 this would pull the node forward a year); later, a DO-330 qualification kit for a Lean or Comparator checker.
infra-tool-qualification.merge_note: A1: merged verif-checker-not-generator (same achievement: certification credit for AI-written proofs via a qualified checker). verif rated it 2029/2028/2028 Medium; capability 2031+/2030/2029 Low/Medium/Medium. Kept the capability id (shared tier-0) and the scenario parametrization ('regulator credit for AI proofs' S2 2030 is the client's base-case premise). verif's argument is kept as the upside signpost: under DO-330 qualification is needed only for tools whose output is not otherwise verified, so AI-written SPARK/Frama-C proofs checked by existing qualified checkers need only plan acceptance (software certification plan, SOI audits); a DO-178C or NPR 7150.2 project taking such credit in 2028 would pull this node forward a year. Airbus A380 unit-test replacement (2002) and DO-333 show the mechanism. Capped at Medium (regulator acceptance). Dependents verif-afss-part450 and verif-new-entrant-advantage were moved to stay after it.
infra-tool-qualification.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic + advocate (definition): 'achieved' is now plan acceptance on the checker-not-generator route, with completed certification 2-4 years later; Lean-kernel qualification named as a later step dependents do not need. Skeptic: infra-verified-numerics and verif-spec-engineering moved from hard to soft (FDIR or parser proofs need no verified floating point; human-written specs qualify). Advocate's split into a separate verif-checker-route-credit node at S2 2029 rejected: it re-creates verif-checker-not-generator, which A1 merged into this node, and it would move the client's base-case premise (first credit S2 2030). Advocate's 2026 evidence added to status. Years and bands unchanged.

verif-independent-check.title: Independent checks of AI math
verif-independent-check.description: Outside groups run Comparator on the labs' Lean challenges and audit formal statements against the manuscripts, moving key results from T3 to T4.
verif-independent-check.status_oct2026: Not yet for any openai/math family. Kingy AI (Oct 6, 2026) ran Comparator on three challenge targets on an 8 GiB VM: one passed twice, two hit a 7 GiB memory cap; same operator, no statement audit, so no tier change. Hexagon launched Oct 6 (beta; Buzzard on its advisory board) but does not require formalization and holds no OpenAI deposits yet. Precedent: Buzzard's Comparator run on Anthropic's FLT (Sep 4, 2026).
verif-independent-check.why: A Comparator run takes about a minute for small targets but exceeded a 7 GiB memory cap on others (Kingy AI, Oct 6); the statement audit needs a domain expert for days per family. Headline Lean families (102, 362) should reach T4 within one to three months; the long tail of 127 formalized families and the 245 unformalized ones takes years. Under S2, AI-assisted statement audits speed the tail. Headline checks happen in the shared present and do not depend on the scenario's capability curve, so S1 equals S2 and S3.
verif-independent-check.strongest_case_small: Human bandwidth is the limit: a few dozen qualified readers per field and 722 manuscripts at once. Independent machine checks confirm only formal statements, and statement gaps already exist (the quasi-RH challenge targets zeta only).
verif-independent-check.signpost: Hexagon, Buzzard's group or another expert team publishes a Comparator pass plus statement audit for 102 or 362.
verif-independent-check.calibration_note: B-trunk: band set by the capability.json scenario parametrization (S2 is the client premise), not by the fw-horizon-scorecard pathway default (P2 Medium); this node is a human-bandwidth milestone, not an implication of a catalog result.
verif-independent-check.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor: S1 2027 -> 2026 (human checks of a released repo are scenario-independent); Comparator run-time claim corrected to the only outside run; P2-override note added.

capability-horizon-compounding.title: Month-long autonomous research tasks
capability-horizon-compounding.description: AI agents complete, at 50% reliability or better, technical research tasks that take a human expert a full work-month (~170 hours), up from about a work-week in late 2026.
capability-horizon-compounding.status_oct2026: METR measured frontier 50% time horizons of ~16-20 hours in Feb-Mar 2026 and says its suite cannot reliably measure above ~16 hours (Frontier Risk Report, May 19, 2026); GPT-5.6 Sol was ~11.3 hours (95% CI 5-40, flagged unreliable; Jun 26, 2026). Long-run doubling ~7 months since 2019, ~4 months in 2024-25 (METR, Jul 14, 2025). In mathematics the internal model returns, in ~3 hours of compute, results that take experts weeks to months.
capability-horizon-compounding.why: Parametrization: start at ~40 h (one work-week) in Oct 2026, one 7-month doubling past the measured 16-20 h. S1 doubles every 12-18 months: ~76 h end-2027, ~230 h end-2029, ~700 h end-2031 (~4 work-months). S2 doubles every 6-9 months: ~150 h end-2027 (range 120-200), ~1,300 h end-2029, ~12,000 h end-2031 (2-26 work-years across the 6-9 month range). S3 follows S2 to end-2027 then doubles every ~3 months, so the metric stops being meaningful around 2029. The month threshold is the point where a whole applied-math project (model, analysis, proof, code) fits in one autonomous run. Crossing ~170 h needs 2.09 doublings from ~40 h: about mid-2029 in S1 (25-38 months), about early 2028 in S2 (13-19 months; ~150 h at end-2027), and the same in S3, which equals S2 until 2028. S1 reaches ~700 h by 2031, so High.
capability-horizon-compounding.strongest_case_small: METR suites saturate and measure well-specified software tasks; research is open-ended and judgment-heavy; 80%-reliability horizons are several times shorter than 50% horizons, and engineering needs high reliability. Capability is jagged across domains.
capability-horizon-compounding.signpost: A successor horizon suite (METR or Epoch) reporting a frontier 50% horizon of 80 hours or more by end-2027 (S2 on track) or under 40 hours (S1).
capability-horizon-compounding.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Advocate + auditor: S1 2030 -> 2029 and S1 Medium -> High (the node's own parametrization crosses 170 h in 2029 and reaches ~700 h by 2031). Auditor + skeptic: S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 equals S2 until 2028). Advocate's S2 2027 rejected: it relies on METR's ~4-month doubling, faster than S2's 6-9 months.

capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.title: AI speeds up its own development 3x
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.description: AI systems accelerate frontier AI research and engineering, including chip design and software stacks, by 3x or more overall - the hinge between S2 and S3.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.status_oct2026: METR estimates ~1.5x acceleration during Claude Opus 5.5's development, a ~30% chance of 2x, and judges it unlikely to fully automate AI R&D (Sep 22, 2026). OpenAI's chief scientist names recursive self-improvement and automated alignment research as priorities (Sep 10, 2026). Agentic EDA (Cadence, Synopsys, OpenAI-Synopsys) applies the same loop to chips.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.why: Software-side acceleration is bounded by compute for experiments. Epoch: frontier training compute grows ~5x/yr, compute stock ~3.4x/yr, GW-scale sites take ~2.1 years at ~$38B per GW; Anthropic alone lists ~$518B of decade-long compute obligations. S3 assumes acceleration past 3x by 2028 converts into ~10x/yr effective efficiency gains, collapsing the cost of cognitive work; even then the recursion runs on fabs and power, which are a physical clock.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.strongest_case_small: Amdahl's law inside AI labs: experiments need GPUs, and CoWoS, HBM and power supply chains are physical. METR reports weak judgment and foresight. Safety holds (GPT-6.1 Astra) and government review slow deployment even when capability races ahead.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.signpost: Lab system cards or METR reporting 2x+ uplift with high confidence; frontier release cadence under 30 days across several labs; AI-designed accelerator tape-outs.

capability-cost-collapse.title: A research result costs less than an engineer-day
capability-cost-collapse.description: The public price of a research-grade math result (problem posed to checked proof or derivation) falls below ~$1,000 and then below ~$100, cheaper than one day of a specialist's time.
capability-cost-collapse.status_oct2026: Internally ~3 hours of Pro-tier compute per result; OpenAI put Astra's ten August results at ~$2,000 at GPT Sol API rates (~$200 per published success; failed attempts excluded). GPT-6 Astra is public in ChatGPT and the API (Sep 2026), with a new $500/month Pro tier and a cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol reported as near-Astra at a fifth of the price (press). Epoch: price for a fixed capability level fell 9-900x per year in 2022-25; AI chip price-performance improves ~49%/yr.
capability-cost-collapse.why: About $200 per published result on lab-chosen problems; failed attempts are not included (about 9% of posed problems survived in openai/math), so per accepted result the cost could be about $2,000, and 1,000 results a year cost ~$0.2-2M (one to ten engineers) before checking, which dominates either way. Illustratively, an Oct-2026-grade result falls to ~$20-70 by 2028 in S1 (about 2-4x a year, slower than Epoch's historical 9-900x) and ~$1-10 in S2 (about 6-20x a year). Price stops being a gate for math in every scenario; access, trust and integration remain.
capability-cost-collapse.strongest_case_small: The cost of checking dominates the cost of producing: a $200 proof that needs a $20,000 expert audit is a $20,000 result. Frontier tasks get longer, so spend per frontier task may stay flat even as fixed-capability prices fall.
capability-cost-collapse.signpost: Lab price sheets for long-horizon reasoning tiers; enterprise contracts that bundle research math with Lean output; space-firm disclosures of AI analysis spend.
capability-cost-collapse.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: per-result cost qualified (selected successes; ~10x higher per accepted result; checking dominates). Auditor arithmetic: S1 rate restated to match ~$20-70 by 2028. Advocate: soft edges to adoption and dev-capital-cut so the node is no longer dangling. Year and band unchanged.

capability-controlled-data-access.title: Frontier math on export-controlled and classified networks
capability-controlled-data-access.description: Research-grade models run inside ITAR/EAR-compliant, CUI and classified environments, so space primes, Space Force and NRO programs can pose problems with export-controlled engineering data.
capability-controlled-data-access.status_oct2026: GenAI.mil is available to the ~3M-strong DoD workforce, with ~1.7M users onboarded, with a ChatGPT-based 'ChatGPT Mil', Grok and Gemini (Fortune, Sep 1, 2026; ~500,000 power users per DefenseScoop, Sep 23); OpenAI, Google, xAI and others were cleared for classified networks (May 2026). The DoD designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk, upheld by the DC Circuit on Sep 25, 2026, barring contractors from using Claude on DoD work - the lab behind the only Comparator-checked mega-formalization (FLT). Civil NASA is unaffected: JPL used Claude to plan two Perseverance drives (Dec 2025).
capability-controlled-data-access.why: Much space engineering data (propulsion, GNC, hypersonics, defense payloads) is ITAR-controlled, and P1 works best when teams pose problems with real data. Accredited government clouds have trailed commercial releases by months (general). No US export control restricts API access to closed models today; controls target chips (general), and policy can still remove a lab overnight. The research-math tier needs its own IL6/TS accreditation after public release (mid-to-late 2027 in S2, 2028 in S1), so S2/S3 2028 and S1 2029. Regulator cap not applied and gate coded as adoption: labs already hold classified-network clearances (May 2026), so accrediting a newer model is a delay, not acceptance of AI results. S1 is Medium because public access arrives only in 2028 plus the accreditation lag.
capability-controlled-data-access.strongest_case_small: The math itself is not controlled: engineers can pose sanitized problems without technical data. Defense adoption is limited by security culture and model-weight custody more than availability. Policy volatility cuts both ways.
capability-controlled-data-access.signpost: A research-math-capable model accredited at IL6 or Top Secret; a change to the Anthropic designation; State Department or DDTC guidance on AI processing of ITAR technical data.
capability-controlled-data-access.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: years +1 (accredited clouds trail public release by months; Anthropic exclusion removes a candidate). Auditor: GenAI.mil figure corrected (available to ~3M, 1.7M users); S1 band High -> Medium; regulatory gate with High band resolved by recoding the gate as adoption with an explicit note. Its hard edge into capability-engineering-adoption is now soft.

revisions.from: Frontier math on ITAR and classified networks

capability-open-weights-math.title: Open-weight model at research-math level
capability-open-weights-math.description: An open-weight model matches the October-2026 internal research-math level, removing lab release decisions and access controls as a gate for everyone, including adversaries.
capability-open-weights-math.status_oct2026: Not yet. Press frames Moonshot's Kimi K3 as Astra's competitor (Aug 2026); the US threatened to blacklist Moonshot over distillation (Jul 22, 2026). Open models have historically trailed the closed frontier by about a year (general).
capability-open-weights-math.why: With a ~12-month open-weight lag, the Oct-2026 internal level reaches open weights in late 2027 to 2028 under S2. For space this matters two ways: on-premises use with ITAR data without cloud accreditation, and competitors and adversaries getting the same on-demand math for trajectory design, constellation tasking and weapons-relevant analysis.
capability-open-weights-math.strongest_case_small: Open models may lag more at the frontier of math reasoning (RL compute is expensive), and distillation crackdowns could widen the gap; most engineering math does not need the frontier anyway.
capability-open-weights-math.signpost: An open-weight model solving FrontierMath Erdos problems or matching GPT-6 Astra's ErdosBench score.
capability-open-weights-math.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 2027 -> 2028 (open weights trail public models ~12 months; S3 equals S2 until 2028). Advocate: soft edges to adoption (on-premises ITAR use) and new entrants (foreign access).

capability-cheap-trust.title: Trust in days: automated statement audits
capability-cheap-trust.description: AI-assisted pipelines check that a formal statement matches the engineering claim (definitions, hypotheses, units, scope), cross-check proofs with independent agents and produce human-readable audit trails, cutting the cost of trusting an AI result from expert-weeks to days. Covers adoption by journals, Hexagon, labs and engineering teams, not regulator acceptance (see physclock-credibility-evidence-standard).
capability-cheap-trust.status_oct2026: Statement gaps are real: openai/math's quasi-RH challenge targets only zeta; the outside run of the Pi Exponent target found its formal statement omits a manuscript consequence. Human review does not scale to 722 manuscripts. AGMAI (Sep 29) and the Simons Institute report (Sep 28) call for disclosure and lineage norms.
capability-cheap-trust.why: In engineering, statement gaps become specification errors, the main residual risk in formally verified systems (general). An adversarial auditor model plus Lean plus a human sign-off turns P1 answers into evidence a design review can accept. This is the node that moves the bottleneck from proving to understanding (tr-position-5) back toward engineering. Engineering claims involve continuous math (PDE, numerics, stochastic processes) where Lean coverage stays thin until infra-mathlib-applied (S2 2028; best agent 34.9% on StochBench, per frontier research), and an audit pipeline worth relying on needs a track record that starts only with public research-math access (mid-to-late 2027 in S2), so S2 and S3 are 2028. The final judgment stays human, so days, not hours.
capability-cheap-trust.strongest_case_small: Generator and auditor models can share blind spots; the final judgment of whether a property is the right one is irreducibly human and domain-specific.
capability-cheap-trust.signpost: Hexagon or a journal adopting AI-assisted statement audits as standard; an engineering team publishing an AI audit trail for a continuous-math claim (PDE, numerics or a stochastic model).
capability-cheap-trust.calibration_note: B-trunk: band set by the capability.json scenario parametrization (S2 is the client premise), not by the fw-horizon-scorecard pathway default (P2 Medium); this node is a capability milestone, not an implication of a catalog result.
capability-cheap-trust.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: S2/S3 2027 -> 2028, hours -> days, soft edge from infra-mathlib-applied. Auditor: review-board acceptance moved out of the signpost (that is the Medium-capped regulatory node downstream), scope note added, P2-override note. Bands unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): lettered citation 'position h' replaced with the KB position id tr-position-5.

capability-algorithm-discovery.title: AI-discovered algorithms in space codes
capability-algorithm-discovery.description: AlphaEvolve-style search (a model proposes code, an automatic evaluator scores it) improves practical heuristics and kernels used in space operations and engineering: constellation scheduling, conjunction screening, trajectory solvers, onboard compression, CFD kernels.
capability-algorithm-discovery.status_oct2026: AlphaEvolve's scheduling heuristic recovers ~0.7% of Google's fleet compute, a kernel sped up 23% (1% off Gemini training time) and FlashAttention up to 32.5% (May 14, 2025); generally available to Google Cloud customers since Jul 9, 2026. Unlike the catalog's galactic speedups (107, 130 - no practical gain), these have practical constants. Hardness results (102, 117, 125, all [L], T3) mark where general-purpose gains are capped.
capability-algorithm-discovery.pathway: P1 (public AlphaEvolve-style search on teams' own evaluators; catalog families 102, 117 and 125 act via P3)
capability-algorithm-discovery.why: It needs only an evaluator function, which space operations have (schedule value, screening runtime, compression ratio). For a 10,000-satellite constellation, a few percent of tasking or ground-contact efficiency is worth tens of millions of dollars a year (general). The hardness results (P3) tell teams to stop chasing general solvers and invest in instance structure, which is exactly what evolutionary search exploits.
capability-algorithm-discovery.strongest_case_small: Gains are incremental (single-digit percent); structured instances already solve well with commercial MIP solvers; worst-case ceilings say little about real instances.
capability-algorithm-discovery.signpost: A constellation operator or space agency publishing an AI-discovered heuristic in production with measured gains.
capability-algorithm-discovery.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor: pathway P4 -> P1 (transfer of a generally available tool; the P4 default would cap it at Medium). Band High kept. Advocate's soft edges to comms-hardness-aware-tasking and astro-catalog-scale-screening are outside this branch and passed to those branches in notes.

capability-learned-emulators.title: AI emulators of space physics codes with stated error bounds
capability-learned-emulators.description: The weather-model playbook - train on decades of simulation or reanalysis data, run ~1,000x cheaper - applied to space codes (CFD and aerothermal, plasma, thermosphere, structures), with calibrated uncertainty or error bounds relative to the parent code; using them for margins still requires validation against test or flight data.
capability-learned-emulators.status_oct2026: Weather: ECMWF's AIFS operational Feb 25, 2025, up to 20% better on some measures at ~1,000x less energy, though at 28 km versus 9 km grid spacing. Space: NASA and IBM released the open Surya heliophysics model (Aug 20, 2025; 16% better flare classification, nine years of SDO data) and SuryaBench (Mar 2026). CFD surrogates are common in design exploration but not trusted for margins (general).
capability-learned-emulators.why: Emulators remove the compute cost of design loops and ensembles. Weather moved from research models to operations in about 15 months on the back of 40+ years of reanalysis. Space domains split: where training data can be generated by simulation (CFD, structures, thermal) emulators are data-unconstrained and arrive first; where data come only from nature (one Sun, rare extreme storms, few hypersonic flights) they arrive late and extrapolate poorly. AIFS and Surya were built without research-grade applied math, so AI applied math accelerates this node (code-relative error bounds) rather than gating it; any certificate bounds error against the code, not against physics. Pathway P4 (a faster method with practical constants entering codes); band above the P4 default because the AIFS precedent shows research-to-operations inside ~15 months.
capability-learned-emulators.strongest_case_small: Emulators are only as good as their training data, and extrapolation to new vehicles or extreme storms - exactly where margins matter - is where they fail. Coarser resolution (as with AIFS) can hide local extremes such as peak heating.
capability-learned-emulators.signpost: NOAA SWPC or ESA running an AI model in operations; a launch provider using a surrogate with stated error bounds in flight-readiness analysis.
capability-learned-emulators.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: certified-bounds claim narrowed to code-relative bounds; cap-applied-math hard -> soft. Skeptic + auditor: S3 2027 -> 2028. Auditor: pathway P6 -> P4 with a stated reason for the High band. Bands unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): soft edge from frontier-certified-pde-error (B-math-frontier request 3).

capability-engineering-adoption.title: On-demand applied math in space engineering
capability-engineering-adoption.description: Space engineering organizations routinely pose their own hard analysis problems (stability, bounds, convergence, inverse problems, trade studies) to frontier models and use the checked answers in design reviews.
capability-engineering-adoption.status_oct2026: Early. JPL used Claude to plan two Perseverance drives with human review (Dec 2025); NASA and IBM ran a compressed model on the ISS (May 2026); IEEE Spectrum reports engineers' distrust of non-deterministic outputs (Sep 28, 2026). SpaceX owns a frontier lab (SpaceXAI; Grok releases every 35-58 days) and says its Grok bot will route tasks to the best model, including Claude Opus 5.5 (Oct 7, 2026).
capability-engineering-adoption.why: Most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems: a specialist analysis that takes 2-8 weeks (general) becomes hours plus a check. Vertically integrated firms that own both models and hardware (SpaceX/SpaceXAI) adopt first; primes constrained by ITAR and DoD rules follow 6-12 months later; agencies last. A vertically integrated first mover (SpaceX/SpaceXAI, which routes tasks to the best available model) can use frontier models in internal design work during 2027, but routine use of checked answers in design reviews needs the Oct-2026 level in outside hands (mid-to-late 2027 in S2) plus trust tooling (2028), so S2 stays 2028 and S3, which equals S2 until 2028, moves to 2028. Classified and ITAR access gates only the defense-prime segment, so it accelerates adoption rather than gating it.
capability-engineering-adoption.strongest_case_small: Analysis is rarely on a space program's critical path; answers still need checking; legacy processes, roles and liability slow uptake; AI may expand analysis scope rather than speed programs.
capability-engineering-adoption.signpost: A major prime or NASA center publishing standard work for AI-derived analysis; AIAA papers where an AI-derived proof or bound is used in a flight design.
capability-engineering-adoption.calibration_note: A3: Band logic: hard prerequisites cap-applied-math and capability-cheap-trust are Medium in S1, so S1 High -> Medium.
capability-engineering-adoption.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 2027 -> 2028 and controlled-data-access hard -> soft. Advocate's S2 2027 rejected (debate recorded): the S2 premise starts the 5-10x cognitive multiplier in 2028 and design-review use needs public-level capability plus trust tooling; the first-mover point is kept in why. Advocate soft edges from capability-cost-collapse and capability-open-weights-math added. Cascade: four physclock S3 dependents move to 2028.

capability-ai-eda-space-processor.title: AI-designed radiation-tolerant space processor
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.description: Agentic EDA designs and formally verifies a radiation-tolerant processor, SoC or AI accelerator designed for orbit (error correction, upset-aware layout, selective redundancy); it is taped out and heavy-ion tested, with design and verification credited mainly to agentic EDA.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.status_oct2026: Agentic chip design is moving fast in commercial EDA (Cadence fully autonomous ChipStack design agent, Jun 1 2026; Synopsys autonomous debug and implementation workflows with Microsoft, evaluated by AMD, Jul 27 2026; OpenAI-Synopsys agreement on a chip-design model, Sep 30 2026). Space-targeted accelerators are in co-design (Nvidia Space-1 Vera Rubin module, Mar 2026; a SpaceX version of the VR72 per Musk, Oct 1 2026; Musk has said Tesla's AI7/Dojo3 is aimed at space-based compute, press reports, unverified here). Space processors lag commercial nodes by roughly a decade (general).
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.why: Design and verification (12-24 months for a rad-hard SoC, general) compress several-fold; fabrication (3-4 months per run), scarce heavy-ion beam time and, for traditional space parts, QML-class qualification (1-2 years) do not. Orbital compute adds a funded commercial customer with no certifying regulator, which raises the odds of an AI-designed space accelerator, but credit to agentic EDA for an Nvidia or Tesla part is unlikely to be disclosed. First tape-out in 2029-30 under S2; flight qualification of traditional rad-hard parts after 2031. Chain (S2): research-grade math public 2027 -> AI multiphysics design with guarantees and agentic EDA (cap-design-optimization, 2028) plus agent-written hardware proofs (verif-hardware-proof-agents, 2028) -> a radiation-tolerant SoC designed and formally verified 2028-29 -> tape-out (3-4 months per run) and heavy-ion test 2029-30 -> credited first silicon 2030 (Medium; disclosure of the AI share is the main risk).
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.strongest_case_small: Space is moving to COTS processors with system-level mitigation, the rad-hard market is small, and qualification rather than design sets the schedule.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.signpost: A rad-hard SoC tape-out credited mainly to agentic EDA, with published heavy-ion test results.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor: EDA dates corrected to the auditor's primary sources (Jul 27 and Sep 30 2026; the earlier dates came from a news-search RSS feed). Advocate: description broadened to include accelerators designed for orbit (commercial customer, no regulator). Advocate's S2 2030 -> 2029 and S3 Medium -> High rejected: zero lag behind cap-design-optimization (2028) plus fab and beam time, and attribution 'mainly to agentic EDA' is unlikely to be disclosed. Years and bands unchanged.

capability-ai-native-spacecraft.title: Spacecraft engineered mostly by AI flies
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.description: An operational spacecraft whose design analyses, trade studies and flight-software verification artifacts were majority AI-generated (with human review) reaches orbit and operates.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.status_oct2026: Not yet. Ingredients exist piecemeal: AI-generated engine and structural geometry, agentic coding, JPL drive planning, agentic chip design.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.why: Chain (S2): engineering adoption 2028 -> smallsat design-complete -> build, integration and environmental test in 12-18 months (lag ladder) -> rideshare launch -> operations 2029; S3 the same (S3 equals S2 until 2028); S1 2031. It needs adoption and agentic analysis, not multiphysics optimization with guarantees, so design optimization is an accelerator. A small company with no legacy process is the likely first mover; build, integration and test bind, not cognition or rideshare slots, which are not scarce. This is a process outcome, not a performance claim.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.strongest_case_small: It changes who does the engineering, not what flies: performance gains are small, 'majority AI-generated' is hard to verify, and the first claims will be marketing.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.signpost: A company or agency announcing such a mission with published AI-generated verification evidence, followed by on-orbit success.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder. S3 2028 put first flight in the same year as its hard prerequisite cap-design-optimization (S3 2028). Chain (S3): design optimization 2028 -> smallsat design-complete -> build and integration 8-14 months (12-18 months at the S3 physical multiplier 1.3-1.5x) -> rideshare -> first operations 2029. S3 2028 -> 2029; S1/S2 unchanged (one year after prerequisites).
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + advocate: cap-design-optimization hard -> soft; binding gate launch -> fabrication. Advocate soft edge from struct-agentic-analysis-workflows added. Advocate's S2/S3 2028 rejected because it depended on adoption in 2027, which was not accepted; years unchanged.

capability-program-cycle-compression.title: Development cycles shrink by a quarter to a third, not 10x
capability-program-cycle-compression.description: Development time (concept to launch) for new space systems started after AI adoption falls measurably. Amdahl ceiling: about 38% shorter in S2 (51% in S3, 18% in S1) if a third of the critical path is cognitive and fully compressible. Expected realized compression for typical programs started in 2028 or later: about 20-30% in S2 (about 35-45% in S3, 10-15% in S1), with fast commercial programs nearer the ceiling and government flagships at 10-15% (appropriations).
capability-program-cycle-compression.status_oct2026: Not yet. Major NASA projects routinely run late, mostly in hardware, integration and test (GAO reporting, general).
capability-program-cycle-compression.why: Illustrative critical-path shares (general): requirements and trades 10%, design and analysis 15%, software 10%, fabrication and procurement 25%, integration and test 25%, qualification and reviews 10%, launch campaign 5%. Speedups of 5-10x on cognitive work and 1.1-1.2x on physical work (S2) give a 1.6x speedup, a ~38% shorter schedule; S3 (20-50x cognitive, 1.3-1.5x physical) ~51%; S1 (2x cognitive) ~18%. These are ceilings: they assume every cognitive step is on the critical path and fully compressible. Requirements negotiation, hardware-in-the-loop software testing and review gates compress far less, and long-lead parts (12-24+ months) often run in parallel with design, so compressing design can leave the critical path unchanged; each 10 points of effectively compressible cognitive share is worth about 7 points of compression. Counting more of the analysis inside test and build phases as cognitive (anomaly diagnosis, procedures, data reduction, material-review paperwork) lifts the S2 ceiling to roughly 45%, but the table's 1.1-1.2x physical multipliers already credit about 10 of those 60 points (if the residual physical work runs at 1.0x), so most of that gain is already inside the 38%. Fewer design escapes found in test cut rework, a second-order gain. Chain (S2): engineering adoption 2028 -> commercial programs started 2028 or later (smallsat lag ladder 12-18 months) -> first completions 2029-30 -> an attributable schedule analysis 2031. S3: 2030. Band Medium: evidence must come from programs started after adoption and finished by 2031, and government flagships dilute any average. Uncrewed commercial programs need no certifier, so the binding gate is integration and test hardware (experiment), not qualification.
capability-program-cycle-compression.strongest_case_small: Schedules are set by funding profiles, supply chains (rad-hard parts 12-24+ months), launch manifests and politics; teams may spend the gain on more analysis and scope (Jevons) instead of shorter schedules.
capability-program-cycle-compression.signpost: A GAO, ESA or company schedule analysis attributing cycle-time reduction to AI; smallsat build times falling below 9 months for new designs.
capability-program-cycle-compression.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Debated (skeptic vs advocate, auditor on wording). Skeptic accepted: 38% is a ceiling, realized lower; S2 2030 -> 2031, S3 2029 -> 2030 (only post-adoption programs count). Advocate partly accepted: the qualification cap was misapplied (gate -> experiment), cap-design-optimization hard -> soft, soft edges from mishap analysis and cheap mass; its 35-50% S2 figure rejected as largely double-counting what the 1.1-1.2x physical multipliers already credit, and its S2 2029 / S3 High rejected (depended on adoption in 2027). Realized range set at 20-30% in S2 between the skeptic's 15-25% and the advocate's 35-50%. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): soft edges from frontier-math-unbinds (B-math-frontier request 3) and physclock-commercial-analysis-first-qual (B-certification request 2).

comms-ai-cryptanalysis.title: AI agents audit cryptography at research grade
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.description: Frontier models run closed-loop cryptanalysis: they propose attacks on published schemes, protocols and parameter sets, test them, and return exact witnesses for a human to judge. Achieved here means major vendors and standards submitters routinely run such audits, and a standards body cites one in a review.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.status_oct2026: Partly exists. Olejnik and Naskręcki (arXiv 2608.21986, Aug 22 2026) report an autonomous agent workflow that found failures in eight published constructions, for example a Ring-LWR commitment that opens to any message and a lattice e-voting protocol that loses receipt-freeness. None is a NIST-standardized scheme. ML attacks on LWE recover only sparse or small secrets at reduced parameters (NoMod, arXiv 2510.02162). openai/math contains no attack on factoring, discrete log or lattices (tl-position-5).
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.why: The failures found so far sit one level above the hardness assumption: encodings, simulators, parameter certification, protocol composition. That is where space security is weakest. Bespoke key-management and command-authentication protocols on constrained links are written by small teams and rarely reviewed by cryptographers. Once research-grade models are public (cap-research-math-public), an audit that took a specialist weeks costs hours of compute, so every new satellite security protocol can be attacked before launch. Under S2 agent task horizons double every 6-9 months, so by 2028 agents audit whole protocol suites, not single constructions. The node depends on the internal model's capability becoming public (S1: 2028), so it is capped at Medium in S1 (fw-horizon-scorecard); S2 and S3 assume public release in 2027 as a scenario premise.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.strongest_case_small: The breaks so far are in obscure, non-standard constructions. Standardized primitives (AES-256, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) have decades of expert scrutiny. Most real-world failures come from implementation bugs and key handling, which human audits with existing tools already target.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.signpost: An AI-found break or parameter downgrade in an IETF, CCSDS or NIST-standardized scheme; NIST or CCSDS stating that AI audits were used in a selection or review.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.calibration_note: A3: Internal consistency: the node's why ties routine audits to public research-grade models (cap-research-math-public), which arrive 2028 in S1. S1 2027 -> 2028; band unchanged. (The hard prerequisite should arguably be cap-research-math-public, not the internal model.) A4: Hard prerequisite moved from cap-research-math-internal to cap-research-math-public, as A3 recommended. The why ties routine audits to public research-grade models, and the years already match (2028/2027/2027).
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Auditor: S1 High -> Medium (public-release dependency cap). Skeptic: achieved narrowed - NIST and CCSDS rely on community analysis rather than running audits themselves. Years unchanged.

comms-expander-constructions.title: Optimal expander graphs built explicitly (conditional)
comms-expander-constructions.description: 178 builds nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs, the best possible spectral expanders, deterministically for every degree d>=3 and all large even sizes. 177 constructs bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension, a building block studied for locally testable codes and quantum LDPC codes.
comms-expander-constructions.why: Conditional. A laser mesh in which each satellite has 3-4 terminals is a bounded-degree graph, and Ramanujan graphs give the largest spectral gap at that degree: short paths, high bisection bandwidth and graceful degradation when links fail. But a Ramanujan topology needs links between arbitrary satellites, which line-of-sight, range and slew limits forbid, and asymptotically good qLDPC and locally testable codes were built in 2021-22 without 177 (Panteleev-Kalachev), so the engineering effect through 2031 is nil. The band covers use in network or code design (P6: Low in S1, Medium in S2 by graph convention), dropped one band because both premises are T1.
comms-expander-constructions.strongest_case_small: Random d-regular graphs are already within ε of Ramanujan with high probability, and bipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree have been known to exist since 2013 (general). Real laser topologies are dictated by orbital geometry, link range, pointing and terminal slew time (+Grid, Motif, demand-aware designs), not by abstract graph choice.
comms-expander-constructions.signpost: A constellation-topology study that imposes Ramanujan-like structure under real geometric constraints and beats the best geometric heuristic by 10% or more in diameter or bisection bandwidth.
comms-expander-constructions.calibration_note: A3: T1 premise rule: families 178 and 177 have no Lean main result (T1) and the band is for the mathematics being established. One band down: Medium/High/High -> Low/Medium/Medium. Lead decision pending (auditor): the openai/math repo has Comparator statements plus solution modules for families the catalog marks without L (273, 124, 177, 110, 111, 279); the catalog L flag may undercount. Catalog tiers kept until the lead rules. If the lead accepts the repo-Lean finding (177 T3, 178 T1), restore Low/Medium/Medium and rest the band on 177.

comms-expander-constructions.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Auditor: the A3 drop was measured against 'mathematics established' while the bands equal the P6 no-drop convention; chose one metric (use in design, P6) and applied the T1 drop: Low/Medium/Medium -> Speculative/Low/Low. Skeptic: added why qLDPC/LTC do not depend on 177 and why Ramanujan topologies are geometrically infeasible; description softened from 'the expansion behind' to 'a building block studied for'.

comms-certified-interference-bounds.title: Provable interference compliance for shared spectrum
comms-certified-interference-bounds.description: Interference showings for NGSO-GSO and NGSO-NGSO sharing delivered as certified bounds instead of Monte Carlo runs: interval or proof-backed bounds on time-weighted throughput degradation, unavailability and aggregate EPFD, with the model assumptions written as a checkable specification. Achieved means operators use such bounds in at least one filing or bilateral coordination agreement.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.status_oct2026: FCC 26-26 (Report and Order, adopted Apr 30, released May 1 2026, SB Docket 25-157) replaced NGSO-GSO EPFD limits with private good-faith coordination, backed by adopted criteria when coordination fails: 3% time-weighted throughput degradation, 0.1% absolute unavailability increase, a supplemental -10.5 dB I/N for 80% of time, and a 3-degree GSO-arc avoidance angle. The Jan 9 2026 waiver (DA 26-36) had allowed 8 co-frequency beams per location with a 4-degree angle; the April order removed the beam cap, reduced the angle to 3 degrees (a relaxation for NGSO) and declined aggregate limits. GSO operators could seek to reintroduce aggregate limits through reconsideration, the D.C. Circuit or the WRC-27 cycle (33FG). FCC Part 100 (Jul 22 2026) moves licensing to yes/no certifications. FCC NGSO-NGSO rules (FCC 24-117) use 3% throughput degradation and 0.4% added unavailability over an orbital simulation (Roberts, arXiv 2609.36122). ITU Article 22 EPFD limits still govern internationally. Measured low-frequency EPFD from constellations exceeds radio-astronomy thresholds in 50-70% of samples (arXiv 2609.01995). No catalog family applies.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.why: The regulatory shift turned compliance from checking a power mask into a statistical claim about simulating tens of thousands of satellites. Disputes are now about simulation assumptions and tail events. Aggregates are where Monte Carlo is least trustworthy: keeping one interferer under threshold needs 8.1 degrees of separation, five need 15.5 and twenty need 27.0 (Roberts). A certified bound with a written specification can be re-checked by a rival operator or the FCC in hours. The math (geometry, order statistics, interval arithmetic) is expert-scarce rather than open, and existing interval and validated-numerics tools (Arb, INTLAB, VNODE-LP) suffice, so the Lean-verified floating-point toolchain (infra-verified-numerics) accelerates but does not gate it. In S2, research-grade applied math is public in 2027, and preparing a filing or coordination agreement with a new method takes months, so the first certified showings appear in 2028; S3 follows S2 through 2027. In S1 they wait for public models and some years of diffusion.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.strongest_case_small: Spectrum disputes are commercial and political, not mathematical, and regulators accept Monte Carlo. Certified worst-case bounds are conservative and could cost capacity against statistical showings. The contested inputs (antenna patterns, traffic models, deployment plans) stay contested. Under FCC 26-26 compliance is negotiated privately first, so formal showings are needed mainly when coordination fails or at the ITU, and with aggregate limits declined, certified aggregate bounds matter mainly for ITU Article 22 and radio astronomy.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.signpost: An FCC or ITU-R WP4A filing citing machine-checked or interval-certified interference bounds; an operator publishing an open, verified EPFD or degradation calculator.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Auditor: FCC 26-26 facts corrected from the primary source (criteria adopted as backstops; 4->3 degrees came in the April order and is a relaxation; aggregate limits declined) - cross-checked against 33FG's table. Advocate: infra-verified-numerics hard -> soft (interval tools exist) accepted; Part 100 added; advocate's S2 2028 -> 2027 rejected (skeptic: months of filing preparation; auditor: private coordination first and no aggregate limits weaken the 2027 forcing event). Skeptic: S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 follows S2 through 2027). Bands unchanged.

comms-certified-network-optimization.title: Near-optimal mesh routing with a proven gap
comms-certified-network-optimization.description: Joint optimization of laser-terminal pairing, routing and rate allocation over a time-expanded horizon that charges link acquisition and re-pointing time, at 10,000+ satellites, with a certified optimality gap (for example a Lagrangian dual bound) computed at operational cadence; user-beam frequency assignment is handled separately. Achieved means an open or vendor solver delivers such certified gaps at Starlink scale.
comms-certified-network-optimization.status_oct2026: The per-snapshot joint problem is NP-hard. A Lagrangian decomposition into matching, shortest paths and an LP gains 35-145% throughput over non-joint baselines in simulation (arXiv 2601.21914), and a graph neural network that predicts the dual prices matches it orders of magnitude faster (arXiv 2601.21921). Topology designs tested on three months of Starlink data report up to 2.3x capacity and 45% lower delay than +Grid (arXiv 2602.07756). The baselines are naive and operator practice is proprietary. Family 120 (almost-linear exact matching and prescribed-degree factors, T1) solves the terminal-pairing subproblem asymptotically fast. The Lagrangian work covers laser-terminal matching and routing only, with no acquisition or switching cost and no beam or frequency assignment; the fast GNN variant carries no certificate.
comms-certified-network-optimization.premise_tier: n/a (capability); T3 for the 102 ceiling, T1 for 117 hardness and 120
comms-certified-network-optimization.why: A certificate turns a capacity question into an investment decision. With a 3% dual gap, more capacity has to come from terminals, satellites or spectrum; with a 30% gap it can come from software. The math (decompositions, convergence and gap proofs, problem-specific relaxations) is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems (tl-position-4), so it becomes a P1 item as soon as research-grade models are public. A dual bound certifies any instance without any hardness theorem; the ceilings (UGC; 117, conditional) only explain why certified gaps are instance-specific, so frontier-approx-ceilings is context (soft), not a prerequisite. Interference-coupled frequency assignment has weak dual bounds, which is why it is left out. Operator adoption is modelled in comms-certified-mesh-operations.
comms-certified-network-optimization.strongest_case_small: Operators such as SpaceX already run strong in-house optimization. Realistic gain over their practice is probably 5-20% capacity (judgment), while V3 hardware is a 10x per-satellite step (33FG). Family 120 adds nothing practical at this scale: a 10,000-node, ~50,000-edge matching takes milliseconds with classical algorithms. Terminal count, acquisition time and gateway capacity bind first.
comms-certified-network-optimization.signpost: An operator, SDA or a vendor publishing optimality-gap metrics for live routing; an open solver with certified gaps at Starlink scale.
comms-certified-network-optimization.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: frontier-approx-ceilings hard -> soft (a Lagrangian bound needs no hardness proof); description narrowed to what the cited evidence supports (matching and routing, time-expanded with acquisition time; frequency assignment separate); gate adoption -> cognitive (adoption lives in mesh-operations). Rejected the advocate's cap-research-math-public hard -> soft and S1 2028 -> 2027: S1 is the plateau case and the node's own why ties it to public research-grade models. Years and bands unchanged.

comms-verified-routing-software.title: Formally verified constellation routing software
comms-verified-routing-software.description: Machine-checked proofs that routing, handover and topology-reconfiguration code is loop-free and deadlock-free, converges under link churn and meets latency bounds. Agents produce the proofs and maintain them as the code changes.
comms-verified-routing-software.status_oct2026: An agent extended a 3,000-line SMT network verifier with OSPF areas, BGP route reflection and L3VPN by counterexample-guided learning against emulated routers (arXiv 2608.11340, Aug 2026). Satellite-specific work is small, for example model checking of a TDM inter-satellite-link algorithm (arXiv 2511.09485). The broader evidence is the openai/math pipeline: 127 families with agent-written Lean (T3), strongest in discrete mathematics, which is what protocols need.
comms-verified-routing-software.premise_tier: n/a (capability; no catalog family is load-bearing)
comms-verified-routing-software.why: With handovers about every 15 s and a continuously changing topology, test coverage of control-plane states is poor; proofs cover all states. Commercial communications networks face no certification gate, so progress is limited by writing specifications of dynamic topologies, which agents began doing in 2026. Discrete properties formalize well: 20 of 40 theoretical-CS families in the release have Lean proofs.
comms-verified-routing-software.strongest_case_small: Mega-constellation operators ship software weekly and value iteration speed over proofs. Outages come more from hardware faults, space weather and the ground segment than from routing logic, and orbital dynamics and timing are hard to specify.
comms-verified-routing-software.signpost: An operator or SDA prime disclosing machine-checked proofs for routing or handover code; a satellite-network verifier released by a lab or vendor.
comms-verified-routing-software.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 follows S2 through 2027; timed models of link acquisition must be specified first). Auditor: trust tiers apply to results, not the pipeline. Bands unchanged.
