comms-pq-verified-implementations.title: Proven-correct post-quantum crypto for space processors
comms-pq-verified-implementations.description: Agents produce implementations of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, HQC and hash-based signatures for space targets that have no verified library today (SPARC LEON, rad-hard RISC-V such as PIC64-HPSC and NOEL-V, FPGA fabric), with machine-checked functional correctness, constant-time and masking (side-channel) proofs, plus certified failure-probability bounds. Achieved means such a library exists for at least one of these targets and a flight program adopts it.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.status_oct2026: Exists for mainstream CPUs, not yet for most space processors. mlkem-native (AWS-LC, PQ Code Package): all AArch64 and x86-64 assembly is proved functionally correct, memory-safe and constant-time in HOL Light, and the C code memory- and type-safe with CBMC (human-led proofs; no AI assistance stated). Radiation-tolerant AArch64 parts exist (for example AMD XQR Versal, Cortex-A72; general), so part of the space need is already covered without AI. The Jasmin compiler is proven to preserve the IND-CCA security of an ML-KEM implementation used in Signal (Rocq, arXiv 2511.11292). Lean 4 proofs of arithmetic masking for NTT hardware found that one open accelerator masks only one round (arXiv 2604.20793). A certified ML-KEM-768 decryption-failure bound of 2^-164.81 holds in a stated abstraction (arXiv 2609.09983). NIST picked HQC as its backup KEM on Mar 11 2025; final standard expected 2027.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.why: Most real cryptographic failures are implementation bugs and side channels, not broken mathematics (general). Space adds unusual targets (LEON or radiation-hardened RISC-V cores, FPGAs) and tight memory, so verified libraries must be re-targeted and re-proven. That is proof labor, which agents now supply. The AI-attributable part is this re-targeting and masking work; AArch64 and x86-64 are already done. Flight-software and crypto baselines freeze long before launch and qualification compresses only 1.2-1.5x after 2029-30 (physclock), so adoption by a flight program trails the proofs by about a year. Certification credit is a separate node.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.strongest_case_small: FIPS 140-3 and NSA evaluations are test-based and slow. Many satellites use certified hardware crypto modules where code proofs add little, and programs freeze crypto choices years before launch.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.signpost: A verified ML-KEM, ML-DSA or LMS library released for a radiation-hardened processor; a flight program citing machine-checked crypto proofs.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: narrowed to targets without verified libraries (mlkem-native already covers AArch64/x86-64, verified against its README); S2/S3 2027 -> 2028 (flight-program adoption within a year is inconsistent with the qualification gate). Resolver: S1 2028 -> 2029 for the same lag and to keep S1 behind S2. Advocate's S1 2027/High rejected: the AArch64 result is human-made and not attributable to the AI-math channel, and the advocate's 'AI-assisted proofs' claim is not supported by the AWS post or the README. Bands unchanged.

comms-code-design-on-demand.title: Custom channel codes on request
comms-code-design-on-demand.description: AI designs codes and decoders for specific links, with machine-checked finite-blocklength performance claims. Targets: short packets for direct-to-device signaling, IoT and telecommand; photon-counting optical links; synchronization and deletion channels. Achieved means an AI-designed short-block code or decoder with machine-checked finite-blocklength claims is submitted to 3GPP or CCSDS or ships in a product.
comms-code-design-on-demand.status_oct2026: LLM-guided search found seven record binary linear codes, improving 22 table entries, each verified exhaustively (arXiv 2609.37056, Sep 2026). A search for quantum LDPC bivariate-bicycle codes cost about $400 of inference (arXiv 2606.02418). Sep 2026: a Lean-formalized deletion-channel capacity bound (arXiv 2609.13351; the abstract does not mention AI assistance) and AI-assisted, Lean-formalized proofs of three binary-channel conjectures (arXiv 2609.27991). Catalog family 119 (Courtade-Kumar and Hellinger conjectures, L, T3) shows information-theory conjectures are within the model's reach; capability evidence only. Short-block polar and LDPC designs sit fractions of a dB from finite-blocklength bounds (arXiv 2503.02782, 2512.17834).
comms-code-design-on-demand.why: Long-block codes are near capacity, so the remaining gains are in short blocks and unusual channels, where design is expert-scarce rather than open. 0.5 dB is about 12% power, and on a handset uplink at the edge of a beam that can decide whether a link closes. Standards cycles (3GPP NTN, CCSDS, 2-4 years) bind handset D2D and agency links. Proprietary physical layers (Starlink user and gateway links, laser ISLs, third-party mini lasers) can adopt new codes faster, by firmware where the decoder runs on reprogrammable hardware, but fixed-function decoder ASICs still need a hardware cycle. Either way first adoption trails public research-grade models (2027 in S2) by about a year.
comms-code-design-on-demand.strongest_case_small: Coding gains are small next to antenna gain, power and spectrum. Standards bodies are conservative, decoder complexity, latency and patents decide adoption, and most space links already use standardized LDPC, turbo or polar codes. Record minimum-distance codes do not by themselves give link margin; decoder complexity and the weight spectrum at practical lengths decide gains, and the headroom left is tenths of a dB.
comms-code-design-on-demand.signpost: A 3GPP NTN or CCSDS contribution containing an AI-designed code; AI-found record codes appearing in a product.
comms-code-design-on-demand.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: years 2028/2027/2027 -> 2029/2028/2028 (adoption gate; the node's own why says standards bind; 2026 evidence improves distance tables, not dB); achieved defined. Advocate: proprietary air interfaces can adopt faster - accepted as text, with the caveat that decoder ASICs limit firmware swaps, so not as a reason to keep 2027; advocate's soft edge to comms-crqc-before-2031 rejected (classical link codes are not the qLDPC channel; that route is now comms-ai-crqc-resource-cuts). Auditor: 2609.13351 is not described as AI-assisted. Bands unchanged.

comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.title: Machine-checked security proofs for satellite quantum keys
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.description: Composable finite-key security proofs for satellite QKD passes (decoy-state BB84, BBM92, continuous-variable QKD) that include real device imperfections and non-IID signals. Numerical parts are certified and the core argument is formalized.
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.status_oct2026: Human progress in 2026: an analytic finite-key proof with source and detector imperfections (arXiv 2606.29943); a numerical framework valid against coherent attacks with non-IID signals (arXiv 2605.12984); a GEO-QKD finite-key feasibility study (arXiv 2605.29706). Entanglement-based passes are finite-key limited (arXiv 2602.11833). Lean-QIT (arXiv 2607.09632) is the first reusable Lean layer for quantum Shannon theory. Catalog: 272 T1 (context only).
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.premise_tier: n/a (capability transfer); 272 T1 is context only (conditional)
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.why: A LEO pass gives a few minutes of link; Jinan-1 shared up to 1.07 Mbit of secure key per pass (Nature, Mar 2025). At such block sizes finite-key penalties are large, and evaluators do not accept proofs that ignore device flaws. Tighter proofs that include imperfections raise certified key per pass (judgment: 10-40% at short passes). More important, they are what a security evaluation needs. The math is hard but within research-grade applied math. Formalization waits on quantum-information coverage in Lean, which S2 assumes catches up during 2027-29. The part resting on 272 is conditional (T1).
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.strongest_case_small: Key yield is set by loss, background light, weather and detectors, so proof tightness adds tens of percent at most. Satellite QKD as flown uses trusted nodes, so the satellite stays a point of trust whatever the proof says.
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.signpost: Eagle-1, SpeQtre or QEYSSat publishing security analyses with machine-checked components; an ETSI or ISO QKD evaluation citing formal proofs.
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.calibration_note: A3: Wording rule only: the 272 part is conditional (T1). B-networks: 276 dropped as not load-bearing; bands rest on P1->P2 capability transfer.

revisions.from: Tight, machine-checked security proofs for satellite QKD

comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Auditor: 276 (classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping) is not an input to composable finite-key proofs, so it was removed and the premise relabelled. Skeptic: S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 follows S2 through 2027; Lean quantum-information coverage began only Jul 2026). Bands unchanged.

comms-optical-availability-models.title: Certified availability for optical ground networks
comms-optical-availability-models.description: Validated stochastic models of cloud, turbulence and pointing outage that predict the availability of a whole optical ground network with site diversity, with bounds good enough to sign service-level agreements against.
comms-optical-availability-models.status_oct2026: The bottleneck has moved from peak rate to repeatable service (Turyshev, arXiv 2606.23711, Jun 2026). NASA LCRD two-site combinations gave 83.8-88.5% availability; high reliability may need about 10 sites at least 500 km apart; fixed cost is of order $3-4k per TB at 0.5 h/day of contact. Peak demonstrations: 200 Gbps from LEO (TBIRD), 1.8 Gbps operational GEO relay (EDRS), 267 Mbps from about 19 million miles (DSOC, which ended Sep 2 2025 after returning 13.6 Tbit).
comms-optical-availability-models.why: Availability is a correlated-weather problem. Long cloud climatologies exist, so the modeling is cognitive work that compresses under S2. Validation needs multi-year availability records from operating multi-site optical networks, which only accumulate in real time: the only multi-year multi-site record is LCRD's two sites (83.8-88.5%), and a 10-site network will not exist before about 2029-30. That data gate holds S3 to the S2 year. Validated models good enough to sign SLAs against are model confidence (P5).
comms-optical-availability-models.strongest_case_small: Availability is bounded by climatology, and site selection already uses standard cloud statistics, so better models move siting by a few percent. The number of telescopes, a capital decision, sets availability.
comms-optical-availability-models.signpost: ESA, NASA, KSAT or a commercial optical network publishing measured multi-site availability against predictions.
comms-optical-availability-models.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: S2/S3 2028 -> 2029 (data gate does not compress; the node's own why requires multi-site records that do not exist before ~2029). Auditor: pathway P1->P6 -> P1->P5 (validated models for SLAs are model confidence). Bands unchanged.

comms-quantum-receiver-theory.title: Receivers that beat photon counting
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.description: Theory and practical designs for joint-detection optical receivers that recover part of the gap between pulse-position modulation with photon counting and the Holevo limit, at deep-space photon flux and realistic background light.
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.status_oct2026: The Green Machine receiver showed superadditive capacity over any symbol-by-symbol receiver with BPSK in the photon-starved regime (Nature Communications, 2025). Photon-information-efficiency limits for PPM are reviewed in arXiv 2503.13161; a greedy receiver approaches the Helstrom bound for PPM (arXiv 2403.02634). DSOC used PPM with a 64-pixel superconducting-nanowire detector array (76% detection efficiency) at Palomar. Single-user Holevo capacity of the lossy channel is already known (general), so this node does not depend on family 273.
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.why: In the photon-starved regime, each extra bit per received photon is worth as much as a larger ground aperture, and aperture is the dominant cost of a deep-space optical ground terminal. Designing structured quantum measurements with provable gains uses established quantum detection theory (Helstrom, Holevo), so it needs research-grade applied math, not new validated physics; cap-physics-theory accelerates it. Proving that the gain survives background light, loss and timing jitter needs laboratory experiments, which set the year.
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.strongest_case_small: Joint-detection gains shrink quickly with background light and receiver optical loss, and daytime and near-Sun links are background limited. PPM with superconducting detectors is already within a few dB of practical limits (general), and no deep-space optical mission committed before 2031 is known to plan for such a receiver (general).
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.signpost: A lab demonstration of a receiver beating optimized PPM photon counting at deep-space-like flux with background; NASA or ESA funding a flight receiver study.
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: hard prerequisite cap-physics-theory replaced by cap-applied-math, with cap-physics-theory kept as a soft edge (joint-detection design uses established theory). Years unchanged (experiment gate binds).

comms-constellation-design-optimizer.title: Constellation design with proven compliance
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.description: Design tools that co-optimize orbital shells, beam plans, spectrum use and laser topology, and output both a filing-ready design and certified interference and capacity bounds. Achieved means an operator or tool vendor uses such a tool to produce the technical annex of at least one FCC or ITU filing; regulator acceptance of the certified bounds as a compliance method is not required.
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.status_oct2026: More than 10,000 commercial communications satellites operate in LEO and 50,000+ more are planned; Amazon filed for a 5,105-satellite direct-to-cell constellation in Jul 2026 (Roberts). On Sep 30 2026 the FCC opened more than 1,000 MHz for satellite services in the 12.7-13.25 GHz and 42-42.5 GHz bands (33FG). Design tools are in-house and uncertified. FCC Part 100 (Jul 22 2026) moves licensing to yes/no certifications with standardized schedules (Schedule F for frequency data), so compliance artifacts become machine-readable inputs. ITU EPFD validation still uses prescribed software (ITU-R S.1503 methodology).
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.why: As filings multiply and sharing becomes performance-based, value moves to designs that are provably compliant and dense. That needs multiphysics design optimization with guarantees (cap-design-optimization, S2 2028) plus the two certified-bound nodes, so it trails them by about a year. Filers must still run the methodology the FCC and ITU prescribe; certified bounds are added evidence, which is why the achievement is defined as use in an annex rather than regulator acceptance.
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.strongest_case_small: Constellation design is constrained by launch, manufacturing, spectrum rights and business plans. Filings are partly strategic placeholders, and incumbents' in-house tools are good.
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.signpost: A filing whose technical annex comes from a design optimizer with certified bounds; a tool vendor or new entrant shipping such a tool.
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Debate: skeptic S3 High -> Medium (regulator cap) vs advocate S2 Medium -> High (three High prerequisites, Part 100, demand). Resolved by defining achievement as use in a filing annex without regulator acceptance, so no cap applies and S3 stays High; S2 stays Medium because three High prerequisites in conjunction, the P6 default (Low) and incumbents' in-house tools do not support >70%. Bands and years unchanged.

comms-hardness-aware-tasking.title: Tasking and ground planning built on proven limits
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.description: Tools for Earth-observation tasking, downlink scheduling, ground-station-as-a-service allocation and ground-station siting that combine exact solvers on structured instances, certified-gap heuristics and documented approximation ceilings, with AI formulating each mission's variant on request.
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.status_oct2026: EOS-Bench (arXiv 2604.25782) spans up to 1,000 satellites and 10,000 requests. Exact integer programming for ground-station selection stops scaling before Planet's 96-satellite fleet, while decomposition stays within 95% of optimum on small cases (arXiv 2510.03438). Ground-station-as-a-service revenue scheduling is NP-hard (arXiv 2608.22222). Catalog: 102 [L] T3; 125 [L] T3 (the deterministic (1+2/e+eps) algorithm and the threshold under P!=NP have Comparator statements, MetricKMedian and KMedianThreshold); 124, 110, 111 T1; 104 [L] T3 only for a randomized version (the deterministic headline and the stochastic and parity extensions are T1).
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.why: The ceiling effect is immediate, but most value comes from capability transfer. Each mission has its own constraints (agility, memory, energy, cloud forecasts, contact windows), and a model that formulates and proves a bespoke scheduler in hours replaces months of operations-research work. Operators adopt within the P1 lag of 0-2 years after public access, so reported use trails cap-research-math-public by about a year. 124 (conditional) solves exactly the Garey-Johnson three-machine case (unit jobs with precedence constraints on three identical machines); it has no release times or deadlines, so it does not model contact-window scheduling. 110 and 111 give worst-case guarantees for online request handling. Mesh-routing solvers (comms-certified-network-optimization) help but are not needed: Earth-observation tasking and ground-station scheduling do not use laser-mesh routing.
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.strongest_case_small: Tasking is limited by satellites, agility, cloud cover and downlink, which are physics and capital. The 1+2/e k-median algorithm needs candidate sites and does no better than MIP on siting problems with a few hundred candidates. 111 asserts no polynomial-time implementation, and 124 is a narrow special case. k-median on Earth-surface sites has a PTAS, so the 1+2/e ceiling does not bind siting.
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.signpost: Earth-observation operators or ground-station-as-a-service providers reporting AI-formulated schedulers with certified gaps; public benchmarks reporting optimality gaps alongside scores.
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.calibration_note: A3: Band logic: hard prerequisite comms-certified-network-optimization is Medium in S1, so S1 High -> Medium. Lead decision pending (auditor): the openai/math repo has Comparator statements plus solution modules for families the catalog marks without L (273, 124, 177, 110, 111, 279); the catalog L flag may undercount. Catalog tiers kept until the lead rules.
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: comms-certified-network-optimization hard -> soft (tasking does not use mesh routing); years 2028/2027/2027 -> 2029/2028/2028 (adoption gate plus P1 lag 0-2 years after public access in 2027 under S2; same-year operator reporting not credible); 124 example corrected; PTAS note added. Auditor: 125 is T3 per lean/docs/125.md. Bands unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): soft edge from capability-algorithm-discovery (B-trunk request 2).

comms-crypto-agile-architecture.title: Crypto-agile satellites with proven update paths
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.description: Spacecraft security designs that can change algorithms in orbit: hybrid classical plus post-quantum key exchange, hash-based signatures for commands and software, and a code-based fallback such as HQC. Key-management, rekey and update protocols are proven secure by machine and sized for constrained links. Achieved means at least one operator flies or contracts a crypto-agile design whose rekey and update protocols carry machine-checked proofs; no certifier needs to accept the proofs.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.status_oct2026: NIST IR 8547 (draft, Nov 2024): RSA, ECDSA and ECDH at 112-bit security deprecated by 2030; all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms disallowed by 2035. NSA CNSA 2.0 sets national-security-system milestones running to 2035 (general). Post-quantum certificate-based authentication is costly on satellite links, which motivates pre-shared-key designs (arXiv 2607.23007) and quantum-safe IKE variants (arXiv 2605.28660). Gidney (arXiv 2505.15917, May 2025) cut the estimate for factoring RSA-2048 to under a million noisy qubits in under a week, from 20 million in 2019. 2026 estimates fell further: under 100,000 superconducting physical qubits for RSA-2048 (Pinnacle, arXiv 2602.11457, Feb 2026) and about 10,000-26,000 reconfigurable neutral atoms (Cain et al., arXiv 2603.28627, Mar 2026). Google set a 2029 deadline to move its authentication services to post-quantum cryptography (Mar 2026). NIST IR 8547 was still an initial public draft as of mid-2026. CNSA 2.0: all new National Security System acquisitions must be CNSA 2.0 compliant from Jan 1 2027.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.why: A GEO satellite launched in 2028 operates to about 2043: eight years past NIST's 2035 cutoff and possibly past the first code-breaking quantum computer. An in-orbit swap path is the main hedge for public-key key management (telecommand on pre-shared AES-256 keys is already quantum-safe), and it must work the first time. Proving the update and rekey protocols is proof labor that agents remove; protocol provers (Tamarin, ProVerif) and verified ML-KEM code already exist, so agents mainly remove the cost. AI cryptanalysis (comms-ai-cryptanalysis) and falling quantum resource estimates make the threat model concrete but are motive, not prerequisites. Commercial operators need no certifier for this, and CNSA 2.0 pulls government designs the same way, so the certification cap applies to comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm, not here.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.strongest_case_small: Migration is mandated regardless of AI. Many satellites use pre-shared symmetric keys (AES-256) for telecommand, which are already quantum-safe, and certification bodies do not yet credit AI-produced proofs.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.signpost: A CCSDS space-link-security profile with hybrid or post-quantum options; a GEO operator announcing in-orbit-updatable post-quantum crypto; NSA or NIAP accepting machine-checked protocol proofs as evidence.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: comms-ai-cryptanalysis hard -> soft (agility is mandated regardless; cryptanalysis is motive); 'only hedge' corrected; S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 follows S2 through 2027). Advocate: the Medium cap was misapplied because the achievement needs no certification; with achieved defined as one operator flying or contracting such a design, S2/S3 Medium -> High (P2 tier-4 nodes are High in S2 elsewhere in the graph when no certifier is involved); gate qualification -> adoption to match. Auditor: 2026 resource estimates and IR 8547 status added. Advocate's claim that AWS proofs were AI-assisted not used (unsupported).

comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.title: Flight demo of verified post-quantum command links
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.description: A satellite flies post-quantum or hybrid authenticated telecommand and key exchange using machine-checked implementations, and performs an in-orbit algorithm swap.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.status_oct2026: We found no flight with machine-checked implementations. SEALSQ/WISeSat markets post-quantum-secured IoT smallsats launched on SpaceX rideshares (Dec 2025); algorithms and verification are not specified in the cited report. Verified ML-KEM already exists for AArch64 and x86-64 (mlkem-native, HOL Light), so the AI-dependent part is mainly the machine-proven update protocol and the in-orbit swap.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.why: Once the architecture and verified code exist, a demo needs only a rideshare slot and a cooperative bus. Launch cadence does not bind for a cubesat-class demo, but integration lead times of 12-18 months do (general), plus commissioning before an in-orbit swap. The in-orbit swap is the new part: it shows the 15-year-asset problem can be managed. The band stays at the P2 default (Medium): someone has to fund, manifest and disclose a specific mission, and none is known.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: This adds assurance, not capability. Post-quantum crypto can fly without proofs, and the first operators to need it (governments) will use their own certified modules.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.signpost: An announced mission plan with an in-orbit post-quantum algorithm swap and published proofs.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.calibration_note: A3: Band logic: its hard prerequisite comms-crypto-agile-architecture is Medium in every scenario, so the demo cannot be High. S2/S3 High -> Medium.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: S3 2028 -> 2029 (architecture now S3 2028, plus 12-18 months integration and commissioning). Advocate's S2/S3 Medium -> High rejected: lifting the architecture's cap removes the inherited ceiling (A3 reason now obsolete) but does not make a specific funded, disclosed demo more likely than not; the P2 default is Medium and no mission is announced. Bands unchanged.

comms-holevo-receiver-demo.title: Ground demo: optical receiver beats photon counting
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.description: A ground or lab demonstration in which a joint-detection receiver beats optimized PPM with photon counting by 25% or more in bits per received photon, at deep-space-like photon flux and background.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.status_oct2026: Superadditivity has been shown in the lab with BPSK (Green Machine, 2025), but not under deep-space conditions with background light.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.why: Full chain: cap-applied-math -> comms-quantum-receiver-theory (designs, S2 2029 / S3 2028) -> low-loss photonic circuits (multi-project-wafer runs take roughly 6-9 months each, and 2-3 iterations are typical, general) -> superconducting nanowire detector integration -> tests against realistic background. The experiment gate compresses only 1.1-1.3x (S2) and 1.3-1.5x (S3) (physclock), so a demo lands about two years after the designs. S3's autonomous labs shorten the iteration loop but not fabrication. The 25% target is hard physics: background light and optical loss erase superadditive gains, and the Green Machine beat symbol-by-symbol BPSK, not optimized PPM. A ground demo is new theory into tools (P6, default Low), not a flown system.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.strongest_case_small: Gains shrink with background light and optical loss, the PPM-plus-SNSPD baseline keeps improving, and there is no flight slot to use such a receiver before 2031.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.signpost: A peer-reviewed demonstration at photon flux and background matching a Mars-distance link.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic + auditor: S3 Medium -> Low (two bands above the pathway default with no stated basis). Skeptic: S2 2030 -> 2031, S3 2029 -> 2030 (fabrication iterations and an experiment gate that compresses 1.1-1.5x); pathway P6->P7 -> P6 (a lab demo is not a flown system).

comms-space-qkd-network-demo.title: Multi-node satellite quantum-key demonstrations
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.description: Satellite QKD missions deliver keys among three or more ground nodes in different countries in routine campaigns: Eagle-1 in-orbit validation, SpeQtre, QEYSSat, SPOQC and successors to China's Jinan-1.
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.status_oct2026: Jinan-1 (Nature, Mar 19 2025): 23 kg payload, ~100 kg portable ground station, up to 1.07 Mbit of secure key per pass, and a key between China and South Africa over 12,900 km (trusted-node satellite). ESA lists Eagle-1's launch for late 2026/early 2027, followed by three years of in-orbit validation. The SpeQtre ground campaign produced 7.56 kbps at 4.78% QBER over 1.8 km (arXiv 2605.19689). QEYSSat has a digital twin (arXiv 2608.21968). SPOQC (12U, discrete- and continuous-variable payloads) launched Mar 30 2026 on Transporter-16, with full quantum experiments expected in the second half of 2026 (The Quantum Insider).
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.why: These missions are funded and largely built, so they run on the physical clock regardless of AI mathematics. They are the platform where AI-tightened proofs (comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs) would be applied. Physical anchor, independent of AI mathematics; the P7 default (Speculative) is not applied because the missions are funded and built.
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.strongest_case_small: This node is the physical anchor: no scenario moves it, and AI mathematics adds little to it.
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.signpost: Eagle-1 launch and its first published key-exchange campaign.
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Auditor: pathway 'physical enabler (feeds P2)' -> P7 (grounding rule: valid tag required); SPOQC status de-staled (launch verified via The Quantum Insider). Years and bands unchanged.

comms-certified-mesh-operations.title: Mega-constellation mesh run with certified optimality
comms-certified-mesh-operations.description: A large LEO operator runs laser-mesh routing and radio resource allocation in production with certified per-snapshot optimality gaps and verified control-plane software.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.status_oct2026: No operator has disclosed this. Starlink, Amazon Leo and SDA's transport layer (Tranche 1 transport launches began Sep 10 2025 with 21 satellites, per 33FG; further 2026 launches, count not verified) run proprietary or government software stacks.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.why: Value: judgment of 5-20% more delivered capacity at fixed hardware, plus fewer control-plane outages. Mega-constellation revenues are tens of billions of dollars a year (general), so even 5% is a lot of money. But the node needs one operator to adopt two independent things (certified gaps and a verified control plane), validate them in emulation and roll them out in stages on a live network of more than 10,000 satellites, so it trails its 2028 (S2) prerequisites by about a year. It is observable only if a proprietary operator (SpaceX, Amazon, SDA) discloses it. A vertically integrated operator that owns its own frontier model could move faster; that is the upside behind the S3 High.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.strongest_case_small: Operators may already be near-optimal on their own instances. Hardware upgrades (V3: 10x per satellite) and the regulatory lift (EPFD reform, reported at up to 7x capacity) dwarf a software gain (33FG), and certificates are a nice-to-have.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.signpost: Operator engineering talks or filings citing optimality gaps or formal verification of routing; SDA contract language requiring them.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic + auditor: S2 High -> Medium (conjunction of two High prerequisites is about 55-65% before adoption and disclosure; P2/P4 defaults are Medium). Auditor: S1 Medium -> Low (both S1 prerequisites Medium). Skeptic: S2 2028 -> 2029 and S3 2028 -> 2029 (same-year as verified routing leaves no time for emulation and staged rollout; integration compresses ~1.2x). S3 stays High. SDA status de-staled; the Jul 2026 third-mission claim is not verified so it is not asserted.

comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.title: Phone-to-satellite service scheduled around interference
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.description: Direct-to-device and broadband constellations schedule beams, power and emissions against certified interference budgets for adjacent bands, other operators and radio astronomy, instead of using blunt avoidance zones. Achieved means an operator runs EPFD-budgeted predictive scheduling in production, disclosed or confirmed by an observatory agreement; an FCC order is not required.
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.status_oct2026: SkyShare (arXiv 2609.00821) schedules spot beams within EPFD-budgeted regions and cuts unserved cells by up to 90.68% versus boresight avoidance at 25 radio-astronomy sites, using Starlink geometry and no laser-mesh routing. The 2620 MHz D2D downlink's second harmonic already causes at least 59% geodetic-VLBI data loss (arXiv 2608.11659). D2D spectrum is consolidating: on May 12 2026 the FCC approved EchoStar's spectrum sales, including 65 MHz (AWS-4, H-block, unpaired AWS-3) to SpaceX for $17B, with a $2.4B escrow condition imposed on EchoStar (AT&T bought about 50 MHz) (33FG). Starlink's D2C service got a +10 dB power waiver in Mar 2025 (33FG). WRC-27 agenda item 1.13 (Shanghai, Oct-Nov 2027) considers MSS allocations for direct connectivity to IMT user equipment between 694/698 MHz and 2.7 GHz, with protection of terrestrial mobile service.
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.why: Coexistence is moving from static masks to dynamic, budgeted scheduling, and doing it precisely gains operators served cells, so incentives line up. Certified budgets let science users and regulators trust a schedule without seeing proprietary traffic. Scheduling beams against EPFD budgets is its own problem (SkyShare needs no mesh routing), so comms-certified-network-optimization is an accelerator, not a prerequisite. One vertically integrated operator controls D2C satellites, spectrum and its own frontier model, which supports the S3 date; in S2 a year of adoption lag after the bounds (2028) is assumed. The harmonic problem is set by filters, and the incentive to protect science bands is weak without regulation, which holds S2 at Medium.
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.strongest_case_small: Harmonics and out-of-band emissions are fixed by filters in hardware, not by scheduling. D2D capacity is set by spectrum holdings, aperture size and power, and operators have weak incentives to protect science bands without regulation.
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.signpost: An operator agreement with a radio observatory or NSF that uses predictive, budgeted scheduling; an FCC order referencing certified coexistence budgets. WRC-27 agenda item 1.13 outcome and any pfd limits it sets to protect neighbouring terrestrial networks.
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic + auditor: S2 High -> Medium (P4 default; weak incentives for science bands; disclosure needed). Skeptic: comms-certified-network-optimization hard -> soft (SkyShare solves it without mesh routing); S1 2030 -> 2031 and S1 Medium -> Low (needs a lag after the S1 2030 bounds). S3 kept High with the auditor's definition (no FCC order, so no regulator cap); skeptic's S3 Medium and S3 2029 rejected - the advocate's vertically integrated path is the optimistic case. Advocate's S2 2029 -> 2028 rejected (it assumed bounds in 2027, which was not accepted). Auditor: EchoStar detail corrected. Advocate: WRC-27 AI 1.13 added (verified via Transfinite).

revisions.from: Predictive coexistence scheduling for direct-to-device

comms-optical-ground-network-service.title: Weather-robust optical ground network service
comms-optical-ground-network-service.description: An optical ground network sells weather-inclusive availability of about 99% for LEO or GEO data return, using site diversity, availability models and autonomous scheduling.
comms-optical-ground-network-service.status_oct2026: Operational optical relay exists: EDRS at 1.8 Gbps, with 80,000+ links at 99.53% reliability (arXiv 2606.23711). EDRS's optical link is LEO-to-GEO and its ground leg is Ka-band RF, so 99.53% is space-to-space link reliability over 8 years, not weather-inclusive optical ground availability. DLR reports an 8-node Australasian optical network design at 99.98% availability (design study, via Turyshev). Direct-to-ground optical service at high availability does not yet exist at scale.
comms-optical-ground-network-service.why: Better models and schedulers say where to put telescopes and how to use them. About 99% availability needs about 10 sites at least 500 km apart, each taking roughly 18-36 months to build (general), and capital compresses only 1.15-1.3x (S2) (physclock). With validated availability models arriving in 2029 (S2), sites committed afterwards cannot sell an SLA before 2030. Scheduling tools for ground stations already exist and accelerate this node rather than gate it. Chain (S2): applied math public 2027 -> validated optical-link availability models (comms-optical-availability-models, 2029) -> sites chosen and committed 2029 -> 18-36 months of construction across about ten sites -> a weather-robust service with an SLA from 2030 (Medium).
comms-optical-ground-network-service.strongest_case_small: RF ground networks already deliver, and demand for optical downlink may stay limited to a few high-rate customers. Capital cycles for ground networks are long.
comms-optical-ground-network-service.signpost: A commercial optical ground network announcing an availability service-level agreement; ESA or NASA contracting for optical ground service at a stated availability.
comms-optical-ground-network-service.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic + auditor: EDRS figure clarified (LEO-GEO link reliability, Ka-band ground leg), DLR 8-node design added. Skeptic: S2/S3 2029 -> 2030 (site builds after the models; capital 1.15-1.3x); comms-hardness-aware-tasking hard -> soft (ground-station schedulers exist). Bands unchanged.

revisions.reason: framework rule: tier 5-7 outcome by 2031 needs its chain written out

comms-space-qkd-backbone.title: Certified quantum-key service from space
comms-space-qkd-backbone.description: An accredited European or allied satellite QKD service (for example the EuroQCI space segment) routinely delivers keys to government users across 10 or more ground nodes, with a security evaluation that accepts its finite-key proof.
comms-space-qkd-backbone.status_oct2026: Demonstrations only (see comms-space-qkd-network-demo). ESA lists Eagle-1's launch for late 2026/early 2027, followed by three years of in-orbit validation; no operational date for the EuroQCI space segment is published. China is reported to plan an operational satellite QKD service around 2027 (unverified), on its own timeline and independent of AI proofs; it does not count here.
comms-space-qkd-backbone.why: Physical chain: Eagle-1 launch (late 2026/early 2027) -> three years of in-orbit validation (to about 2030) -> operational procurement -> satellites built and launched -> accreditation. That points to 2031 or later in every scenario. The service needs satellites, ground terminals and a security evaluation; AI mathematics shortens only the evaluation, and accreditation can use human-written finite-key proofs, so comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs accelerates rather than gates it. The physical clock (procurement, launch) sets the year, which is why S3 equals S2.
comms-space-qkd-backbone.strongest_case_small: Western security agencies have preferred post-quantum cryptography to QKD for national-security use (general). Trusted-node satellites limit the security gain, and budgets may go to PQC instead.
comms-space-qkd-backbone.signpost: A EuroQCI space-segment procurement award; an accredited security evaluation of a satellite QKD service.
comms-space-qkd-backbone.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic: comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs hard -> soft (accreditation can use human proofs); scope restricted to an accredited European or allied service (China's service would fire ~2027 regardless of AI and says nothing about this channel); S2/S3 2030 -> 2031 and Medium -> Low on the Eagle-1 chain (ESA dates verified). China 2027 claim marked unverified (the cited Laser Focus World article does not state it; SCMP not retrievable).

comms-pq-fleet-migration.title: Satellite fleets crypto-agile before the 2035 cutoff
comms-pq-fleet-migration.description: From this year, most new government and major commercial satellites carry in-orbit-updatable post-quantum crypto with machine-checked update paths, and legacy fleets are protected by ground-side controls.
comms-pq-fleet-migration.status_oct2026: Government migration planning is under way (NIST IR 8547, CNSA 2.0); space-specific post-quantum profiles are still being written (general).
comms-pq-fleet-migration.why: Mandates (NIST IR 8547, CNSA 2.0 for new national-security acquisitions from Jan 2027) will put post-quantum crypto on new satellites; AI mathematics makes the machine-checked version affordable. The machine-checked part is what mandates do not drive: it needs buyers to ask for it (comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm, itself Low in S2) or the dominant operators to choose it. Counted by number, new satellites are dominated by proliferated LEO lines (Starlink, Starshield, SDA) that turn over in 12-24 months and can take crypto changes over the air, so the 2-4 year GEO contract lag applies mainly to GEO and flagship buses; that sets the earliest year one to two years after the architecture. Whether those lines carry machine-checked update paths, and disclose it, sets the band.
comms-pq-fleet-migration.strongest_case_small: The migration happens with or without AI proofs. The AI contribution is assurance quality, which buyers may not pay for.
comms-pq-fleet-migration.signpost: Government satellite RFPs requiring crypto-agility and machine-checked evidence; the first GEO comsat contract with in-orbit post-quantum update.
comms-pq-fleet-migration.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder using the node's own reasoning: contracts are signed 2-4 years before launch, so "most new satellites" carrying the 2028 (S2) architecture cannot launch before 2030. S1 2030 -> 2031 (Medium -> Low; S1 architecture 2029), S2 2029 -> 2030; S3 unchanged (architecture 2027).
comms-pq-fleet-migration.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Debate: skeptic later and lower (S1 >2031 Speculative, S2 2031 Low, S3 2030) vs advocate earlier (S2 2029, S3 2028; count-weighted proliferated LEO turns over fast). Resolved: advocate's count-weighting accepted for the lag, so S2 2030 and S3 2029 stay; skeptic accepted on the band - 'with machine-checked update paths' is the procurement-norm content, which mandates do not drive, so S2 Medium -> Low; S1 -> >2031 and Speculative (S1 architecture 2029 plus the lag). Why rewritten: the old 'S3 does not beat S2' contradicted the years.

comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.title: Software adds 10%+ capacity on the same hardware
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.description: AI-produced mathematics and software (certified optimization, coexistence scheduling, custom codes) raise a major constellation's usable capacity by at least 10% at fixed hardware and spectrum, compared with the same hardware run with 2026-era software, disclosed by the operator or measured independently, by 2031.
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.status_oct2026: Capacity gains for 2026-2031 are dominated by hardware (V3 satellites: a 10x per-satellite step, ~50x fleet lift with full Gen2 deployment) and regulation (Ku co-frequency beams per location from 1 to 8 by the Jan 2026 waiver, then uncapped by FCC 26-26) (33FG). 33FG finds urban and dense-urban cells still supply-bound at V3 scale.
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.why: The old 'share of the gain' metric was undefined: against a 10x hardware step, a 10% share needs about a 10% software gain under additive attribution but about 29% under log attribution. The node now asks the direct question: does software add 10% at fixed hardware? The branch judgment is 5-20%, centred near the threshold, and gains must be attributable to AI-produced work (not operators' own non-AI software) and disclosed, so S2 is Low. The mechanism for the upside: cheap mass (V3 on Starship) moves the binding constraint in dense cells from hardware to spectral reuse under the 3%/0.1% coordination criteria, where beam scheduling across overlapping satellites sets capacity. Design tools and handset codes act through new satellites and 3GPP chipset cycles that do not reach measured 2026-2031 capacity, so they are accelerators only.
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.strongest_case_small: Attribution is nearly impossible from outside and operators will not disclose it; hardware and spectrum dominate.
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.signpost: Operator statements attributing capacity gains to software or AI; capacity per satellite rising faster than hardware specifications imply.
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Skeptic + auditor: S2 Medium -> Low (on the node's own 5-20% judgment, attribution and disclosure, the 10% threshold is about 20-30% likely). All three lenses: metric undefined; adopted the auditor/advocate fixed-hardware definition and retitled. Skeptic: comms-constellation-design-optimizer and comms-code-design-on-demand hard -> soft (they act through satellites and chipsets that do not fly at scale by 2031); S3 2029 -> 2030 (mesh operations now S3 2029). Advocate's S3 Medium -> High rejected (attribution and disclosure do not compress under S3); its two-curve mechanism added to why. '10-30%' corrected to the branch's 5-20%.

comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.title: Machine-checked crypto becomes a procurement norm
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.description: Government space buyers (for example SDA, or ESA for IRIS²) require machine-checked implementation and protocol proofs for the security functions of new satellites.
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.status_oct2026: We found no such requirement. Aviation already gives credit for formal methods (DO-333) (general), but AI-produced proofs are not qualified tools today (tl-position-6).
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.why: Once proofs are cheap and have been shown in flight, buyers can demand them at little cost; this is the strategic payoff of the verification channel. A buyer does not need regulators to qualify the AI that wrote the proofs: the trusted base is the proof checker (Lean, HOL Light, Rocq), so infra-tool-qualification accelerates this node rather than gating it. It still takes an institutional decision after the flight demo, and SDA solicits a new tranche about every two years; politics and appropriations do not compress in any scenario (physclock 1.0x), so S3 does not beat S2. Capped at Medium for buyer acceptance; Low in S2 because the demo must come first and only one or two solicitation windows remain before 2031.
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.strongest_case_small: Procurement rules change slowly and are written by people who distrust AI-generated evidence. Tool qualification may lag well past 2031.
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.signpost: An SDA, ESA or NSA solicitation listing machine-checked proofs as a requirement (evaluation credit alone does not count).
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.revision_note: B-networks resolver: Advocate: infra-tool-qualification hard -> soft (the trusted base is the proof kernel; a buyer can require checked proofs without qualifying the generator) - accepted. Advocate's S2 2029 / S3 2028 rejected: the flight demo (S2 2029, S3 2029) must come first and the one-year lag is kept, so S3 2029 -> 2030 (politics 1.0x). Skeptic: S2 Medium -> Low (institutional step after the demo with ~2-year solicitation cadence) and signpost aligned with 'require'. S3 stays Medium.

comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.title: International shift to provable spectrum sharing
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.description: The ITU follows the FCC in replacing fixed EPFD limits with performance-based sharing criteria and checkable compliance showings.
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.status_oct2026: The FCC moved domestically on Apr 30 2026 (FCC 26-26), without certified bounds (33FG). ITU Radio Regulations Article 22 EPFD limits remain. EPFD revision is not a regulatory agenda item at WRC-27 (Shanghai, Oct 11-Nov 12 2027): WRC-23 invited ITU-R studies of the Article 22 limits to inform WRC-27 'without any regulatory consequences' (quoted in FCC 26-26), so WRC-27 can at most adopt an agenda item for WRC-31, the earliest point of regulatory action.
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.why: Certified showings remove one technical objection to performance-based rules (that compliance cannot be checked) and can inform the ITU-R studies for 2028-31, but the decision is political consensus among administrations, many of them protective of GSO incumbents, and it runs on the conference calendar. Because the FCC moved without certified bounds, they accelerate this node rather than gate it. No scenario moves the calendar, so the year is 2031 (WRC-31) in all three; the host administration's own large NGSO filings may help an agenda item pass at WRC-27 but do not move the date.
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.strongest_case_small: GSO operators and many administrations oppose relaxing the limits, and the issue may not be on an agenda before the conference around 2031.
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.signpost: WRC-27 adopting a WRC-31 agenda item on Article 22 EPFD limits; the positions of China (about 200,000 NGSO filings) and the main GSO administrations; ITU-R study groups adopting performance-based methods.
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.revision_note: B-networks resolver: All three lenses: status corrected - EPFD is not a WRC-27 regulatory item, only a possible WRC-31 agenda item (verified via Runway Girl Network; auditor's FCC 26-26 quote). Skeptic: comms-certified-interference-bounds hard -> soft (the FCC moved without them). Auditor: S1 >2031 -> 2031 (calendar is scenario-independent). Advocate's signpost added. Bands unchanged (Low).

comms-crqc-before-2031.title: Code-breaking quantum computer before 2031
comms-crqc-before-2031.description: A quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 or 256-bit elliptic-curve keys exists before the end of 2031. It would expose legacy satellite links and any recorded traffic protected by them.
comms-crqc-before-2031.status_oct2026: Resource estimates fell fast through human work: Gidney (May 2025) put RSA-2048 at under a million noisy physical qubits for under a week; Pinnacle (arXiv 2602.11457, Feb 2026) at fewer than 100,000 physical qubits with qLDPC codes at 1e-3 error, 1 us cycles and 10 us reaction time (runtime about a month, unverified; preprint); Cain et al. (arXiv 2603.28627, Mar 2026) at as few as 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits, with P-256 discrete logs in a few days on about 26,000. Google set a 2029 deadline for moving its authentication services to post-quantum cryptography (Mar 2026). IBM's roadmap: Starling 2029 (~200 logical qubits, 1e8 operations), Blue Jay 2033 (~2,000 logical, 1e9 operations). Family 279 (exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set, T1) does not reduce qubit or error-correction budgets (tl-position-5). The largest machines remain far below the needed scale with logical gates (general).
comms-crqc-before-2031.premise_tier: n/a (hardware race); 279 is T1, conditional and not load-bearing
comms-crqc-before-2031.why: This is a hardware race; it does not need AI-run labs, so cap-autonomous-labs is an accelerator, not a prerequisite. AI mathematics reaches it mainly by cutting resource estimates (comms-ai-crqc-resource-cuts), which lowers the bar but builds no hardware; under S3, AI could also compress quantum-hardware design loops. Fabrication, yield, error rates and control still bind. Vendor roadmaps reach the needed logical scale around 2033, and expert surveys give low odds within five years, so S2 stays Speculative, at its upper edge after the 2026 estimates. It matters here because any satellite whose key exchange is RSA or ECC, and whose traffic was recorded, is exposed when this node fires, which is why the crypto-agility nodes matter now.
comms-crqc-before-2031.strongest_case_small: Scaling from today's machines to about 10^4-10^6 physical qubits (roughly 1,000-1,500 logical) running for days to weeks within five years is far beyond historical trends, the 2026 estimates assume error rates, cycle times and connectivity not yet shown at scale, and most expert surveys put a CRQC later (general).
comms-crqc-before-2031.signpost: Fault-tolerant logical-qubit operation at the 100+ logical-qubit scale below threshold; neutral-atom arrays above 10,000 atoms with logical gates; any AI-credited cut in Shor resource estimates (comms-ai-crqc-resource-cuts). If logical-qubit-at-scale milestones land in 2027, revisit S2 Speculative -> Low.
comms-crqc-before-2031.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: hardware race; 279 is not load-bearing. Lead decision pending (auditor): the openai/math repo has Comparator statements plus solution modules for families the catalog marks without L (273, 124, 177, 110, 111, 279); the catalog L flag may undercount. Catalog tiers kept until the lead rules.
comms-crqc-before-2031.revision_note: B-networks resolver: All three lenses: cap-autonomous-labs hard -> soft (a CRQC does not require AI-run labs). Auditor + advocate: 2026 estimates added (Pinnacle and Cain et al. verified on arXiv); the old signpost (<100,000 qubits) was already met, so replaced; 'million error-corrected qubits' corrected. Skeptic: IBM roadmap added. Debate on S2 band: auditor Speculative -> Low vs skeptic and advocate keep Speculative; kept Speculative (fabrication gate unchanged; roadmaps ~2033), with the advocate's revisit trigger in the signpost. Soft edge from new node comms-ai-crqc-resource-cuts; advocate's soft edges from code-design and expander-constructions rejected (qLDPC codes used in estimates do not depend on 177 or on classical link-code design).

frontier-applied-posing.title: Engineering math posed as precise problems
frontier-applied-posing.description: Engineers and AI agents translate engineering questions (a stability margin, an error bound, whether a sensor layout determines a material property) into precise mathematical statements with explicit assumptions, ideally Lean-stated, and pool them in open problem banks like the ~4,000 problems OpenAI posed for pure mathematics.
frontier-applied-posing.status_oct2026: No applied problem bank exists at that scale. The Oct 6 problem set was pure-math-skewed: 16 PDE and 12 dynamics families of 372; formalized 3 of 16 and 2 of 12. First applied formal benchmarks: CAM-Bench (May 2026, 1,000 Lean targets in optimization, numerical linear algebra, numerical analysis; textbook-level, many concepts missing from Mathlib) and StochBench (Sep 2026, 450 stochastic-process problems; best agent 34.9%). Ilin (Mar 2026) formalized a Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium result in 10 days for ~$200 with agents, one mathematician, 229 prompts and zero human-written code; the failure modes were 'hypothesis creep' and 'definition-alignment bugs' (posing errors) plus agent avoidance behaviors.
frontier-applied-posing.why: For most applied problems the hard step is the statement, not the proof: which norm, which regime, which idealization. The catalog shows capability on hard PDE (362 Vlasov-Maxwell, the forced Navier-Stokes blowup), so the scarcity of applied results reflects what was posed. Under S2 models pose candidate statements from engineering context and agents build missing library pieces (Urban 2026: 130k lines of topology in the Megalodon prover, not Lean, in two weeks for ~$100). Textbook-level applied targets already exist (CAM-Bench), so the new content must be engineering-derived problems, which ITAR/EAR and proprietary rules keep in-house: export control keeps problems out of open banks, not out of internal posing. Posing at scale is an adoption step after public access (P1 lag), so 2028 in S2 and S3. Human review of definitions remains essential (Ilin). This node gates frontier-math-unbinds, accelerates frontier-xc-certified and capability-engineering-adoption, and feeds P2 verification chains through formal specification work (verif-spec-engineering).
frontier-applied-posing.strongest_case_small: Much of applied mathematics' value lies in modeling judgment that does not reduce to theorem statements; engineers do not think in theorems; export control (ITAR/EAR) and proprietary concerns will keep the most valuable space problems out of open banks, so posing stays artisanal inside each program.

frontier-euler-blowup-r3.title: Euler blowup in open space, proven
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.description: A rigorous, likely computer-assisted, proof that the 3D incompressible Euler equations on R^3 with no boundary form a finite-time singularity from smooth, finite-energy data. It is the inviscid, unforced stepping stone to the Navier-Stokes question.
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.status_oct2026: Proven with a boundary by Chen-Hou (computer-assisted, 2022-23); Chen-Hou posted clarification notes in Jul and Aug 2026 answering a 2025 critique, so such proofs take years to settle. Low-regularity C^{1,alpha} blowup without boundary is known (Elgindi 2021, general; Chen May 2026). Smooth data on R^3: numerical evidence only. DeepMind's 'Discovery of unstable singularities' (Sep 2025) reached near double-precision profiles for the boundary case. Ganeshram-Duruisseaux-Anandkumar (Sep 2026) report a candidate self-similar R^3 profile and a stability framework; the finite set of explicit estimates is still missing. Forced Euler blowup was announced machine-checked by Alpoge-Buckmaster (Sep 2026). Not in the openai/math catalog.
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.why: Ingredients exist: an AI-found candidate R^3 profile (Ganeshram-Duruisseaux-Anandkumar, Sep 2026), a stability framework that reduces nonlinear stability to a large but finite set of explicit estimates (not yet done), and computer-assisted estimate machinery. Difficulty is about the level that fell on Oct 6 (judgment: 0 doublings beyond), so discovery in 2027 is plausible under S2. Acceptance, not discovery, sets the year: the bar is a Lean- or interval-verified proof with an independent re-run; Chen-Hou's 2022 boundary proof was still drawing clarification notes in Jul-Aug 2026; and a Lean route needs verified interval arithmetic (infra-verified-numerics: S2 and S3 2028). Hence S2 and S3 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027), S1 2029. It accelerates frontier-ns-unforced and the ideal-MHD part of frontier-mhd-wellposedness (ideal MHD with zero field is Euler) but is a prerequisite of neither. Spillover, the one concrete channel from this famous problem to engineering: the interval-verified proof machinery it requires (rigorous enclosures, fixed-point arguments around a numerical profile, formal interval arithmetic) is the same stack that guaranteed error bounds for engineering PDEs need (frontier-certified-pde-error, infra-verified-numerics). Band = judged chance the result is established (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance) by 2031; the engineering implication is judged separately and is nil to Low (P5).
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.strongest_case_small: No engineering effect. Euler is inviscid, and any singularity would sit far below the molecular mean free path in a real fluid. Its value is as a credibility signal and a stepping stone.
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.signpost: A Lean- or interval-verified proof of smooth R^3 Euler blowup, with an independent re-run (Hexagon, Comparator or a second group).

frontier-ns-unforced.title: Unforced Navier-Stokes settled, either way
frontier-ns-unforced.description: A proof of global smoothness for the unforced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations (Clay statements A/B), or of finite-time blowup from smooth data with zero force, on R^3 or the torus. This is the question most analysts mean by 'the Navier-Stokes problem'. Fefferman's official breakdown statements (C)/(D) allow a smooth, decaying force, so a verified forced blowup belongs to prop-ns-forced-verified and frontier-ns-clay-cd-ruling, not to this node.
frontier-ns-unforced.status_oct2026: Open. OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 claim (Lean, T3) concerns forced flows; OpenAI states it establishes Clay statement (C), and also (D), but says it will not claim the prize. The Clay Institute still lists Navier-Stokes as unsolved; its president Martin Bridson called the evaluation 'deliberately unhurried'. Clay rules require publication in a qualifying outlet, two years, and general acceptance. A self-published replay (Sep 17, 2026) reports the Lean certificate builds with no sorry; this is not a Comparator run with a statement audit, so the tier is unchanged. Lei-Ren (Sep 28) wrote an expository reconstruction of the profile construction and call it 'a major advance'. Petrillo-Glimm (Sep 20) proposed the 'positive defect problem' as the target for a programmatic unforced search. Family 376 (T1) embeds universal computation in forced flows, Tao's proposed route to blowup.
frontier-ns-unforced.premise_tier: n/a (target unproven; forced precursor T3); 376 is T1, conditional and not load-bearing. Depends on a lab posing it to the unreleased internal model until research-grade access is public (2027 S2, 2028 S1)
frontier-ns-unforced.why: One rung beyond what fell. Removing the forcing means a singularity must sustain itself against viscosity, likely via an unstable self-similar profile stabilized by a computer-assisted argument, or a Tao-style computing flow (376, T1, conditional and not load-bearing). A regularity proof would need methods beyond energy estimates (Tao's averaged-NS blowup barrier, general). Judgment: 1-2 difficulty doublings past the Oct 2026 level, plus about a year for a Lean or independent check. S2 (6-9 months per doubling): capability mid-2027 to early 2028, settled and checked about 2029 (Medium). S3: the same capability date and faster checking give 2028; with roughly 3-month doublings from 2028, settlement by 2031 is likely (High) because either answer counts. S1 (12-18 months per doubling): capability late 2027 to late 2029, so 2030 at the earliest and Low by 2031. Smooth Euler blowup and the forced-NS check are stepping stones (soft links), not prerequisites: a regularity proof needs neither, and Euler blowup does not imply Navier-Stokes blowup. Band = judged chance the result is established (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance) by 2031; the engineering implication is judged separately and is nil to Low (P5). Either answer acts only through P5 (tl-position-2).
frontier-ns-unforced.strongest_case_small: Zero engineering effect. CFD codes regularize, any blowup would sit below molecular scales, and a regularity proof confirms what every code assumes. The public reception ('AI solved fluid dynamics') may exceed the technical effect; the paper should address this head-on.
frontier-ns-unforced.signpost: A lab claims unforced blowup or regularity with a Lean proof and the Clay Institute responds; or no credible claim by end-2029, which favors S1.
frontier-ns-unforced.calibration_note: A3: Premise label and internal-model dependency noted (scorecard). Bands unchanged; matches prop-ns-clay-unforced. A4: Why text no longer names the id that was merged into this node.

frontier-turbulence-rigorous.title: Turbulence laws proven
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.description: Theorems that 3D Navier-Stokes with natural forcing (smooth, generic or white-in-time) dissipates energy at a rate independent of viscosity (the 'zeroth law') and obeys Kolmogorov-type inertial-range scaling, in a well-posed statistical framework.
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.status_oct2026: Onsager's conjecture is proven for Euler (Isett 2018; intermittent version Novack-Vicol 2023). Anomalous dissipation for forced Navier-Stokes is known only for constructed forcings (Brue-De Lellis 2023, general), now shown stable under geometric perturbation (C. Li, May 2026). Anomalous diffusion of passive scalars is proven (Armstrong-Vicol 2025), and the Kolmogorov 4/5 law holds conditionally for stochastic forcing (Bedrossian et al. 2019, general). The zeroth law for generic forcing and any intermittency correction remain open. No catalog family.
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.premise_tier: n/a (future results; statements must be posed); depends on the unreleased internal model until public research-grade access (2027 S2, 2028 S1)
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.why: This is the theory engineering actually wants, because closures need statistics, not trajectories. It is harder than NS regularity in two respects: the right statements must be invented, so posing is part of the problem (judgment: 2-4 doublings plus posing), and only one answer counts, since the zeroth law for natural forcing may be false or unprovable in a given framework. At S2's 6-9 months per doubling, capability arrives late 2027 to late 2029; with posing and checking, 2030. S3 keeps Medium for the same truth risk, though it arrives a year earlier. Chain: zeroth law and scaling, then a rigorous LES convergence theory (prop-les-convergence-theory, now merged into frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd), then closures with error bounds for canonical flows, then (data-gated) engineering closures (prop-closure-theory, hyper-sbli-heating-closure). Band = judged chance the result is established (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance) by 2031; the engineering implication is judged separately and is Low (P5->P6).
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.strongest_case_small: Kolmogorov scaling has been built into turbulence models since 1941, so a proof changes no RANS or LES practice. The costly engineering errors come from wall-bounded separation, transition, compressibility and chemistry, where DNS and experiment data bind, not theorems.
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.signpost: A proof of the zeroth law for Navier-Stokes on the torus with a fixed smooth or white-in-time forcing; or a lab release with a turbulence-theory family.
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.calibration_note: A3: Internal-model dependency noted (scorecard); bands unchanged.

frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.title: Boltzmann and Landau equations proven well-behaved
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.description: Global existence, uniqueness and smoothness for the space-inhomogeneous Boltzmann and Landau equations with physical interactions (including Coulomb and very soft potentials), far from equilibrium. These are the kinetic equations behind rarefied reentry, DSMC and collisional plasmas.
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.status_oct2026: The space-homogeneous cases are done: Landau with Coulomb potential does not blow up (Guillen-Silvestre, Acta Math. 2025), and homogeneous Boltzmann with very soft potentials follows from monotone Fisher information (Imbert-Silvestre-Villani 2024). Inhomogeneous: regularity is known conditional on hydrodynamic bounds (Imbert-Silvestre program; Fernandez-Real-Ros-Oton-Weidner 2025), and a new continuation criterion largely rules out lifting a 3D Euler singularity into kinetics (Golding-Henderson-Silvestre, May 2026); it is not a regularity proof. The catalog claims 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation, T1) and 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases over its lifespan, with fluctuations, T1); 362 (relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, T3) shows problems of this kind now fall. Not yet posed to the internal model as far as is public.
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.premise_tier: n/a (analog evidence: 362 at T3; 363/364 at T1, conditional)
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.why: Comparable in difficulty to 362, which was claimed in the Sep-Oct run (judgment: about D0), and the human program is close: conditional regularity reduces it to hydrodynamic bounds, and there is a new continuation criterion. Discovery could come in 2027 under S2 once a lab poses it; acceptance sets the year. A claim alone is T1, PDE is the release's least formalized area (3 of 16 families), and a long unformalized kinetic manuscript is absorbed on the 1-3 year expert clock (tr-position-5) until applied Lean libraries arrive (infra-mathlib-applied: S2 and S3 2028). Hence S2 and S3 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027), S1 2029. The S2 band is Medium, not High, because the node needs a positive answer for both Boltzmann and Landau with physical potentials far from equilibrium, and the truth may be partial (judgment). Band = judged chance the result is established (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance) by 2031; the engineering implication is judged separately. Effect: P5 confidence for DSMC and kinetic codes, plus quantitative moment and decay bounds that can feed solver error control (hyper-kinetic-solver-certification, plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics; tl-position-2 exception).
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.strongest_case_small: DSMC and kinetic codes have matched wind-tunnel and flight data for decades. Any inhomogeneous blowup would occur far from reentry conditions. The binding errors in rarefied aerothermodynamics are gas-surface interaction and chemistry data.
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.signpost: A proof (human or AI) of global regularity for the inhomogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, or a lab kinetic-theory family covering it.
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.revision_note: B-math-frontier: [skeptic+auditor] S2 2027 -> 2028 (a claim needs acceptance; no Lean path before applied Lean libraries; 1-3 year expert clock). frontier-nonuniqueness-map.title: Where fluid and kinetic models are not unique
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.description: A systematic set of nonuniqueness and ill-posedness results, with matching uniqueness criteria, for the Euler, Navier-Stokes, Boltzmann and MHD models engineers simulate. It marks which regimes need an extra selection principle (entropy condition, vanishing-viscosity limit, finer physics).
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.status_oct2026: Convex integration gives nonuniqueness of weak Euler and NS solutions (general), including for compressible Euler with Riemann data (Chiodaroli-De Lellis-Kreml 2015, general), and sharp forced nonuniqueness for SQG (ARMA, Oct 2026). Ill-posedness in supercritical Sobolev spaces (Duke, Aug 2026). Catalog: 363 Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation (T1); 376 universal computation in forced NS (T1); the Sep 8 forced NS blowup (T3).
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.premise_tier: n/a (future results; forced-NS precursor T3); 363 and 376 are T1, conditional examples. Depends on the unreleased internal model until public research-grade access (2027 S2, 2028 S1)
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.why: Negative results act fastest (fc-position-1 exception; tl-position-2). A nonuniqueness theorem for a regime tells V&V teams that solver-to-solver disagreement there may come from the equation rather than the code. Entropy admissibility is not enough: compressible Euler has infinitely many admissible solutions for some Riemann data (Chiodaroli-De Lellis-Kreml 2015, general), and mesh-refined Kelvin-Helmholtz simulations converge only in statistics (Fjordholm-Kappeli-Mishra-Tadmor 2017, general). The actionable V&V output is which quantities are statistically, not pointwise, convergent; 'add a selection principle' is not a solved recipe. Convex-integration constructions are long, technical and constructive, which suits agents. A map is a body of results whose signpost needs citation by a V&V or DSMC group, so it lands a year after the first results (S2 2028). Examples resting on 363 and 376 are conditional (T1). Feeds frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd; draws on hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check. Band = judged chance the result is established (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance) by 2031; the engineering implication is judged separately and is nil to Low (P5).
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.strongest_case_small: The constructions use wild, low-regularity data (velocity below Holder 1/3) with no physical counterpart, and numerical dissipation already acts as a selection principle. Practitioners have lived with Scheffer-Shnirelman nonuniqueness since the 1990s without changing practice.
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.signpost: A nonuniqueness result for compressible NS or Boltzmann with physically reasonable data (bounded entropy, shock-tube-like), cited by a CFD V&V or DSMC group.
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.calibration_note: A3 note superseded (B-math-frontier, auditor): the scorecard internal-model cap (Medium unless a public model of similar capability exists) is lifted because every scenario makes research-grade capability public before 2031 (S2/S3 2027, S1 2028). If that premise fails, these bands drop to Medium. Premise label: the map is future work; 363 and 376 are conditional examples.

frontier-landau-damping-general.title: Landau damping settled for realistic plasmas
frontier-landau-damping-general.description: Long-time behavior of collisionless and weakly collisional plasmas settled beyond the idealized setting, either by proving nonlinear Landau damping or by proving that it fails. The settings are: Sobolev (finite-regularity) data in unconfined or screened settings where echo counterexamples do not apply; whole space; bounded domains with absorbing or emitting walls; magnetized plasmas (phase mixing along the field, with or without weak collisions; collisionless modes transverse to the field are undamped Bernstein waves and do not Landau-damp); and full electromagnetic (Vlasov-Maxwell) fields near stable equilibria, with explicit rates. The node is reached when at least one of these variants is settled. The results say when and how fast kinetic fluctuations damp, which is what Landau-fluid closures imitate.
frontier-landau-damping-general.status_oct2026: Mouhot-Villani (2011, torus, Gevrey) is now Lean-formalized (Bedrossian, Sep 2026). Results since then: unconfined 3D near Poisson equilibrium (Ionescu-Pausader-Wang-Widmayer 2022; new proof by Nguyen-Wei-Zhang, arXiv 2411.18408); unconfined 2D (Ionescu-Nguyen, Sep 2026); screened two-species with large data (Wang-Xiao-Xiong, arXiv 2603.16767, Mar 2026); weak-collision Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck (Y. Luo, arXiv, Jan 2024). Known limits: on the torus, finite-regularity damping can fail through plasma echoes (Bedrossian 2016, general). In a uniform magnetic field, modes transverse to B are undamped Bernstein standing waves while other modes Landau-damp, and weak collisions add relaxation on an O(nu^-1/3) time scale (Bedrossian-Wang, arXiv 1805.10756, linearized). Nonlinear magnetized and full Vlasov-Maxwell long-time behavior are open. Catalog 362 (T3) supplies global smoothness for one-species relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, a prerequisite for long-time questions.
frontier-landau-damping-general.premise_tier: T3 (362, analog evidence). The band does not depend on the internal model becoming public. The node needs only one variant settled; human programs (Ionescu, Pausader, Bedrossian, Nguyen and coauthors) have produced new settings at about one a year since 2022; and labs can pose the problem internally (cap-research-math-internal, 2026).
frontier-landau-damping-general.why: An active human program is closing in, and the difficulty is catalog-level. Formalization has started (Bedrossian), so kinetic theory is now formalizable despite the 3-of-16 PDE formalization rate. Downstream, quantitative damping rates and echo thresholds justify the linear dispersion relations used in electric-propulsion and space-weather wave models. For kinetic closures (plasma-kinetic-closures) they are a confidence input (P5), not a prerequisite. Landau-fluid closures (Hammett-Perkins 1990, general) were derived from linear theory, and engineering closures are calibrated. Hall-thruster electron-cyclotron drift turbulence grows from Bernstein-type modes that do not Landau-damp, so a correct magnetized result may be negative. The plasma domain's long-time Landau damping node is merged here.
frontier-landau-damping-general.strongest_case_small: Plasma physics has used Landau damping since 1946 and confirmed it experimentally. Proofs give rates in small-perturbation regimes where linear theory already works, and Hall-thruster anomalous transport is turbulence, not damping.
frontier-landau-damping-general.signpost: A theorem settling the nonlinear long-time behavior of magnetized Vlasov-Poisson (phase mixing along B, uniform in a weak collision frequency; persistence or stability of Bernstein modes across B), or nonlinear Landau damping for an unconfined or screened Vlasov-Maxwell system near a stable homogeneous equilibrium at Sobolev regularity. A proven failure counts.

frontier-mhd-wellposedness.title: Which plasma fluid models make mathematical sense
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.description: Ill-posedness and singularity results for Hall and electron MHD, ideal-MHD blowup inherited from Euler, and conditional regularity and continuation criteria for resistive MHD in 3D, the models used for space weather, magnetic nozzles and fusion-propulsion concepts. A stretch goal is rigorous bounds on magnetic reconnection rates. Excludes 3D global regularity of visco-resistive MHD, which contains the Navier-Stokes problem as the zero-field case (frontier-ns-unforced).
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.status_oct2026: Local well-posedness is classical. 3D global regularity is open and inherits Euler's difficulty: ideal MHD with zero field is Euler, so a smooth R^3 Euler blowup gives ideal MHD blowup directly. Hall-MHD is ill-posed near some steady states (Jeong-Oh 2022, general); reduced electron-MHD models form singularities (Dai 2025); ideal MHD below the classical threshold (Giardi, Sep 2026). Fast reconnection lacks rigorous theory. No catalog family.
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.premise_tier: n/a (future results); depends on the unreleased internal model until public research-grade access (2027 S2, 2028 S1)
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.why: Ill-posedness matters in practice: codes that include Hall terms need regularization, and the map tells space-weather and nozzle modelers which models give results that converge under refinement (P3). Ideal-MHD blowup follows directly from smooth Euler blowup (soft link: frontier-euler-blowup-r3); Hall- and electron-MHD results need no Euler input; reconnection-rate bounds are harder (judgment: 1-2 doublings). Weak feed to plasma-eruption-onset-theory and plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory. Band = judged chance the result is established (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance) by 2031; the engineering implication is judged separately and is nil to Low (P5).
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.strongest_case_small: Space-weather forecast skill is limited by solar boundary data (magnetograms) and coronal physics, not well-posedness. Operational solar-wind codes carry known numerical diffusion that already regularizes.
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.signpost: A proof of finite-time blowup from smooth, finite-energy data for 3D ideal, Hall or electron MHD (beyond the zero-field Euler case), or a rigorous resistive reconnection-rate bound.
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.calibration_note: A3 note superseded (B-math-frontier, auditor): the scorecard internal-model cap (Medium unless a public model of similar capability exists) is lifted because every scenario makes research-grade capability public before 2031 (S2/S3 2027, S1 2028). If that premise fails, these bands drop to Medium.
