hyper-optimal-test-design.title: Information-optimal ground and flight test design
hyper-optimal-test-design.description: Bayesian optimal experimental design and sequential model calibration choose arc-jet conditions, shock-tube shots and flight sensor placements. Each test is aimed at the uncertainties that drive TPS thickness: material conductivity, radiative excitation rates and the transition N-factor.
hyper-optimal-test-design.status_oct2026: The methods are known but rarely applied at program scale. The Ames Arc Jet Complex is the agency's sole ground test facility for reentry TPS, and its throughput is limited: in 2026 the 30 kW mARC II needed a cooling-sleeve fix just to extend run times. The Artemis I char-loss investigation took 121 tests across 8 campaigns. New U.S. arc-jet capacity is being built independently of AI: Kratos Project Helios (20-25 MW arc jet plus a 200 kW fiber laser, $68.3M, awarded 23 Oct 2025 under the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program), plus defense arc-heating capacity at AEDC (advocate source, not re-verified).
hyper-optimal-test-design.why: When facility hours are the binding constraint, the lever is information gained per run. Well-designed sequential calibration campaigns can cut the runs needed for parameter estimation by 2-5x (judgment); where envelope-coverage qualification matrices fix the test list, the gain is ~20-30%. Applied to the arc-jet and EAST queues, this multiplies the scarcest physical gate in the domain, which defense money is expanding only by a few facilities by ~2028-30. It accelerates the tier-3 physics nodes and the margin chain but is not required by any of them: SRL's probabilistic margins (2026) and the Artemis I root cause (121 conventional tests) were found without it. Domain instance of physclock-optimal-test-campaigns.
hyper-optimal-test-design.strongest_case_small: Qualification requirements (envelope coverage) often fix test matrices, not information value, and facility availability sets the schedule. The real gain may be 20-30%, not 2-5x.
hyper-optimal-test-design.signpost: NASA Ames, ESA or a commercial plasma-tunnel operator advertises adaptive, model-driven test campaigns.
hyper-optimal-test-design.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] Hard edges to hyper-certified-margin-uq, hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing, hyper-ablator-multiscale-response and hyper-radiation-kinetics made soft (none needs OED to exist). [skeptic] Years 2028/2027/2027 -> 2029/2028/2028: the signpost is an adoption event and test-article fabrication plus arc-jet scheduling take 6-12 months, so same-year-as-public-access assumed zero lag; S3 equals S2 before 2028. Gate experiment -> adoption. Why: '2-5x (general)' relabelled as judgment with the 20-30% qualification case. [advocate] Kratos Helios arc jet added to status (verified on kratosdefense.com); the advocate's claim that the link to physclock-optimal-test-campaigns was missing is wrong (it already exists as a soft edge).

hyper-certified-margin-uq.title: Heat-shield margins from on-demand uncertainty analysis
hyper-certified-margin-uq.description: Deterministic aerothermal factors and a separate material branch, combined by the traditional three-branch root-sum-square method, are replaced by a joint probabilistic budget that carries material, aerothermal and recession uncertainty across the full aeroshell to a reliability statement on bondline temperature, set up on demand by AI agents. The open part, bounding model-form error for ground-to-flight extrapolation, is split out as hyper-model-form-error-bounds.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.status_oct2026: NASA's SRL TPS design (IPPW 2026) uses Mars 2020-derived aerothermal factors (convective 1.22 forebody / 2.0 aftbody, radiative 1.5 / 1.47, pressure 1.05 / 1.25, shear 1.25 / 1.5), a FIAT Monte Carlo bondline margin and +20% recession, combined by the three-branch RSS method; material properties dominate the thickness (conductivity 2-sigma ~32%). A preliminary alternative-margining Monte Carlo at one stressing forebody location (8,000 FIAT cases; aerothermal factors sampled uniformly between 1 and the existing margins, i.e. assuming those factors bound the truth) found ~75% of baseline thickness keeps the bondline below its limit in ~99% of cases, against 0 of 8,000 exceedances at full thickness (1 at 80%, 160 at 70%); full-aeroshell analysis is listed as future work. SRL itself ended when Mars Sample Return received no FY2026 funding (appropriations passed Jan 2026).
hyper-certified-margin-uq.why: Adding deterministic factors compounds conservatism where the worst cases do not coincide. NASA's preliminary, forebody-only SRL Monte Carlo suggests the traditional thickness may be ~25% conservative at one location, but that thinning is bought by accepting ~1% per-location exceedance under an aerothermal error model capped at the existing factors, which excludes the up-to-2x VUV under-prediction found for the same 8 km/s entry. Joint UQ of this kind is solved in principle but expert-scarce, the classic case where on-demand AI applied math pays first (P1, then P5). This remains the shortest path from AI mathematics to mass on a flown vehicle, with the model-form piece (hyper-model-form-error-bounds) deciding how far the thinning can be trusted.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.strongest_case_small: The mathematics was never the barrier; risk posture is. Probabilistic TPS methods have existed for about 20 years (general), and Artemis I's char loss pushes NASA toward more margin, not less.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.signpost: A published full-aeroshell joint probabilistic TPS margin analysis (material, aerothermal and recession uncertainty propagated together to a bondline reliability statement), set up largely by AI agents, from NASA, ESA, a university or a capsule maker.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.revision_note: B-entry: [auditor] Split: retitled to the solved-in-principle joint budget; the open model-form part moved to new node hyper-model-form-error-bounds; 'stacked' corrected to three-branch RSS; gate adoption -> cognitive (adoption is hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing). [skeptic+auditor] SRL anchor number restated with its assumptions (single location, aerothermal error sampled within existing factors, ~1% exceedance accepted, full aeroshell future work) and MSR cancellation added. [skeptic vs advocate] Both wanted S2 = S3 (S3 equals S2 before 2028); resolved at 2028 for both (skeptic's lag argument; the signpost needs publication). [skeptic] Signpost replaced (old one duplicated hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing and was an agency-acceptance event). Skeptic's S2 High -> Medium and gate -> data were addressed by the split instead: they apply to the model-form node. Hard edge from hyper-optimal-test-design made soft. Bands Medium/High/High unchanged.

revisions.from: Joint probabilistic TPS margin budgets on demand

hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.title: Certified error bounds for hypersonic flow codes
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.description: Proven a-posteriori error bounds and formally verified kernels (positivity-preserving shock capturing, stiff finite-rate chemistry integrators, radiation-transport quadrature). Kernel-level properties (positivity, conservation, stiff-integrator stability) are proven and kept separate from physics-model error; whole-solution heat-flux error bars remain out of reach.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.status_oct2026: The release does not touch this: stiff numerics and radiation transport are absent, and only 3 of 16 PDE families are formalized. Practitioners study grid convergence informally, and it enters radiative-heating uncertainty budgets as a 'structural' term.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.why: Separating numerical error from model error stops grid effects from being double-counted inside physics margins. In S2, Mathlib coverage of PDE and numerics plus a verified-numerics toolchain (both ~2028 in S2) make kernel-level proofs routine, and P2 adoption in production codes typically follows 2-4 years later. Proofs about the full solution remain out of reach. Numerical error is not the dominant TPS uncertainty, so production adoption (the signpost) lacks demand pull by 2031 in S2.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.strongest_case_small: Numerical error is rarely the dominant uncertainty; transition, radiation and material properties are. Multi-D compressible Euler weak solutions are known to be non-unique, so global certified bounds need assumptions engineers cannot check.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.signpost: A Lean- or Coq-verified flux or chemistry integrator adopted in a NASA, DLR or commercial production aerothermal code.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] Description corrected (it claimed certified heat-flux error bars, contradicting its own why). [skeptic] S2 Medium -> Low (no demand pull for production adoption; the node's own strongest case). [advocate, partly accepted] Stale '(~2029)' toolchain date corrected to ~2028 in S2; advocate's earlier years (S2 2029, S3 2028) rejected because the signpost is production adoption and P2 runs 2-4 years after the libraries.

revisions.from: Certified error bounds for hypersonic CFD kernels

hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.title: Certified simulation of thin upper-atmosphere flow
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.description: Hybrids of DSMC, Fokker-Planck and discrete-velocity methods, with proven consistency with the Boltzmann equation and quantified statistical error, used for high-altitude aerocapture passes, early-entry heating and plume backflow.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.status_oct2026: DSMC (SPARTA and other codes) is standard practice, and a Fokker-Planck module in SPARTA matches DSMC at lower cost. No production solver carries certified error bounds. DSMC convergence to the Boltzmann equation is already proven (Wagner 1992, general); the dominant error is collision-model input. Families 363 and 364 are manuscript-only (T1).
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven; 363/364 at T1 are supporting only)
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.why: Transitional-regime heating (Knudsen number ~0.01-1) matters for upper-atmosphere entry, early-entry heating and plume backflow; aerocapture peak heating occurs in the continuum. Today it is DSMC with expert-tuned collision models. Certified solver-to-Boltzmann error bounds raise confidence (P5) without changing predicted heat fluxes. The band rests on the capability channel; the T1 catalog results (363/364) are supportive only and conditional.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.strongest_case_small: Rarefied contributions to total heat load are small for most capsules, because peak heating occurs in the continuum (general). Certified bounds also do nothing about collision cross-section uncertainty.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.signpost: A kinetic code release with published, proven error estimates, or AI-derived collision models validated against shock-tube data.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] Hard edge from hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check (a T1-premise node) made soft, so the node no longer rests on a T1 premise and needs no band drop. [skeptic] Wagner 1992 DSMC convergence noted; pathway P5->P6 -> P5 (confidence, not heating numbers, per the domain nil_effects); aerocapture emphasis removed. Years and bands unchanged.

revisions.from: Error-controlled kinetic solvers for the rarefied-to-continuum gap

hyper-tps-inverse-nde.title: Math for finding hidden heat-shield damage
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.description: Uniqueness and stability theory, plus algorithms, for recovering hidden TPS defects (bondline disbonds, subsurface cracks, density variation) from surface thermography, ultrasound and strain data. This includes which defects a given sensing mode provably cannot see.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.status_oct2026: Family 372 (global uniqueness for smooth isotropic elasticity from boundary data) is T1. Family 365: only its manuscript 'Nonuniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities in three dimensions' has a formalized main result in lean/formalization.yaml (T3, unaudited); the headline joint metric-and-connection recovery result is manuscript-only (T1, conditional). Family 366 (planar Mumford-Shah crack regularity) is T1. Practice relies on visual, tap and thermographic inspection with empirical thresholds. Starship's heat shield has about 18,000 tiles; Musk has described the job as inspecting tens of thousands of tiles.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 365 formal part T3, headline T1; 372 and 366 T1; all conditional and supportive only
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.why: Rapid reuse benefits from inspect-by-exception: cheap sensors that show which tiles need attention. Uniqueness and stability results say when boundary data determine interior properties. Nonuniqueness for anisotropic conductivity and only logarithmic stability for boundary-data inversion are classical (Kohn-Vogelius 1984; Mandache 2001; general), Lipschitz scalar conductivities are already known to be uniquely determined (general), transient thermography is a different data type, and multi-modal inspection is already standard. So 365's formalized rough-coefficient nonuniqueness is at most a conditional P5 caution, not a new design rule. The main lever is P1: AI makes bespoke inversion and probability-of-detection modelling for a specific tile stack cheap. The band is Medium because the signpost needs a published POD scheme, which needs seeded-defect specimen campaigns (MIL-HDBK-1823A practice, general), and the largest operator does not publish.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.strongest_case_small: These theorems concern smooth, isotropic media, while tiles are porous, anisotropic and full of sharp interfaces. Industrial NDE runs on empirical probability-of-detection curves, and SpaceX will use cameras plus machine learning regardless.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.signpost: A reusable-vehicle operator or NASA publishes a model-based TPS inspection scheme with probability-of-detection derived from inverse theory.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.calibration_note: A3: Cross-domain parity and band logic. Its why says the capability channel drives the band, and the comparable struct-shm-inverse-limits (inverse-problem detection limits for structural inspection, same years, same data gate) is Medium/High/High. At Low/Medium/Medium it also sat below its own hard dependents hyper-tile-damage-accumulation (Medium/High/High) and hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield (S1 Medium). Bands Low/Medium/Medium -> Medium/High/High; premise relabelled n/a because the T1 families are supportive, not load-bearing.

hyper-transition-prediction-theory.title: Predicting when hypersonic airflow turns turbulent
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.description: A validated model that predicts transition onset on 3D vehicles from the freestream disturbance environment, surface roughness and ablation blowing, to within ~+/-20% in transition Reynolds number, without per-vehicle tuning.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.status_oct2026: Genuinely open. A coordinated international effort was published as an AIAA virtual collection in Mar 2026. BOLT-1B showed that flight transition differs from conventional-tunnel transition (Jan 2026), and its forebody took ~14 months and 100+ staff to build.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.why: Turbulent heating is roughly 3-5x laminar (general), so without trusted transition prediction, slender and lifting vehicles carry TPS sized for turbulent flow over much of their acreage. Predictive transition could save tens of percent of acreage TPS mass on such vehicles (judgment). Under S2, AI can produce the theory by 2029-30. Validation needs flight transition datasets: open ones remain a handful (BOLT, HIFiRE), while defense datasets grow toward dozens a year (MACH-TB up to 50 tests a year, reusable Talon-A) inside classified enclaves that S2 models can reach (capability-controlled-data-access, S2 2028) but whose results may not be published. The flight disturbance environment is poorly characterized, and a blind test needs a new instrumented article (BOLT-1B's forebody took ~14 months). The physical clock keeps S2 at Low.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.strongest_case_small: Blunt capsules and Starship's belly transition early anyway, and designs already assume turbulent heating. The payoff falls mainly on hypersonic gliders and weapons, not most space vehicles.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.signpost: A blind prediction in which an AI-assisted model lands transition onset on a new flight test within 20%.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] S3 2029 -> 2030: a blind prediction on a new flight needs the theory (cap-physics-theory S3 2028) plus a ~14-month instrumented article, and flight count compresses only 1.3-1.5x in S3. [advocate, partly accepted] Soft edge from capability-controlled-data-access and defense-dataset growth added to why; S2 Low -> Medium rejected: classified validation may never be published, the disturbance-environment problem remains, and the domain signpost makes a flight-validated prediction the trigger for that raise. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): controlled-data-access year in why updated to S2 2028 (B-trunk).

revisions.from: Predictive hypersonic transition (receptivity, roughness, ablation)

hyper-sbli-heating-closure.title: Better heating models where shock waves hit the vehicle
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.description: AI-derived RANS and wall-model closures (non-Boussinesq, variable turbulent Prandtl number, roughness and blowing) that predict separation extent and peak heating in shock-boundary-layer interactions (flaps, control surfaces, tile steps and gaps) to within ~+/-15-20% of DNS and experiment.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.status_oct2026: Standard RANS fails on hypersonic SBLI. The 2025 review by Raje, Parish, Hickey, Cinnella and Duraisamy lists SBLI heat transfer, compressibility, turbulence-chemistry interaction and ablation roughness and blowing as open research needs. The release contains no turbulence-closure results.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.why: Flap, hinge-line and gap heating set the local TPS on Starship-class flaps and control surfaces, which today are designed with LES or DNS spot checks plus factors. Deriving closures is a theory problem that AI can attack (constraint-respecting symbolic models trained on DNS) once enough DNS data exists. DNS is compute-bound, and AI-era compute growth helps. In S2 the cognitive part lands by ~2029, and data and validation take about another year.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.strongest_case_small: Machine-learned RANS closures have repeatedly failed to generalize outside their training data (general). Wall-modeled LES on GPUs may bypass RANS closures by 2030 and make the question moot.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.signpost: A closure published with demonstrated out-of-distribution accuracy on unseen SBLI geometries in a blind comparison.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+advocate] Hard edge from hyper-flight-data-pipeline made soft (closures are trained on DNS and validated against DNS and ground facilities; the signpost is a blind ground comparison). [advocate] Soft edge from capability-learned-emulators. [skeptic vs advocate] Skeptic S2 Medium -> Low accepted (P6 default Low; out-of-distribution generalization is where ML RANS closures repeatedly fail; +/-15-20% approaches SBLI peak-heating scatter). Advocate's S3 High and gate data -> cognitive rejected: more DNS compute does not fix out-of-distribution failure, and blind validation still needs ground experiments; S3 stays Medium.

revisions.from: Turbulence closures for shock interactions and cold-wall heating

hyper-radiation-kinetics.title: Predicting glowing-gas heating on the fastest entries
hyper-radiation-kinetics.description: State-resolved excitation and dissociation kinetics (the CO 4th positive system in CO2 atmospheres; N and O VUV emission for Earth return), built from ab initio rates plus shock-tube data, that cut radiative-heating uncertainty from 30-100% to ~15-25%.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.status_oct2026: For SRL's 8 km/s Mars entry, baseline simulations under-predicted VUV by up to 2x against EAST, and three UQ methods gave 30-100% uncertainty (Hansson, 24 Sep 2026). The forebody radiative heating factor is 1.5. Mars Sample Return, including SRL, received no FY2026 funding (appropriations passed Jan 2026), removing the motivating mission; no funded crewed 12+ km/s return exists either.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.why: Radiative uncertainty sets the 1.5x factor on Mars forebody radiative heating. For large-radius Earth return at 12 km/s or more, radiation dominates and the uncertainty decides material choice (HEEET-class versus PICA). Halving the uncertainty could bring the factor toward ~1.2-1.25 and cut the radiative design heat load by ~15-20% (judgment). AI can generate rate sets and reduced kinetics for the few-electron species involved (N, O, N2, CO), but the missing physics at SRL (heavy-particle excitation) was found by measurement, EAST shot time follows mission pull, and S2 cognition does not compress the shock-tube gate.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.strongest_case_small: The gap is experimental, not theoretical. The best AI theory still needs shock-tube shots that take months to schedule, and with SRL cancelled few programs will pay for them before 2031.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.signpost: A paper at a radiation workshop (RHTGSM or IPPW) in which AI-generated rate sets match EAST VUV spectra within 20% without tuning.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.revision_note: B-entry: [auditor] Family 275 removed (worst-case many-electron QMA-hardness; DFT-functional hardness already known; the needed rates are for few-electron species; the T1 claim lacked 'conditional'); pathway and premise relabelled. [skeptic] S2 Medium -> Low (MSR/SRL cancelled, verified via The Register; the gate is shock-tube data; the 20%-without-tuning signpost is below 30% in S2); S3 Medium kept. [auditor] 'large-radius' qualifier added. Hard edge from hyper-optimal-test-design made soft; [advocate] soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands.

revisions.from: Closing the radiative-heating gap (Mars, Venus, 12+ km/s return)

hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.title: Heat-shield surface chemistry from first principles
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.description: Finite-rate oxidation, nitridation and catalytic-recombination models for carbon, SiC and silica-based (tile coating) surfaces, derived from quantum chemistry plus molecular-beam data, to replace tuned recession and catalycity parameters.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.status_oct2026: Finite-rate models exist, for example vitreous-carbon oxidation mechanisms extended to FiberForm (the PICA precursor), but they rely on fitted mechanisms. Family 278 claims a proof that Kohn-Sham ensemble representability fails (T1, conditional); family 275 claims QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energies (T1, conditional). Both are foundational or worst-case and do not bound the approximate-functional DFT used for surface rates (general).
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven); families 278 and 275 are T1, so anything resting on them is conditional; here they serve only as ceilings
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.why: On reusable, non-ablating tiles, surface catalycity can shift heating by tens of percent up to ~2x between the non-catalytic and fully catalytic limits (general), so designers assume the worst case. Recession-rate uncertainty sets the 20% recession margin on ablators. AI-built mechanisms validated by autonomous molecular-beam and plasma-tunnel experiments (S2 from ~2028-29) could tighten both, but molecular-beam and plasma-tunnel data come from a few specialized facilities and arc-jet calibration remains the gate.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.strongest_case_small: Real surfaces evolve through contamination, oxide growth and microstructure change, so first-principles rates are only one input. Arc-jet calibration remains mandatory, and arc jets are scarce.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.signpost: Autonomous plasma-tunnel or molecular-beam experiments publish AI-designed reaction mechanisms that predict catalytic heating within 20% on a new material.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.revision_note: B-entry: [auditor] 278/275 restated with 'claims' and 'conditional' (T1 wording rule) and their near-nil relevance noted. [skeptic] Hard edge from cap-autonomous-labs made soft (data come from specialized conventional facilities). [advocate, partly accepted] Autonomous-experiment date aligned to ~2028-29; soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands; S3 Medium -> High rejected (P6 default Low; the signpost needs plasma-tunnel or arc-jet validation on a new material, which compresses only 1.3-1.5x).

revisions.from: First-principles gas-surface chemistry for heat-shield materials

hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.title: Predicting how heat-shield material burns away
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.description: Multiscale material response that goes from pore scale to volume average, with mathematically justified homogenization, calibrated permeability and pyrolysis kinetics, and criteria for spallation and char failure. It should be able to predict an Avcoat-type char loss before flight.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.status_oct2026: PATO recession predictions match plasma-tunnel data to about +/-20% (ESA conference, 2026). The Artemis I char-loss root cause (Avcoat lacking permeability, letting gas pressure build in the char) was found only after flight, through 121 tests. Artemis II splashed down on 10 Apr 2026 after a modified, non-skip entry, with reduced char loss on the same heat-shield design.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.why: Material-property uncertainty dominates TPS thickness (SRL: conductivity 2-sigma ~32%). A failure mode the models missed cost Artemis a trajectory change and an investigation of more than a year. An AI that formulates and checks thermomechanical failure criteria from micro-CT microstructure addresses the cognitive part. Validation needs arc-jet time, which in S2 is stretched by optimal test design.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.strongest_case_small: Batch-to-batch permeability in Avcoat is a manufacturing process-control problem, and better models do not make material uniform.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.signpost: A pre-test prediction of a char or spallation anomaly that arc-jet or flight data later confirms.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] Hard edge from hyper-optimal-test-design made soft (validation needs arc-jet shots, not a particular design of them). [advocate] Soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands (arc-jet utilization). Years and bands unchanged.

revisions.from: Predictive ablator response (pyrolysis, permeability, spallation)

hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.title: Damage-accumulation model for reusable ceramic tiles
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.description: A predictive model of tile cracking, edge chipping, bond fatigue and hot-gas ingress through gaps over repeated entries, tied to inspection data, so that operators can inspect by exception and set life limits per tile zone.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.status_oct2026: Starship V3 Flight 13 (24 Jul 2026) deliberately stressed the heat shield: minimal tile loss, but cracked tiles and streaks at tile boundaries that suggest hot-gas penetration. Load-sensing tiles were flown and reflown tiles were tested. Musk said on 4 Aug 2026 that he would call the heat shield problem solved. Dan Rasky (co-inventor of PICA) called the current TPS a dead end for rapid reuse (29 Jul 2026). Flight 14 reached orbit on 28 Sep 2026 and splashed down; no ship has been caught or reflown.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.why: Shuttle-era tile programs needed extensive inspection between flights (general). Rapid reuse at Starship scale needs model-based triage that narrows inspection to flagged zones, plausibly a few percent of tiles per flight (judgment). Fatigue and fracture modeling plus Bayesian updating from load-sensing tiles is expert-scarce applied math that AI makes cheap. The data clock is the number of reflights.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.strongest_case_small: SpaceX would build this anyway with in-house ML on inspection imagery, and AI mathematics adds at most a few months. The hard problem may be material (ceramic tile fatigue under thermal cycling), and no model removes that.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.signpost: A tile-TPS operator (SpaceX, Sierra Space) states zone-level tile life limits or an inspect-by-exception policy, with per-reflight tile replacement counts.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] Hard edge added from physclock-starship-full-reuse: the model's data clock is reflights of the same tiles, and no ship has been caught or reflown. [skeptic+advocate] Hard edge from hyper-tps-inverse-nde made soft (camera/ML and direct inspection can substitute). Hard edge from hyper-flight-data-pipeline made soft because that node now counts only data shared beyond the operator, while this model runs on the operator's own reflight data (soft edge from new hyper-fleet-aerothermal-twin). [skeptic] S2/S3 2028 -> 2029: zone-level cycles-to-failure needs several reflights per ship after a 2027 first reflight; S3's 1.3-1.5x physical multiplier does not change that. [auditor] S2/S3 High -> Medium (P6 default Low; proprietary data; disclosure needed). [skeptic] Signpost replaced (old one duplicated hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield). | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): Flight 13 date harmonized to Jul 24, 2026.

hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.title: AI designs vehicle shape, trajectory and heat shield together
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.description: Multi-fidelity co-optimization of vehicle shape, entry trajectory and TPS layout, using AI-built surrogates (neural fields, reduced-order models) with validated or certified error bars. It cuts an entry-vehicle design cycle from months to days.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.status_oct2026: Surrogates exist in research: physics-enhanced 3D neural fields for Orion (arXiv 2603.28791, Mar 2026), and LLM CFD agents (OpenFOAMGPT 2.0, CFDAgent) that automate setup. None is used in production for certified EDL design.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.why: Entry design iterates between aerodynamics, trajectory and TPS, and each loop needs nonequilibrium CFD at 10-100 trajectory points (general). Agents plus surrogates could compress a cycle 10-30x (judgment). That opens shapes that were too costly to explore, such as lifting bodies and biconic Mars landers, and lowers the analysis-cost barrier for small companies (see the aerocapture demo). The loop can run on margin factors and transition correlations; certified margins and on-demand stability analysis improve it but do not gate it. Commercial entry-vehicle makers (SpaceX, Varda, Inversion) face no certification body for their design method, and the threshold is a design review citing AI-surrogate trade studies, not certification credit, consistent with capability-engineering-adoption (High, S2 2028) and capability-ai-native-spacecraft (High, S2 2029).
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Design-cycle time is rarely on a program's critical path; test and fabrication are. Neural surrogates struggle with shocks and extrapolation, and high-consequence final designs will still need full CFD plus test.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.signpost: A NASA or commercial entry-vehicle design review that cites trade studies driven by AI surrogates.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] Hard edges from hyper-certified-margin-uq and hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand made soft (accelerators, not gates). [advocate] Soft edge from capability-engineering-adoption; S2 Medium -> High for consistency with the capability branch's High ratings for engineering adoption and AI-native spacecraft in S2. [skeptic vs advocate] Skeptic's S3 High -> Medium rejected: the band is judged at 2031, three years after S3 diverges from S2, and S3 must stay >= S2.

revisions.from: AI-run aerothermal design loop (shape + trajectory + TPS)

hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.title: Probabilistic heat-shield sizing adopted in practice
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.description: A NASA program, an ESA mission or a commercial capsule maker formally sizes heat-shield thickness to a reliability target using joint probabilistic margins rather than stacked factors.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.status_oct2026: Shown only as a preliminary, forebody-only alternative-margining study for SRL (~75% of baseline thickness kept the bondline below its limit in ~99% of Monte Carlo cases at one location; IPPW 2026). That study sampled aerothermal error uniformly between 1 and each margin factor, so radiative error was capped at 1.5x, while the companion radiation study found VUV under-predicted by up to 2x against EAST. SRL no longer proceeds: Mars Sample Return received no FY2026 funding (Jan 2026). Varda makes its C-PICA heat shields in-house; it lost W-4 on reentry in May 2026 (cause not public).
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.why: Applying SRL-style thinning frees up to ~1-3% of entry mass for Mars-class entries (judgment; an upper bound, since bond, carrier structure and aftbody mass do not scale with ablator thickness) and less for LEO-return capsules, whose margin stack lacks the 1.5 radiative factor. On ablator-shielded NASA 20 t-class Mars lander concepts that is plausibly 0.5-1 t (judgment); it does not apply to Starship's reusable tiles. Commercial capsule makers are not bound by NASA margin policy, but adoption happens at a design review about a year after the method is available, is visible only if disclosed, and post-Artemis I and post-W-4 risk posture pushes operators to spend margin on reliability. A NASA crewed adopter would be capped at Medium.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.strongest_case_small: For small capsules TPS mass is small in absolute terms and reliability matters more. Post-Artemis I, NASA flagship and crewed programs will resist thinner margins.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.signpost: A NASA EDL margin-policy update, or Varda, Inversion or another capsule maker disclosing reliability-based TPS sizing or reduced TPS mass.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] S2/S3 High -> Medium: adoption is a cultural/policy clock (~1.0x) that S3 cognition does not compress, the nearest NASA adopter (SRL) was cancelled with MSR, and commercial adoption is mostly unobservable. [skeptic] S2/S3 2028 -> 2029: same-year adoption after the enabling method assumed zero lag. [skeptic] '1-4% (general)' relabelled as a judgment upper bound for Mars-class entries; 0.5-1 t figure scoped to ablator-shielded NASA concepts. [auditor] SRL Monte Carlo caveats and MSR cancellation added. Hard edge from hyper-optimal-test-design made soft; soft edge from new hyper-model-form-error-bounds.

hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.title: Validated models of braking with engines at supersonic speed
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.description: Predictive models of plume-shock interaction, aerodynamic forces and moments, and heating during supersonic retropropulsion (SRP) for 20-100 t Mars landers, reduced to control-oriented models with quantified uncertainty and accepted by a lander program.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.status_oct2026: NASA's EDL Architecture Study found that all its 20 t human-scale concepts need SRP. Large DES and CFD runs on leadership supercomputers are the main tool (general). Falcon 9 and Starship Earth-reentry burns are the only full-scale data; most are proprietary, though a limited NASA-SpaceX Falcon 9 reentry-burn dataset from the 2014-era data-sharing agreement is public (general; NTRS 20180006608).
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.why: Uncertainty in aero-propulsive interaction feeds GNC control margins and the propellant budget, and SRP propellant is a large share of landed mass (general). On-demand applied math turns expensive unsteady CFD campaigns into reduced-order models with uncertainty bounds. Validation needs flight data that only SpaceX holds at scale.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will validate empirically through Earth flights and accept risk on early Mars attempts. NASA's human Mars EDL has no decision driver before 2031.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.signpost: Published SRP models validated against Starship or Falcon flight data and accepted by a lander program.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] Signpost: 'or a NASA Mars architecture selecting a lander concept' deleted (not evidence of validated models); status notes the limited public Falcon 9 dataset. Hard edge from hyper-flight-data-pipeline made soft: that node now counts only data shared beyond the operator, and the skeptic notes capsule and testbed flights carry no SRP data; validation data are SpaceX's own. Years and bands unchanged.

revisions.from: Validated supersonic-retropropulsion aero-propulsive models

hyper-certified-edl-guidance.title: Proven-correct guidance for entry and landing
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.description: Entry, aerocapture and powered-descent guidance (numerical predictor-corrector, convex powered-descent guidance) delivered with machine-checked proofs of convergence, constraint satisfaction and floating-point error bounds for the flight implementation, and accepted as verification evidence.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.status_oct2026: Convex powered-descent guidance has pen-and-paper proofs (general). Flight code is verified by test and Monte Carlo. The release shows agentic Lean at scale for mathematics, not for flight code, and no tool is qualified.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.why: Proofs of robust convergence under atmospheric-density and dispersion assumptions reduce Monte Carlo burden and perceived risk, and certification regimes already give credit for formal methods. The node is conjunctive: general credit (infra-tool-qualification, plan acceptance S2 2030, Medium) plus one specific EDL project accepting proofs within about a year, so S2 is Low (the A4 logic used for verif-hls-autonomy-certification); S3 stays Medium. No aerocapture mission is manifested before 2031: NASA's ARRIVAL Earth-orbit aerocapture demonstration was at conceptual design in June 2025, so its guidance baseline freezes before credit exists. The realistic first cases are CLPS or HLS powered descent and commercial reentry capsules. Capped at Medium in every scenario because acceptance is required.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.strongest_case_small: Guidance mishaps have historically come from requirements, sensor and integration errors, not from algorithm convergence, and a proof of the wrong specification is worthless.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.signpost: A NASA or commercial EDL flight-software release with formal proof artifacts accepted as verification evidence.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic: S2 band Medium -> Low (conjunction of general credit and one EDL project within a year, the A4 logic); aerocapture motivation replaced, since ARRIVAL was at conceptual design in Jun 2025 (checked: Military & Aerospace Electronics, Jun 27 2025). Advocate's re-pointing to a separate checker-route node rejected with that node. Years unchanged.

revisions.from: Formally verified entry, aerocapture and powered-descent guidance

hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.title: Predicting radio blackout during reentry
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.description: Coupled tools for nonequilibrium flowfield, electron density and full-wave electromagnetics that predict and minimize RF blackout through antenna placement, aft-side relay to constellations, and magnetic or electrostatic windows.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.status_oct2026: Starship relays through Starlink during reentry. Magnetic-window theory is at the screening-model stage (Lieu, arXiv 2608.10018, Aug 2026). The reentry sheath is collisional and weakly ionized, so family 362 (collisionless relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, T3) does not bear on it.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.why: This is a coupled-physics analysis that is solved in principle but expert-scarce, so AI makes it routine for every vehicle. Better electron-density prediction also benefits from the ionization kinetics in the radiation node.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.strongest_case_small: Relaying through the wake to Starlink already largely solves the operational problem. Magnetic windows need heavy, high-field magnets, so the practical impact is small.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.signpost: A published coupled flowfield-plasma-EM blackout prediction, set up by AI agents, validated against flight signal-attenuation or electron-density data (RAM-C II or shared capsule telemetry) and used in a vehicle antenna-placement trade.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor vs advocate] S3 2027 -> 2028 rather than S2 2028 -> 2027: all three agree S2 = S3 before 2028; two lenses put it at 2028 (a validated, published tool a year after applied-math access). [skeptic+auditor] Signpost replaced (the old one, active blackout mitigation in flight, 'would be a surprise before 2030' and contradicted a High node dated 2028). [skeptic] Hard edge from hyper-flight-data-pipeline made soft (pipeline capsules carry thermal sensors, not plasma diagnostics). [advocate] Soft edge from capability-controlled-data-access.

revisions.from: Coupled plasma-sheath and RF-link prediction tools

hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.title: Rapidly reusable orbital heat shield (ship scale)
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.description: One Starship-class orbital vehicle reflies at least 5 times, with heat-shield turnaround under ~2 weeks and tile replacement limited to a small fraction per flight.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.status_oct2026: First orbital flight on 28 Sep 2026 (Flight 14, two orbits, early deorbit, splashdown). No ship has been caught or reflown; Musk gives the Flight 15 ship-catch attempt 'at least 50 or 60 percent' odds. The tile stress test on Flight 13 showed cracking and gap streaks; Musk called the heat-shield problem solved (4 Aug 2026) while Dan Rasky called the current tile TPS a dead end for rapid reuse (29 Jul 2026).
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.why: Ship catch, then reflight, then 5 reflights is a hardware-iteration sequence paced by flight count. Super Heavy: first catch Oct 2024 and first caught-booster reflight ~7 months later, yet V3 boosters failed landing burns on Flights 12-13 in 2026, so booster reflight is not routine two years on. Falcon 9 took ~4 years from first landing to a booster's 5th flight (general), and each life data point costs a flight (physclock reuse-learning row, 0.8-0.9x in S2). Mach33's base case has 3.3, 4.8, 8.9 and 18 flights per stack in 2027-30; 18 implies a ~20-day average turnaround in 2030, so a ship with 5 reflights and under-2-week heat-shield turnaround is on the base path around 2030 in S2. AI damage models, fleet-trained heating models and inspection theory pull it forward by perhaps 6-12 months; they do not change the ceramic material or the flight clock. The band stays Medium in every scenario: this node is strictly harder than physclock-heavy-cadence-100 (High in S2), and the dead-end risk is real.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.strongest_case_small: SpaceX gets there through empirical hardware iteration, with or without AI mathematics. If the tile concept is a dead end for rapid reuse (Rasky), the fix is a new TPS architecture, a fabrication and qualification problem measured in years.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.signpost: First ship catch and reflight (2027?), with published turnaround time and tile replacement counts.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+advocate+auditor] Hard edges from hyper-tile-damage-accumulation and hyper-tps-inverse-nde made soft (the node's own strongest case: SpaceX gets there with or without AI mathematics). [advocate] Soft edges added from physclock-twin-reflight-clearance and new hyper-fleet-aerothermal-twin. [skeptic] Years 2030/2029/2028 -> 2031/2030/2029: no ship caught as of Oct 2026; S3 2028 predated S3's divergence from S2; the advocate's own Mach33 arithmetic puts the base path at ~2030. [advocate vs skeptic/auditor] Advocate's S2/S3 High rejected: 5 reflights with <2-week turnaround is strictly harder than 100+ reusable launches a year, so High there implies roughly Medium here, consistent with physclock nodes. [skeptic] Booster-reuse sentence replaced with the Super Heavy record. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): soft edge from physclock-twin-reflight-clearance removed: this node is a hard prerequisite of that one, so it cannot accelerate it (hard/soft 2-cycle).

hyper-thinner-tps-flown.title: Flown heat shield sized with reduced, model-based margins
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.description: A flown reentry capsule or planetary probe whose TPS was sized by probabilistic, model-based margins and is at least ~10% thinner (or lighter) than the same operator's previous flown design for a comparable entry, with the reduction attributed to probabilistic sizing and flight data confirming the bondline predictions.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.status_oct2026: Commercial capsules fly every few months: Varda W-5 (Jan 2026) and W-6 (recovered May 2026) were recovered, W-4 burned up on reentry (22 May 2026). W-6 flew two NASA Ames instrumented eChar shoulder tiles and a Sandia nose tile with TPS material samples, so the instrumented flight-experiment channel exists. Varda holds an FAA Part 450 operator licence (Jun 2025, issued for W-4) that covers repeated W-series reentries without mission-by-mission approval (valid through 2028 per The Register, 2029 per Wikipedia). NASA's preliminary SRL study suggests ~25% thinning at one location under stated assumptions.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.why: This is the shortest chain in the domain from AI mathematics to flown hardware. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math (2027) -> joint margin budgets on demand (hyper-certified-margin-uq, 2028) -> a capsule maker adopts probabilistic sizing at a design review (2029) -> shield build and arc-jet check (12-18 months on the lag ladder) -> a commercial reentry with an instrumented bondline (2030). The transferable thinning for LEO capsules (~7.5-7.8 km/s, little radiative heating) is smaller than SRL's Mars figure, hence the >=10% threshold. It frees up to ~1-3% of entry mass (judgment) and turns each flight into a calibration point. P7 defaults to Speculative; the band is raised to Medium in S2 and S3 because commercial capsules iterate in months, operator licensing no longer gates each flight, and no certification body must accept margins. It cannot exceed its adoption prerequisite (Medium), and S3 adds no physical speed-up to the launch and adoption gates that bind here.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.strongest_case_small: Capsule makers may prefer to spend the margin on reliability and reuse rather than mass, so the change may be invisible from outside. Payload mass is rarely the binding constraint on small capsules.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.signpost: A capsule operator reports flight-measured bondline temperatures matching pre-flight probabilistic predictions on a thinned heat shield.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder. S3 2028 equalled its prerequisite hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing (S3 2028). A capsule heat shield sized by the new method is a derivative payload: 12-18 months design-complete to flight (8-14 months at S3 physical speed). Chain (S3): probabilistic sizing 2028 -> shield build and arc-jet check -> commercial capsule reentry 2029. S3 2028 -> 2029; band unchanged.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] Threshold redefined against the operator's own previous design (stacked-factor baseline is unobservable for commercial operators; LEO thinning smaller than Mars). [skeptic] S2/S3 2029 -> 2030, following the sizing shift plus the 12-18 month lag ladder. [skeptic+auditor vs advocate] S3 High -> Medium; advocate's S2 Medium -> High rejected: both S2 and S3 sit at the Medium of the hard prerequisite hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing, which resolves the advocate's 'no S2/S3 mechanism' point in the other direction. [advocate+auditor] Part 450 licence and W-6 instrumented tiles added to status (licence verified; validity date differs between sources). Full P7 chain written out.

hyper-aerocapture-demo.title: First aerocapture flight demonstration
hyper-aerocapture-demo.description: A vehicle uses a single atmospheric pass to capture into orbit (an Earth demonstration), validating the guidance, aerothermal and model-correlation performance that a planetary flagship would need before relying on aerocapture.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.status_oct2026: Aerocapture has never flown. On 11 Sep 2026 Inversion received a $350k firm-fixed-price NASA order to study an Arc-based Earth aerocapture demo, running to 30 Jun 2027 with NASA Ames support. Inversion's Arc, a maneuvering lifting reentry vehicle, is planned to fly first in 2026, so a candidate demo vehicle exists. Uranus studies find MSL-heritage aeroshells adequate; that a flight demo must precede flagship reliance is widely assumed (general, unverified against the cited abstract).
hyper-aerocapture-demo.why: Chain (S2): the $350k NASA/Inversion study ends 30 Jun 2027 -> a NASA flight award in FY2028 at the earliest, or Inversion self-funding (capital and appropriations, 1.0x; continuing resolutions are common) -> Arc modification and guidance, dispersion, aerothermal and rarefied analysis (AI-compressed) -> rideshare launch -> single-pass Earth aerocapture, 2030 at the earliest. AI collapses analysis cost, so a small commercial vehicle could attempt the demo for tens of millions of dollars, but analysis cost was never the barrier: funding and a ride bind, and S3 cannot speed a 2027-28 funding decision because S3 equals S2 until 2028. Without an award by 2028 the domain's own signpost keeps this Low.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.strongest_case_small: Analysis cost was never the barrier; NASA funding is, and the planetary budget is under pressure. The study is only $350k.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.signpost: NASA awards a flight contract for an aerocapture demo after the study ends in June 2027.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] S2/S3 Medium -> Low (P7 default Speculative; only a $350k study is funded; capital gate 1.0x). [skeptic] S2/S3 2029 -> 2030 (FY2028 award plus ~2 years build and manifest). [skeptic+auditor] Hard edges from cap-applied-math and hyper-flight-data-pipeline made soft. [advocate] Soft edges from hyper-aerothermal-design-loop and hyper-certified-edl-guidance (the why names this analysis); kinetic-solver soft edge not added (aerocapture peak heating is continuum, per skeptic). [advocate] Arc first-flight status added. [auditor] 'Require a flight demo' claim marked unverified; chain written out.

hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.title: Ground-validated design basis for 12-14 km/s Earth return
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.description: A validated aerothermal environment (radiative plus convective) and TPS response model (HEEET-class 3D woven material) for crewed Mars-return or other large-radius (nose radius above ~2-3 m) Earth entries at 12-14 km/s, where radiation dominates, with radiative uncertainty of 25% or less, accepted by a mission project.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.status_oct2026: HEEET is qualified for ~1,500-8,000 W/cm2 and 1-10 atm (HEEET-1004). Radiation becomes first-order above ~12 km/s for large nose radii. Small fast sample-return capsules already fly ~12-13 km/s entries on heritage PICA-class TPS (Stardust, OSIRIS-REx; general), where radiative heating is minor at small nose radius; CNSA's Tianwen-2 capsule (landing planned 29 Nov 2027) and JAXA's MMX (launch NET 19 Oct 2026, sample return 2031) are funded examples (~12 km/s class, general). No funded large-radius or crewed 12+ km/s entry is planned before 2031.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.why: Specific kinetic energy is ~72 MJ/kg at 12 km/s against ~30 MJ/kg from LEO, and for large-radius bodies radiation dominates. Radiative uncertainty sets material choice and thickness. Chain (S2): mission pull -> AI-built kinetics and ablator models (2030) -> EAST and arc-jet validation (1-2 years) -> project acceptance, 2031 at the earliest. Without a mission to pull the work, nobody spends the shock-tube and arc-jet time.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.strongest_case_small: No funded large-radius or crewed mission needs it before 2031. Ground facilities cannot replicate the combined environment, and flight tests at these speeds are extremely rare.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.signpost: NASA or ESA selects a mission with Earth entry at 12 km/s or more and a radiative heating factor below 1.3.

hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.title: Next large inflatable or folding heat shield flies
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.description: An orbital-entry flight of an inflatable (HIAD) or mechanically deployable (ADEPT) aeroshell of 10 m class or larger, the scale path toward the 16-18 m aeroshells studied for heavy Mars landers.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.status_oct2026: LOFTID (6 m) flew in Nov 2022. No funded 10 m-class follow-on was found as of Oct 2026. Commercial inflatable decelerators now fly on rideshare: ATMOS Space Cargo's Phoenix 1 inflated its heat shield before entry interface on Bandwagon-3 (Apr 2025), though it was not recovered; none is 10 m class. NASA's EDL Architecture Study considered HIAD and ADEPT for 20 t Mars payloads.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.why: Coupled fluid-structure-thermal behavior of flexible TPS (nonlinear membrane mechanics, flutter, fabric permeability) suits AI applied math well, but LOFTID flew without it. Chain: NASA STMD, ULA or a commercial firm funds a 10 m+ HIAD or ADEPT flight (no line as of Oct 2026) -> multi-year build (LOFTID took several years; general) -> secondary ride on a LEO launch -> orbital entry, 2030 at the earliest in every scenario, because the capital gate compresses 1.0x.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.strongest_case_small: Starship's rigid-body approach to heavy Mars EDL may make deployables irrelevant for cargo, and no budget line exists.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.signpost: NASA or ULA announces a LOFTID follow-on flight.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] Hard edge from cap-applied-math made soft (LOFTID flew without AI mathematics; the gate is a budget line). [auditor] S1 >2031 -> 2030 (capital gate is 1.0x, so S1 should not trail S2 on cognition alone); chain written out. [advocate, verified on SatNews] ATMOS Phoenix 1 added. Bands Low x3 unchanged.

hyper-mars-heavy-landing.title: First landing of 20 t or more on Mars
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.description: A Starship-class or other vehicle lands 20 t or more intact on Mars, demonstrating heavy Mars EDL: entry at ~6-7.5 km/s, aerobraking, then retropropulsive descent.
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.status_oct2026: On 8 Feb 2026 Musk said SpaceX had shifted focus to a city on the Moon, with Mars to follow in roughly 5-7 years. The S-1 (20 May 2026) gives no Mars date. Starship reached orbit on 28 Sep 2026 and has not yet attempted propellant transfer. The late-2026 window is effectively not being used for a landing attempt (general inference).
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.why: The binding clock is the 26-month synodic window. Chain: first ship-to-ship propellant transfer (prop-ship-transfer-demo, 2027?) -> tanker campaign for trans-Mars injection -> uncrewed launch in the late-2028/early-2029 window or the Feb-Mar 2031 window -> 6-7 month cruise -> entry at ~6-7.5 km/s in CO2 plus supersonic retropropulsive landing, arriving ~Sep-Nov 2031 for the later window. SpaceX has made no 2028-window commitment and in Feb 2026 put Mars about 5-7 years out behind a Moon-first priority, so a landing by end-2031 most likely needs first-attempt success on the last window. AI mathematics improves SRP and aerothermal models, which raises the odds of a first attempt succeeding but cannot add windows; the gates (windows, propellant transfer at scale, corporate priority) compress ~1.0x in every scenario, so the band is Low in all three. Radiative heating matters more than for Earth return at this speed for a ~9 m vehicle (hyper-radiation-kinetics).
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.strongest_case_small: AI mathematics has a near-nil effect on whether or when this happens. SpaceX's strategic choice and orbital refilling decide.
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.signpost: A SpaceX commitment to the late-2028 window, or the first ship-to-ship propellant transfer (2027?).
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+advocate+auditor] Hard edge from hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models made soft (SpaceX can land on proprietary empirical models and accept risk, per the SRP node's own strongest case). [skeptic] Hard edge from hyper-flight-data-pipeline removed (capsule and testbed data carry no Mars SRP information); owner data enter via soft edge from hyper-fleet-aerothermal-twin (advocate). [advocate] Soft edge from hyper-radiation-kinetics (CO2 radiative heating at large nose radius). [skeptic+auditor] S3 Medium -> Low: the S3 'whole program' argument acts on gates that compress ~1.0x. [skeptic] '0.5-1 t on a 20 t-class lander' removed here (it applies to ablator-shielded NASA concepts, not Starship tiles). [auditor] Chain written out.

hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.title: Point-to-point rocket cargo, repeated demonstration flights
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.description: At least 3 suborbital point-to-point flights deliver 30 t or more of cargo to remote landing sites, with the vehicle recovered, per the Space Force Point-to-Point Delivery (P2PD) concept.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.status_oct2026: AFRL awarded SpaceX a $102M, 5-year contract (2022) to demonstrate rocket cargo; the program goal is ~100 short tons anywhere within an hour, and a demonstration was targeted as early as 2026. The Johnston Atoll environmental assessment (filed Feb 2025; up to 10 reentry-vehicle landings a year) was suspended in July 2025. No demonstration as of Oct 2026.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.why: Chain: ship catch and reflight (physclock-starship-full-reuse) -> landing at a remote pad under a new environmental assessment -> range, overflight and host-nation approvals -> 3 recovered cargo flights. Three demo flights need a ship that survives entry and lands, not 5 reflights at 2-week turnaround, and suborbital P2P entries are below orbital speed. Of the remaining gates only the aerothermal design is cognitive, and it is already adequate. AI mathematics has essentially no effect on the regulatory and range gates.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.strongest_case_small: The effect is nil. The program's fate turns on DoD priorities and SpaceX's manifest.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.signpost: A new environmental assessment or range agreement for P2PD landing sites.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+advocate+auditor] Hard prerequisite hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield replaced by physclock-starship-full-reuse; rapid reuse and the fleet-trained heating model kept as soft edges. [auditor, verified on Wikipedia] Status corrected: the source does not support '~30 t in a 2026 test' ($102M contract, ~100 short-ton goal, demo as early as 2026). Chain written out. Years and bands unchanged (regulatory gate).

hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.title: Routine, cheap reentry: 50+ commercial returns a year
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.description: Commercial capsule returns (in-space manufacturing, defense hypersonic testbeds, cargo) exceed ~50 a year worldwide, and TPS is no longer a pacing or major cost item. Counts free-flying return capsules only; excludes Starship and other launch-vehicle stage returns and ISS crew and cargo vehicles.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.status_oct2026: Varda 2026 to date: W-5 (29 Jan) and W-6 (18-19 May) recovered, W-4 failed and burned up (22 May); its stated monthly-by-2026 target has slipped. Varda's FAA Part 450 operator licence (Jun 2025) removes mission-by-mission approval for W-series reentries. Inversion's Arc has not yet flown (first flight planned 2026); The Exploration Company and others are developing capsules (general). Landing sites are limited, for example Koonibba in South Australia.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.pathway: P7 (market and physical clock; AI-math effect marginal)
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.why: Going from ~3-5 commercial returns a year (2026) to 50+ is a >10x increase, and announced cadences in this tree have missed by 1.5-3x or more (physclock slip table). Chain (S2): Varda reaches monthly (2027-28) -> 3-4 more operators reach monthly cadence -> MACH-TB Task Area 3 capsule tests and in-space manufacturing demand fill manifests -> 50+ a year, 2031 at the earliest. Binding: demand for returned products, rideshare slots, landing-site licensing and operations staffing. AI mathematics contributes at the margin: cheaper qualification by analysis for each new capsule variant, thinner and partly reusable TPS (up to ~1-3% of entry mass), faster design iterations and some operations automation (S3). Licensing reform (physclock-licensing-in-weeks) and cheap launch (physclock-heavy-cadence-100) matter more than any of these.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.strongest_case_small: Demand is unproven, TPS is already a small share of cost, and launch rideshare cadence and reentry licensing bind first.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.signpost: A count of commercial reentries in 2028 above 20, with more than one operator.

hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.title: Aerocapture baselined for an outer-planet flagship
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.description: NASA or ESA baselines aerocapture for a Uranus, Neptune or Titan orbiter, cutting cruise time by years and shifting propellant mass to science.
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.status_oct2026: The Uranus Orbiter and Probe baseline uses propulsive orbit insertion with a 13-15 year cruise (arXiv 2310.14514). Uranus aerocapture studies find MSL-heritage aeroshells adequate (NTRS 20240014677); that a flight demo must come first is widely assumed (general).
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.why: Aerocapture can cut cruise to Uranus by several years and save insertion propellant (Uranus aerocapture literature). Chain: aerocapture demo succeeds (2030 at the earliest) -> NASA new start for the Uranus Orbiter and Probe, or an ESA study, adopts aerocapture -> aerocapture is baseline at mission concept review (2031 or later). Flagship programs run 8-15 years and appropriations compress 1.0x. AI-cheapened analysis and verifiable guidance lower perceived risk, but a first-ever demo (Low) and a flagship baseline decision must both land inside 2031.
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.strongest_case_small: Pressure on NASA's planetary budget makes any new flagship baseline decision unlikely before 2031, whatever the technology.
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.signpost: A Uranus flagship study update that carries aerocapture as baseline rather than as an option.
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] S2/S3 Low -> Speculative (conjunction of a Low first-ever demo and a flagship decision; P7 default). [skeptic] S2 2031 -> >2031, S3 2030 -> 2031 (a baseline in the demo year assumed zero review lag; demo now 2030). [auditor] Chain written out; cruise-time claim sourced to arXiv 2310.14514; 'requires a flight demo' marked general.

materials-dft-limits.title: Proven limits of the workhorse quantum-chemistry method
materials-dft-limits.description: Theorems marking where Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT), and any efficient universal method for electronic energies, must fail: some ensemble densities have no Kohn-Sham representation (278), the ground-state energy of continuum Coulomb systems is QMA-hard (275), and an atom can bind only a bounded number of extra electrons (263, conditional; only its large-ionization asymptotics are formalized).
materials-dft-limits.status_oct2026: Claimed in openai/math (Oct 6, 2026). 278 and 275 are manuscript-only (T1). 263's Lean part covers only large-ionization asymptotics for the nonrelativistic two-spin Coulomb atom (I_m(Z)/m^(7/3) tends to a Thomas-Fermi constant), T3; the bounded-excess-charge (ionization conjecture) headline is manuscript-only (T1). No named outside expert endorsement or Comparator run found as of Oct 7, 2026.
materials-dft-limits.why: DFT is the workhorse for screening alloys, ceramics, semiconductors, battery electrolytes and propellant chemistry. If 278 holds, some ensemble densities have no Kohn-Sham representation even with the exact functional; whether physically relevant open-shell or defect systems fall in that class is not shown (conditional, speculative mapping). If 275 holds, no efficient classical or quantum algorithm computes ground-state energies of all molecules and solids, assuming QMA is not contained in BQP. Ceiling results act within months (P3): they tell method developers to stop seeking one universal functional and to invest in domain-specific, data-driven corrections and targeted high-level methods. Band: P3 defaults to High; one band down in every scenario because the ceilings are conditional on 278 and 275 (T1). Formalization of continuum quantum mechanics catching up by ~2028 (S2/S3) speeds checking but does not raise the chance that an unverified result is correct.
materials-dft-limits.strongest_case_small: Practitioners already treat DFT as an uncontrolled approximation, and QMA-hardness of the universal functional on lattice models has been known since 2009 (general). Worst-case hardness says nothing about the structured instances space engineers compute. No code, workflow or flown material changes because of these theorems.
materials-dft-limits.signpost: A named electronic-structure theorist endorses or refutes 278/275 (moving them to T2), or an outside Comparator run of 263, by mid-2027; 278 cited in a functional-development paper as the reason for a design choice.
materials-dft-limits.calibration_note: A3: T1 premise rule: the drop for 278 and 275 (T1) was applied only in S1; future formalization speeds checking but does not raise the chance an unverified result is correct. Medium/High/High -> Medium/Medium/Medium; why reworded to say conditional.

materials-mlip-certified-uq.title: Atomistic AI models with trustworthy error bars
materials-mlip-certified-uq.description: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) that report calibrated, property-level uncertainty (melting point, diffusion barrier, elastic constants) with documented coverage on held-out chemistries (formal coverage only under stated distribution-shift assumptions) and out-of-distribution flags, so atomistic predictions can feed design decisions without case-by-case DFT checks.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.status_oct2026: Universal MLIPs are fast but uncertified. Meta's UMA family was trained on ~500M structures; UMA-M-1.1 scores F1 = 0.929 on Matbench Discovery, and UMA-S runs 1,000 atoms at ~16 steps/s on one GPU and fits >100,000 atoms in 80 GB (arXiv 2506.23971). Ensemble and conformal uncertainty methods exist, but without guarantees for properties derived from long molecular-dynamics runs; distribution-free conformal coverage does not survive covariate shift unless the likelihood ratio is known (Tibshirani et al., arXiv 1904.06019), and otherwise degrades with the size of the shift (Barber et al., arXiv 2202.13415). No catalog family addresses this.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.why: MLIPs are roughly 10^4-10^5 times cheaper than DFT for the same atoms (general), enabling nanosecond simulations of 10^5-atom cells, the scale where creep-relevant diffusion, grain-boundary oxidation and radiation-damage cascades happen. What blocks engineering use is trust: errors in unfamiliar configurations propagate unpredictably into derived properties. Bounding that propagation (perturbation bounds for stochastic dynamics, conformal coverage under distribution shift) is bespoke applied math that S2's research-grade capability attacks directly; the binding gate then becomes high-level reference data to test coverage, which is why the node lands in 2028, a year after cap-applied-math. Coverage on novel chemistries is conditional on the stated shift assumptions by construction. Unlocks high-throughput alloy, ceramic and electrolyte screening with error bars.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.strongest_case_small: Certification is only relative to the reference method, which inherits DFT's own errors (see 278); and the properties engineers qualify (creep, fatigue, toughness) are governed by microstructure at micron-to-millimetre scales that atomistics never reaches.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.signpost: A major MLIP release (UMA, MACE or Orb successors) ships property-level uncertainty with published coverage tests on held-out chemistries by end-2027, and NASA or AFRL ICME workflows adopt it.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (timing, two lenses): S2 and S3 2027 -> 2028; a data-gated node cannot land the same year as cap-applied-math (2027) because coverage must be tested against new high-level reference data and long MD runs. Description: 'coverage guarantees' -> documented coverage, formal only under stated shift assumptions (Tibshirani et al. 1904.06019; Barber et al. 2202.13415). Status: UMA figures corrected (auditor; arXiv 2506.23971). Bands unchanged; downstream nodes (2028-2030) stay consistent.

materials-multiscale-certified.title: Certified bridges from microstructure to part properties
materials-multiscale-certified.description: Quantitative homogenization and coarse-graining theorems with computable error bounds for nonlinear, inelastic, random microstructures (printed metals, ceramic-matrix composites), so effective properties and their scatter follow from microstructure statistics with certified error.
materials-multiscale-certified.status_oct2026: Quantitative stochastic homogenization exists for linear elliptic problems; plasticity, damage and fatigue in random microstructures remain open (general). No catalog family addresses it, and the release's PDE formalization is thin (3 of 16 PDE families have Lean).
materials-multiscale-certified.why: This is a genuinely open research problem, not an expert-scarcity problem: today engineers bridge scales with calibrated empirical models and test scatter. Under S2, AI does research-grade PDE analysis by 2027-28, making a usable certified bound for one engineering class (for example elasto-viscoplastic polycrystals with porosity) plausible by 2029. Payoff: predicted scatter of fatigue and creep properties from microstructure, the missing link that would let allowables lean on models instead of hundreds of coupons.
materials-multiscale-certified.strongest_case_small: Rigorous bounds for nonlinear problems tend to be loose; engineers already get usable answers from calibrated crystal-plasticity finite elements; and fatigue is governed by rare worst defects (extreme-value statistics), not homogenized averages.
materials-multiscale-certified.signpost: A peer-reviewed or Comparator-checked quantitative homogenization result for a nonlinear inelastic random medium with explicit constants by 2028; Mathlib gains Sobolev-space and homogenization infrastructure.

materials-allowables-stats-framework.title: Design allowables from far fewer test coupons
materials-allowables-stats-framework.description: Statistical methods with proven coverage (hierarchical Bayesian, ICME-informed, transfer learning across machines and lots) that yield A- and B-basis design allowables from far fewer physical tests, accepted in MMPDS Volume II, CMH-17 and NASA-STD-6030 practice.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.status_oct2026: MMPDS created Volume II for process-sensitive materials such as additively manufactured (AM) metals; Senvol's machine-learning approach was shown equivalent to the conventional approach in America Makes work; America Makes still funds conventional allowables (GOTHAAM, $5.5M, 2026 call, AM 7075-class aluminium across three machine classes). NASA is characterizing ~50 AM materials across 8,000+ samples. NASA-STD-6030 (2021) ties allowables to statistical process control of each qualified process.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.why: Directly computed MMPDS-style A/B values traditionally need about 100 observations from at least 10 heats or lots, and a nonparametric A-basis needs 299 (general). For AM, 'a new process means a new material' (NASA AMRL framework, Apr 2026), so each machine and parameter set restarts the clock. Methods that pool information across machines and lots with provable tolerance-bound coverage could cut coupons 40-60% (assumption) and, more importantly, lots and calendar time. The math is solved in principle but expert-scarce, exactly what on-demand AI supplies; handbook-committee acceptance binds, so the band is capped at Medium. 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, Lean, T3) is theory for the posterior sampling these methods use; constants unknown, effect marginal.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.strongest_case_small: Statistics were never the hard part: regulators want physical lot-to-lot variability that only production time generates; handbook committees revise on multi-year cycles; and any coverage proof rests on assumptions (exchangeability across machines) that reviewers will dispute.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.signpost: An MMPDS or CMH-17 coordination group approves a model-informed or Bayesian allowables method, or a NASA-STD-6030 revision references model-based allowables, by 2029.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.calibration_note: A3: Cross-domain consistency: handbook acceptance (MMPDS, CMH-17, NASA-STD-6030) of AI-derived allowables methods is a standards revision, which physclock-credibility-evidence-standard puts at S2 2029 (standards revise on 3-6 year cycles). S1 2030 -> 2031, S2 2028 -> 2029; S3 unchanged; bands unchanged (capped Medium).
materials-allowables-stats-framework.revision_note: B-certification: [auditor] Signpost date 2028 -> 2029 to match the S2 year. Note: the A3 calibration cited '3-6 year' standards cycles from physclock-credibility-evidence-standard, now corrected to 8-10 years for base standards; this node's years stand because MMPDS and CMH-17 coordination groups can approve methods between base revisions (general).

materials-autonomous-characterization.title: Reliable automated structure identification
materials-autonomous-characterization.description: Robust, uncertainty-aware solution of the characterization inverse problem (automated Rietveld refinement, disorder-aware phase identification, fusion of X-ray, neutron and electron-microscopy data) so autonomous labs' claims of new materials survive expert scrutiny.
materials-autonomous-characterization.status_oct2026: The A-Lab's 41 claimed novel compounds (from 58 targets) were disputed by Palgrave, Schoop and colleagues (ChemRxiv Jan 2024; PRX Energy 2024), who judged automated Rietveld analysis unreliable and concluded no new materials had been shown; Jakob, Margraf et al. (Adv. Mater. 2025) estimate that 80-84% of GNoME's predicted stable compounds are likely disordered in practice.
materials-autonomous-characterization.why: Autonomous-lab throughput (DeepMind's UK lab plans hundreds of materials per day) is worthless if phase identification is wrong. Structure refinement is a non-convex inverse problem with identifiability limits; AI applied math can supply identifiability analysis, Bayesian refinement with calibrated posteriors and explicit disorder models. This unlocks credible closed-loop discovery, which the space chains (PV absorbers, coatings, electrolytes) need first.
materials-autonomous-characterization.strongest_case_small: Some ambiguities are physical (powder X-ray diffraction cannot distinguish certain orderings), so resolving them needs neutron, synchrotron or electron-microscope time, a facility gate that math cannot remove.
materials-autonomous-characterization.signpost: A blind round-robin in which automated characterization matches expert refinement on at least 90% of samples, or an autonomous-lab discovery paper that passes a published expert audit, by 2027.
materials-autonomous-characterization.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (fact, contradicted): the A-Lab claimed 41 novel compounds (from 58 targets), not 43; the 80-84% disorder estimate comes from Jakob, Margraf et al. (Adv. Mater. 2025), not 404 Media. Years and bands unchanged.

materials-learned-functionals.title: Chemical accuracy from cheap quantum chemistry
materials-learned-functionals.description: Machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals and atomistic models trained on wavefunction-level data that reach about 1 kcal/mol accuracy at semi-local DFT cost, extended from main-group molecules to transition metals, oxides and solids.
materials-learned-functionals.status_oct2026: Microsoft's Skala (preprint Jun 2025) reaches 2.8 kcal/mol on the GMTKN55 benchmark and chemical accuracy on small-molecule atomization energies at semi-local cost; transition metals and solids are not yet covered. 278 (T1, conditional) marks a class of ensemble densities that no Kohn-Sham scheme can represent.
materials-learned-functionals.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 278 is T1, conditional, bounds the scope only
materials-learned-functionals.why: Cutting energy errors from ~3-5 kcal/mol (hybrid functionals, general) to ~1 kcal/mol changes the reliability of rankings for propellant decomposition pathways, oxide-scale formation on ceramics and superalloys, defect levels in radiation-damaged semiconductors and electrolyte stability windows. Reference data bind: coupled-cluster and quantum Monte Carlo labels are compute-expensive, so S2 brings the node forward mainly through AI-derived exact constraints and active learning that cut data needs. For multireference transition-metal chemistry the coupled-cluster references are themselves rarely accurate to 1 kcal/mol (general), so the target is partly limited by its own benchmarks; that keeps the band at Medium even in S3. 278 (T1, conditional) tells developers where Kohn-Sham-based learning must fail (strong static correlation), steering effort to embedding methods there. Alloy design and main-group energetics do not need this node (soft links): alloys run on CALPHAD and kinetics, energetics on main-group chemistry Skala-class functionals already cover.
materials-learned-functionals.strongest_case_small: Most space-materials properties are limited by temperature, kinetics and microstructure, not by 1-3 kcal/mol of electronic energy; and 278/275 (T1, conditional) set worst-case limits for strongly correlated systems.
materials-learned-functionals.signpost: A learned functional with documented error of 1 kcal/mol or less on transition-metal and solid-state benchmarks, released openly, by 2028.
materials-learned-functionals.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: 278 bounds scope; the band rests on capability.
