physclock-new-entrant-fast-orbit.title: A new reusable launcher from start to orbit in three years
physclock-new-entrant-fast-orbit.description: A program in any country started in 2027 or later reaches orbit with a reusable medium or heavy launcher within three years of program start.
physclock-new-entrant-fast-orbit.status_oct2026: Historical: Falcon 9 about 5 years (2005-2010) and Electron about 5 years to orbit (2013-2018) (general); New Glenn announced 2016 for 2020 and flew Jan 2025; Neutron announced Mar 2021 and is NET Q4 2026; the BE-4 engine alone took from 2011 to first flight in Jan 2024 (Wikipedia).
physclock-new-entrant-fast-orbit.why: Even with cognitive work nearly free, engine development (hot-fire campaigns, turbopump failures), pad construction (2-4 years) and flight-test learning set a floor of about 4-5 years. AI's best case removes about a year, and only programs started after AI adoption (2027-28 in S2) benefit. The realistic path is a derivative built around an existing engine family: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 (TQ-12-family methalox engines from Zhuque-2) hopped in Jan 2024, reached orbit Dec 3 2025 and landed its first stage on its second flight, Aug 18 2026 (Wikipedia), on roughly a four-year derivative timeline without AI help (general). Clean-sheet multipliers of 0.8-0.9x (S2) and 0.7-0.8x (S3) on such a timeline give about 3.2-3.6 years in S2, so Speculative, and 2.8-3.2 years in S3, so Low. FAA licensing reform and AI-run test stands help U.S. entrants but are not gates for every entrant.
physclock-new-entrant-fast-orbit.strongest_case_small: This node is itself the small-effect case; the exception would be a derivative vehicle built around an existing engine.
physclock-new-entrant-fast-orbit.signpost: A 2027-28 program reaching full-scale hot fire within 12 months and pad readiness within 24.
physclock-new-entrant-fast-orbit.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Debated: skeptic wanted FAA-only scope and S3 Low -> Speculative; advocate wanted global scope, S2 Speculative -> Low and soft licensing/test-stand edges. Resolved: global scope with soft edges (advocate), years and bands unchanged because the Zhuque-3 derivative precedent (~4 years) times the physclock multipliers lands just above 3 years in S2 and at about 3 in S3.

physclock-satellite-gen-cadence.title: New satellite generations every year
physclock-satellite-gen-cadence.description: Leading commercial constellation operators field a new satellite generation (new bus or payload, not only software) about every 12 months, against 18-36 months today.
physclock-satellite-gen-cadence.status_oct2026: Starlink: v0.9 May 2019, v1.0 late 2019, v1.5 2021, v2 mini Feb 2023, v2 mini optimized (average satellite mass down from 623 kg to 575 kg, 96 Gbps), V3 (about 1 Tbps, about 2 t) first flown on Flight 13 (Jul 2026) and first orbited on Flight 14 (Sep 28 2026). V3's timing was gated by Starship, not the satellite. V2 mini production reached six a day by Mar 2023 (Wikipedia; Mach33). SpaceX's first compute satellite, Starmind AI1 (spec disclosed Jun 2026), uses modular, interchangeable chip inserts, and its power target rose from 150 kW (Jun) to about 250 kW (Oct 2026) (Mach33).
physclock-satellite-gen-cadence.why: Chain (S2): engineering adoption 2028 -> first AI-era bus or payload designed, qualified and retooled in about 12-15 months -> fielded 2029 -> a second generation about 12 months later shows the cadence, 2030. S3: same adoption year, but commercial generations compress 0.5-0.7x (18-36 months becomes 9-25), so 2029 at the optimistic edge; an annual cadence sits at the favorable end even there, so Medium. Design, software and verification compress in S2; payload qualification, radiation testing, line retooling and the launcher bind (V3's timing was set by Starship). Upside not driven by AI math: orbital-compute satellites may track the accelerator makers' annual cadence (general) with modular chip inserts on a common bus, making a yearly payload generation a chip swap. Faster generations raise capacity per kilogram (V3 carries about three times V2 mini's capacity per kilogram, Mach33).
physclock-satellite-gen-cadence.strongest_case_small: Generation cadence is set by launcher steps and fleet economics (about five-year satellite life), not design speed; operators may prefer continuous incremental change.
physclock-satellite-gen-cadence.signpost: A Starlink V3.x or V4 announcement within 18 months of V3; Amazon Leo's second-generation timeline.

plasma-vm-wellposed.title: Relativistic plasma equations proved well-behaved (checked)
plasma-vm-wellposed.description: The claimed proof that the 3D relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell system has global smooth solutions for smooth finite-energy data passes an outside Comparator run and a statement audit, moving from T3 to T4. The system is the kinetic equation for collisionless plasma coupled to Maxwell's equations; family 362 covers one species in 3D, per the release overview. This is the Glassey-Strauss global-regularity problem, open since the 1980s.
plasma-vm-wellposed.status_oct2026: Family 362 [L], T3: agent-written Lean main result in the repo, unchecked by outsiders as of 2026-10-07; no outside commentary on 362 found in search. Before the release, only continuation criteria (Glassey-Strauss 1986: smooth while momentum support stays bounded), small-data and symmetric results existed, e.g. vacuum stability for relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann (Cao and Li, arXiv 2601.04018, Jan 2026).
plasma-vm-wellposed.why: The Lean proof exists, so a Comparator run is cheap; the slow part is the statement audit (does the Lean definition of the system, its function spaces and 'finite energy' match what physicists mean?). The March 2026 AI-assisted formalization of the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium reported exactly these definition-alignment bugs and hypothesis creep, which is why the gate is formalization rather than cognition. Hexagon (launched Oct 6, 2026) exists to do this. Once T4, kinetic codes for the one-species relativistic system are known to approximate a solution that exists and stays smooth for all time: a confidence gain, per tl-position-2. Real plasmas have at least two species, so the multi-species case stays open.
plasma-vm-wellposed.strongest_case_small: Codes never waited for this; physicists assumed it. The theorem covers the whole-space relativistic system without walls, collisions or external circuits, while Hall-thruster, magnetic-nozzle and magnetosphere codes use electrostatic, non-relativistic, collisional or bounded-domain versions that are different equations. Nothing in a thruster, forecast or fusion device changes.
plasma-vm-wellposed.signpost: An outside Comparator report and statement audit for family 362 posted on Hexagon or by a kinetic-theory group within 12 months. The audit must state whether the Lean statement covers one species only and which data class it assumes (e.g. compact momentum support versus finite energy). A definition mismatch found in the audit would break this node.
plasma-vm-wellposed.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (statement-gap rule, tr-position-2): title and description scoped to one species, 3D, per the release overview; signpost asks the audit to state species and data class. Why no longer says every collisionless code is covered. Years and bands unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): lettered citation 'per analyst position (d' replaced with the KB position id per tl-position-2.

plasma-lean-kinetic-library.title: A formal library for plasma equations
plasma-lean-kinetic-library.description: Agreed, reusable Lean definitions of Vlasov-Poisson/Maxwell, Landau and Boltzmann collision operators, ideal and Hall MHD, and their standard solution concepts, so any claimed result about a plasma model can be audited against a fixed statement.
plasma-lean-kinetic-library.status_oct2026: Mathlib coverage of PDE is thin (3 of 16 PDE families in the release have Lean). Proof of concept: one mathematician supervising Gemini DeepThink, Claude Code and Aristotle formalized the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium characterization in 10 days for about $200, writing no code (arXiv 2603.15929, Mar 2026).
plasma-lean-kinetic-library.why: A single statement audit can use bespoke definitions reviewed by experts, as in the 10-day, ~$200 VML case (arXiv 2603.15929). The shared library matters for reuse across 363, 364 and any future plasma theorem, and for machine-checked numerics (plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics). The limit is agreeing on definitions, not writing proofs. Under S2, Mathlib analysis/PDE coverage catches up 2027-29 and a plasma layer follows within a year; S3 follows S2 through 2027.
plasma-lean-kinetic-library.strongest_case_small: Engineering codes do not use Lean, and a definitions library mostly serves mathematicians. Matching a Lean object to the equation a physicist actually simulates still needs scarce human experts.
plasma-lean-kinetic-library.signpost: A Mathlib or Hexagon pull request adding standard definitions of the Vlasov-Maxwell system and its solution concepts, cited by a family-362 audit.
plasma-lean-kinetic-library.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: why no longer claims audits need a shared library (contradicted plasma-vm-wellposed, S1 2027, which uses bespoke definitions). Resolver consistency: S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027; the trunk resolver moved infra-mathlib-applied S3 to 2028). Bands unchanged.

plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics.title: Plasma simulations with certified error bars
plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics.description: Convergence proofs and computable error bounds for structure-preserving Vlasov-Maxwell, particle-in-cell (PIC) and MHD discretizations, increasingly machine-checked, so code verification can state 'discretization error below X' instead of relying on convergence studies.
plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics.status_oct2026: Structure-preserving (geometric) PIC and finite-element schemes exist with proved conservation properties (general). Convergence theorems assume a smooth solution on the time interval; local theory and continuation criteria already supply that on finite intervals, and family 362 [L, T3] would add global smoothness for one-species relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell. Engineering PIC (Hall thrusters, nozzles, magnetospheres) mostly solves electrostatic, non-relativistic Vlasov-Poisson, globally regular in 3D since 1991-92 (Pfaffelmoser; Lions-Perthame, general). PIC statistical noise and the electron-to-xenon mass ratio of about 1:239,000 (stiffness) lack rigorous error control (general).
plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics.why: Under S2, AI does numerics with certified error bounds by 2027-28 and the verified floating-point toolchain matures 2027-29, so the first certified kinetic-solver modules appear ~2029. Practical value: replacing grid- and particle-count convergence studies (often several times the cost of the production run, general) with proof-backed estimators, and giving ML surrogates a certified reference to be checked against. S3 High: formalization-gated work runs on the cognitive clock, which S3 compresses 20-50x from 2029; all S3 hard prerequisites are High by 2028; and the node needs only one code team to ship one machine-checked module (a Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau theorem took 10 days and ~$200 in Mar 2026, arXiv 2603.15929).
plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics.strongest_case_small: Turbulent plasma simulations are chaotic, so rigorous long-time error bounds grow with the Lyapunov time and can be valid but useless for the time-averaged transport engineers want. Model-form error (closures, wall physics) dwarfs discretization error in Hall-thruster and space-weather codes.
plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics.signpost: A plasma code team (e.g. WarpX, GEMPIC, GX) ships a module with a machine-checked convergence or conservation proof and uses it in a V&V report.
plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: hard edge from plasma-vm-wellposed -> soft; premise_tier -> context only (finite-interval convergence needs local smoothness only; engineering PIC is electrostatic and non-relativistic). Advocate: S3 Medium -> High (cognitive-clock node; all S3 hard prerequisites High by 2028; one module from one code team suffices). S1/S2 unchanged.

plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale.title: Full-thruster kinetic simulation becomes affordable
plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale.description: AI-designed algorithms (implicit and asymptotic-preserving PIC, low-rank and sparse-grid Vlasov solvers, bounded learned subgrid models) make 3D whole-device kinetic simulation of a Hall thruster with real mass ratio, real geometry and wall physics a days-long rather than infeasible calculation.
plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale.status_oct2026: Facility-scale kinetic simulations of Hall thrusters do not yet exist at feasible cost (Whittaker, Marks, Gorodetsky, AIAA 2026). 3D PIC with wall charging, secondary emission and near-plume outflow (Liu, Zhao, Zhao, arXiv 2603.14849, Mar 2026) shows anomalous transport self-organizing into near-wall pathways, but at reduced scale. In fusion, GPU-native gyrokinetics (GX) already runs useful turbulence cases in minutes on one GPU.
plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale.why: Algorithm invention for multiscale kinetic problems is expert-scarce work that S2 makes on-demand by 2027-28 (P1), and its product is practical algorithms (P4). Order-of-magnitude cost today (general arithmetic, judgment): at real density, cells that resolve electron-cyclotron drift waves (~50-100 micrometres) give ~1e9-1e10 cells over a 5 kW thruster and its near plume. With ~100 particles per cell and ~1e7 cyclotron-resolving implicit steps for ~1 ms of simulated time, that is ~1e18-1e19 particle pushes, weeks to months on a full exascale machine. Implicit energy-conserving PIC already exists, so reaching 'days' needs another ~10-100x from algorithms (sparse-grid, low-rank, asymptotic-preserving, subcycling) plus 2028-31 hardware. That makes hero runs feasible, which is all this node claims. Design loops that need hundreds of evaluations stay out of reach, so design runs through the closure (plasma-hall-anomalous-closure). Band: S2 Medium, the P4 default, given the node's own strongest case (gains may stall near 10x); S3 High because recursive AI compounds algorithm gains after 2028.
plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale.strongest_case_small: The problem spans six-plus orders of magnitude in time scale; some cost may be irreducible and algorithm gains could stall near 10x. Even perfect kinetic simulations inherit uncertain wall, secondary-emission and facility-pressure physics, so cheaper runs do not automatically remove uncertainty.
plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale.signpost: A published full-device 3D PIC of a >=5 kW Hall thruster at real mass ratio and real geometry, with neutrals and wall emission, covering >=0.5 ms of simulated time and completed in under a week.
plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027; cap-applied-math is 2027 in both). Skeptic: signpost now measures affordability only; the no-tuning accuracy test moves to plasma-hall-anomalous-closure; unsupported 10-100x stacking sentence replaced by cost arithmetic. Auditor: pathway P1->P6 -> P1->P4; S1 Medium -> Low, S2 High -> Medium (P4 default; resolver arithmetic puts today's cost at ~1e18-1e19 particle pushes, weeks to months on a full exascale machine, so 'days' needs another 10-100x). S3 High kept.

plasma-gk-surrogates.title: Millisecond fusion-turbulence models trusted in design
plasma-gk-surrogates.description: Neural and quasilinear surrogates of gyrokinetic turbulence that run in milliseconds, carry calibrated uncertainty, and are trusted inside reactor-design and scenario-planning loops in place of hours-to-weeks nonlinear simulations.
plasma-gk-surrogates.status_oct2026: Already arriving through ML, not frontier math: surrogates of the GX code trained on >200,000 nonlinear simulations over ~23,000 stellarator configurations run in ~ms and are used directly in equilibrium optimization (Churchill, Landreman et al., arXiv 2609.28730, Sep 23 2026); GyroSwin cuts fully resolved nonlinear gyrokinetics cost ~1,000x (arXiv 2510.07314); PQLS calibrates a quasilinear saturation rule by Bayesian inference, separating parameter and model-form uncertainty (arXiv 2609.29336, Sep 24 2026). Multiscale nonlinear runs can cost ~640,000 node-hours (general; reported for GKV on Fugaku, primary source not checked).
plasma-gk-surrogates.why: The training data and ML methods exist; DOE's Genesis Mission/STELLAR-AI (PPPL, Jan 2026) includes StellFoundry, an AI stellarator-design project. AI applied math adds out-of-distribution error bounds and principled UQ on top, raising trust from 'useful screening tool' to 'design-of-record input'.
plasma-gk-surrogates.strongest_case_small: This is ML engineering already underway, so the AI-math increment is small. Surrogates trained on adiabatic-electron simulations miss kinetic-electron and electromagnetic effects that matter at reactor-relevant pressure, so trust may stay limited to early design.
plasma-gk-surrogates.signpost: A fusion company publishes a design whose surrogate-predicted transport is later confirmed within its stated error bars by experiment (W7-X or a new device).
plasma-gk-surrogates.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor: GKV node-hour figure marked (general) because the source was a search summary; STELLAR-AI wording matched to its source (StellFoundry). Years and bands unchanged.

plasma-swx-data-assimilation.title: Sun-to-Earth ensemble forecasting with honest uncertainty
plasma-swx-data-assimilation.description: Coupled data assimilation from the Sun (SDO imagery and magnetograms, coronagraphs) through the solar wind (SOLAR-1 at L1) to the magnetosphere, ionosphere and thermosphere, producing ensemble forecasts with calibrated probabilities rather than single deterministic runs (demonstrated in a research or pre-operational testbed; operational transition is a later step).
plasma-swx-data-assimilation.status_oct2026: SOLAR-1 (ex-SWFO-L1) launched Sep 24, 2025 and reached L1 Jan 23, 2026. NOAA's WAM-IPE gives 2-day ionosphere-thermosphere forecasts (operational since July 2021, upgraded 2023). NASA/IBM's open Surya heliophysics foundation model (Aug 2025, 366M parameters, 9 years of SDO data) beats flare benchmarks by ~16% up to 2 h ahead. STEREO-A (70.6 degrees ahead of Earth, Oct 2026) and PUNCH (2025) add off-axis and 3D views. Density models rarely propagate uncertainty to orbit decisions (CPAESS 2026 workshop abstract).
plasma-swx-data-assimilation.why: Ensemble data assimilation for a nonlinear, sparsely observed coupled system (filter design, model-error estimation, localization, feature alignment of CME fronts) is bespoke, expert-scarce applied math; S2 makes it on-demand by 2027-28. Terrestrial weather shows what DA buys: roughly a day of useful lead time per decade (general).
plasma-swx-data-assimilation.strongest_case_small: Space weather is observation-starved: one L1 point, a few coronagraph viewpoints and no routine coronal magnetic-field measurement. Assimilation cannot create information that is not observed; Kay et al. (2024) attribute CME arrival-time errors mainly to input reconstruction and background solar wind.
plasma-swx-data-assimilation.signpost: A published assimilative ensemble Sun-to-Earth forecast system with reliability diagrams on CCMC benchmarks (research or pre-operational testbed) by 2028; SWPC or ESA operational transition by 2030.
plasma-swx-data-assimilation.revision_note: B-safe-orbits: Skeptic and auditor: signpost split into testbed demonstration by 2028 and operational transition by 2030 (research-to-operations runs on appropriations; WAM-IPE took years to reach operations in July 2021), and maturity stated in the description. Auditor: Surya is 366M parameters (InfoQ). S3 2027 -> 2028: capability.json defines S3 as S2 until 2028 with the same end-2027 horizon, and the trunk resolver moved infra-verified-numerics and infra-mathlib-applied to S3 2028 (skeptic, systemic finding).

plasma-kinetic-closures.title: Simpler plasma models with proven error bounds
plasma-kinetic-closures.description: Physics theory that derives fluid closures (electron heat flux, anomalous resistivity, pressure anisotropy, Landau-fluid terms) from kinetic theory with stated validity domains and error bounds, replacing ad hoc closures in thruster, magnetic-nozzle and magnetospheric fluid codes.
plasma-kinetic-closures.status_oct2026: Engineering plasma codes are fluid or hybrid with hand-tuned closures; magnetic-nozzle expansion is nearly collisionless and needs a non-trivial electron closure (Kim et al., PSST 2023). No catalog family addresses closures. Family 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases, with fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan; T1, conditional) is a step in the same particles-to-kinetic-to-fluid derivation program, methodological relevance only.
plasma-kinetic-closures.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven); family 364 is T1 and used only as methodological context, so any reliance on it would be conditional
plasma-kinetic-closures.why: S2 assumes AI builds and validates physics theory and reduced models from 2028-29; closures are the canonical such task. Validation needs kinetic simulation data (plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale) and diagnostics such as incoherent Thomson scattering, which already exist at university labs. Landau-damping theorems (frontier-landau-damping-general) add confidence but are not needed: Landau-fluid closures were built from linear theory (Hammett-Perkins 1990, general). Data-driven closures with UQ count. This general theory accelerates, but does not gate, the Hall-thruster closure and magnetic-nozzle theory.
plasma-kinetic-closures.strongest_case_small: Closures in turbulent, wall-bounded plasmas may not exist in closed form (they are non-local and history-dependent); the best achievable may be data-driven closures with UQ, which do not need frontier math.
plasma-kinetic-closures.signpost: A closure derived with AI assistance is adopted in a production code (HallThruster.jl, Hall2De, BATS-R-US) and cuts the number of calibrated parameters.
plasma-kinetic-closures.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + advocate + auditor: hard edge from frontier-landau-damping-general -> soft. plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.title: Solving the 60-year Hall-thruster electron transport puzzle
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.description: A validated model of anomalous cross-field electron transport in Hall thrusters, first-principles or data-driven (trained on whole-device kinetic simulations and non-invasive measurements), that predicts transport from the local plasma state across thrusters and operating points without per-condition calibration.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.status_oct2026: Open research problem since the 1960s. Codes calibrate an anomalous collision frequency to each operating point. A self-consistent closure using plasma density, neutral density and electron temperature captures peak electron temperature and performance on a 9 kW magnetically shielded thruster but cannot place electron temperature and ion velocity profiles correctly at the same time (Brick, Roberts, Jorns, IEPC-2025-361). NASA's Joint Advanced Propulsion Institute (JANUS) Predictive Engineering Model, with one pressure-parameterized transport model, fits SPT-140 calibration data within 7% (thrust) and 15% (discharge current), with 8%/17% when extrapolated to orbit; the authors note discharge current is not reliably predicted at higher power (Whittaker et al., AIAA 2026). Thomson scattering finds electron temperatures ~2x higher than probes.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.why: The candidate mechanisms (electron-cyclotron drift, gradient-drift and ionization instabilities, near-wall conductivity) are known. What is missing is affordable whole-device kinetic simulation plus a reduction to a closure, first-principles or data-driven. Data-driven model discovery on thruster data already exists in published form (Jorns, PSST 27:104007, 2018; Jorns, Marks, Dale, AIAA 2020-3622). A general kinetic-closure theory (plasma-kinetic-closures) helps but is not required. S2 delivers the cognitive steps by ~2029. The binding gate is a validation campaign across several thrusters with non-invasive electron diagnostics at low background pressure, which takes about a year, so 2030. Band S2 Low: P6 default, two Medium hard prerequisites (kinetic solvers, cap-physics-theory) and a strict criterion; S3 Medium.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.strongest_case_small: Sixty years of failure suggests transport is multi-mechanism, geometry-specific and coupled to the test facility; even a good closure may only reach ~5% accuracy, a modest gain over today's calibrated 7-15%. Thrust is already predicted well by calibration, and programs qualify by test regardless.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.signpost: A closure that predicts discharge current within 5% across at least three different thrusters (e.g. H9, SPT-140, AEPS) without refitting, published by end-2030.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + advocate: hard edge from plasma-kinetic-closures -> soft; description admits data-driven closures. Skeptic: S2 Medium -> Low (P6 default; two Medium hard prerequisites; strict criterion); signpost date aligned to the S2 year. Advocate's S2 2030 -> 2029 rejected (validation across three thrusters takes about a year after the 2028 solvers and 2029 theory). Auditor: Whittaker figures restated as fits to calibration data, with discharge current not reliably predicted.

plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.title: How plasma leaves a magnetic nozzle, settled
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.description: Accepted kinetic theory and validated simulation of how plasma detaches from a magnetic nozzle and how electrons cool during the expansion: the thrust-producing stage of VASIMR, helicon thrusters and most fusion-drive concepts.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.status_oct2026: Kinetic electron cooling governs energy balance, ion acceleration and detachment (Kim et al., PSST 2023); fully kinetic PIC studies attribute electron detachment to inertia and gyroviscous effects. Ground chambers distort far-plume detachment measurements (general).
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.why: Once kinetic solvers are cheap (S2 2028), fully kinetic simulation can settle detachment without a general closure theory, which accelerates but does not gate it (plasma-kinetic-closures, soft). The gate is validation: detachment happens far downstream, where vacuum chambers have walls and background gas, so an in-space measurement would settle it. The only named candidate (Pulsar Fusion's Sunbird in-orbit demonstration, 2027) has no committed far-field diagnostic. Band S2 Low (P6 default); S3 Medium.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.strongest_case_small: Detachment may be handled empirically well enough for current thrusters; the binding constraints for VASIMR-class and fusion drives are power supply mass and thermal rejection, not nozzle physics.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.signpost: Far-field plume measurements in orbit from a magnetic-nozzle thruster (Pulsar Fusion's Sunbird exhaust test is targeted for orbit in 2027) that match a pre-registered kinetic prediction.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Advocate: hard edge from plasma-kinetic-closures -> soft (the fully kinetic route needs only the solvers). Skeptic: S2 Medium -> Low (P6 default; no committed far-field in-space diagnostic; Medium solver prerequisite). Advocate's S2 2030 -> 2029 rejected (no in-space validation measurement is planned before 2029). S3 Medium kept.

plasma-eruption-onset-theory.title: Predicting when the Sun erupts
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.description: Physics-based, probabilistic prediction of flare and CME onset (torus and kink instability thresholds, reconnection onset) from observed active-region magnetic fields, 1-3 days ahead, beating the best operational statistical or ML forecast on an independent benchmark (for example by at least 0.1 Brier skill score at 24 h).
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.status_oct2026: Operational flare forecasts are mostly statistical; Surya (Aug 2025) improves short-horizon (up to 2 h) flare forecasting by ~16%. The coronal magnetic field is not routinely measured; reconstructing it from photospheric magnetograms (force-free extrapolation) is an ill-posed inverse problem (general).
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.why: Two things are cognitive and compress under S2: theory of instability onset in realistic 3D fields, and regularized inverse methods for the coronal field with uncertainty. Fifteen years of SDO data plus DKIST and Solar Orbiter give enough to test against. The data gate binds on how much skill is achievable, not on whether progress happens.
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.strongest_case_small: Eruptions may be triggered by small-scale flux emergence below observational resolution, which would cap predictability no matter how good the theory is.
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.signpost: A physics-informed eruption forecast whose Brier skill score for M-class-plus flares at 24 h exceeds the best statistical or ML baseline on the same independent community benchmark by at least 0.1 (reaching about 0.3), by 2028.
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.revision_note: B-safe-orbits: Skeptic: success criterion was nearly met already (statistical flare forecasts beat climatology); now requires beating the best operational statistical or ML forecast on an independent benchmark, and the signpost is stated relative to that baseline. Years and bands unchanged.

plasma-thermo-density-uq.title: Upper-atmosphere density and drag with honest error bars
plasma-thermo-density-uq.description: Thermospheric density nowcasts and 1-3 day forecasts with calibrated uncertainty that bring public, operator-usable products from empirical-model spread (20-40% disagreement even in quiet times) to HASDM-class error (about 10-15%) and keep them calibrated through 2-6x storm enhancements, by assimilating drag observed on thousands of constellation satellites (which needs operator attitude and thrust data, since constellation satellites station-keep continuously), so LEO orbit predictions and covariances stay realistic through geomagnetic storms. Storm-time forecast skill beyond about a day stays bounded by CME arrival and magnetic-orientation forecasts.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.status_oct2026: Density is the dominant error in low-orbit prediction; storms raise it 2-5x within hours and empirical models disagree by 20-40% even in quiet times (CPAESS 2026 abstract). Gannon storm, May 2024: density up to ~6x baseline within 12 h, decay of tracked objects 38 -> 180 m/day, thousands of satellites maneuvered, Ap forecasts underpredicted by 100-300 at 1-3 day lead (Parker and Linares 2024). Feb 2022: a minor (G1-G2) storm raised drag up to 50% at the ~210 km deployment altitude (SpaceX update, Feb 2022) and 38 of 49 new Starlink satellites reentered. The Space Force's High Accuracy Satellite Drag Model (HASDM; Storz et al. 2005) already assimilates calibration-satellite drag into JB2008-based nowcasts and is described as the state of the art; its 2000-2019 archive is public as the SET HASDM database, and ML emulators of it reach <10% MAE (Licata et al., arXiv 2109.07651) and 11% with well-calibrated uncertainty (Licata and Mehta, arXiv 2201.02067). Starlink ephemerides are posted publicly via Space-Track and CelesTrak supplemental GP (general).
plasma-thermo-density-uq.why: Thousands of GNSS-tracked constellation satellites are potential drag probes. Using them requires joint estimation of density and each satellite's unknown, attitude-dependent ballistic coefficient, net of continuous thrusting, an identifiability and estimation problem that is solved in principle but expert-scarce, which S2's on-demand applied math supplies by 2028; an operational product with data access follows in 2029. The increment over HASDM is scale (thousands of probes rather than a calibration set), public access and calibrated 1-3 day forecasts, so the AI-math share is modest. The gates are data access (the attitude, ballistic-coefficient, thrust and maneuver logs that density inversion needs are proprietary, although Starlink ephemerides themselves are public) and storm-driver forecasts. Sun-to-Earth assimilation helps the 1-3 day forecast but is not needed for the nowcast, so it is a soft input.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.strongest_case_small: At storm time most error comes from the driver forecast (Kp/Ap and the CME's magnetic field), not from the density model, so nowcast gains matter less to operators than 24-72 h forecasts, which stay data-limited (see plasma-bz-forecast).
plasma-thermo-density-uq.signpost: NOAA, Space Force or the Commerce space-traffic system adopts an assimilative density product built on commercial constellation ephemerides, with published calibrated uncertainty, by 2029.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.merge_note: A1: merged astro-thermosphere-drag-uq (same achievement viewed from the conjunction side; astro >2031/2029/2028 Low/Medium/Medium, plasma 2030/2029/2028 Medium/High/High). Kept the plasma id (space-weather physics owner) and its better-sourced data-assimilation view (Gannon storm, Parker-Linares 2024; Feb 2022 Starlink loss; CPAESS 2026), so years and bands follow plasma. Astro's caution is recorded in the description (storm drivers forecast at most 1-2 days ahead; Starlink lowering shells to ~480 km raises drag sensitivity). Astro's hard prerequisites cap-physics-theory and astro-nongaussian-uq-certified were converted to soft: calibrated density estimation is an estimation problem that needs neither new physics theory nor certified Pc math. astro-leo-safety-at-scale now depends on this node.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.revision_note: B-safe-orbits: Skeptic and auditor: the Space Force's HASDM (operational assimilative drag model, 'state of the art') and ML emulators with calibrated uncertainty (<10% MAE, arXiv 2109.07651; 11% with well-calibrated uncertainty, arXiv 2201.02067; both abstracts checked by the resolver) were missing, so the description's 20-40% baseline (model disagreement) and the AI-math increment were overstated. Advocate and auditor: hard edge from plasma-swx-data-assimilation made soft (nowcasting is an estimation problem). Advocate's earlier years (S2 2028, S3 2027) rejected: the gate is data access (attitude, ballistic-coefficient and thrust logs; Starlink station-keeps continuously), the signpost is an operational product, and S3 equals S2 through 2028. Auditor: Feb 2022 storm wording corrected (G1-G2 'minor'; 50% from SpaceX's update); why's 'by 2028' reconciled with the S2 2029 year.

plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.title: Deuterium-helium-3 fusion demonstrated at useful rates
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.description: Experimental demonstration of significant deuterium-helium-3 fusion power, the fuel most fusion-propulsion concepts assume because only ~5% of its energy comes out as neutrons versus ~80% for D-T (general), at the several-times-higher temperatures it requires.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.status_oct2026: Helion's Polaris reported the first private D-T fusion and 150 million deg C plasma (Feb 2026) and says it is working toward D-He3 temperatures; Helion's 50 MW Microsoft target is 2028. No D-He3 burn at meaningful power anywhere. Fuel arithmetic (18.3 MeV per reaction): a 1 GW(fusion) D-He3 engine burns ~54 kg of He-3 per year of operation, against a terrestrial supply from tritium decay of a few kilograms per year (supply figure general), while a 1 MW demonstrator running 1,000 h needs ~6 g. Helion plans to make He-3 itself via D-D fusion (TechCrunch, Feb 2026). About 0.37 GW-yr of D-D fusion breeds 50 kg directly (about 0.18 GW-yr if bred tritium is also left to decay), so at scale the fuel gate becomes D-D fusion capacity, coupled to plasma-fusion-net-gain, not natural supply.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.why: This is a physical-clock node: it needs hotter, better-confined plasma and He-3 fuel. AI theory and AI-run campaigns (plasma-ai-fusion-operations) help optimize pulsed FRC operation and interpret diagnostics, but they do not heat plasma; under S3 autonomous experimental campaigns could compress the program by a year or so. Chain (S3): Polaris D-T at ~13 keV (150 million deg C, Feb 2026) -> D-He3 needs several-times-higher ion temperature plus a He-3 supply -> Orion-class device (2028 target) -> peer-reviewed D-He3 rates in 2031 at the earliest.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.strongest_case_small: The AI-math effect here is close to nil; it is included to show where the chain to fusion propulsion is actually gated.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.signpost: Helion or TAE publishes measured D-He3 fusion rates (14.7 MeV proton spectra, neutron fraction) in a peer-reviewed venue.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (grounding rule) + skeptic + advocate: dated physical chain added; He-3 supply framing qualified (bred He-3 via D-D fusion; demonstrators need grams). Soft edge from new plasma-ai-fusion-operations. Years and bands unchanged.

revisions.from: D-He3 fusion demonstrated at useful rates

plasma-ep-predictive-design.title: Design-before-build electric thrusters
plasma-ep-predictive-design.description: Engineering codes that predict a new Hall or gridded-ion thruster's thrust, efficiency, oscillations and plume within a few percent before hardware exists, and extrapolate ground tests to space with quantified uncertainty.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.status_oct2026: The JANUS Predictive Engineering Model, with one pressure-parameterized transport model, fits SPT-140 calibration data within 7% (thrust) and 15% (discharge current) and extrapolates ground data to orbit within 8%/17% for the SPT-140 flown on Psyche; discharge current is not reliably predicted when extrapolating at higher power (Whittaker et al., AIAA 2026). Higher-fidelity Hall2De must be recalibrated per operating condition. NASA states its VF-5 facility reproduces known ground-to-flight differences for AEPS (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026).
plasma-ep-predictive-design.why: Predictive design runs through a validated transport closure (plasma-hall-anomalous-closure), first-principles or data-driven, inside cheap fluid or hybrid codes, or through surrogates trained on many kinetic runs, which amounts to the same thing. Whole-device kinetic simulation alone supplies training and validation data: at days per run on a leadership-class machine it cannot serve the hundreds of evaluations a design loop needs (arithmetic in plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale). A new Hall thruster typically takes several build-test iterations at roughly a year each (general); a predictive code could cut iterations from ~3-4 to ~1-2 (general, judgment). Validation needs test data across designs, which binds the year. The band follows the closure: S2 Low, S3 Medium.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.strongest_case_small: Industry already builds thrusters successfully by build-test-iterate, and small-satellite thrusters iterate cheaply. The value concentrates in high-power devices where testing is hard, a small part of the market.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.signpost: A thruster designed with a predictive tool meets performance within 5% on its first hot fire, documented at IEPC or AIAA by 2030.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: hard edge from plasma-hall-anomalous-closure added (a days-per-run kinetic simulation cannot serve a design loop; 'either sufficient' removed); S2 Medium -> Low following the closure. Advocate's soft-edge version, S2 2029 / S3 2028 and S3 High rejected (see debates); its pathway label P1->P6 accepted. Auditor: Whittaker figures restated. Iteration figures marked judgment. Years unchanged.

plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.title: Thruster life proven with shorter wear tests
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.description: Erosion and wear models (low-energy sputter yields, pole-cover and cathode-keeper erosion, near-wall plasma) validated well enough that NASA or ESA credits model-based extrapolation for part of the 100% demonstrated-life (wear-test) requirement, not just the margin. Today's practice is 100% test plus 50% margin by analysis. The credit shortens multi-year wear tests.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.status_oct2026: NASA already qualifies EP thruster life by 100% test with 50% margin by analysis (Anderson 2009 standard, cited in Williams et al. 2026). AEPS (12 kW; the PPE bus is now repurposed for SR-1 Freedom): three flight thrusters delivered 2025, environmental qualification complete, contract closeout mid-to-late 2027. The QM-2 wear test runs fall 2026 to Sep 2029 to at least 100% of per-thruster throughput (1,770 kg xenon requirement, 50% margin by analysis), and the SEP project closes out in 2029. SEP tracked insufficient validation of the margin-setting erosion model as a boarded red risk. JPL near-field plume data and JANUS modeling have since reduced plasma-interaction uncertainty (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026). Pole erosion is now the life limiter in magnetically shielded thrusters, and erosion models have underpredicted measured rates (U. Washington thesis 2025).
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.why: A 23,000-hour wear test is 2.6 years of continuous firing. Running ~10,000 hours and extrapolating with an accepted model would save ~1.5 years and tens of millions in facility time (general). The step beyond today's practice is predicting how erosion evolves as surfaces wear, beyond the tested duration. That needs a near-wall transport model that stays valid as geometry changes (plasma-hall-anomalous-closure, hard) and a rule for crediting model evidence (physclock-credibility-evidence-standard, hard). Design-before-build (plasma-ep-predictive-design) and certification of AI-written proofs (infra-tool-qualification, which covers software proof credit, not physics wear models) help but are not required. Chain (S3): closure validated 2029 -> a wear test planned for partial credit accumulates ~10,000 h (~14 months), checked against long-duration data (AEPS QM-2 completes Sep 2029) -> qualification review -> 2031 at the earliest. S2 lands at the horizon, one step later. The regulator rule caps the band at Medium; after compounding it is Low in all scenarios.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.strongest_case_small: Agencies are conservative and the decisive inputs are materials data (sputter yields at tens of eV), not plasma mathematics; the worst life limiters (e.g. pole erosion) were discovered in test, not predicted. AEPS lessons learned center on risk management, contract oversight and requirements, not physics. Commercial and NASA programs have long used erosion models to project life beyond a test's duration for mission studies (general), so the new step is institutional.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.signpost: NASA or ESA revises its EP life-qualification standard, or a NASA or ESA program accepts a life qualification in which less than 100% of the throughput requirement is demonstrated by test and the rest by a validated model, by 2031.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): All three lenses (verified in Williams et al. 2026): NASA already qualifies EP life by 100% test with 50% margin by analysis, and the AEPS QM-2 wear test runs fall 2026 to Sep 2029, so the node is redefined to the real increment (credit for part of the 100% test) and the AEPS-by-2029 signpost dropped. Advocate + auditor: infra-tool-qualification hard -> soft (DO-178C/DO-330 proof credit is not the path for physics wear models). Resolver: plasma-ep-predictive-design hard -> soft (qualifying an existing thruster does not need design-before-build); plasma-hall-anomalous-closure kept hard against the advocate. Skeptic: S3 2030 -> 2031 and S3 Medium -> Low; advocate's S2 2030 Medium / S3 2029 rejected (see debates). Soft edge from new plasma-aeps-life-qual.

revisions.from: Thruster life qualified with less than a full-duration wear test

plasma-stellarator-design-loop.title: AI-closed-loop fusion-machine design
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.description: Integrated optimization of stellarator (and other) magnetic configurations against turbulence, fast-ion losses, coil buildability and manufacturing tolerances in weeks, producing designs whose confinement is predicted with error bars.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.status_oct2026: Surrogates in the optimization loop already enable objectives such as full radial heat-flux profiles (arXiv 2609.28730); open optimizers exist (general) and Proxima's ConStellaration benchmark dataset is public (arXiv 2506.19583). Proxima Fusion raised EUR 130M (Jun 2025): Stellarator Model Coil 2027, Alpha demonstration 2031. Type One Energy plans Infinity Two (350 MWe) for the mid-2030s (general; the cited WNN article covers Infinity One only). Family 146 (Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard map, T1, conditional) concerns the textbook model of magnetic-island overlap and field-line chaos: confidence in theory only.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven); family 146 is T1 and context only, so any reliance on it would be conditional
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.why: S2's multiphysics design optimization (2028) plus trusted surrogates closes the loop, and the pieces already exist (surrogates inside optimization loops, open benchmarks, DOE STELLAR-AI). The node is the tool, so its gate is data (validated surrogates and benchmarks). Fabrication gates the machines it designs: coil tolerances of millimetres over metre-scale coils decide whether designs perform as optimized. It has no space-technology unlock except as a soft accelerator of compact fusion-drive design (plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure), because the same loop applies to FRC-plus-nozzle configurations.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Stellarator design is already highly optimized; the binding constraint for fusion is building and operating devices, so better paper designs add no fusion power before 2031.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.signpost: A stellarator company or national lab adopts as its design of record an end-to-end optimized configuration (surrogate turbulence, fast-ion losses, coil buildability and tolerances) produced in weeks. Predicted-versus-measured field errors on a built coil set (Proxima's 2027 model coil is the first chance) are the follow-on check.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + advocate: binding_gate fabrication -> data (the node is a design tool; fabrication gates the machines it designs). Advocate (evidence checked by auditor): S2 2029 -> 2028 (surrogates already inside optimization loops, open benchmarks, STELLAR-AI; only hard prerequisite cap-design-optimization is S2 2028). Signpost changed so the tool can be observed without a built coil. Auditor: Type One Infinity Two marked (general), source mismatch. Advocate: soft edge to plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure. Bands unchanged.

revisions.reason: grounding rule: T1 premise must say conditional

plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.title: A credible paper design of a fusion rocket
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.description: An integrated design of a fusion propulsion system (e.g. Direct Fusion Drive: small field-reversed configuration plus magnetic nozzle, D-He3) whose confinement and nozzle sub-models are validated against experiment, with the D-He3 burn sub-model taken from theory because no device has reached those regimes. The design shows specific power >= 1 kW/kg and multi-year life and closes gaps that today's concept studies wave away.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.status_oct2026: Direct Fusion Drive is a concept modeled by Princeton Satellite Systems and tested at small scale at PPPL (PFRC); reports that PSS and Pulsar Fusion apply ML to the PFRC experiment are unverified. Pulsar's Sunbird exhaust reportedly achieved first plasma with krypton in March 2026 with no fusion (unverified: the source could not be retrieved); its in-orbit demonstration is targeted for 2027 (pulsarfusion.com).
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.why: Paper closure is cognitive and compresses under S2/S3, but every sub-model (confinement scaling of small FRCs, D-He3 burn, detachment, radiation and thermal loads) needs data from regimes no device has reached, so the design stays conditional on plasma-dhe3-burn-physics (Low in all scenarios). Band S3 Low: P6 default, and a conditional design cannot sit above its burn-physics premise.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.strongest_case_small: Many paper designs already exist; a better one does not change investment or timelines unless experiments back its sub-models.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.signpost: NASA, DARPA or ESA funds a fusion-propulsion design whose confinement and nozzle sub-models are validated against PFRC-2 or Polaris-class data.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 Medium -> Low. Auditor wording adopted (the skeptic's stated alternative): D-He3 burn sub-model taken from theory, so no hard edge from plasma-dhe3-burn-physics and years unchanged. Auditor: PSS/Pulsar ML claim and Sunbird first-plasma detail marked unverified. Advocate: soft edge from plasma-stellarator-design-loop.

plasma-fusion-net-gain.title: First magnetic-fusion net energy gain
plasma-fusion-net-gain.description: A magnetic-confinement device reaches scientific gain Q > 1, or Helion delivers net electricity, establishing the energy source that fusion propulsion would ultimately need.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.status_oct2026: CFS SPARC: the first of 18 toroidal-field magnets was placed on its assembly jig in Jan 2026; first plasma is targeted for 2027 (slipped from 2025 and 2026), with Q > 1 targeted shortly after (Wikipedia). Helion Polaris: first private D-T fusion, 150 million deg C (Feb 2026); Microsoft PPA target 2028 for Orion. TAE announced a merger with Trump Media (Dec 2025, close expected mid-2026; completion not confirmed as of Oct 2026). Its Copernicus device was cancelled in Nov 2025 because the Norm device made it unnecessary, and its Da Vinci device aims at net fusion energy in the late 2020s (Wikipedia).
plasma-fusion-net-gain.why: Physical-clock anchor: magnets, vacuum vessel, assembly, commissioning and tritium operations set the date. Chain: SPARC TF magnets installed 2026-27 -> first plasma 2027 -> D-D then D-T campaign -> Q>1 in 2028 at the earliest; Helion Orion (50 MW, Microsoft PPA) targeted 2028. AI contributes through plasma control and scenario design (plasma-ai-fusion-operations, soft) and faster commissioning in S3, not through mathematics. S3's 1.3-1.5x experiment multiplier applies only after 2028 and cannot pull Q>1 into SPARC's first-plasma year.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.strongest_case_small: The AI-math contribution is close to nil; this node is in the tree to show the gate on fusion propulsion is hardware.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.signpost: SPARC first plasma date and the start of its D-T campaign; Helion's first electricity from Orion.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 2027 -> 2028 (physical-clock node; S3 equals S2 through 2027-28; SPARC first plasma is itself 2027). Auditor (verified): TAE's Copernicus was cancelled Nov 2025; unsourced SPARC vacuum-vessel date replaced by the verified TF-magnet milestone; dated chain added. Advocate's S3 Medium -> High rejected (hardware binds; one of its three attempts is cancelled); its plasma-ai-fusion-operations added as a soft accelerator.

plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.title: AI-designed thruster flies and performs as predicted
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.description: First in-space operation of an electric thruster whose magnetic circuit, channel and cathode were designed mainly by an AI optimization loop over physics-based (calibrated or kinetic) models, with on-orbit performance inside the pre-flight predicted band and the design attribution published.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.status_oct2026: No such thruster exists. Small-satellite Hall and ion thrusters go from design to flight in roughly 18-36 months (general); Starlink flies thousands of Hall thrusters (krypton, then argon) designed by conventional iteration (general). Today's calibrated engineering models carry 8% (thrust) and 17% (discharge current) ground-to-orbit errors on the SPT-140 (Whittaker et al., AIAA 2026). LEAP 71's computational loop already designs rocket engines (prop-ai-engine-design-loop).
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.why: Two routes. (1) Generic AI design (P1): an optimization loop over Bayesian-calibrated engineering models designs the magnetic circuit, channel and cathode, as LEAP 71's loop does for rocket engines. Without a predictive transport closure the first article will likely miss its targets, so one extra build-test iteration is expected. (2) With predictive design (plasma-ep-predictive-design, soft), the first article is right first time and a year is saved. Chain (S2): cap-design-optimization 2028 -> first article and ground test 2029 -> second iteration and acceptance 2030 -> rideshare or the operator's own constellation (smallsat lag 12-18 months, physclock) -> first flight 2031. Commercial operators carry their own EP risk with no certifying authority above them (general), so qualification is not the gate. S3: AI-run test stands (2028) shorten the iteration -> 2030. Band: S2 Low because the chain lands at the horizon with no slack and the node needs published flight data with the design attributed mainly to AI; S3 Medium with one year of slack. A spacecraft majority AI-engineered (capability-ai-native-spacecraft, S2 2029) is a different claim: it concerns engineering labor on known designs, not a new plasma device performing as predicted.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.strongest_case_small: The gain may be a few points of efficiency or a lighter magnetic circuit; the EP market is driven by cost, propellant (xenon/krypton/argon) supply, power-processing-unit mass and production rate, not design optimality.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.signpost: A startup or prime announces a thruster 'designed in simulation, first-article meets spec' and manifests it for flight.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Advocate (structure): plasma-ep-predictive-design hard -> soft, cap-design-optimization added as hard, pathway P7 -> P1->P7: as worded, the node needs an AI-designed thruster whose flight performance falls in its pre-flight band, which a generic AI design loop over calibrated models plus ground test can deliver without the closure. Timing between the lenses: S2 >2031 -> 2031 (advocate's 2030 rejected: without a closure the first article needs an extra build-test iteration), S3 2031 -> 2030. Skeptic + auditor's S3 Medium -> Low not applied because their zero-slack chain ran through predictive design, no longer the gate; advocate's S2 Medium / S3 High rejected. Soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands.

plasma-high-power-ep-life.title: 100 kW-class thruster runs for thousands of hours
plasma-high-power-ep-life.description: A >= 100 kW electric thruster (nested Hall, lithium MPD or VASIMR-type) demonstrates >= 5,000 hours of ground operation with validated wear projections toward the ~23,000 hours a crewed Mars nuclear-electric mission needs.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.status_oct2026: NASA/JPL's lithium MPD thruster reached 120 kW (Feb 24, 2026); next phases target 500 kW-1 MW per thruster; a crewed mission needs 2-4 MW total and >23,000 h of thruster operation (NASA). VASIMR VX-200SS ran 88 h at 80 kW (Jul 2021), with no newer public endurance result found.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.why: 5,000 h is seven months of continuous firing, which cannot start until a flight-like 100 kW unit and a facility able to hold low background pressure at that power exist (~2028-29 at best). Wall-clock test time does not compress with cognition.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.strongest_case_small: The AI-math effect is close to nil on this node; model-based life credit (plasma-ep-life-by-analysis) is the only lever and it needs the test data first.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.signpost: NASA announces a >1,000 h test of a >=100 kW thruster by 2028.

plasma-abep-demo.title: Air-breathing electric propulsion flight test
plasma-abep-demo.description: A very-low-orbit satellite that scoops residual atmosphere and uses it as electric-propulsion propellant to cancel drag, demonstrated in orbit.
plasma-abep-demo.status_oct2026: Laboratory demonstrations only (general). Intake design is a rarefied-gas (Boltzmann/DSMC) problem; families 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation) and 364 (Boltzmann from Newtonian gases) are T1 and bear on confidence in the kinetic equations used, conditional, not on intake designs. Albedo's Clarity-1 (launched Mar 14, 2025) flew at 350-380 km on xenon ion propulsion for nine months with a drag coefficient 12% better than design (Albedo, Jan 2026).
plasma-abep-demo.premise_tier: n/a (funding and hardware gate); 363 and 364 are T1, conditional and not load-bearing
plasma-abep-demo.why: AI design optimization of intakes and discharge chambers is cognitive and fast under S2, but a flight demo needs funding, an atomic-oxygen-tolerant discharge and a ride, which binds. Conventional design can also produce the demo, so AI design (cap-design-optimization) accelerates it but is not a prerequisite. Chain (S2): AI-optimized intake and discharge design 2028 -> atomic-oxygen-tolerant discharge endurance test 2029 -> funded demo plus rideshare (18-24 months) -> flight 2031. S3 runs one year earlier.
plasma-abep-demo.strongest_case_small: Atomic-oxygen erosion of discharge parts, low intake efficiency and power-per-drag are physics and materials limits. Conventional EP at 350-380 km already works, as Clarity-1 showed (275 km was its design altitude, not demonstrated), which weakens the business case.
plasma-abep-demo.signpost: An ABEP in-orbit demo is manifested with a launch date before 2030.
plasma-abep-demo.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: hard edge from cap-design-optimization -> soft (a physical demo that conventional design can achieve; funding, atomic oxygen and a ride bind). Auditor (grounding rule): dated chain added; Clarity-1 altitude corrected (275 km was the design altitude, not demonstrated). Years and bands unchanged.

plasma-active-shielding.title: Magnetic radiation shield for crews
plasma-active-shielding.description: A superconducting-magnet active shield demonstrated in space that meaningfully reduces crew dose from solar particle events and galactic cosmic rays at acceptable mass.
plasma-active-shielding.status_oct2026: EU SR2S reached TRL 3 overall (some components TRL 4). A 2022 NASA NIAC Phase I studied CREW HaT, an open Halbach-torus HTS configuration (final report Feb 21, 2024; NTRS 20250002403).
plasma-active-shielding.why: AI design optimization can trim coil mass and stress, but deflecting GeV-scale cosmic rays requires a large field-times-length product over a crew-sized volume (general), which sets a mass floor; space qualification of large HTS coils and cryogenics is a multi-year hardware program. Conventional design can produce a demo, so AI design accelerates it but is not a prerequisite.
plasma-active-shielding.strongest_case_small: Physics-bound: the Stormer deflection physics is already understood, so better math does not change the mass floor.
plasma-active-shielding.signpost: A funded in-space demonstration of a large HTS magnet (any purpose) flying by 2029.
plasma-active-shielding.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: hard edge from cap-design-optimization -> soft (field-length mass floor and HTS qualification bind). Auditor: NIAC study dated correctly. Years and bands unchanged.

plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.title: Fusion-powered thrust in space
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.description: A spacecraft producing mission-useful (newton-class) thrust in orbit from a fusion device operating at or above scientific breakeven, using a low-neutron fuel (in practice D-He3). A sub-breakeven device emitting measurable fusion products does not count.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.status_oct2026: No fusion device has net gain at propulsion scale. Pulsar Fusion's Sunbird exhaust (no fusion) is targeted for an in-orbit demonstration in 2027 (pulsarfusion.com).
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.why: Requires net-gain fusion in a compact, flight-mass device, a suitable low-neutron fuel, and a launch-approved system. With the node defined as useful thrust at or above breakeven, the hard edges to plasma-fusion-net-gain and plasma-dhe3-burn-physics are ordering constraints. Even S3's near-free cognition leaves every one of these gated by experiments, fabrication and regulation.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node records a nil effect inside the horizon.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.signpost: A fusion-propulsion company shows measured fusion products from a flight-configured device on the ground.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: description strengthened to mission-useful thrust from an at-or-above-breakeven device on low-neutron fuel, so the hard edges to net gain and D-He3 burn are valid ordering constraints; advocate's softening of those edges rejected (it fit only the weaker wording). Auditor: unsupported PSS 'as early as 2028' clause removed; Sunbird status sourced. Years and bands unchanged.

plasma-cme-arrival-skill.title: Solar-storm arrival forecast within about 8 hours
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.description: Operational CME arrival-time forecasts whose best routinely-run ensemble reaches mean absolute error <= 8 h (vs 10.3 h for NASA M2M's Ensemble WSA-Enlil+Cone and 13.2 h across all CCMC scoreboard submissions), with calibrated probability windows.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.status_oct2026: CCMC Arrival Time Scoreboard, 2013-2023: 1,702 predictions of 256 impacting CMEs, bias -2.5 h, mean absolute error 13.2 h, standard deviation 17.4 h, only slight improvement; the most established models do better (EnsWEC M2M: MAE 10.3 h on 95 predictions), and errors are dominated by CME reconstruction and background solar wind (Kay et al., Space Weather 2024). STEREO-A is 70.6 degrees ahead of Earth (Oct 7, 2026, STEREO Science Center) and gives a side view now; PUNCH (2025) adds polarimetric 3D imaging and CCOR coronagraphs fly on GOES-19 and SOLAR-1. ESA's Vigil at L5 (carrying NOAA's CCOR coronagraph) is planned to launch in 2031.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.why: AI-built ensembles, multi-view assimilation and better background-solar-wind modeling (coronal field extrapolation, an ill-posed inverse problem where mathematics genuinely helps) could cut the best ensemble's MAE by roughly 20-30% (judgment, illustrative), enough to reach 8 h before Vigil data exist. Validation runs on an event-count clock that does not compress: about 24 impacting CMEs a year on average, fewer near the next solar minimum around 2030, and with an error SD near 17 h about 40 events (roughly two years) are needed to show 8 h against 10.3 h. Chain (S2): assimilation methods 2028 -> real-time scoreboard submissions 2028-30 -> operational transition 2031. S3 saves a year on methods and transition, not on events.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.strongest_case_small: Eleven years of model development barely moved the error, including periods when STEREO-A gave a side view (roughly 2020-22, general); the limit is input reconstruction and background wind, and robust day-ahead skill may need Vigil.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.signpost: The best routinely-submitting scoreboard model posts MAE below 9 h over at least 40 impacting CMEs (about a 24-month window) during 2027-29.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.revision_note: B-safe-orbits: Skeptic: S2 2030 -> 2031, S3 2029 -> 2030, S2 band Medium -> Low on the event-count clock (resolver checked: Kay et al. 2024 Table 2 gives 256 impacting CMEs over 2013-2023; with SD 17.4 h a 20-event MAE has ~2.3 h standard error, so showing <= 8 h needs ~40 events, about two years, with fewer CMEs near the ~2030 minimum). Auditor: baseline corrected (13.2 h is the all-submission average; EnsWEC(M2M) is at 10.3 h, weighted 9.9 h, on 95 predictions, checked in Table 3); '~30-40%' marked as judgment and restated against the best ensemble; signpost merged with the skeptic's event-count version. Advocate: strongest case rewritten (STEREO-A gives a side view now, 70.6 degrees ahead on Oct 7, 2026, checked; earlier side-view periods did not cut error), soft edges from science-helio-tomography and the new side-view monitor node.

plasma-bz-forecast.title: Knowing a solar storm's magnetic punch a day ahead
plasma-bz-forecast.description: Forecasting the southward magnetic field (Bz) of an incoming CME 12-24+ hours before arrival: the main driver of geomagnetic storm severity and of the storm-time density errors that hit satellites.
plasma-bz-forecast.status_oct2026: Magnetic structure is recognized as the main bottleneck; operationally Bz is known only as the CME passes L1, roughly 30-60 minutes before impact (SOLAR-1 operational 2026; timing general). Established short-term in-situ reconstruction tools mostly need a human in the loop; arXiv 2602.06926 (Feb 2026) automates one pipeline from partial L1 passage (~5 h timing and ~10 nT field errors), at lead times of hours.
plasma-bz-forecast.why: Requires either routine coronal magnetic-field measurement or in-situ monitors well upstream of L1, neither of which will exist by 2031. AI theory can extract partial skill from source-region magnetograms (flux-rope chirality and orientation rules), which is why S2/S3 are Low rather than Speculative.
plasma-bz-forecast.strongest_case_small: This is an observation limit, not a mathematics limit.
plasma-bz-forecast.signpost: Funding of a sub-L1 or off-Sun-Earth-line in-situ monitor, or a source-region method with Bz-sign skill above 70% on 50+ events.
plasma-bz-forecast.revision_note: B-safe-orbits: Skeptic: hard edge from plasma-eruption-onset-theory made soft (Bz depends on flux-rope orientation, chirality and rotation, not on onset timing); soft edges added from science-helio-tomography and the new side-view monitor node. Auditor: arXiv 2602.06926 is an automated pipeline, so the status no longer cites it for the opposite point. Years unchanged (>2031).
