plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.title: Storm-proof low-orbit operations
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.description: Constellation operators and space-traffic services run conjunction screening and station-keeping on probabilistic density forecasts with realistic covariance, so that at the next G4+ storm the number of objects losing custody and of emergency maneuvers is at least halved versus May 2024.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.status_oct2026: During the May 2024 storm thousands of satellites maneuvered and conjunction assessment was poorly predictable even a day ahead (Parker and Linares 2024); KANOPUS-V 3 lost ~917 m of semi-major axis within days (CPAESS 2026 abstract). SpaceX's response to the Feb 2022 loss was operational (higher insertion orbits) (general).
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.why: Once density products carry calibrated uncertainty (2029 in S2), propagating it into covariance and screening is mature astrodynamics; the gate is adoption by operators and the government catalog, which typically takes 1-2 years and faces the FY2027 Office of Space Commerce cut. The May 2024 degradation came mostly from storm-driver forecasts (Ap underpredicted by 100-300 at 1-3 days), which stay data-limited (plasma-bz-forecast), and the government catalog already runs assimilative density (HASDM), so the achievable gain is partial. Validating the outcome also needs a G4+ storm in 2029-31, in the declining phase of Cycle 25 (maximum Oct 2024, SIDC), when G4 storms still occur but less often (general).
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.strongest_case_small: The largest operators already manage storms with margin and autonomy; the benefit concentrates in smaller operators and the public catalog. Losses like Feb 2022 were an operations choice and were fixed operationally. Fast-revisit sensing (SpaceX Stargaze, minutes-latency orbit updates) can deliver much of the custody gain without new density math.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.signpost: At the next G4+ storm, count objects losing custody and emergency maneuvers versus May 2024.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.revision_note: B-safe-orbits: Skeptic and auditor both: S3 band High -> Medium (adoption gate barely compresses in S3; government catalog faces an ~80% Office of Space Commerce cut; P6 default Low). Skeptic: 'storms no longer cause...' replaced with a testable criterion (at least halved versus May 2024 at the next G4+ storm); Stargaze added to strongest case. Advocate's S2 2029 High and S3 2028 rejected: they assume zero adoption lag after the 2029 density product and credit a non-AI sensing system (Stargaze) for the AI-math node; the advocate's soft edge from constellation-hosted tracking accepted.

plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.title: Probabilistic radiation-belt and charging forecasts days ahead
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.description: Probabilistic, physics-consistent forecasts of MeV electron flux and surface/internal charging hazard, 1-3 days ahead for CME-driven enhancements and up to about a week for recurrent high-speed-stream driving, used in satellite operations (for example deferring an orbit-raise or electric-propulsion firing through a charging peak).
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.status_oct2026: SWPC's operational Relativistic Electron Forecast Model (REFM) already gives deterministic 1-3 day >2 MeV electron fluence forecasts at GEO from 30 days of solar-wind speed (SWPC). Random-forest models (VAMPIRE/COVEN, Jun 2026) forecast ~2 MeV flux threshold crossings up to 6 days ahead from the AL index history alone (Northumbria); SPARTAI gives multi-day MeV forecasts (Oct 2025); transformer and LSTM pipelines forecast 1 MeV flux 6 h ahead (arXiv 2605.15752). Charging codes (SPIS, NASCAP-2K) are mature; PAGER internal-charging models were validated against GEO anomalies (IEEE TPS 2026).
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.why: ML forecasts and a deterministic operational baseline exist; AI applied math adds coupling to physics-based diffusion models and calibrated probabilities so operators can act on them. Week-ahead skill exists only for recurrent high-speed-stream driving (27-day recurrence); CME-driven enhancements stay at 1-3 days. The binding step is adoption: an agency product (SWPC or ESA) and an operator or insurer procedure citing it. Chain (S2): calibrated physics-coupled methods 2028 -> SWPC or ESA pre-operational probabilistic product 2029 -> an operator or insurer procedure citing it 2029-30. Software-only, so no hardware lag; agency R2O and operator uptake set the pace, which is why S2 is Medium.
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.strongest_case_small: Already ML-driven, so the math increment is modest; designers will keep worst-case design environments (e.g. AE9/AP9) regardless of forecasts, so design margins do not shrink.
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.signpost: SWPC or ESA adopts a multi-day MeV electron probability product and an operator or insurer cites it in procedures.
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.revision_note: B-safe-orbits: All three lenses: hard edge from plasma-swx-data-assimilation made soft (radiation-belt forecasts run on L1 solar wind, in-situ flux and geomagnetic indices; COVEN uses only the AL index history, checked). Skeptic and auditor: 'size shielding and charging margins' deleted (designers keep AE9/AP9). Auditor: S1 Medium -> Low, S2 High -> Medium, gate data -> adoption (signpost is agency R2O plus operator citation; P6 default Low; week-ahead ML products exist); 'a week' -> 'up to 6 days' (checked). Skeptic: SWPC REFM baseline added; week-ahead skill limited to recurrent high-speed streams; title adjusted. Advocate's S2 2028 rejected (agency adoption plus operator citation in the year after applied math arrives leaves no R2O time). Advocate's soft edge into materials-cots-orbital-compute-ops not applied (outgoing edge into another branch).

plasma-vleo-at-scale.title: Commercial constellations below 300 km
plasma-vleo-at-scale.description: At least 100 commercial satellites operating sustainably below 300 km altitude, with propellant and drag margins sized from validated density statistics.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.status_oct2026: Albedo's Clarity-1 operated at 350-380 km for nine months (Mar-Dec 2025) and projects five-year life at 275 km averaged over solar cycles; it lost contact due to a radio memory fault, not drag (Albedo, Jan 2026). Solar Cycle 25 peaked Oct 2024; the declining phase runs to ~2030, lowering mean density but still producing large storms.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.why: Validated density statistics trim only the model-error share of the drag reserve; most of the reserve at 250-300 km covers solar-cycle and storm variability (density varies several-fold over a cycle, general), which no density model removes, so plausible savings are ~10-20% of drag propellant (illustrative). That helps VLEO business cases at the margin, but constellations need capital, launches and production first.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.strongest_case_small: Capital, demand for very-high-resolution imagery, EP throughput and atomic-oxygen-tolerant hardware bind this, not density mathematics.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.signpost: A sub-300 km operator raises >= $100M and orders >= 50 satellites by 2028.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.revision_note: B-safe-orbits: Skeptic: hard edge from plasma-thermo-density-uq made soft (Clarity-1 flew at 350-380 km and projects five-year life at 275 km without calibrated density products; the node is capital-gated), and the margin arithmetic corrected: most of the drag reserve covers solar-cycle and storm variability that no density model removes. Years and bands unchanged.

plasma-nep-mars-cargo.title: Megawatt electric cargo ships to Mars
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.description: An operational nuclear-electric (or megawatt solar-electric) cargo vehicle with MW-class electric propulsion flying to Mars.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.status_oct2026: NASA estimates 2-4 MW and >23,000 h thruster life for crewed nuclear-electric missions. Earlier NASA Glenn COMPASS work sized a ~1.9 MWe system for a 2-year crewed round trip and ~200 t cargo stages (general). Highest demonstrated single-thruster power: 120 kW lithium MPD (Feb 2026). NASA says NEP architectures needing up to 300 kW of EP can be built by clustering 12 kW AEPS thrusters, with Xe and Kr cluster tests under way (Williams et al. 2026). SR-1 Freedom (>20 kWe, Dec 2028 target, Gateway PPE bus with three 12 kW AEPS and four 6 kW Hall thrusters) would be the first NEP flight, at about 1% of MW class.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.why: Needs a flight reactor or MW-class arrays, launch approval for a space reactor, and life-tested MW-scale EP; each is a multi-year hardware and regulatory program. Clusters of qualified 12 kW thrusters cover the few-hundred-kW range, so MW class still needs higher-power thrusters (plasma-high-power-ep-life) or impractically large clusters (~80-330 units). The solar route rides on compute-satellite power buses (AI1: ~150 kW array at ~127 W/kg on a ~2.1 t satellite, 33FG reconstruction, Jun 2026; struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet, soft). That route could enable 100 kW-class solar-electric tugs, but not MW cargo before 2031.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node records a nil effect inside the horizon.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.signpost: A funded flight-reactor program with a launch date, or a >= 500 kW thruster test campaign announced.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor: COMPASS figure marked (general); SR-1 calibration point added. Advocate: NASA's clustering path (up to 300 kW from 12 kW thrusters) added; its proposal to soften plasma-high-power-ep-life and add a compute-bus tug as a hard prerequisite rejected (MW class lies beyond NASA's stated cluster range; the tug is not a causal precondition). Compute-satellite power route recorded as a soft edge from struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet. Years and bands unchanged.

plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.title: Faster, cheaper electric-propulsion development
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.description: Development-to-qualification time for new EP thrusters falls ~15-30% (S2), up to ~40% (S3), and build-test iterations roughly halve because physics-based models replace parts of empirical iteration and wear testing. The ceiling is the Amdahl bound on whole-program compression (~38% S2, ~51% S3; capability.json); EP schedules are dominated by wear-test hours and by program, supplier and requirements problems.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.status_oct2026: AEPS: contract awarded 2016 (general); AEPS contract closeout mid-to-late 2027, but the QM-2 life wear test runs fall 2026 to Sep 2029 and the SEP project closes out in 2029, about 13 years (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026).
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.why: Combines predictive design (fewer iterations) with model-based life credit (shorter wear tests). Life credit lands in 2031 at the earliest even in S3, and the outcome needs at least one full development-to-qualification cycle started after both tools exist, so it cannot be observed by 2031 in any scenario. Chain (S3): predictive design 2029 + life credit 2031 -> a new program started 2030-31 -> qualification 2033 or later even at a 3-year pace.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.strongest_case_small: Program management, supply chain and funding dominate EP schedules; AEPS's own lessons learned are about risk management, contract oversight and requirement definition, not physics.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.signpost: A new EP product announced with qualification completed in under three years, citing model-based life credit.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 2031 -> >2031 (a full program cycle must start after life credit, which now lands 2031 at the earliest); S2 Low -> Speculative. Auditor: S3 Low -> Speculative (skeptic kept Low; resolver sided with the auditor because the hard prerequisite lands at the horizon). Skeptic: magnitude 30-50% -> ~15-30% (S2), up to ~40% (S3), within the Amdahl bounds. Skeptic + auditor (verified): AEPS took ~13 years including the life test, not 11. Advocate's S2 2031 / S3 2030 Medium rejected (its comparison nodes have since moved to S2 2031 / S3 2030).

prop-ns-forced-verified.title: Forced Navier–Stokes blowup independently checked
prop-ns-forced-verified.description: Outside experts run Comparator on the Lean proof and audit the statement of OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 claim that the forced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations can blow up from smooth, finite-energy data. This moves that claim from T3 to T4. The concurrent Buckmaster-Alpöge Euler, Boussinesq and porous-medium blowup proofs are a parallel, separate check. Whether the result also satisfies Clay's breakdown statements (C)/(D) is a separate institutional question (frontier-ns-clay-cd-ruling).
prop-ns-forced-verified.status_oct2026: Claimed Sep 8, 2026 with a 166-page manuscript and Lean repository (~17 h formalization; ~88 h of ~10,000 agents). OpenAI frames the result as establishing Clay statement (C), and also (D); Clay still lists the problem unsolved. Buckmaster and Alpöge posted Euler/Boussinesq/IPM blowup preprints with Lean formalizations about 12 h before the announcement (Decrypt reported the most advanced result still awaiting a final Lean check at disclosure), followed by a public credit dispute. Santibañez-Leal (Zenodo, Sep 17) replayed the NS and Euler Lean certificates through the kernel with zero sorryAx; that is not a Comparator run or statement audit, so the tier is unchanged. No independent review found as of Oct 7, 2026: T3. Duraiswami (arXiv 2609.17642, Sep 15, 2026) found nothing to suggest the mechanism is reachable in a flow one computes or builds. Related but separate: family 376 (universal computation in forced NS) is a catalog family, manuscript-only (T1).
prop-ns-forced-verified.why: The Lean code is public and the dispute guarantees scrutiny, so a Comparator run plus a statement audit is likely within about 12 months in every scenario. The engineering consequence is a confidence change only (tl-position-2): the forced equations alone can fail to determine the flow, which CFD practice already assumes by adding numerical or model dissipation. No solver, closure or engine design changes. It is a stepping stone (soft link) to frontier-ns-unforced, not a prerequisite.
prop-ns-forced-verified.strongest_case_small: The forcing is engineered to drive the singularity, and real propellants would cavitate or form shocks long before it occurs (Duraiswami 2026). Rocket CFD resolves or models scales where the continuum assumption itself fails. The propulsion impact is essentially nil. The node is on the tree to mark a dead end readers would otherwise take for a breakthrough.
prop-ns-forced-verified.signpost: First published Comparator report and statement audit for the NS Lean repository (via Hexagon or the IAS advisory group), expected within 6-12 months. A gap would drop the claim to T1.
prop-ns-forced-verified.revision_note: B-math-frontier: [skeptic] catalog_families 376 removed (the Sep 8 claim is outside the 722-paper catalog; 376 stays in status as a related, separate T1 family); description scoped to the OpenAI claim, Buckmaster-Alpoge as a parallel check. [auditor] status: kernel replay, Clay framing, Alpoge-Buckmaster Lean status; lettered position citation fixed. [advocate S2/S3 2026 rejected: signpost itself expects 6-12 months; no outside Comparator run a month after the claim; Hexagon has no deposits.] Hard edge into frontier-ns-unforced made soft; edge into prop-les-convergence-theory (engines-materials) left for that branch.

prop-certified-stability-rom.title: Certified combustion-stability models
prop-certified-stability-rom.description: Low-order acoustic-network or Galerkin models of chamber thermoacoustics, delivered with rigorous linear and nonlinear stability margins: Lyapunov or sum-of-squares certificates and bounds on Hopf bifurcation and triggering amplitude under an uncertain flame-response band.
prop-certified-stability-rom.status_oct2026: Solved in principle but expert-scarce. DLR/TU Delft network models predict acoustic frequencies within <5% on two research combustors (de Jong Cantarino et al., IJSCD 2026). Growth rates and triggering thresholds still hinge on flame response, and reliable, efficient instability prediction remains rare (JAXA 2025). Family 143 [L] (uniform limit-cycle bounds, Hilbert's 16th) is T3 but theory only: it bounds how many oscillation states can coexist in planar polynomial amplitude models, with no practical constant.
prop-certified-stability-rom.why: Stability analysis of a given model is bespoke but routine mathematics, exactly the kind that becomes on-demand under tl-position-4. With public research-grade models in 2027 (S2), a team can get certified margins for every injector variant in days instead of a specialist's months. The value is capped by the flame-response input (prop-flame-response).
prop-certified-stability-rom.strongest_case_small: Certifying the stability of a model with the wrong flame response gives false comfort: a proof of the wrong property. Bomb tests stay mandatory. The F-1 lesson is that triggered (nonlinear) instability is what destroys engines, and its inputs are physical.
prop-certified-stability-rom.signpost: A published AI-produced stability analysis that predicts unstable modes and triggering thresholds on a rig (DLR BKD/BKH, Purdue CVRC) before the test.
prop-certified-stability-rom.revision_note: B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027; cap-applied-math is 2027 in both, so the same one-year lag applies). lettered citation 'under position (a' replaced with the KB position id under tl-position-4.

prop-cfd-auto-vv.title: Automated checks that engine flow simulations are right
prop-cfd-auto-vv.description: AI agents run code verification (manufactured solutions), solution verification (grid and time-step refinement; adjoint or a-posteriori error estimates for steady and RANS cases), uncertainty quantification and NASA-STD-7009-style credibility assessment on every propulsion simulation at near-zero marginal labor. Compute for solution verification of unsteady LES stays several times the base run (a 2x refinement of a 3D unsteady case costs ~8-16x, general), adjoint error estimates do not apply to chaotic LES, and credibility (validation) remains capped by test data.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.status_oct2026: Solved in principle, but rarely done in full on engine-design CFD because it is labor-intensive (general). CFD Vision 2030 progress reviews flag separated-flow prediction and UQ as persistent gaps (Aerospace America, Dec 2022).
prop-cfd-auto-vv.why: Every CFD result becomes a number with an error bar that separates numerical error from model-form error. That ends two expensive failure modes: hardware built on an unconverged simulation, and tests run to settle a question the simulation had already answered. It is also a prerequisite for any regulator credit for simulation.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.strongest_case_small: Validation data, not verification labor, limit V&V. Error bars on RANS are dominated by closure error, which verification cannot remove.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.signpost: An AI-generated credibility assessment accepted in a NASA or prime-contractor design review, or AI-automated solution verification in AIAA CFD Prediction Workshop entries.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (claim, accepted): labor collapses but compute does not; solution verification of unsteady LES costs several times the base run and adjoint error estimates diverge on chaotic LES. Soft edge from frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd (all three lenses; the merged LES-convergence node said it feeds this one). Advocate's S2 2028 -> 2027 rejected: adoption gate cannot land the same year as its capability prerequisites (lag ladder). | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027; the resolver's own lag-ladder argument against S2 2027 applies to S3 too).

prop-mass-gauging.title: Low-gravity propellant gauging limits
prop-mass-gauging.description: Proofs of which tank-fill states can be identified in microgravity from boundary sensors (capacitance, radio-frequency or impedance-type tomography), plus gauging algorithms with guaranteed error bounds.
prop-mass-gauging.status_oct2026: Gauging is a focus area of NASA's CFM portfolio, alongside boil-off and transfer. Family 365 [L]: its formalized main result is nonuniqueness of bounded measurable scalar conductivities on a 3D ball (T3, unaudited by outsiders), the part used here as a ceiling: some rough interior configurations cannot be told apart from boundary data alone without priors or extra sensing. Its headline, joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch, is unformalized (T1, conditional).
prop-mass-gauging.pathway: P1 (+P3 via classical log-stability limits, general)
prop-mass-gauging.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 365's formalized part (3D scalar-conductivity nonuniqueness, used as the imaging ceiling) is T3; its metric/connection recovery headline is T1 (conditional, context only)
prop-mass-gauging.why: Gauging uncertainty turns into reserve propellant: 1% of a 1,200 t depot load is ~12 t, about 0.1 of a 120 t tanker (illustrative, general), so the economic stake is small. Gauging needs a scalar (total mass), which can be identifiable even when the interior configuration is not; 365's formalized part concerns rough (bounded measurable) 3D scalar conductivities and its T1 headline concerns joint metric and connection recovery, so it bounds full tomographic imaging, not mass estimation. The practical ceiling for few-electrode capacitance gauging is classical logarithmic instability (general). The ceiling side tells designers not to rely on full tomographic reconstruction and to fuse sensors with thermodynamic models.
prop-mass-gauging.strongest_case_small: Operators can gauge after a settling burn with conventional sensors and accept the margin. The formalized nonuniqueness in family 365 concerns rough (bounded measurable) 3D conductivities, which may not match real tank fill states.
prop-mass-gauging.signpost: Flight gauging accuracy reported from LOXSAT or the Starship transfer demo (target <=1%).

prop-closure-theory.title: Turbulence and combustion models with guarantees
prop-closure-theory.description: AI-built RANS, LES subgrid and flamelet closures that are realizable, frame-invariant and consistent in known limits, carry generalization bounds, and are validated across separated, swirling and reacting benchmark classes without per-case tuning.
prop-closure-theory.status_oct2026: Open; this is the field's central modeling problem. RANS cannot reliably predict separated flows (CFD Vision 2030). ML closures often fail to generalize beyond their training data (JFM 2025; arXiv 2604.25824, Apr 2026). A propulsion example: k-omega SST under-predicts LH2 tank self-pressurization by 15-16% and vapor temperature by up to 40%, versus 3% for laminar and 7% for IDDES (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025).
prop-closure-theory.why: Closure error is the dominant model-form error in propulsion CFD: wall heat flux for cooling, mixing, nozzle separation. Under S2 the cognitive part (deriving constrained closures, proving consistency) is fast. What binds is high-fidelity data at engine conditions. DNS at engine Reynolds numbers is infeasible even at exascale (Pele's largest run: 60 billion cells), and high-pressure reacting validation experiments take years. Success requires validation across separated, swirling and reacting classes without per-case tuning plus a blind workshop result; blind AIAA workshops run on roughly 2-3-year cycles (general), so a closure derived when cap-physics-theory lands cannot be blind-validated the same year. P6 defaults to Low. Flame-response and turbopump tools benefit (soft links) but do not need closure guarantees.
prop-closure-theory.strongest_case_small: Turbulence closure has resisted 60 years of work and may be fundamentally underdetermined, because averaging loses information. A provably consistent closure need not beat a tuned one on a specific engine. LES and hybrid methods are already replacing RANS in design-critical areas.
prop-closure-theory.signpost: An AI-derived closure tops the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource separated-flow cases and a blind AIAA workshop case without retuning.
prop-closure-theory.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (timing/band, concrete mechanism accepted): S2 2029 -> 2030, S3 2028 -> 2029, S2 Medium -> Low. The success criterion includes a blind workshop win, which cannot happen in the year the theory capability lands (cap-physics-theory S2 2029 / S3 2028); data at engine conditions bind; P6 default Low. Edges to prop-turbopump-tool (skeptic + advocate) and prop-flame-response (skeptic + advocate) made soft. S3 Medium kept. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2029 -> 2030: the why says a closure cannot be blind-validated in the year cap-physics-theory lands, and B-trunk moved that anchor to S3 2029. S3 band Medium kept.

prop-flame-response.title: Predictive flame response at engine pressures
prop-flame-response.description: First-principles prediction of injector flame transfer functions and transcritical real-fluid mixing for LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 at 100-350 bar. This is the missing input that decides whether a chamber mode grows.
prop-flame-response.status_oct2026: Measured on subscale rigs or extracted from costly LES; wall-modeled LES at engine conditions is described as prohibitively expensive (JAXA 2025). Raptor reached 350 bar chamber pressure in a development test that Musk reported in May 2023 (per newspaceeconomy, Apr 16, 2026), deep in the supercritical regime where injection models lack validation (general).
prop-flame-response.why: With flame response predicted, certified reduced models (prop-certified-stability-rom) predict growth rates, not just frequencies. Flame transfer functions are already computed by LES with existing subgrid models; what is missing is validated real-fluid, transcritical injection physics at 100-350 bar and rig data, so closure theory (prop-closure-theory) accelerates the work but is not required. Validation can start against decades of archived rig data, but it then needs about a year of blind rig tests. That experimental year binds in S2 and S3 alike: chain (S2) cap-physics-theory (2029) -> model -> blind rig year -> 2030; (S3) 2029 (cap-physics-theory, moved from 2028 by B-trunk) -> 2030.
prop-flame-response.strongest_case_small: Flame response depends on manufacturing detail (injector tolerances, additive-manufacturing roughness) and on transient states that models won't capture. Rigs remain necessary for every new injector family.
prop-flame-response.signpost: Blind prediction of an unstable mode's frequency and amplitude to within ~10% on a JANNAF, ESA or DLR combustor before the test.
prop-flame-response.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (timing, two lenses): S2 2029 -> 2030; the node's own text says a year of blind rig tests binds, yet S2 equalled its prerequisites' year. prop-closure-theory hard -> soft (skeptic + advocate: flame transfer functions are computed by LES with existing subgrid models; what is missing is transcritical real-fluid injection physics and rig data). Soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands (advocate). Advocate's S3 2029 -> 2028 rejected: theory capability lands in S3 2028 and the blind rig campaign (8-9 months at 1.3-1.5x) cannot finish the same year. Fact fix (auditor, verified): the 350 bar milestone was reported in May 2023, not 2026. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2029 -> 2030: the node's own rule (a blind rig year after the theory capability, in S2 and S3 alike) applied to cap-physics-theory S3 2029 after B-trunk moved it from 2028. Band unchanged.

prop-rde-mode-theory.title: Predictive theory of detonation-engine wave modes
prop-rde-mode-theory.description: A validated model of how many detonation waves an RDRE runs, when it switches modes, and how injectors couple to the waves, as functions of flow rate, mixture and back-pressure, so that engines can be designed to hold one stable mode.
prop-rde-mode-theory.status_oct2026: Open research: wave-mode bifurcation (APS DFD 2025), dynamic injector-response models (Mar 2025), and model equations that capture qualitative mode-locking (arXiv 2003.06655). Hardware is ahead of theory: NASA's InRoDES 10,000 lbf-class LOX/LCH4 thrust chamber, tested from Sep 2025, fired for just over 340 s in Dec 2025, and an earlier full-scale NASA RDRE combustor ran 251 s at more than 5,800 lbf (NASA).
prop-rde-mode-theory.why: Higher specific impulse at equal average chamber pressure is a theoretical potential that NASA is still assessing; the demonstrated RDRE benefit is a much shorter combustor and an engine 10-50% shorter overall (NASA NTRS 20240000933). Either benefit needs stable, predictable modes. This is nonlinear-dynamics mathematics that S2 makes cheap. Hot-fire campaigns take days to weeks, but blind validation needs a new geometry designed, printed and hot-fired after the model exists (months), so S2 lands in 2029.
prop-rde-mode-theory.strongest_case_small: RDRE development is advancing empirically (340-s firings, Venus flight). Theory may mostly explain what tests already found; the real gates are thermal management of a compact chamber and nozzle integration.
prop-rde-mode-theory.signpost: A published model that predicts mode transitions on a new RDRE geometry blind, confirmed by NASA or AFRL tests.
prop-rde-mode-theory.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (claim, verified at NTRS 20240000933): the Isp gain is a 'potential ... currently being assessed', the demonstrated benefit is a 10-50% shorter engine, and the record does not mention a 5x lower feed pressure (removed). Timing (skeptic, accepted): S2 2028 -> 2029; blind validation needs a new geometry designed, printed and hot-fired after the model exists. Fact fix (auditor, re-verified on nasa.gov): only the Dec 2025 InRoDES firing exceeded 340 s; the 251 s figure belongs to an earlier full-scale RDRE combustor test, not Sep 2025. Soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands. Advocate's S3 Medium -> High rejected (P6 default Low; one band above default is already Medium).

prop-cfm-models.title: Validated microgravity cryogenic fluid models
prop-cfm-models.description: Predictive models of self-pressurization, slosh, line chilldown and tank-to-tank transfer in low gravity, validated on flight data with quantified uncertainty (tank pressure within ~5%, boil-off within ~10%).
prop-cfm-models.status_oct2026: In 1 g, CFD reaches 3% (laminar) to 7% (IDDES) on tank pressure, but results hinge on the turbulence model and a tuned evaporation accommodation coefficient (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025). Microgravity data are scarce (ZBOT on ISS). NASA's CFM portfolio lists maturing predictive models through flight-prediction comparisons as an objective. LOXSAT (Eta Space/Rocket Lab, a 9-month LOX demo) was set for no earlier than Jul 17, 2026; the sources found do not confirm whether it has flown.
prop-cfm-models.why: Boil-off and transfer losses drive the tanker count (SpaceX '10-ish' vs NASA 'high teens'). In an illustrative depot model (tables), boil-off of 0.05-0.3%/day costs ~1 extra tanker at one tanker per 6 days, and 0.3-0.5%/day costs 3-5 extra at one per 12 days. These are the physical losses; a validated model recovers only the margin held against their uncertainty (re-running the same model, planning for +50% boil-off instead of a validated +/-10% costs 0-1 tanker at a 6-day cadence, more only at slow cadence and high loss). In S2 the analysis is near-instant once flight data exist, but the data arrive on the launch clock: validation within ~5% on pressure and ~10% on boil-off across fill levels, coasts and attitudes needs several transfer flights and weeks-long storage, which come with the 2028-29 depot campaigns. Conditional on SpaceX or NASA publishing transfer and boil-off data (LOXSAT gives a small-tank public LOX dataset); otherwise the model exists only inside SpaceX and the node is unobservable.
prop-cfm-models.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will learn empirically from its own flights and keep the data, and margins will follow measured performance whether or not a public model exists.
prop-cfm-models.signpost: Publication of transferred mass, boil-off and chilldown losses from the first Starship ship-to-ship transfer, or NASA model-vs-flight comparisons from LOXSAT.
prop-cfm-models.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (timing, concrete mechanism accepted): S2 2028 -> 2029. The data gate runs on the launch clock; the first ship-to-ship transfer is S2 2027 and was still unscheduled in Sep 2026, and validation across fill levels, coasts and attitudes needs several transfer flights and weeks-long storage, which arrive with the 2028-29 depot campaigns; prop.json itself rated this 'High by 2028 if flight data are shared'. Added the data-sharing conditional and the 'physical loss vs model margin' correction (skeptic + auditor; depot table reproduced and margin re-simulated). Soft edge from new node prop-loxsat-cfm-flight-data (auditor). S1/S3 and bands unchanged.

prop-psi-models.title: Predictive plume–surface interaction for landers
prop-psi-models.description: Validated models of how lander engine plumes erode regolith (rarefied-to-continuum gas flow, granular ejecta, cratering), used to set landing-site and engine-placement requirements.
prop-psi-models.status_oct2026: NASA reports that poorly constrained flight data inhibit accurate PSI prediction. Langley's vacuum-sphere PSI tests run through spring 2026, and MSFC PSI tools support HLS (NTRS 2023). Families 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation) and 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases, incl. fluctuations) are T1 and touch the kinetic theory beneath DSMC. Conditional; P5 confidence only.
prop-psi-models.pathway: P1->P6 (363/364 P5 link has nil engineering effect)
prop-psi-models.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise via cap-applied-math); 363 and 364 are T1, conditional, with nil engineering effect
prop-psi-models.why: Starship HLS already uses smaller mid-body methalox landing thrusters for terminal descent to raise the plume impingement point (general). Predictive PSI now sets standoff and throttle limits, landing-site and pad requirements, and keep-out zones for nearby base assets under repeated landings at one site, and it decides whether sintered pads are needed (auton-sinter-process-control). This is applied numerics plus data: DSMC for the rarefied gas phase (already adequate) coupled to CFD-DEM ejecta models calibrated on flight imagery. The data gate eases with landing cadence: SCALPSS 1.1 on Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Mar 2025) returned plume-surface imagery and stereo elevation maps, so every instrumented CLPS or HLS landing is a PSI experiment. Families 363 and 364 have nil engineering effect: DSMC's convergence to the Boltzmann equation is already proven (Wagner 1992, general), so new foundations for Boltzmann do not change DSMC practice. They are noted only as conditional (T1) theory context.
prop-psi-models.strongest_case_small: DSMC already works for the gas phase. The gaps are granular physics and lunar flight data, which no theorem supplies, and operators can engineer around PSI with pads, throttling or thruster placement.
prop-psi-models.signpost: Pre-landing PSI predictions matched by post-landing imagery from CLPS or Artemis landers.
prop-psi-models.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: bands match capability-driven T3 physics nodes (no T1 drop was applied or needed).
prop-psi-models.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (fact): the Raptor-plume framing was outdated, because Starship HLS uses mid-body landing thrusters for terminal descent. The why now lists what PSI still decides. Skeptic: 363/364 labeled nil engineering effect (Wagner 1992); pathway P5+P6 -> P1->P6. Advocate (edge): cap-physics-theory moved from hard to soft and cap-applied-math added as hard. Predictive PSI is DSMC plus CFD-DEM calibrated on flight data, which is applied numerics plus data and not new theory. Advocate's S3 2029 -> 2028 rejected: the gate is validation against landing imagery, and S3 cognition equals S2 through 2028, so S2 = S3 = 2029. New soft input from auton-lunar-heavy-cargo-landing; new soft outputs to auton-sinter-process-control (skeptic), auton-robotic-landing-pad and auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops (advocate). Bands unchanged.

prop-ntp-fuel-model.title: Nuclear thermal fuel behavior model
prop-ntp-fuel-model.description: A validated multiphysics model of carbide or CERMET fuel corrosion, cracking and fission-product release in 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen under irradiation and thermal cycling. These are the physics that set NTP temperature, Isp and life.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.status_oct2026: GA-EMS fuel survived six thermal cycles to 2,600 K in flowing hydrogen at MSFC (Jan 2025), without irradiation. Core materials that endure 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen at >3 MPa remain the critical obstacle (general literature). Neutron transport (Monte Carlo) is mature (general). Families 278 (Kohn-Sham ensemble representability fails) and 275 (QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy) are T1 ceilings on DFT-based materials modeling (P3, conditional). They are context only: fuel-performance codes use fitted potentials and empirical correlations, so neither bears on how NTP fuel models are built.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 278 and 275 are T1 ceilings, conditional, context only
prop-ntp-fuel-model.why: Fuel life and temperature set NTP's ~900 s Isp, against ~450 s for LOX/LH2 (general). A predictive model narrows the irradiation test matrix. But 'validated under irradiation' needs test-reactor fluence plus post-irradiation examination (1-3 years combined, general), and no combined irradiation-plus-hot-hydrogen test facility exists (general). Autonomous labs speed up non-nuclear hot-hydrogen tests, not neutron dose, so S3 lands 2030 at Low.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.strongest_case_small: Fuel qualification is inherently empirical and regulators will require data. Families 278 and 275 confirm DFT limits that practitioners already work around.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.signpost: Release of a combined hot-hydrogen plus irradiation dataset (INL/MSFC) with blind model predictions.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 Medium -> Low; skeptic: S3 2029 -> 2030 (irradiation fluence plus post-irradiation examination take 1-3 years that no cognitive multiplier shortens). Skeptic: families 278 and 275 relabelled context only.

prop-stability-design-tool.title: Design out combustion instability before hot fire
prop-stability-design-tool.description: An integrated workflow (predicted flame response, a certified reduced-order stability model and uncertainty quantification) that ranks injector and chamber designs by stability margin before hardware is built, used on a real engine program.
prop-stability-design-tool.status_oct2026: Instability is still found and fixed on the test stand. For the F-1, 'Project Go' ran 2,000 tests on 210 injector designs over two years before bomb tests showed damping within 45 ms (enginehistory.org; NASA History, Jul 12, 2019). Modern programs iterate faster with cheap additive injectors, but the loop remains test-driven.
prop-stability-design-tool.why: If even a third of instability redesign loops are avoided, a new engine saves months to a year and tens of hardware sets (judgment, general). The math (stability certificates) is fast under S2; flame-response validation on rigs is not, and the tool must then be used on a real engine program (the F-1 stability campaign took two years of tests). Chain (S2): prop-certified-stability-rom (2028) + prop-flame-response (2030) -> ranking injector designs on an engine program before hardware (2031 at the earliest). The gate is rig and hot-fire validation of the tool's rankings, not customer qualification.
prop-stability-design-tool.strongest_case_small: For well-funded teams, SpaceX-style rapid iteration with cheap 3D-printed injectors already makes testing cheaper than prediction (600+ Raptors built by Apr 2026). Bomb tests and stability rating stay mandatory, so the tests saved are development tests, not qualification tests.
prop-stability-design-tool.signpost: An engine program reports first-article stability qualification with no injector redesign and credits predictive tools.
prop-stability-design-tool.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (timing/band, two lenses): S2 2030 -> 2031 and S2 Medium -> Low (needs validated flame response, now S2 2030, then use on a real engine program). S3 2029 -> 2030 (skeptic; same lag after flame response S3 2029). Gate qualification -> experiment (skeptic + advocate: the tests saved are development tests; the real gate is rig and hot-fire validation of the tool's rankings). Gate convention (advocate, accepted): the first mover is a self-certifying commercial operator; FAA Part 450 regulates public safety, not engine materials or test counts, so the regulator/certification Medium cap does not apply unless the node needs NASA crew, NSSL or other customer certification. The band here rests on physical clocks, not on that cap. Soft edge from physclock-optimal-test-campaigns (advocate). | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2030 -> 2031 and S3 Medium -> Low: prop-flame-response moved to S3 2030, and the node's own chain needs rig and hot-fire validation after it (experiment gate, 1.3-1.5x in S3), so S3 now matches S2 (2031, Low).

prop-ai-engine-design-loop.title: AI-generated engines at scale
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.description: Computational engineering models generate complete additively-manufactured engines (geometry, regenerative cooling, injectors) in weeks. The node counts as achieved when a >=200 kN AI-generated engine completes a full-duration hot fire.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.status_oct2026: LEAP 71's Noyron generated a 5 kN LOX/kerosene aerospike that worked on its first firing (Dec 18, 2024). In Dec 2025 two Noyron-designed 20 kN LOX/CH4 engines (a bell and an aerospike) went from specification to first flame in under three weeks; the bell ran above 93% combustion efficiency over a week-long campaign, while the aerospike reached full chamber pressure (50 bar) but fired only once because of start-transient problems (LEAP 71, Dec 11, 2025). The 200 kN LOX/CH4 XRA-2E5, intended for the upper stage of the Oryx reusable launcher being developed with Aspire Space, was printed as one Inconel 718 part in 289 h (Mar 2026); its hot fire, planned before 2027, was not confirmed as of Oct 7, 2026. The Exploration Company licensed Noyron (Mar 24, 2026). Venus Aerospace credits 'AI-enabled design software' for its RDRE (Mercury Fund, Jul 21, 2026).
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.why: Design labor collapses toward zero, so the loop period is set by print time (~2 weeks for a large part) and test-stand availability. Once cap-design-optimization arrives, AI math adds guarantees such as proven cooling-channel thermal margins, but the loop already exists without it.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Design labor was never the long pole for large engines; reliability growth and qualification are. Noyron-style tools encode engineering rules rather than frontier mathematics, so the openai/math release adds little here.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.signpost: A full-duration XRA-2E5 hot fire, and the first orbital flight on an AI-generated main engine.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (grounding, accepted): pathway relabelled 'P1 (marginal; not AI-math-driven)' since the node itself says Noyron encodes engineering rules. Advocate (fact, accepted; verified at leap71.com): Dec 2025 20 kN methalox engines added to status; XRA-2E5 hot fire marked unconfirmed; the advocate's TEC '5-year licence' and Nyx-2028 details could not be verified (source returned 403) and were not added. Soft edge to prop-rde-flight-demo added. Years and bands unchanged.

prop-turbopump-tool.title: Predictive turbopump cavitation and stability
prop-turbopump-tool.description: Models that predict rotating cavitation, cavitation surge and rotordynamic instability for new inducer and pump designs before water-flow and hot-fire tests.
prop-turbopump-tool.status_oct2026: CFD predictions of cavitation instabilities depend strongly on the chosen cavitation and turbulence models, and 3D linear perturbation theories with dynamic transfer matrices are advancing (Pisa thesis, Jun 2025). On Starship Flight 12 (May 22, 2026) the booster lost an engine on ascent and more during boostback, ending in a hard Gulf landing (SpaceNews via 33FG); on Flight 13 (Jul 24, 2026) only 10 of 13 landing engines relit (Spaceflight Now). No official cause has been given.
prop-turbopump-tool.why: Turbopump instabilities are a leading cause of engine failures (general). Stability analysis of transfer-matrix and rotordynamic models is applied math that S2 makes cheap. The uncertain inputs (cavitation compliance, mass-flow gain) are calibrated on water-flow rigs, which are cheap and fast, so closure guarantees help but are not required. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math (2027) -> transfer-matrix models calibrated on archived inducer data (2027-28) -> blind water-rig confirmation on a new inducer (2029 at the earliest).
prop-turbopump-tool.strongest_case_small: Water-flow rig tests are cheap compared with hot fire, and design rules are mature, so prediction may save little.
prop-turbopump-tool.signpost: A blind prediction of rotating-cavitation onset for a new inducer, confirmed in a rig test.
prop-turbopump-tool.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Edge: prop-closure-theory hard -> soft (advocate + skeptic). Timing (advocate, concrete mechanism accepted): with closure guarantees no longer gating, the remaining gate is blind water-rig confirmation, which the node itself calls cheap; S2 2030 -> 2029, S3 2029 -> 2028. Advocate's S3 Medium -> High rejected (P1->P6, P6 default Low; blind prediction for a new inducer is still a modeling problem). Soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands. Fact fix (auditor): Nerra Network newsletter replaced by primary reports of Flight 12 (SpaceNews via 33FG news 518, verified) and Flight 13 (Spaceflight Now). | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): Flight 13 date harmonized to Jul 24, 2026 (launch date per 33FG news 596 / Wikipedia flight list; trunk and verif already used Jul 24).

prop-life-twin.title: Probabilistic engine life prediction for reuse
prop-life-twin.description: Physics-based life models for thermomechanical fatigue, low-cycle fatigue and creep in chambers, turbines and additively-manufactured parts, with uncertainty quantification, updated after each flight from sensors and inspection.
prop-life-twin.status_oct2026: Life estimation is hampered by heat-flux uncertainty, the choice of plasticity model and a lack of specimen characterization (Lisbon thesis 2024; Polito 2025). The methods are Morrow, Norton and Miner, validated on SSME-era data. Families 372 (global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity) and 366 (planar Mumford–Shah crack regularity) are T1 links to inspection inverse problems. Conditional, P5.
prop-life-twin.why: Reuse economics turn on refurbishment intervals. Probabilistic life models with UQ are expert-scarce applied math, the category S2 makes cheap; automated CFD V&V (prop-cfd-auto-vv) improves the heat-flux input but is not required, since thermal loads can come from engine instrumentation. Merlin fleet data are deep, but Raptor 3 (first flight May 2026; full-flow staged combustion with an oxygen-rich preburner, so different failure modes from kerosene gas-generator Merlins) has little, so data still bind for Starship-class engines.
prop-life-twin.strongest_case_small: Operators extend life through fleet-leader experience anyway, so any gain is internal and hard to observe. Heat-flux uncertainty (a closure problem) limits physics-based accuracy.
prop-life-twin.signpost: An operator or NASA discloses model-based (not fleet-leader-only) engine life limits, or NASA accepts probabilistic life analysis for crewed reuse.
prop-life-twin.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (edge + claim, accepted): prop-cfd-auto-vv hard -> soft (life models are calibrated on instrumented engines, inspection and fleet data; CFD V&V improves the heat-flux input but is not required). The 'data binds less' sentence contradicted the node's own data gate: the reflown fleet is kerosene gas-generator Merlins, whose wear does not transfer to Raptor 3. Years unchanged (cap-applied-math 2027 still precedes 2028).

prop-start-transient.title: Predictive engine start and relight transients
prop-start-transient.description: Validated system-level models of line chilldown, ignition, turbopump spin-up and combustion onset for in-flight relights after a coast, used to design start sequences with quantified margin.
prop-start-transient.status_oct2026: A live 2026 problem: on Flight 13 (Jul 24, 2026) only 10 of 13 booster engines relit for landing, and about five were running at splashdown (Spaceflight Now). Start transients are stiff differential-algebraic systems with uncertain two-phase chilldown physics (general).
prop-start-transient.why: Relight reliability gates booster catch, ship landing and, most critically, HLS lunar descent after days to weeks in orbit. Relight failures come mainly from propellant conditioning and gas ingestion, two-phase line chilldown, igniter performance and turbopump spin-up; chemistry-integration error is negligible next to rate-constant and two-phase uncertainty, so certified stiff solvers (frontier-stiff-certified) help but do not gate it, while line chilldown (prop-cfm-models) does. Every flight supplies validation data for short coasts; the long-coast regime that matters for HLS gets data only with the depot campaigns, which keeps S2 at Medium.
prop-start-transient.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will probably fix relight empirically within a few flights, and models will follow the data rather than lead it.
prop-start-transient.signpost: Several consecutive Starship flights with full booster and ship relight success, especially after long coasts.
prop-start-transient.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (band): S1 Medium -> Low (S1 earliest year is 2031, the window edge). Skeptic (edge, accepted): frontier-stiff-certified hard -> soft; chemistry-integration error is negligible next to rate-constant and two-phase uncertainty (the stiff node admits it); prop-cfm-models stays hard. prop-verified-engine-software.title: Formally verified engine control software
prop-verified-engine-software.description: Machine-checked proofs that engine-controller and health-management logic (start sequencing, redlines, abort logic, numerical filters) meets its specification, produced by AI agents at low cost and accepted as verification evidence in a NASA human-rating or crewed-program review.
prop-verified-engine-software.status_oct2026: Certification standards already give credit for formal methods (DO-178C/DO-333), but AI agents and Lean are not qualified tools. The agentic formalization capability exists: openai/math formalized the main results of 162 papers in weeks. Redline logic matters: newsletter commentary named a sensor trip as one hypothesis for the 2026 Raptor 3 boostback shutdowns (unverified; no primary source).
prop-verified-engine-software.why: Engine controllers are safety-critical, and false or missed shutdowns from redline logic recur as a failure mode (general). Launch engines are not type-certified, and Part 450 licenses public safety, not engines, so the acceptors are crewed programs (RS-25 on SLS, Raptor on HLS, Merlin on crewed Falcon 9, BE-7 on Blue Moon): a handful of programs whose software baselines change slowly. The node needs general credit (infra-tool-qualification, plan acceptance S2 2030) plus a human-rating review that accepts the evidence, so by the A4 conjunctive rule used for verif-hls-autonomy-certification it sits a year later and a band lower: S2 2031 Low, S3 2030 Low, S1 Speculative. The uncertified counterpart, launch operators re-proving engine and abort logic on every flight, is verif-launch-fsw-per-flight.
prop-verified-engine-software.strongest_case_small: Most engine failures are physical rather than software. Commercial launch licensing does not require formal verification, and writing correct specifications remains the bottleneck.
prop-verified-engine-software.signpost: The first NASA crewed-program review that accepts AI-generated formal proofs as verification evidence for propulsion controller software.
prop-verified-engine-software.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic + auditor: S2 2030 -> 2031, S3 2029 -> 2030 and S2 band Medium -> Low (zero lag after the general-credit premise; only crewed programs can accept the evidence). Auditor: S1 Low -> Speculative and S3 Medium -> Low under the A4 rule (a dependent of a Medium regulatory node with a further uncertain human-rating step belongs below Medium); skeptic's S3 Medium rejected for consistency with verif-hls-autonomy-certification. Skeptic: description 'accepted in certification' -> crewed-program review; Raptor sensor-trip claim labeled as unverified commentary. Advocate's re-pointing to a separate checker-route node rejected with that node; its uncertified counterpart is added as verif-launch-fsw-per-flight.

prop-ship-transfer-demo.title: Ship-to-ship cryogenic transfer demonstrated
prop-ship-transfer-demo.description: Two Starships dock in low Earth orbit and transfer tens to 100+ tonnes of LOX and liquid methane, with measured boil-off, chilldown loss and transfer efficiency.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.status_oct2026: Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14 (Sep 28, 2026) and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites (Mach33, Sep 30, 2026). Ship-to-ship transfer has not flown and was not yet scheduled as of Sep 2026 (Wikipedia); Flight 15 (NET Oct 19, 2026) targets the first ship catch and begins testing docking and hatch mechanisms for the transfer demonstration (Basenor). Internal tank-to-tank transfer was done on Mar 14, 2024. NASA OIG (Mar 2026) calls cryogenic transfer 'one of the most significant technical challenges'.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.why: Flights and vehicle readiness set the timing, and AI mathematics moves this node by roughly zero. It is on the tree because its data unlock prop-cfm-models and, downstream, the refueling economy.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node exists to show the physical clock. The AI-math effect on its date is nil.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.signpost: Announcement and flight of the propellant-transfer mission, with the transferred mass disclosed.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (fact, contradicted; verified): Flight 15 is a single-vehicle flight and cannot perform ship-to-ship transfer; the transfer demo was not yet scheduled as of Sep 2026 (Wikipedia, updated Oct 4, 2026), and Flight 15 (NET Oct 19, 2026) targets the first ship catch and begins docking and hatch tests (Basenor). Years and bands unchanged.

prop-rde-flight-demo.title: Detonation engine flies in space
prop-rde-flight-demo.description: A rotating detonation rocket engine of about 1,000 lbf or more operates as primary propulsion in a space or lander flight demonstration, beyond suborbital hops.
prop-rde-flight-demo.status_oct2026: Venus Aerospace flew a 2,000 lbf RDRE to 4,400 ft (May 2025). Juno Propulsion won a NASA TechLeap prize for a NASA-funded flight test later in 2026 (small thruster). NASA's InRoDES is a 10,000 lbf-class pump-fed LOX/LCH4 engine whose thrust chamber fired for just over 340 s in Dec 2025 (NASA); a vacuum test comes next, then transfer to industry.
prop-rde-flight-demo.why: Hardware is limited by testing and funding. Cheaper analysis under S2 (mode theory, thermal design) trims iterations but cannot shorten vacuum testing, flight integration or the wait for a funded flight slot. S3 equals S2 until 2028, and autonomous test stands (S3 2028) cannot pull a funded flight into the same year, so all three scenarios share 2029. Chain: InRoDES vacuum test and industry transfer, or a Venus- or Juno-class program (2026-28) -> funded >=1,000 lbf space or lander demonstration (2029 at the earliest; P1 marginal).
prop-rde-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: A small in-space RDRE firing (Juno) may come in 2026-27 regardless of AI math. The >=1,000 lbf demo depends on a customer and money, not mathematics.
prop-rde-flight-demo.signpost: A Juno Propulsion in-space RDRE firing, NASA InRoDES vacuum-test results, or a lander provider baselining an RDRE.
prop-rde-flight-demo.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (timing, accepted): S3 2028 -> 2029; S3 equals S2 until 2028, and autonomous test stands (S3 2028) cannot pull a funded flight into the same year. Auditor: pathway 'P1 (marginal)' and soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands; advocate: soft edge from prop-ai-engine-design-loop (Venus credits AI-enabled design). InRoDES durations corrected (only Dec 2025 exceeded 340 s). Chain written out. Bands unchanged.

prop-ntp-ground-test.title: Nuclear thermal engine ground hot fire
prop-ntp-ground-test.description: A fission-heated hydrogen engine (5-12.5 klbf subscale) fired on the ground with full exhaust capture: the first U.S. NTP reactor test since NERVA (1972).
prop-ntp-ground-test.status_oct2026: DRACO was cancelled in the FY2026 budget request (May 2025) because falling launch costs eroded its ROI (DARPA's McHenry, Breaking Defense, Jun 27, 2025). Congress directed >=$110M for NTP in FY2026, and Administrator Isaacman committed to execute it (Sen. Britt, Apr 29, 2026). The White House Space Nuclear Initiative (Apr 14, 2026) prioritizes NEP (SR-1 Freedom, 20 kWe, Mars launch at end-2028) and lunar surface power, with 'common NEP/NTP components'. A high-pressure exhaust capture system for 5-12.5 klbf tests exists as a design (NASA, 2023).
prop-ntp-ground-test.why: As of Oct 2026 there is no funded NTP engine program of record. A reactor ground test needs a program start, a fueled reactor, an exhaust-capture facility and nuclear safety approval, which on historical precedent takes 5+ years from start (general). AI compresses design and safety-analysis documentation (S2/S3) but not facility construction, fuel fabrication or approvals. Chain: no program of record -> earliest program start FY2027-28 -> fueled reactor and a new exhaust-capture facility (a design only today), likely with an EIS (2-4 years) -> 2032 at the earliest even at S3's 0.8-0.9x. Appropriations compress 1.0x, so the node is Speculative by 2031 in every scenario.
prop-ntp-ground-test.strongest_case_small: Policy and money decide this node, and the policy pivot to NEP was driven by cost and launch prices, not mathematics.
prop-ntp-ground-test.signpost: FY2027 or FY2028 budgets fund an NTP ground-test facility and reactor, or DOE and NASA announce an NTP program of record.
prop-ntp-ground-test.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (mechanism checked against the physclock gate table): S3 2031 -> >2031; S2 and S3 Low -> Speculative. No program of record; a 5+ year precedent at 0.8-0.9x plus an EIS of 2-4 years gives 2032 at the earliest; appropriations compress 1.0x.

prop-hls-refuel-campaign.title: Full lunar-lander refueling campaign
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.description: Roughly 10-20 tanker flights fill a depot in LEO, which transfers a full load to Starship HLS for a lunar landing (uncrewed demo or crewed).
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.status_oct2026: NASA OIG (Mar 2026): more than 10 tankers are needed, the landing is planned for 2028, and NASA tracks a 'top risk' that cryogenic technologies won't be mature. ASAP (Sep 2025) warned HLS could be 'years late'. Estimates run from SpaceX's '10-ish' to NASA's 'high teens'. NASA plans an interim Artemis test flight in LEO in 2027 before landing attempts (Spaceflight Now, Jul 2026).
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.why: Launch cadence binds. At one tanker every ~6 days a campaign takes about 2 months, and every slip in cadence multiplies boil-off losses (tables). Validated boil-off and transfer models (prop-cfm-models) trim ~0-1 tanker of planning margin per mission at a 6-day cadence, more only at slow cadence and high boil-off, a regime operators avoid by flying faster. Reliable relights (prop-start-transient) protect the landing rather than the tanker count. Schedule gain: weeks to months. Chain (S2): prop-ship-transfer-demo (2027) -> 10-20-tanker depot fill on the launch clock -> transfer to HLS (2029 at the earliest; P1->P7). S1 and S2 share the date and band because launch cadence runs on its own curve (physclock: 0-0.5 year earlier in S2); S3's broader acceleration of hardware iteration and mishap closure (launch 0.5-1 year earlier) lifts it to 2028 and High.
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.strongest_case_small: AI mathematics is not on the critical path. Vehicle reliability, launch cadence, docking and pad turnaround are.
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.signpost: The first depot-filling campaign with >=5 tankers flown, and NASA confirming a landing date after the 2027 LEO test.
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (claim, two lenses): '~1-4 tankers saved' conflated the physical boil-off loss with a model's value; corrected to ~0-1 tanker of planning margin (depot table reproduced; margin re-simulated). Soft edges added (advocate): prop-cfm-models, prop-start-transient, prop-mass-gauging, physclock-ai-mishap-analysis, physclock-heavy-cadence-100, so the tree shows what the text already credits. Bands kept: advocate's S2 High and auditor's S3 2029/Medium both rejected (see debates). Chain written out.

prop-rde-operational.title: Detonation engines in operational service
prop-rde-operational.description: RDREs used as production propulsion on a commercial lander, upper stage or in-space vehicle, with predictable, qualified behavior.
prop-rde-operational.status_oct2026: There is no operational RDRE anywhere; only demonstrations exist (see prop-rde-flight-demo).
prop-rde-operational.why: Operational use requires a qualified engine whose mode behavior is predictable across throttle and mixture ranges. Mode theory buys that predictability faster, but empirical envelope mapping can also supply it, so it accelerates rather than gates. Qualifying a new combustion mode for operational use has historically taken several years after the first flight demo (general), and a customer must commit. Chain (S2): prop-rde-flight-demo (2029, physical) [+ prop-rde-mode-theory 2029, soft] -> envelope qualification -> production contract (2031 at the earliest; P1->P6->P7). P7 defaults to Speculative.
prop-rde-operational.strongest_case_small: Even with perfect theory, an Isp gain that is still unproven and a shorter chamber may not justify the qualification cost for most missions. Defense missiles and hypersonics, not space, may be the first operational users.
prop-rde-operational.signpost: A lander or upper-stage provider contracting an RDRE as baseline propulsion.
prop-rde-operational.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (band/timing/edge, accepted): S2 Low -> Speculative (P7 default; needs flight demo, then several years of envelope qualification, then a customer); S3 2030 -> 2031 (flight demo now S3 2029); prop-rde-mode-theory hard -> soft (empirical envelope mapping can also deliver predictability). Claim fix: the ~10% Isp gain is unproven (NTRS 20240000933). Chain written out (grounding rule).

prop-reuse-extended.title: Model-based engine reuse life
prop-reuse-extended.description: Reusable engines whose overhaul and inspection intervals are set by validated probabilistic life models, extending the flights between overhauls (for example 2x) without added risk.
prop-reuse-extended.status_oct2026: Reuse life today is extended mainly by fleet-leader experience (general). Raptor 3 had accumulated >40,000 s of runtime by Apr 2026 (newspaceeconomy).
prop-reuse-extended.why: Cheaper refurbishment and faster turnaround feed directly into launch cost. Life models pull fleet-leader life extension forward by roughly 6-12 months (physclock reuse-learning row, 0.8-0.9x in S2); a 2x interval is an illustration that still has to be earned in flight cycles, because each life data point costs a flight. Data arrive on the launch exponential: Mach33's base case has flights per stack rising from 3.3 (2027) to 8.9 (2029) and 18 (2030), which needs overhaul intervals to stretch several-fold, and at near-zero analysis cost an operator doing that will lean on calibrated life models. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math (2027) -> prop-life-twin (2028) -> Raptor 3 fleet cycles after physclock-starship-full-reuse (2027) and ~90 Starship flights in Mach33's 2028 reference case -> overhaul intervals set by calibrated models (2029 at the earliest; P1->P6->P7). The band stays Medium because the model must be validated on fleet leaders and the practice must become visible.
prop-reuse-extended.strongest_case_small: The gains are internal and hard to observe, and operators may extend life empirically just as fast.
prop-reuse-extended.signpost: Operator statements tying engine overhaul intervals to analytic life models (for example as Starship flights per stack pass ~9, Mach33's 2029 base case), or NASA reuse certification for crewed flights citing probabilistic life analysis.
prop-reuse-extended.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (claim, accepted): replaced the 'doubled overhaul interval is plausible' sentence with the physclock quantification (models pull fleet-leader life extension forward 6-12 months; each life data point costs a flight). Chain written out (grounding rule). Soft edge from physclock-heavy-cadence-100 (advocate: data arrive on the launch exponential). Skeptic's S2 2029 -> 2030 and advocate's S2/S3 Medium -> High both rejected (see debates): ~90 Starship flights in Mach33's 2028 reference case make model-set intervals in 2029 a fair optimistic edge, but validation on fleet leaders and visible attribution keep the band at Medium; no regulator cap is involved. Gate convention (advocate, accepted): the first mover is a self-certifying commercial operator; FAA Part 450 regulates public safety, not engine materials or test counts, so the regulator/certification Medium cap does not apply unless the node needs NASA crew, NSSL or other customer certification. The band here rests on physical clocks, not on that cap.

prop-ntp-crewed-mars.title: Nuclear thermal stage for crewed Mars
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.description: A flight-qualified NTP stage (~900 s Isp) available for crewed Mars transits, cutting trip time by up to ~25% (per DOE) and reducing crew radiation dose.
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.status_oct2026: There is no funded NTP flight program (DRACO was cancelled in 2025), and NEP was chosen for SR-1 Freedom (2028).
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.why: This requires a ground test, a flight demo and crew-rating, each a multi-year effort, and none has started. Math is not on the critical path.
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.strongest_case_small: The node is on the tree to mark a ceiling: AI math cannot fund a reactor or license a test.
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.signpost: An NTP flight-demo program of record with a launch date.

prop-engine-dev-compression.title: Engine development time and cost cut
prop-engine-dev-compression.description: New liquid engines reach qualification with materially fewer hot-fire tests and redesign loops (for example >=30% fewer than the same organization's previous engine program of similar thrust class), with the saving attributed to predictive tools.
prop-engine-dev-compression.status_oct2026: Development remains test-driven. SpaceX has built 600+ Raptors through large-scale test-fail-fix iteration (newspaceeconomy, Apr 2026).
prop-engine-dev-compression.why: Design and analysis compress (P1), but reliability demonstration is statistical. Showing 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes ~230 trials (n = ln 0.1 / ln 0.99) unless customers accept model-based Bayesian credit. For a high-cadence operator, flight starts accumulate fast (a Starship flight logs roughly 65-70 engine starts, general), but starts on one vehicle and build lot are correlated and each failure found resets the clock, so what paces a new engine is finding and fixing failure modes. Models cut redesign loops, not demonstration tests. Combustion instability is the historical driver of those loops, so the stability tool is the hard gate; generative design (prop-ai-engine-design-loop), turbopump prediction and information-optimal test campaigns help but are not individually necessary. New engines take 6-13 years and major versions ~3 years, compressing only 0.8-0.9x (S2) and 0.7-0.8x (S3), so few programs started with S2 or S3 tools qualify by 2031. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math (2027) -> prop-cfd-auto-vv + prop-certified-stability-rom (2028) -> prop-flame-response (2030) -> prop-stability-design-tool (2031) -> program qualification with fewer tests (after 2031). Chain (S3): stability tool (2030) -> an engine program already under way adopts it and attributes fewer tests (2031 at the earliest, Low).
prop-engine-dev-compression.strongest_case_small: The cheapest route to reliability is already high-rate testing of cheap hardware, so prediction competes with a very fast empirical loop.
prop-engine-dev-compression.signpost: A program publicly attributing a reduced hot-fire count to predictive tools, or a customer (NASA, USSF) accepting model-based reliability credit.
prop-engine-dev-compression.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (band, two lenses): S3 Medium -> Low (new engines take 6-13 years, compressing 0.7-0.8x in S3; hard prerequisites land S3 2027-2030, so only an in-flight program adopting the tools could qualify by 2031, and it must attribute the saving). Edges: prop-ai-engine-design-loop hard -> soft (skeptic) and prop-turbopump-tool hard -> soft (skeptic + advocate); prop-stability-design-tool kept hard (skeptic; advocate's demotion rejected, see debates); prop-cfd-auto-vv kept hard. Soft edges from physclock-optimal-test-campaigns (advocate; advocate's hard edge rejected: test-design savings are not 'predictive tools') and physclock-qual-by-analysis-credit (auditor). Gate qualification -> experiment (advocate convention). Gate convention (advocate, accepted): the first mover is a self-certifying commercial operator; FAA Part 450 regulates public safety, not engine materials or test counts, so the regulator/certification Medium cap does not apply unless the node needs NASA crew, NSSL or other customer certification. The band here rests on physical clocks, not on that cap. Advocate's S2 2031/Medium rejected. Description baseline defined (skeptic). Fleet-start arithmetic folded into why (advocate). Chains written out.

prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.title: Routine orbital refueling economy
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.description: Depots and tankers operate routinely, with dozens of cryogenic transfers per year supporting lunar landers, Mars ships and high-energy missions, and boil-off and transfer losses are predicted rather than padded.
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.status_oct2026: Not yet demonstrated. Eta Space targets a commercial LOX depot (Cryo-Dock) by 2030 (satnews, May 2026).
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.why: The economics depend on tankers per delivered tonne. Boil-off costs ~1-5 extra tankers per HLS-class campaign (illustrative table). Validated boil-off and transfer models recover only the planning margin on top of that, ~0-1 tanker at <=6-day cadence; gauging error at 1% of a 1,200 t load is ~12 t, ~0.1 tanker. Together that is a few percent of campaign launches. The rest comes down to cadence and vehicle reuse. Chain (S2): prop-ship-transfer-demo (2027) -> prop-cfm-models (2029) + prop-hls-refuel-campaign (2029) + physclock-heavy-cadence-100 (2030, after B-trunk) -> more than 20 transfers in a year (2030 at the earliest, from a second lunar campaign plus fuelling Mars ships for the early-2031 window; P1->P6->P7). Chain (S3): the same prerequisites in 2028-29 (heavy cadence 2029) -> early-2029 Mars-window fuelling plus lunar campaigns (2029). The band stays Medium: the earliest years are optimistic and AI mathematics is not on the critical path.
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.strongest_case_small: Launch cadence and vehicle cost dominate, so model-driven savings are second-order.
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.signpost: More than 20 ship-to-ship transfers in a calendar year, or a third-party depot (for example Cryo-Dock) receiving propellant.
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (claim, two lenses): model value restated as margin (~0-1 tanker) and gauging (~0.1 tanker), not the 1-5-tanker physical loss; '10-30% of campaign launches' dropped. Edges (skeptic, accepted): prop-mass-gauging hard -> soft (worth ~0.1 tanker; operators can gauge after a settling burn); physclock-heavy-cadence-100 soft -> hard (dozens of transfers a year need heavy cadence; year-consistent in all scenarios). premise_tier -> n/a (auditor; 365 no longer load-bearing). Timing (advocate, concrete mechanism accepted): S2 2031 -> 2030 and S3 2030 -> 2029 (a second lunar campaign plus Mars-ship fuelling for the early-2031 window, or the early-2029 window in S3, can exceed 20 transfers once all prerequisites land by 2029/2028); this also removes the auditor's 'Medium with earliest year 2031' inconsistency, so the auditor's S2 Low is not applied.
