struct-fsp-radiator-qual.title: Lightweight 600 K radiators qualified for fission power
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.description: Titanium-water or cesium-titanium heat-pipe radiator panels near 3 kg/m2 rejecting the ~230-300 kW of waste heat from a 100 kWe Brayton system, qualified for launch vibration, freeze-thaw and ~10 years of lunar micrometeoroid exposure.
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.status_oct2026: A Cs-Ti heat-pipe panel design reaches 2.98 kg/m2 and rejects >56 kWth at 600 K with launch stresses under 10% of yield (JBIS, Jul 2025; paywalled, unverified in review); ACT's SBIR Phase III work on Ti-H2O/graphite-fiber radiators added freeze-thaw tests and a 10-year lunar MMOD analysis (ICES, Jul 2026); titanium wick treatments studied (AIAA SciTech, Jan 2026). NASA reset the FSP procurement in Mar 2026; no provider is under contract.
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.why: At ~25-30% Brayton efficiency, 100 kWe means rejecting ~230-300 kWt; at an average radiating temperature near 450 K and ~3 kW/m2 net on the lunar surface (general), that is ~100 m2 and ~300 kg of panel at 3 kg/m2. The technology is on track without AI mathematics; qualification testing and program funding set the date.
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.strongest_case_small: The radiator is not the long pole of fission surface power; fuel, licensing and the lander are.
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.signpost: LR-1 provider award and PDR with radiator qualification test results, 2028-29.
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor: with the FSP procurement reset (Mar 2026) and no provider, a 2027-28 PDR is off the table; years 2029 -> 2030 and bands Medium -> Low in all scenarios; JBIS figure marked unverified (paywalled). Advocate: soft edge from struct-two-phase-microgravity-models.

struct-large-sail-flight.title: A 1,000 m2-class solar sail flies
struct-large-sail-flight.description: A solar sail of at least ~1,000 m2 (NASA's follow-on boom class targets up to 2,000 m2) flies, qualified substantially by validated deployment simulation plus subscale tests.
struct-large-sail-flight.status_oct2026: ACS3 flew ~80 m2 (2024); NASA states current composite booms support up to 500 m2 and follow-on booms up to 2,000 m2; no funded 1,000 m2-class flight mission identified (general).
struct-large-sail-flight.why: Better deployment models reduce the risk of scaling 10-25x in area, but the binding gate is a funded mission; sails compete for small science budgets. The math moves the risk, not the money.
struct-large-sail-flight.strongest_case_small: Sail scale-up is gated by funding and membrane durability, not modeling; meanwhile 70-75 m compute-satellite arrays (AI1's 70 m June wingspan; 75 m in the Aug 2026 revision) are flying anyway on the commercial track.
struct-large-sail-flight.signpost: NASA or another agency funds a 1,000 m2-plus sail mission by 2028.
struct-large-sail-flight.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: S3 2030 -> 2031 (no funded 1,000 m2 mission; appropriations compress 1.0x; a 2030 flight would need funding by ~2027, before the hard prerequisite exists). Advocate: soft edge from struct-highflux-radiator-flight (deployable supply base). Auditor: wingspan wording updated. Bands unchanged.

struct-reusable-life-management.title: Sensors and models track wear on reusable stages
struct-reusable-life-management.description: Fully reusable heavy launchers (Starship-class and peers) manage structural life with validated life models (data-driven or physics-based) and built-in sensors, sustaining fast turnaround without routine teardown inspection and with life limits set by analysis rather than fleet-leader experience alone.
struct-reusable-life-management.status_oct2026: Starship reached orbit on Sep 28 2026 with both stages expended at sea (33FG); booster and ship reuse at scale not yet operational; Falcon-class booster reuse relies on inspection and fleet-leader experience (general).
struct-reusable-life-management.why: Needs inspection credit (2030 in S2), data-cleared reflight from a probabilistic life twin (physclock-twin-reflight-clearance, S2 2030 after B-trunk), and flight cycles to build confidence (Mach33 base: 8.9 flights per stack in 2029, 18 in 2030). Physics-based damage closure (struct-damage-tolerance-physics) accelerates but does not gate: operators set life with data-driven models and fleet leaders first. Fleet experience accumulates only with flights, which no cognition compresses. S2 Low because it chains two Medium prerequisites and needs a public description of sensor-based inspection; S3 Medium.
struct-reusable-life-management.strongest_case_small: SpaceX may reach airline-like turnaround empirically, making the AI-math contribution unmeasurable; operators may never publish how they set life limits.
struct-reusable-life-management.signpost: A Starship booster or ship flies 10-plus times with publicly described sensor-based inspection between flights.
struct-reusable-life-management.calibration_note: A3: Follows struct-shm-inspection-credit (now S3 2030) plus flight hours to build confidence. S3 2030 -> 2031; bands unchanged. A4: Why text updated to match the A3 years and bands; it had still described the v0 values. A3's conditional sentence is kept.

struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.title: 100 kW-per-tonne compute satellites in serial production
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.description: Compute satellites at ~100 kW/t (versus AI1's ~70 kW/t design point and a Starlink V3-like ~11 kW/t) built at hundreds to thousands per year.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.status_oct2026: June AI1 spec target 70 kW/t (mass unpublished; ~2.1 t implied, ~71 kW/t on peak per 33FG). SpaceX's stated long-run goal is ~100 kW of compute per tonne (Feb 2026, press report). The Aug 2026 revision (250 kW peak / 175 kW average) and SpaceX's Sep 16 2026 FCC response (under 4,000 kg, under 200 m2 radiator, under 1,500 m2 solar) bound the next design at about 62 kW/t or more on peak; 33FG's Oct 6 reference case reaches ~4.5 t (~56 kW/t). kW/t fell as power rose. 33FG's StarThink V2 reference reaches ~100 kW/t with 2.5 kg/m2 radiators, improved solar and 370 K chips, and 33FG identifies solar areal density as the primary constraint.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.pathway: P7 (AI math second-order via P1 thermal and structural design and P5 chip-life evidence)
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.why: Solar is ~56% of AI1's reconstructed mass, so 100 kW/t depends first on array specific power (struct-light-solar-array-production, then thinner or higher-efficiency cells), then on how hot chips and HBM may run (struct-hot-chip-hbm-qualification), and only then on radiator areal density. From the ~55-62 kW/t of the Sep 2026 envelope, 100 kW/t in serial production by 2031 needs a ~60-80% gain within ~3 years of first flight, against a design trend that has run the other way; that is Low in S2. The AI-math contribution is design optimization of the thermal and structural share and faster accelerated-life evidence for hotter chips. In S3, yearly satellite generations and AI-run factories (1.2-1.3x) keep it Medium.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.strongest_case_small: The October design moved away from 100 kW/t; with cheap launch SpaceX may prefer bigger satellites at ~55-65 kW/t, and solar areal density and chip power density move kW/t more than thermal design.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.signpost: SpaceX discloses a Starmind version at or above 100 kW/t.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.calibration_note: A3: Follows struct-radiator-lightweight-production (now 2030 in S2/S3); serial production of 100 kW/t satellites needs those radiators plus lighter arrays in a production line. S2 2030 -> 2031, S3 2030 -> 2031; bands unchanged. A4: Why text updated to match the A3 years and bands; it had still described the v0 values. A3's conditional sentence is kept.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S2 Medium -> Low (filed envelope implies ~55-62 kW/t; trend runs away from 100). Auditor: S1 Low -> Speculative; new hard prerequisite struct-light-solar-array-production (array specific power is the primary constraint, 33FG). All three lenses: hard edge from struct-radiator-lightweight-production made soft. Soft edges added from materials-perovskite-primary-power (skeptic), physclock-satellite-gen-cadence and the hot-chip node (advocate). Auditor's S3 Medium -> Low not taken and advocate's S3 2031 -> 2030 rejected (see debates). Years unchanged.

struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.title: A 100 kWe fission reactor operating on the Moon
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.description: A fission surface power system delivering at least 100 kWe operates on the lunar surface (one-year demonstration followed by nine operational years in NASA's plan).
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.status_oct2026: Directive (Jul 31 2025): at least 100 kWe, closed Brayton, heavy lander up to 15 t, launch-ready Q1 FY2030, two awards within six months of the RFP. Draft partnership announcements Aug 29 and Dec 5 2025. On Mar 24 2026 NASA said Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be informed by Space Reactor-1 Freedom (Mars launch Dec 2028); on Mar 26 2026 it made the draft Funded Space Act Agreement posting inactive to reassess the development approach. No FSP/LR-1 provider award found as of Oct 2026. NASA-DOE MOU renewed (Jan 2026); a December 2025 executive order calls for a lunar surface reactor ready for launch by 2030.
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.why: Scenario-invariant on purpose: the binding gates are a heavy cargo lander able to land ~15 t (auton-lunar-heavy-cargo-landing, itself behind schedule), nuclear launch approval, HALEU fuel supply and nuclear ground testing. The Q1 FY2030 launch-ready target predates the Mar 2026 procurement reset; with no provider under contract and LR-1 now sequenced behind SR-1, a space reactor's 4-6 years from a funded start (physclock lag ladder) puts launch after 2031. AI mathematics does not move licensing, appropriations or lander schedules, and the first unit's design freezes before AI design tools mature.
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.strongest_case_small: This node is the clearest nil chain in the domain.
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.signpost: LR-1 procurement restart and provider award; SR-1 launch (Dec 2028 target); a heavy-lander cargo landing demonstration; ground test of the flight-design reactor.
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (verified: SAM.gov notice of Mar 26 2026 via bidpulsar; Wikipedia on LR-1/SR-1): status corrected (procurement reset, no provider); years 2031 -> >2031 and bands Low -> Speculative in all scenarios (no provider five years out; LR-1 behind SR-1). | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): hard prerequisite auton-lunar-heavy-cargo-landing added (B-moon-mars request: the node names a ~15 t lander as its gate); the soft edge from prop-hls-refuel-campaign removed as redundant (it is the lander node's hard prerequisite). Years and bands unchanged (>2031, Speculative).

struct-km-monolith.title: Kilometre-scale monolithic structure in orbit
struct-km-monolith.description: A single connected structure at least 1 km across (solar-radiator plane for GW compute, space solar power array or large antenna) deployed or assembled in orbit.
struct-km-monolith.status_oct2026: Starcloud's white paper (Sep 2024) sketches a 5 GW station with a ~4 km x 4 km array assembled modularly; Google Suncatcher (Nov 2025) instead flies 81 satellites within a 1 km radius at 100-200 m spacing; SpaceX said on Oct 6 2026 that Starmind needs ~10-satellite tight-formation clusters at ~10 Tbps; Chinese space-solar-power truss-assembly robotics is active (2026); Caltech's MAPLE beamed power in orbit (2023) with 50 m unit tiles planned.
struct-km-monolith.why: Formation flying is replacing structure: guidance, navigation and optical links give km-scale clusters without km-scale structures, so the business case for a monolith weakens even as modeling improves. Deployment physics (2030 in S2) and certification by analysis (2030) arrive too late to fly a funded km-scale structure by 2031.
struct-km-monolith.strongest_case_small: Even with perfect models, nobody is paying for a monolith when formation flying works; the most likely km-scale builder (Chinese space solar power) runs on its own schedule.
struct-km-monolith.signpost: A funded km-scale assembly demonstration (for example a Chinese space-solar-power milestone), or an orbital-compute operator abandoning formation flying for a monolith.

struct-design-cycle-compression.title: Structures and thermal analysis cycles 2-5x faster
struct-design-cycle-compression.description: Time from a requirement change to signed-off stress, loads and thermal analysis (not design-build-test) compresses 2-5x across the industry, cutting non-recurring engineering and allowing more design iterations per program.
struct-design-cycle-compression.status_oct2026: Agentic FEA is at research-prototype stage (2026); coupled-loads and thermal correlation cycles still take weeks (general).
struct-design-cycle-compression.why: Chain (S2): public applied math 2027 -> agentic FE workflows 2027 -> adoption at vertically integrated firms 2028, primes 6-12 months later -> industry-wide 2-5x 2029. The earliest and most certain effect in this domain. If structures and thermal analysis is ~10-20% of spacecraft non-recurring engineering (general) and agents cut its labor 50-80% (assumption), NRE falls ~5-15%; the larger benefit is more iterations per month, which compounds into lighter, better-margined designs. A 50-80% labor cut is a 2-5x speedup, and human sign-off time stays roughly constant, so turnaround compresses less than the 5-10x cognitive multiplier.
struct-design-cycle-compression.strongest_case_small: Program schedules are bound by hardware procurement and physical tests (thermal vacuum, vibration), not analysis; faster analysis can simply wait longer for the test chamber.
struct-design-cycle-compression.signpost: Primes or new-space firms report analysis cycle-time reductions, or stress-analyst hiring shifts toward review roles, by 2029.
struct-design-cycle-compression.revision_note: B-certification: [skeptic+auditor] Title now says analysis turnaround, not design cycles; capability-engineering-adoption moved from accelerated_by to a hard prerequisite ('across the industry'); S2 2028 -> 2029 (primes follow 6-12 months after vertically integrated firms). [auditor] 3-10x -> 2-5x to match the node's own 50-80% labor cut; tier-7 chain written out. Bands unchanged.

struct-structural-mass-step.title: 5-15% lighter structures on new vehicles and spacecraft
struct-structural-mass-step.description: Vehicles and spacecraft designed from ~2028 show 5-15% lower structural mass for equivalent loads, spacecraft first and launch-vehicle primary structure later. The gains come from knockdowns (buckling-critical barrels), certified margins (strength-critical members), tighter launch environments (secondary structure and boxes) and design optimization; they apply to different parts of dry mass, so they do not simply add.
struct-structural-mass-step.status_oct2026: No measurable trend attributable to AI mathematics (general).
struct-structural-mass-step.why: Chain (S2): first flown AI-sized structure 2031 -> several new designs disclosing comparable dry-mass fractions after 2031; an industry-wide trend cannot show up in the year of the first flight. Needs new designs started after the methods exist (2028-29) to finish qualification and fly; most fleets flying in 2031 were designed earlier. Vehicle-level effect is small: structure saved on an upper stage converts ~1:1 to payload, on a booster ~0.1-0.2:1 (general), so a 10% structural cut is a few percent of payload at most. AI-native spacecraft and AI design optimization accelerate the spacecraft side.
struct-structural-mass-step.strongest_case_small: Launch economics are set by propulsion, reuse and cost, not structural mass (Starship deliberately uses heavier, cheaper stainless steel); measured mass fractions will not separate AI effects from normal improvement.
struct-structural-mass-step.signpost: New vehicle or spacecraft reveals citing AI-derived design rules with disclosed dry-mass fractions.
struct-structural-mass-step.calibration_note: A3: Follows its prerequisite struct-flown-lighter-structure, now 2031 in S3. S3 2030 -> 2031; bands unchanged.
struct-structural-mass-step.revision_note: B-certification: [skeptic] S2 2031 -> >2031 (its hard prerequisite is the first flown article in S2 2031; a trend needs several programs); description notes the gains apply to disjoint parts of dry mass. [advocate] description puts spacecraft first; cap-design-optimization and capability-ai-native-spacecraft added as soft accelerators. Advocate's edge removal (flown-lighter-structure hard -> soft), S2/S3 Medium and S3 2030 rejected (see debates). Bands unchanged.

struct-gw-orbital-compute.title: 1 GW of compute operating in orbit
struct-gw-orbital-compute.description: Cumulative at least 1 GW of compute power in orbit, counted at nameplate (peak) rating: about 4,000 Starmind-class satellites at 250 kW peak (about 5,700 at the 175 kW average rating). At SpaceX's Sep 2026 filing envelope and 33FG's Oct reference (~4.0-4.5 t each, ~55-62 kW/t on peak) that is ~16,000-18,000 t, ~110-180 Starship flights at 100-150 t per flight (fewer tonnes per flight reach dawn-dusk orbit than the LEO reference; assumption), up to ~6 km2 of solar array, and ~0.7-1.3 km2 of radiator panel to reject ~1 GW of waste heat.
struct-gw-orbital-compute.status_oct2026: SpaceX filed for up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites (Jan 2026). Musk (Aug 25 2026) targeted first AI satellites in Q4 2027, 'significant scale' in 2028 and 1 GW in orbit by end-2027, then ~10x a year, and cautioned listeners to treat the projections skeptically. SpaceX's Sep 16 2026 FCC response bounds each satellite under 4,000 kg. Starcloud raised $170M (Mar 2026); Google's first Suncatcher prototype launched Oct 1 2026; Starship reached orbit Sep 28 2026. Mach33 places scaled orbital-compute deployment in the early 2030s. Orbital compute in Oct 2026 is at kilowatt scale (general).
struct-gw-orbital-compute.pathway: P7 (not AI-math-driven; AI math second-order via P1 thermal and reliability design)
struct-gw-orbital-compute.why: 1 GW at ~16,000-18,000 t is ~110-180 dedicated Starship flights plus up to ~6 km2 of solar array, many times Starlink's yearly array output (assumption). With first 100-kW-class flights in 2028 and paying operations in 2029, 1 GW by end-2031 needs ~1,600-2,300 four-tonne satellites a year for ~2.5 years, a large share of all Starship flights in 2029-31, shared with Starlink V3. Chain (S2): Starmind first flight 2028 (struct-highflux-radiator-flight; SpaceX target Q4 2027, slipped per the tree's 1.5-3x calibration) -> paying 100-kW-class operations 2029 (materials-cots-orbital-compute-ops) -> internal launch cost under ~$300/kg (physclock-cheap-mass-internal) and 100+ heavy flights a year (physclock-heavy-cadence-100) -> about 10 compute flights in one year around 2030 (trunk node capability-compute-launch-demand, Medium) -> ~110-180 flights cumulative by end-2031, which leaves no slack: Low in S2. Musk's own 1 GW-by-end-2027 target, stretched by the tree's 1.5-3x slip ratio, lands in 2029-31, and Mach33 places scaled deployment in the early 2030s. S3 keeps Medium because heavy cadence and compute demand arrive about a year earlier and the physical multiplier is 1.3-1.5x, not because of mathematics; S1 is later because a capability plateau weakens demand. AI math is second-order: AI radiator design saves ~350-1,400 t per GW (~2-9% of launched mass), hotter qualified chips ~1,900 t (struct-hot-chip-hbm-qualification), and right-sized radiation mitigation ~5-20% compute per watt (assumption). Catalog family 107 (matrix multiplication exponent at most 9/4, Lean, T3) is a galactic algorithm and contributes nothing (P4 nil). Launch cadence, satellite and array fabrication, and chip supply bind.
struct-gw-orbital-compute.strongest_case_small: Thermal physics (T^4, junction-temperature limits) is unchanged, and the timing is set by Starship cadence and financing; AI mathematics could vanish from the chain without moving this node by more than months.
struct-gw-orbital-compute.signpost: Starmind production rate and dedicated Starship flights per year; FCC authorization of a first Starmind tranche; SpaceX reporting deployed orbital compute in the hundreds of MW by 2030.
struct-gw-orbital-compute.calibration_note: A3: Follows struct-radiator-lightweight-production (now S3 2030). S3 2030 -> 2031; bands unchanged. (Note: 1 GW does not strictly need sub-2.5 kg/m2 radiators; the hard edge could be soft.) A4: Hard edge from struct-radiator-lightweight-production made soft. The why says sub-2.5 kg/m2 radiators save a few percent of launched mass (about 3-11 flights per GW), so 1 GW does not require them. Years stay >2031/2031/2031: launch cadence (100+ heavy flights a year, 2029 in S2), serial satellite production and capital bind, and S3's 1.3-1.5x physical multiplier does not fit 100-140 dedicated flights plus the satellite ramp into 2030. Bands Low/Medium/Medium kept.
struct-gw-orbital-compute.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: S2 Medium -> Low (revised mass ~16,000-18,000 t is 1.3-1.8x the old basis; first flight slips to 2028; zero slack), supported by the trunk resolver's note that 1 GW S2 Medium sat above capability-compute-launch-demand (10 compute flights in a year, S2 2030 Medium) and by Mach33's early-2030s scaled-deployment date. Advocate's S1 >2031 -> 2031, S2/S3 2031 -> 2030 and S3 Medium -> High rejected: their chain used heavy-cadence-100 at S2 2029 / S3 2028, which the trunk resolver moved to 2030 / 2029 (see debates). Auditor + advocate: pathway relabelled 'not AI-math-driven'; chain written out; mass basis and peak-versus-average definition fixed; family 107 nil note added. Auditor's cots-ops hard -> soft not applied: cots-ops is now the non-AI commercial milestone (its AI-math edge is soft), so the edge is a true physical precursor. Soft edges added: light solar arrays, hot-chip qualification, formation clusters, capability-ai-rnd-acceleration (trunk resolver proposal). Years unchanged; S1 Low and S3 Medium unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): soft edge from capability-compute-launch-demand (B-trunk and B-orbital-compute-power requests); kept soft, not hard, because 1 GW could in principle be lofted partly by non-Starship launchers.

verif-code-proof-agents.title: Agents that prove real flight code
verif-code-proof-agents.description: AI agents write contracts, loop invariants and proofs for production embedded code (C, Ada/SPARK, Rust) and discharge them in an existing checker (Frama-C, GNATprove, Verus, or Lean via extraction), at a marginal cost of compute hours instead of proof-engineer years.
verif-code-proof-agents.status_oct2026: Partly exists. Off-the-shelf LLMs produced verified code for 82% of Dafny, 44% of Verus and 27% of Lean specifications in the vericoding benchmark (Sep 2025). The best agent fully solved 27 of 43 repository-scale instances in Vero (Aug 2026), none of the hardest. AI coding agents wrote and verified a bare-metal Ada/SPARK security stack (classical and post-quantum crypto, TLS 1.3, IKEv2, X.509); GNATprove discharged 49,280 proof obligations at a claimed 20-40x lower supervision cost than hand verification, and the agents tried to bypass weak checks (Philipp, arXiv 2607.14340, Jul 2026 preprint). AdaCore released GNAT Foundry Intersection, an agent workflow gated by SPARK proof, requirements-based tests and MC/DC, described as a demonstration, not certification (Sep 14, 2026). OpenAI's pipeline formalized the main results of 162 papers in weeks (openai/math, Oct 6 2026; manuscripts dated Sep 10-Oct 6, formalization timing not separately reported; agent-written, review status unchecked, so T3 as evidence of the pipeline). No catalog family applies; the evidence is the pipeline itself.
verif-code-proof-agents.why: Formal methods in aerospace have been limited by proof labor, not tools: seL4 took about 25 person-years and roughly 27 lines of Isabelle per verified line of C. Proof writing is exactly what agents now do. The remaining gate is mature formal semantics for the target language: strong for SPARK and Frama-C C, weaker for C++ and for Rust in Lean. Under S2, with agent task horizons doubling every 6-9 months, repository-scale success moves from about 63% (Aug 2026) to routine during 2027. Under S1 public models get there by about 2028. 'Achieved' here means verifying a 10-50 KLOC real embedded codebase to functional-contract level with under 10% human proof effort.
verif-code-proof-agents.strongest_case_small: Benchmarks use clean specs and small repositories. Flight code is legacy C and C++ with hardware registers, interrupts, concurrency and undocumented assumptions, where proofs stall on modeling the environment rather than on proof search. A proof of an unreviewed spec adds little assurance.
verif-code-proof-agents.signpost: A tool vendor or agency (AdaCore, AbsInt, TrustInSoft, Galois, NASA, ESA) reports AI-generated SPARK or Frama-C proofs over more than 10 KLOC of real embedded code with human effort a small fraction of the seL4 ratio; Vero-class repository benchmarks pass 90%.
verif-code-proof-agents.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Advocate: Jul 2026 SPARK and Sep 2026 AdaCore evidence added to status. Auditor: 'in under four weeks' corrected (it describes manuscript dates). Skeptic's S1 2028 -> 2029 rejected: the Jul 2026 SPARK result already shows near-target human effort on new code with existing agents, which supports S1 2028. Years and bands unchanged.

verif-skolem-positivity.title: Skolem and Positivity problems settled
verif-skolem-positivity.description: Decide whether a linear recurrence ever hits zero (Skolem) or always stays positive (Positivity), both open in general. They are the exact mathematical core of asking whether a discrete-time linear loop, such as a sampled control law or estimator update, ever crosses a threshold.
verif-skolem-positivity.status_oct2026: Open. Skolem is decidable only up to order 4, and Positivity up to order 5 (Ouaknine-Worrell 2014); extending Positivity to order 6 would require major breakthroughs in Diophantine approximation of transcendental numbers. Some results are conditional on number-theoretic conjectures (general). Not in the openai/math catalog.
verif-skolem-positivity.why: Either a decision procedure or an undecidability proof would fix the ceiling for exact, unbounded verification of linear loops with rational coefficients, and would feed invariant generators and termination provers. It sits at the intersection of logic and number theory, where the Sep-Oct 2026 releases show progress, but the order-6 barrier is a known one, unlike unforced Navier-Stokes, so the S2 band is one below that node (Low). Bands reflect the chance an AI system settles it by 2031, not that it changes flight practice.
verif-skolem-positivity.strongest_case_small: Flight verification never needs exact unbounded decidability. Engineers prove sufficient conditions (Lyapunov functions, linear matrix inequalities, bounded horizons, interval margins) that are already decidable or cheap, and flown code runs in floating point, not exact rationals. Expect a P3 ceiling result with near-nil effect on tools.
verif-skolem-positivity.signpost: A lab, Hexagon or arXiv claim with a Lean statement deciding Skolem at order 5 or above, or Positivity at order 6 or above; verification-tool papers citing it within a year.
verif-skolem-positivity.revision_note: B-math-frontier: [skeptic+auditor] Signpost fixed: Positivity is already decidable up to order 5 (Ouaknine-Worrell, SODA 2014), so it would have fired on a known result; order 6 needs breakthroughs in Diophantine approximation, a known barrier, so S2 band Medium -> Low (S3 stays Medium). Unsupported status sentence removed. [skeptic] pathway P3->P6 -> P3 (tool effect near nil).

verif-game-solving-synthesis.title: Faster solvers for building correct-by-design controllers
verif-game-solving-synthesis.description: Family 104 claims quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games; its Lean part covers only a randomized algorithm for mean-payoff games. These games are the back end of reactive synthesis (building mode logic from temporal-logic specs) and of probabilistic model checking (fault management under random failures).
verif-game-solving-synthesis.status_oct2026: Family 104's Lean main result covers only a randomized quasipolynomial algorithm (success probability at least 7/8) for the zero-threshold winning set of finite mean-payoff games with signed binary weights, plus a counterexample to Truffet's elimination procedure (lean/docs/104.md); that part is T3, unchecked by outsiders. The stochastic-game and parity claims are manuscript-only (T1). Parity games have had quasipolynomial algorithms since 2017 (general). Practical solvers (strategy iteration, value iteration) already handle engineering-sized instances.
verif-game-solving-synthesis.premise_tier: T3 (randomized mean-payoff algorithm, Lean scope); T1 (stochastic games: conditional)
verif-game-solving-synthesis.why: Once independently checked (T4), the mean-payoff result resets the worst-case complexity map for quantitative synthesis; tool builders will cite it as a worst-case upper bound. The probabilistic model-checking implication rests on the stochastic-game part and is conditional (T1). Bands are one step below a checked result for that reason, in every scenario. The node is the result being established and known. Its effect on flight-verification practice is near nil: the 2017 quasipolynomial parity algorithms did not beat Zielonka-type solvers on benchmarks (van Dijk, TACAS 2018).
verif-game-solving-synthesis.strongest_case_small: Worst-case bounds do not govern practice. Real synthesis and model-checking problems are limited by state-space size and specification quality, and existing solvers rarely meet worst cases. No change to flight verification workflows is expected.
verif-game-solving-synthesis.signpost: An independent Comparator run on family 104 via Hexagon; any implementation that beats strategy iteration on standard probabilistic model-checking benchmarks.
verif-game-solving-synthesis.revision_note: B-math-frontier: [auditor] 104 statement gap (lean/docs/104.md, checked): Lean covers only a randomized quasipolynomial algorithm for mean-payoff games plus a Truffet counterexample; stochastic and parity claims are manuscript-only (T1). Bands High -> Medium in every scenario (the engineering link runs through stochastic games, conditional). [skeptic] pathway P3 -> P4 (an algorithm is an upper bound, not a ceiling); wording fixed.

verif-spec-engineering.title: AI-drafted formal specifications
verif-spec-engineering.description: AI turns natural-language requirements, interface control documents and concepts of operations into formal, machine-checkable specifications (contracts, temporal logic, unit-typed interfaces). It checks them for consistency and realizability and flags hidden environmental assumptions for human sign-off.
verif-spec-engineering.status_oct2026: NASA's FRET turns structured English into temporal logic and, through Ogma and Copilot, into runtime monitors that flew in NASA's ICAROUS autonomy framework. Research pipelines (Forge, Jun 2026) close the loop from LLM-written code to Dafny, CSP and Isabelle checks. Spec writing remains scarce senior-engineer work, and no space program publicly uses AI-drafted formal specs for flight-critical functions.
verif-spec-engineering.why: Once proofs are cheap, specs become the bottleneck: a proof of the wrong property is worthless (tr-position-2). In all 9 software-related losses and near-losses in our failure table, the missing piece was an assumption, interface spec or process step, not proof capacity. AI cuts spec drafting and consistency checking several-fold (general). Each spec still needs a qualified engineer to accept that it says what the mission needs, so human review bandwidth binds. 'Achieved' means first use on a flight program for a safety-critical function; it does not imply the spec-review bandwidth that fleet-wide invariants (verif-constellation-verified-updates) or $5-20-per-line costs (verif-assurance-cost-collapse) assume, and those nodes carry that risk in their own bands.
verif-spec-engineering.strongest_case_small: AI drafts may encode the same wrong assumptions the team already holds and give them false authority by making them formal. For domain experts who are not fluent in temporal logic, reviewing a formal spec is not much faster than writing one.
verif-spec-engineering.signpost: NASA, ESA or a lander company publishes a case study of LLM-drafted FRET or contract specs accepted at a flight review; a certification-authority position paper on AI-authored low-level requirements.
verif-spec-engineering.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic: clarified that 'achieved' is first flight-program use, not review bandwidth at fleet scale. Auditor: 'losses' -> 'losses and near-losses'. Auditor's S1 High -> Medium rejected: the node is P1->P2 (P1 default High), and a single flight-program use by 2031 does not need certification or public models beyond the 2028 S1 release. Years and bands unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): lettered citation 'analyst position h' replaced with the KB position id tr-position-2. soft edge from frontier-applied-posing (B-math-frontier request 5).

verif-verified-gnc-numerics.title: Guidance code with proven floating-point math
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.description: Machine-checked bounds on round-off, overflow and conversion errors for guidance, navigation, control and estimation code, generated per module by agents. The tools are Astree, PRECiSA with Frama-C, or Lean FloatLib-class libraries. The result is that a proof about real-number math also holds for the code that flies.
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.status_oct2026: Solved in principle and expert-scarce. Astree proved absence of runtime errors in 132 KLOC of A340 primary flight-control code in 1 h 20 min (2003). NASA verified the floating-point C of the DAIDALUS detect-and-avoid well-clear module with PVS, PRECiSA and Frama-C, including round-off bounds and overflow freedom (2023). In Lean, FloatLib (Sep 2026) unifies IEEE binary and decimal formats, posits and P3109 with proofs; FloatSpec is a port of Flocq in progress.
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.why: Ariane 501 was lost to an unprotected 64-bit float to 16-bit integer conversion. Runtime-error analysis of that class is automatic today, and per-module round-off proofs in the DAIDALUS style become a compute job once agents write the annotations. The coverage gate is verified libraries for linear algebra, quaternion kinematics and filters with floating-point semantics.
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.strongest_case_small: Runtime-error freedom is already cheap with Astree-class tools, and numerical round-off rarely kills missions. The Ariane case needed the right input ranges, which is an assumption problem, not a proof problem.
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.signpost: A Lean or Coq library with a verified floating-point Kalman filter or quaternion propagator; NASA or ESA GNC teams publishing agent-generated round-off proofs on flight code.

revisions.from: Proven floating-point GNC code

verif-closed-loop-guarantees.title: Machine-checked stability for guidance and control
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.description: Proofs that a guidance, control and estimation loop stays inside a safe envelope, including actuator saturation, sampling, delay, sensor gating and mode switches. The proofs use barrier certificates, Lyapunov functions, reachability or differential dynamic logic, and are produced on request rather than by rare specialists.
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.status_oct2026: Tools exist: differential dynamic logic (KeYmaera X), sum-of-squares barrier certificates, reachability analyzers. They have been applied to aircraft collision avoidance (general). Building certificates for saturated, sampled, mode-switching loops is expert-scarce, and nonlinear hybrid verification at full-vehicle scale is partly open. Lean building blocks appeared in 2026: lyapunov-odes-lean (Zenodo, May 31 2026) and Doll and Shames' Lyapunov stability for hybrid systems plus the small-gain theorem in Lean (arXiv 2607.19727, Jul 2026). No catalog family applies (family 143, uniform limit-cycle bounds for Hilbert's sixteenth problem, Lean-formalized and unaudited, is theory-only context, not a premise).
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.why: This is the bespoke math, easier than the catalog's, that tl-position-4 says matters most: a stability or keep-out proof for one control law. Under S2, research-grade applied math is on tap from 2027, and existing provers (KeYmaera X differential dynamic logic, sum-of-squares barrier certificates) with agent-written proofs are a mature route that does not wait for Lean/Mathlib coverage of ODEs and hybrid systems. These certificates are over real numbers; the floating-point gap is closed separately by verif-verified-gnc-numerics or by runtime monitors, so neither the Lean library nor the floating-point node gates this one. 'Achieved' means a machine-checked stability or safety certificate for a flight-representative GNC loop (the flight control law with saturation, sampling delay and mode logic), published or delivered to a program; flight use is tracked in verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight and verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.strongest_case_small: Most flown GNC is close to linear, with well-understood classical margins checked by Monte Carlo. Flight losses trace to sensor logic and assumptions more than to unstable control laws. Proofs over idealized dynamics may not survive unmodeled flexible modes, propellant slosh or plume effects.
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.signpost: An agent-produced, machine-checked barrier certificate for powered-descent or rendezvous guidance published with flight-like dynamics (saturation, delay, slosh).
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: All three lenses: family 143 removed from catalog_families (the node itself says it does not reach this workflow; it would draw a false 'family 143 unlocks GNC stability' edge); premise_tier -> n/a; 'achieved' no longer requires a flown loop (a tier-5 outcome). Skeptic + advocate: infra-mathlib-applied hard -> soft; advocate + auditor: verif-verified-gnc-numerics hard -> soft. Advocate: S2 2028 -> 2027 accepted, because the skeptic's reason to keep 2028 (the numerics edge) is gone and the KeYmaera X/SOS route is mature (mechanism in the verification domain's table; 2026 Lean Lyapunov work checked by the auditor). Downstream nodes do not move. S1 and bands unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): lettered citation 'analyst position (a' replaced with the KB position id tl-position-4.

verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.title: Certified onboard trajectory optimizers
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.description: Embedded SOCP/QP solvers for powered-descent guidance, rendezvous MPC and collision avoidance with machine-checked proofs that, in the flight processor's floating-point arithmetic, they terminate within a fixed iteration budget and return an epsilon-feasible, epsilon-optimal solution or a certified infeasibility flag for every admissible state, paired with cheap runtime certificates (duality gaps) checked each control cycle. One reusable certified component for landers, docking systems and collision-avoidance planners.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.status_oct2026: Onboard convex guidance (lossless convexification) has flight-test heritage on rocket test beds (general). Proofs that a specific solver implementation converges within a fixed iteration and timing budget are rare. Runtime duality-gap certificates are cheap but seldom used as safety evidence. Code-level formal verification of an interior-point algorithm for linear model predictive control has existed since 2018 (Davy, Feron, Garoche and Henrion, arXiv 1801.03833; Cohen's 2018 ENAC PhD continued the line) and was not adopted in flight, which suggests demand, not cognition, has bound.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.why: Crewed landing and propellant transfer increasingly rely on onboard optimization. Certifying it needs both math (convergence and feasibility for every admissible state) and timing evidence on the flight processor. The math compresses under S2; timing characterization on radiation-tolerant processors and HIL qualification bind. Solver termination and epsilon-feasibility are properties of the convex program and the solver, not of closed-loop stability, and feasibility over the admissible set comes from astro-scp-guarantees; a generic SOCP or QP solver needs no astrodynamics library, so closed-loop guarantees and the formal astrodynamics library accelerate rather than gate this node.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.strongest_case_small: Programs can avoid certifying the optimizer by wrapping it in runtime assurance with a simple backup guidance law, which is cheaper and already accepted practice.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.signpost: A lander or HLS provider describing certified onboard optimization in an AIAA GNC paper or design review; verified convex-solver code with worst-case execution time bounds.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.merge_note: A1: merged astro-verified-onboard-solver (same achievement: a proven onboard convex solver). verif had rated it 2031/2029/2028 Low/Medium/Medium with a qualification gate because it bundled timing evidence on radiation-tolerant processors and HIL; astro rated it 2030/2028/2027 Medium/High/High as a formalization milestone. Reconciled by scoping this node to the proofs plus runtime certificates (all hard prerequisites, including infra-verified-numerics and verif-verified-gnc-numerics, land by S2 2028), and leaving flight timing/HIL qualification to verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight and verif-hls-autonomy-certification. Astro's caution kept: a Jun 2026 audit found compilation-based metrics overstate numerical-analysis formalization quality (arXiv 2606.14000).
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic: verif-closed-loop-guarantees and astro-formal-astrodynamics-library moved from hard to soft (solver properties need neither); 2018 interior-point verification precedent added to status (checked: arXiv 1801.03833 is code-level IPM verification for linear MPC; the skeptic's 'SOCP with floating-point analysis' wording is not in the abstract, so it is not repeated). Years and bands unchanged (verified numerics still holds S2 2028).

verif-nn-verification-scale.title: Verifying neural perception at flight scale
verif-nn-verification-scale.description: Proving robustness and correctness properties, over the operational domain, of neural networks used for terrain-relative navigation, hazard detection or pose estimation. This is genuinely open: exact verification is NP-hard, and 'correct perception' resists formal specification.
verif-nn-verification-scale.status_oct2026: VNN-COMP 2025 (8 teams, 16 regular and 9 extended benchmarks) shows steady progress on small and medium networks. Flight-scale vision networks and perception properties remain out of reach. SAE ARP6983 / EUROCAE ED-324 (joint G-34/WG-114; the first issue covers supervised offline machine learning; ED-324 publication scheduled Q4 2026; ARP6983's June 2026 target status unconfirmed as of Oct 2026) and EASA NPA 2025-07 base machine-learning assurance on data and process, not proof. No catalog family addresses it.
verif-nn-verification-scale.why: Exact verification of ReLU networks is NP-hard (general), and the property itself ('detects every hazardous crater') is defined by data, not by math. New relaxations and verification-friendly architectures from on-demand research math could move the frontier, but the gap in specification remains even in S3, which is why the band stays Low.
verif-nn-verification-scale.strongest_case_small: Space programs do not need to verify the network. They wrap it in runtime assurance or use it only for advisory functions, so this open problem may simply be routed around.
verif-nn-verification-scale.signpost: VNN-COMP results on networks at terrain-relative-navigation scale; ED-324/ARP6983 or EASA guidance granting credit for formal robustness proofs of neural networks.
verif-nn-verification-scale.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Auditor: ARP6983 June 2026 target marked unconfirmed (date has passed; only the ED-324 Q4 2026 schedule is confirmed). Years and bands unchanged.

verif-environment-assumption-models.title: Validated sensor and terrain envelopes
verif-environment-assumption-models.description: Formally stated, test-validated envelopes for what sensors and environments can do during critical phases: laser rangefinder and altimeter dropouts and reflectivity, IMU saturation durations, terrain discontinuities, lighting. Proofs can assume them and simulators can sample them.
verif-environment-assumption-models.status_oct2026: Ad hoc. Recent lunar losses trace to sensor and environment surprises: Hakuto-R M1's 3 km crater rim (2023), Resilience's late rangefinder readings (2025), Athena's altimeter interference, low-sun lighting and crater appearance mismatch (Mar 2025), and earlier Schiaparelli's 1 s IMU saturation (2016). LRO maps and flight telemetry exist but are not packaged as formal assumptions.
verif-environment-assumption-models.why: Proofs and tests are conditional on environment assumptions. AI can quickly fuse orbital maps, test data and telemetry into formal envelopes, but the envelopes are only as good as sensor characterization tests and the few landings that produce truth data. S3's autonomous labs speed sensor testing on the ground, not the supply of lunar truth data, which is why even S3 stays Medium. The achievement is packaging test and telemetry data into validated envelopes that change modeling practice (model confidence, P5), not new theory becoming tools, and Medium is the P5 default. It now gates verif-mission-loss-rate and accelerates assumption falsification and lander flight, so the interactive tree shows the assumption gate that the failure table says binds; AI-run test stands and autonomous labs accelerate the ground characterization.
verif-environment-assumption-models.strongest_case_small: Each new site, sensor and lighting condition differs, so envelopes generalize poorly and teams will still discover new failure physics in flight.
verif-environment-assumption-models.signpost: A shared, formally stated lunar-descent sensor and terrain envelope dataset (for example from NASA CLPS or ESA) adopted by two or more lander teams.
verif-environment-assumption-models.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Auditor: pathway P1->P6 -> P1->P5. Skeptic: orphan fixed (hard edge to verif-mission-loss-rate; soft edges to verif-assumption-falsification and verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight). Advocate: soft edges from physclock-ai-run-test-stands and cap-autonomous-labs accepted; advocate's S3 band Medium -> High rejected, because lunar truth data and shared adoption by two lander teams do not speed up with cognition (the node's own reasoning, unchanged by the advocate's evidence). Years and bands unchanged.

verif-assumption-falsification.title: AI red-teaming of flight assumptions
verif-assumption-falsification.description: Agents search physics-based simulations and data for scenarios that break the assumptions under which flight software was proven or tested: terrain steps, saturation longer than designed, sensor delays, reboot timing, unit mismatches. Each finding becomes a test or a strengthened spec.
verif-assumption-falsification.status_oct2026: Monte Carlo dispersion campaigns and temporal-logic falsification tools exist (general). Hakuto-R M1's late landing-site change was not simulated against crater-rim terrain, and Schiaparelli's fault logic did not cover an IMU saturation lasting about 1 s.
verif-assumption-falsification.why: Counterexamples act fastest (fc-position-1): a found scenario changes the design within weeks. Agents can rerun targeted searches over terrain, sensor timing and fault combinations every time the design or landing site changes, which is exactly where Hakuto-R M1, Schiaparelli and Ariane 501 escaped. The gate is the fidelity of simulators and sensor models. Simulation-based falsification and Monte Carlo search run against existing requirements and need public research-grade models (P1), not AI-drafted specs adopted on a flight program, so spec engineering accelerates rather than gates it; validated environment envelopes widen what the simulator can represent.
verif-assumption-falsification.strongest_case_small: AI can only find failures the simulator can represent; Athena's and Resilience's sensor physics would not have appeared in typical simulations. Mature teams already run large dispersion campaigns.
verif-assumption-falsification.signpost: A lander team attributing a design change to AI-found falsifying scenarios; NASA CLPS asking for assumption-falsification reports at mission readiness reviews.
verif-assumption-falsification.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Auditor: hard edge from verif-spec-engineering made soft (falsification runs against existing requirements); hard edge from cap-research-math-public added so the P1 node keeps a capability gate (2028/2027/2027, equal to this node's years). Skeptic: soft edge from verif-environment-assumption-models. Years and bands unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): lettered citation 'analyst position c' replaced with the KB position id fc-position-1.

verif-fdir-model-checking.title: Exhaustive checks of fault logic and configuration
verif-fdir-model-checking.description: Agents build formal models of fault detection, isolation and recovery logic, mode machines, reboot and timing behavior, command sequences and parameter tables from code and interface documents. They then model-check them exhaustively, including emergency in-flight patches.
verif-fdir-model-checking.status_oct2026: Model checkers (SPIN, NuSMV, Kind 2) are mature; building faithful models is the cost. Failures and near-failures in this class: Starliner OFT (mission timer 11 h off, service-module valve-mapping error, 2019), Beresheet (a command to restart one IMU blocked the other IMU's data and set off a chain that shut down the main engine, 2019), Hitomi (wrongly updated thruster parameter, 2016), IM-1 (rangefinder safety switch left enabled; the in-flight patch missed a data-valid flag, per IM's CTO via SpacePolicyOnline, 2024).
verif-fdir-model-checking.why: Four of the nine software-related losses and near-losses in our failure table sit in this class. Agents can extract models from code and interface documents and check every fault combination and command sequence; this needs model extraction and model checking, not deductive code proofs, so verif-code-proof-agents accelerates rather than gates it. Agents can also check emergency patches within hours; IM-1's patch was written and uploaded mid-mission. The binding input is accurate hardware behavior (bus blocking, timer sources), which needs characterization data. Used as an engineering tool without certification credit, it travels P1 into P2, which is why S1 can be High.
verif-fdir-model-checking.strongest_case_small: Starliner's errors were also catchable by the end-to-end integrated test the program did not run (general). The root problem was process discipline, which cheap tools do not guarantee.
verif-fdir-model-checking.signpost: A CLPS or commercial-crew post-flight review crediting model checking with catching a fault-logic error before flight; NASA or ESA tools that automatically extract FDIR models from flight code.
verif-fdir-model-checking.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Auditor: 'losses' -> 'losses and near-losses'; pathway P2 -> P1->P2 (tool use without certification, which justifies S1 High); IM-1 data-valid flag re-cited to SpacePolicyOnline; Beresheet 'reboot loop' and Starliner 'skipped end-to-end test' were not in the cited articles, so the first is softened and the second marked general. Skeptic: verif-code-proof-agents moved from hard to soft (model extraction plus model checking needs no deductive code proofs). Years and bands unchanged.

verif-runtime-assurance.title: Proven safety wrappers for unverifiable autonomy
verif-runtime-assurance.description: Instead of verifying a neural or learned controller, verify a small monitor, a recoverable-set (barrier) condition and a simple backup controller, and switch to the backup before safety is lost (the Simplex architecture). Agents make the proofs of the wrapper and the switching logic cheap.
verif-runtime-assurance.status_oct2026: ASTM F3269 and NASA guidance define runtime assurance. Monitors generated by FRET and Copilot flew in NASA's ICAROUS, and R2U2 targets rovers and small satellites. Spacecraft use is mostly research. The expensive parts are proving the recoverable set and the switching logic.
verif-runtime-assurance.why: Neural and learned components (hazard detection, terrain-relative navigation) cannot be verified directly (see verif-nn-verification-scale), so assurance moves to a small, provable monitor and a simple backup. Agents make the barrier-certificate and switching proofs cheap. The binding gate is showing, on hardware-in-the-loop rigs and in flight, that the backup really recovers.
verif-runtime-assurance.strongest_case_small: Conservative wrappers trigger too often and erode the performance that justified the learned component, and a proven wrapper built on a wrong recoverable-set model is still unsafe.
verif-runtime-assurance.signpost: A lunar lander or rendezvous mission flying a learned component inside a proven Simplex wrapper; runtime assurance referenced in ED-324/ARP6983 or NASA guidance as a certification path.

verif-verified-onboard-stack.title: Formally verified onboard software stack
verif-verified-onboard-stack.description: Formally verified onboard software components fly on ordinary (non-research) missions: an seL4-class separation kernel or hypervisor, a telecommand parser, or software-update authentication; the first operational flight of any one of them counts. Spatial isolation is proven. Timing isolation on multicore processors is measured, not proven, so flight software and onboard AI payloads sharing one multicore processor also needs accepted interference evidence (AC 20-193-style analysis plus measurement).
verif-verified-onboard-stack.status_oct2026: seL4: 8,700 lines of C, 200,000 lines of Isabelle proof, about 25 person-years (estimated under 10 if redone), with 160 bugs found (144 during C verification). ECSS-E-ST-40C Rev.1 and ECSS-Q-ST-80C Rev.2 (Apr 2025) added explicit security requirements. Verified kernels remain niche in space. seL4 has been open source since 2014 and flew on the UNSW-EC0 CubeSat (QB50, 2017, general). MIT Lincoln Laboratory's port of NASA's core Flight System to seL4 took more than a year, mostly building OS services beyond the kernel rather than proofs (NDSS SpaceSec paper).
verif-verified-onboard-stack.why: Kernel proof cost is sunk: seL4 is open source and has flown. The binding costs are OS services, platform ports and drivers for radiation-tolerant processors, qualification, and multicore timing interference on HPSC-class processors, which is measured, not proven. Agent proofs mainly cut the cost of mission-specific telecommand parsers, update authentication and re-verification on new platforms: at seL4's ratio a verified 10 KLOC stack costs roughly $2-5M of proof labor (seL4: about 25 person-years including design and implementation, under 10 if redone), which becomes a compute bill plus spec review. Parsers and update authentication can be uploaded to buses already in orbit; separation kernels need a new bus. Chain (S2): proof agents 2027 -> verified parser and update-authentication stack 2028 -> integration or upload and qualification 12-18 months -> operational flight 2029 (A3 lag ladder). S3 equals S2 through 2028, so S3 is 2029. S2 is Medium, like every comparable tier-5 'flies' node, because adoption and qualification, not proof labor, have kept verified kernels niche.
verif-verified-onboard-stack.strongest_case_small: Isolation proofs assume correct hardware. Multicore timing interference, radiation upsets and processor errata are measured, not proven, and those qualification campaigns stay physical. seL4 is already the target of defense air programs (DARPA PROVERS/INSPECTA, Collins), yet it is niche in space: platform support on radiation-tolerant processors and qualification, not proof labor, bind.
verif-verified-onboard-stack.signpost: A constellation or lander operator announcing a verified kernel or hypervisor in flight; ESA or a defense constellation program requiring formally verified telecommand parsing.
verif-verified-onboard-stack.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder and cross-domain parity. Read as flown on ordinary missions (tier 5); its only prerequisite verif-code-proof-agents is 2027 in S2/S3, so a smallsat-class flight is 2028-29 at the earliest, and every comparable "proof-carrying flight software flies" node (verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight, astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight, comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo, auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight) is S2 2029. Chain (S2): proof agents 2027 -> verified kernel and command stack 2028 -> integration 12-18 months -> flight 2029. S1 2029 -> 2030, S2 2028 -> 2029, S3 2027 -> 2028.
verif-verified-onboard-stack.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic + auditor: S2 band High -> Medium and S3 2028 -> 2029 (kernel proofs are sunk and free; OS services, ports and qualification bind; S3 equals S2 until 2028); auditor: S1 Medium -> Low; skeptic: '$5M' -> '$2-5M'. Advocate's S2 2029 -> 2028 rejected (two lenses opposite; A3 lag ladder), but its scope point is adopted: the first operational flight of any one component counts, and parsers or update authentication can be uploaded to existing buses. Skeptic's proposed new node verif-multicore-timing-evidence not added: it is not necessary for this node as scoped, A1 already left timing and HIL evidence to the flight nodes, and its 2026 flight-qualification evidence could not be checked (source returned 403); the gate is stated in the description and why instead.

verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.title: A lander flies proof-checked descent guidance and fault logic
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.description: A lunar lander flies terminal-descent GNC whose key properties are machine-checked, not only Monte Carlo-tested: altitude plausibility, measurement-rejection gates, engine-cutoff and reboot logic and the guidance law, plus, if the guidance uses an onboard optimizer, its convergence, feasibility and solver numerics. Its assumptions are red-teamed against terrain and sensor models.
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.status_oct2026: Commercial and agency landers 2016-2025: Schiaparelli (IMU-saturation logic), Beresheet (command-triggered reboot loop), Hakuto-R M1 (filter rejected valid altimetry after a crater rim), IM-1 (configuration and patch flag), Peregrine (helium valve), Resilience (rangefinder), Athena (altimeter, lighting, tipped over). No lander has publicly flown formally verified descent logic (general). Agency losses with logic or GNC causes also belong in this record: Chandrayaan-2's Vikram (2019, deviation during the braking phase) and Luna-25 (Aug 2023, engine failed to cut off on time after a control-unit fault) (general). Successes in the same period include Chandrayaan-3 (2023), SLIM (2024, landed on its nose) and Blue Ghost M1 (Mar 2025) (general).
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.why: New-entrant landers face no certifying regulator for mission software and have repeatedly lost missions to logic errors (Beresheet, Hakuto-R M1), so the incentive is strong. Chain (S2): research-grade applied math public 2027 -> verified numerics and fault-logic checks 2027-28 -> GNC toolchain adopted 2028 -> software freeze 12-18 months before flight -> first flight 2029-30 on a CLPS-class lander. Launch slots are not scarce (up to 30 CLPS landings planned from 2027); the development cycle, the freeze and one team's adoption decision bind, not cognition. S3 equals S2 through 2028, so a flown article cannot beat S2's 2029 in S3. Many CLPS-class landers fly closed-form or Apollo-derived guidance with no onboard solver, so optimizer certificates and SCP guarantees accelerate rather than gate this node. Bands: S2 Medium, because several landers fly each year from 2029 but a team must adopt and say so; S3 High, because cognitive work is near-free from 2029 and two flight years remain. No regulator is involved for commercial lunar landers, so there is no Medium cap.
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.strongest_case_small: Half of recent lander losses were hardware or sensor physics (Peregrine's valve, Resilience's rangefinder, Athena's altimeter and lighting), which proofs do not touch. Teams may also adopt quietly and never disclose.
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.signpost: A CLPS or private lander team publicly stating formal verification of descent GNC and fault management in a readiness review or press kit. Precursor (does not count, since it has no launch gate): a terrestrial vertical-landing testbed flying the same proof-checked logic.
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.merge_note: A1: merged astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight (same milestone: first flight of proof-checked descent software; astro 2031/2029/2028 Low/Medium/High, verif 2030/2029/2028 Medium/High/High). Kept the verif id and its failure record (Schiaparelli, Beresheet, Hakuto-R M1, IM-1, Athena). The merged node now requires both guidance-solver proofs (verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates, astro-certified-gnc-toolchain, astro-scp-guarantees) and fault-logic checks, so bands take the stricter astro view. Full chain (S2): research-grade applied math public 2027 -> verified numerics and solver proofs 2028 -> GNC toolchain adopted 2028 -> software freeze 12-18 months before flight -> first flight 2029-30 on a CLPS-class lander or terrestrial testbed; launch cadence and software freeze bind, not cognition. No regulator is involved for commercial lunar landers, so no Medium cap.
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic + auditor: S3 2028 -> 2029 (a 2028 flight freezes software in 2026-27, when S3 equals S2). Skeptic: binding gate launch -> adoption (launch slots are not scarce); astro-scp-guarantees and verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates made soft (closed-form guidance needs no solver proofs); terrestrial-testbed clause moved to the signpost as a precursor; solver proofs made conditional. Skeptic's S3 High -> Medium rejected and advocate's S2 Medium -> High rejected: with the conjunction relaxed and the testbed path removed, Medium in the base case and High in the recursive case keep a meaningful spread (the advocate's high-cadence argument holds only once cognitive work is near-free, i.e. in S3). Auditor: Luna-25, Chandrayaan-2 and the success denominator added (general).

verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.title: Assured autonomous docking, servicing and propellant transfer
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.description: Rendezvous, proximity operations, docking, servicing or debris capture, and ship-to-ship propellant transfer flown with machine-checked passive safety (collision-free under failures), keep-out zones, abort reachability and capture logic, plus runtime assurance on the guidance, used as primary safety evidence.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.status_oct2026: Starship reached orbit on Flight 14 (Sep 28 2026) and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Ship-to-ship propellant transfer has not yet been demonstrated: SpaceX's leaked Nov 2025 HLS schedule targeted June 2026, which slipped, and NASA Administrator Isaacman expected the demonstration in very early 2027, maybe at the end of 2026 (The Space Review, Sep 28 2026); a secondary listing giving Q4 2026 is unconfirmed. Artemis III was reprofiled to a crewed low-Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test with HLS pathfinders from both SpaceX and Blue Origin (readiness no earlier than mid-2027). A landing needs about 15 tanker flights (Spaceflight Now, Jul 2026).
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.why: Each lunar landing chains many autonomous rendezvous and transfers. Proven passive safety and abort logic lower the risk per operation and the test burden per software change. But confidence is gated by flight demonstrations, not by proof capacity, and launch cadence does not compress with cognition. Chain (S2): verif-closed-loop-guarantees 2027; astro-hybrid-rpo-verification, verif-runtime-assurance and astro-certified-gnc-toolchain 2028 -> proofs added as late verification evidence to an already-contracted servicing or inspection mission (contract to launch 2-4 years; software freeze 12-18 months) or to Starship transfer-flight software, which changes between flights -> first flight using them as primary safety evidence, accepted in an operator or NASA safety review, 2029-30. S3: identical through 2028 -> 2029. S1: prerequisites 2030 -> 2031 at the earliest. Starship transfer flights in 2027 fly baselines set before the toolchain exists.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.strongest_case_small: SpaceX builds confidence through flight count; formal proofs may stay internal and invisible. Docking risk is dominated by hardware: mechanisms and cryogenic-transfer physics.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.signpost: Artemis III (late 2027) safety documentation citing formal verification of rendezvous abort logic; the first successful ship-to-ship propellant transfer.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.merge_note: A1: merged astro-verified-rpo-servicing (same achievement for a different customer: servicing/inspection/debris capture vs Starship/HLS transfer; astro >2031/2030/2029, verif 2031/2029/2029, both Low/Medium/Medium). Kept the verif id and its years for the first-of-kind flight of either type. Added astro's prerequisites (astro-hybrid-rpo-verification, astro-certified-gnc-toolchain) and sourcing: commercial servicing demos and ESA CREAM are under way, none uses formal proofs as primary safety evidence; missions take 2-4 years from contract to launch. Confidence is gated by flight demonstrations and launch cadence, not proof capacity.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic + auditor (grounding rule): full tier-5 chain written. Auditor: status corrected ('15-17 flights' was not in the cited article; about 15 tankers per Spaceflight Now; the Q4 2026 date is unconfirmed; Isaacman's 'very early 2027' added from The Space Review, Sep 28 2026; both landers' pathfinders named). Skeptic's S2 2029 -> 2030 and S1 2031 -> >2031 rejected: Starship transfer software changes between flights, so the 12-18-month freeze does not bind every route, and the auditor's chain gives 2029-30 with 2029 as earliest. Advocate's S3 2029 -> 2028 and S3 High rejected: S3 equals S2 through 2028, and the node's own strongest case (proofs may stay internal; hardware dominates docking risk) does not move with cognition. Advocate's soft edge from prop-hls-refuel-campaign accepted. Years and bands unchanged.

verif-constellation-verified-updates.title: Proof-checked software updates across constellations
verif-constellation-verified-updates.description: Each over-the-air update to thousands of satellites is gated by automatic re-proof of key invariants: collision-avoidance decision logic, safe-mode entry, deorbit command and decision logic, command authentication. Proofs re-run in hours, enabling weekly verified releases. A proof covers the command and logic path, not physical deorbit capability such as propulsion health.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.status_oct2026: Starlink satellites made 207,152 avoidance maneuvers from Dec 2025 to May 2026 (more than 355,000 a year); they maneuver autonomously (general; the cited report gives counts, not where decisions are made). Update practices are proprietary, and the FCC requires maneuver reports, not software assurance.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.why: At this volume of onboard decisions, a logic regression in collision-avoidance or safe-mode code is a fleet-wide risk. Once the specs exist, re-proving a fixed set of invariants on every update is a compute job, with no regulator in the loop. The largest operator merged with a frontier AI lab (SpaceX acquired xAI, Feb 2026), so model access, ITAR handling and the update pipeline sit inside one firm, the vertical-integration path the capability domain names as the shortest from AI math to flown hardware. This node is a fleet-wide, strictly stronger instance of astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops, so it is dated and banded no earlier or higher than that node. Chain (S2): proof agents, spec drafting and FDIR model checking 2027 -> operator writes reviewed invariant specs and proof-gated release pipeline 2028 -> first publicly disclosed fleet-wide proof-gated release 2029. Every invariant needs a reviewed spec, which is the bandwidth this branch says binds, and operators disclose little, so S2 is Medium. S3 equals S2 through 2028; it is High only because cognitive work is near-free from 2029.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.strongest_case_small: Operators already manage risk with staged rollouts, telemetry and fast rollback, which may be cheaper than proofs for non-catastrophic functions, and they disclose little.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.signpost: An operator (SpaceX, Amazon Kuiper, defense constellation contractors) or an FCC filing referring to formally verified collision-avoidance or deorbit logic.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic + auditor: S1 2029 -> 2031, S2 2028 -> 2029, S3 2027 -> 2029 (skeptic; auditor proposed 2028, but the prerequisites are 2027 in both S2 and S3 and S3 equals S2 until 2028), bands S1 Medium -> Low, S2 High -> Medium (S3 High kept), because this is a stronger instance of astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops and broke A3's lag ladder. Chain written (auditor). Skeptic: 'deorbit capability' -> 'deorbit command and decision logic'. Advocate: SpaceX-xAI vertical integration added to why; advocate's alternative of raising the general node instead was rejected (see astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops). Auditor: 'mostly decided onboard' is not in the cited source and is marked general.

verif-hls-autonomy-certification.title: Crewed lander autonomy certified with AI proofs
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.description: NASA human-rating (NPR 8705.2C with NPR 7150.2 Class A software), FAA commercial human-spaceflight rules or ECSS accept AI-produced machine-checked proofs as part of the certification evidence for crew-critical GNC autonomy (landing guidance, docking, abort and fault management). The likeliest first case is a block upgrade for a crewed lunar lander.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.status_oct2026: The first crewed landing moved to Artemis IV in 2028 (a Nov 2025 leaked SpaceX HLS schedule reported by Politico Pro gave a crewed landing in Sep 2028, an uncrewed landing in Jun 2027 and a propellant-transfer demonstration in Jun 2026, which has since slipped; 33FG news). NPR 8705.2C requires single-failure tolerance to catastrophic events, crew override of automation, and autonomous capability for functions whose loss would be catastrophic. No human-rated system has used AI-written proofs as evidence.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.why: The 2028 landing's software baseline will largely be set before public research-grade verification arrives, so AI proofs enter through block upgrades for 2029-31 landings. NASA's technical authority must accept the evidence, so the band is capped at Medium. Crewed acceptance needs the general regulator credit (infra-tool-qualification, Medium in S2 and S3) plus a human-rating step of its own, so it sits one band below that node: Low in S2 and S3.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.strongest_case_small: Human rating relies on testing, redundancy and crew override, and proofs add to that evidence rather than replace it. After Starliner, NASA's risk posture favors more testing, not less.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.signpost: NASA HLS or commercial-crew certification documents referencing formal proofs; NASA standards or software-engineering handbook guidance on AI-generated verification evidence.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.calibration_note: A3: Cross-domain consistency: this is the HLS instance of astro-human-rated-proof-credit (AI proofs accepted for crewed GNC), so it cannot be earlier or likelier than that general node, and crewed acceptance should lag the first uncrewed certification credit (S2 2030, S3 2029). Chain (S2): checker-route credit 2030 -> NASA technical authority accepts proofs for an HLS block upgrade 2031 at the earliest. S2 2030 -> 2031, S3 2029 -> 2030; bands Low/Medium/Medium -> Speculative/Low/Low (regulatory, crewed). A4: Resolved the A1/A3 disagreement on S3 (A1 merge patch Medium; A3 Low). Set to Low. The node is conjunctive: infra-tool-qualification (S3 Medium) plus a crewed human-rating step, under a post-Starliner posture that favours more testing. A dependent of a Medium regulatory node with a further uncertain regulatory step belongs below Medium. This also matches the merged astro node's original Speculative/Low/Low. Final: >2031/2031/2030, Speculative/Low/Low.

Reconciled to >2031/2031/2030, Speculative/Low/Medium: human-rating needs general regulator credit for AI proofs first (infra-tool-qualification, S2 premise 2030), uncrewed flight heritage (verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight, S2 2029) and a block-upgrade cycle after the 2028 landing's frozen baseline, so S2 2030 had no slack. Aviation precedent (DO-333 from 2011, years to routine use) supports astro's caution; regulator acceptance caps every scenario at Medium.

Advocate's S3 Low -> Medium and re-pointing to a checker-route node rejected: A4 already resolved S3 at Low (conjunctive regulatory logic under a post-Starliner testing posture), and the checker route is this branch's infra-tool-qualification. Years and bands unchanged.

verif-afss-part450.title: Proof-backed autonomous flight termination under FAA rules
verif-afss-part450.description: Autonomous flight safety system logic and other Part 450 computing-system safety items are licensed with formal proofs as an accepted means of compliance alongside RCC-319 testing.
verif-afss-part450.status_oct2026: Section 450.141 requires operators to identify computing-system safety items, set safety requirements by criticality and use a development process suited to that criticality. AC 450.141-1A, which includes an RCC-319 appendix on mission data loads, is an accepted means of compliance. There is no explicit credit for formal proofs, but the performance-based rule allows alternative means. Under 14 CFR 450.35(a), a means of compliance must be accepted before application acceptance for five items, including the highly reliable flight safety system (450.145(b)); computing-system safety items (450.141) are not among them. RCC 319 editions appeared in 2014, 2019 and 2025.
verif-afss-part450.why: Flight-termination logic is small, critical and well specified, which makes it the ideal first proof target in launch. Part 450 is performance-based and outside the DO-330 tool-qualification regime, so FAA AST acceptance is its own step rather than a consequence of DO-178C or NASA credit; infra-tool-qualification now accelerates rather than gates this node. For computing-system safety items an operator can include checker-verified proofs in its development process now; for the flight safety system itself the FAA must accept a proof-backed means of compliance under 450.35. Chain (S2): proof agents and FDIR model checking 2027 -> an operator includes proofs for computing-system safety items 2028-29 -> FAA accepts a proof-backed flight-safety-system means of compliance 2030. S2 is Low, not Medium: autonomous flight safety systems are already accepted through RCC-319 testing, applicants gain no license time from proofs (see strongest case), and FAA AST is a different office from the aircraft certification office that holds the DO-330 precedent. Regulator acceptance caps every scenario at Medium.
verif-afss-part450.strongest_case_small: License timelines are driven by environmental review, mishap investigations and public-safety analysis, not by software evidence (general). Flight-termination software is already heavily tested, so proofs will not speed licenses or raise launch cadence.
verif-afss-part450.signpost: A license record or FAA-accepted means of compliance citing formal verification of computing-system safety items or flight-safety-system logic. (An RCC-319 revision recognizing formal analysis is unlikely before 2031 on the 2014/2019/2025 cycle.)
verif-afss-part450.calibration_note: A1: its hard prerequisite verif-checker-not-generator was merged into infra-tool-qualification, which keeps the scenario premise for regulator credit for AI proofs (>2031/2030/2029); FAA Part 450 acceptance of proof-backed termination cannot precede that credit. Superseded by B-verified-autonomy: the hard edge from infra-tool-qualification is now soft (Part 450 sits outside DO-330), while years stay at >2031/2030/2029 on FAA AST's own acceptance chain.
